Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation to develop or identify and implement a training program for transportation sector employees on the identification and reporting of suspected human trafficking victims; requiring transportation sector employers to certify by January 1, 2027, and each year thereafter that certain employees have completed the training program; requiring new employees to receive training within 90 days of hiring; removing civil and criminal liability for reporting of suspected trafficking; etc.
Title: Department of Transportation - Human Trafficking Awareness, Training, and Response (See Someone, Save Someone Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: Enacts the See Someone, Save Someone Act, requiring the Maryland Department of Transportation (MDOT) to develop or identify and implement a human trafficking identification and reporting training program for certain transportation employees and contractors. The bill requires employers to certify employee training completion annually starting January 1, 2027, train new hires within 90 days, create reporting procedures and prevention policies, grants civil and criminal immunity for good-faith reporting, and requires public service announcements in English and Spanish at specified transit facilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: State and contract transportation employees working at transit stations, airports, port facilities, and highway rest stops, transit service providers and employers, and potential victims of human trafficking.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by $262,500 in FY 2026 and $137,500 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Transit Administration to develop an online training module ($125,000) and to cover estimated overtime costs for approximately 2,500 employees to complete the training during work hours. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is the primary implementing agency tasked with developing or identifying the human trafficking awareness training program, administering it across affected transportation divisions, collecting employer certifications, and requiring public service announcements at transit facilities.

As the MDOT modal administration operating public transit services and stations, MTA employs the majority of the staff subject to the training mandate and is anticipated by the fiscal note to develop the online training course at an estimated cost of $125,000.
SHA oversees state highways and rest stops; its employees and contract staff working at highway rest stops are subject to the training requirements and safety announcements mandated by the bill.
MAA operates state airport facilities (such as BWI), where employees must receive human trafficking identification training and where bilingual safety announcements must be broadcast or displayed.
MPA operates state port facilities whose staff and contractors are subject to the bill's training requirements and where public service announcements must be implemented.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Safe Harbor Regional Navigator Grant Program; the bill requires employers to establish reporting procedures that connect suspected trafficking incidents to these designated regional navigators.

Synopsis: Clarifying the definition of "physical therapist assistant" as used in the Maryland Physical Therapy Act to mean an individual licensed by the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners; increasing the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9; and requiring the Board to send renewal notices to licensees by electronic means, rather than first-class mail, unless the licensee requests to receive the renewal notice by first-class mail.
Title: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: House Bill 3 clarifies the definition of 'physical therapist assistant', increases the membership of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9 members by adding a second licensed physical therapist assistant, and requires license renewal notices to be sent electronically by default rather than by first-class mail.
responsible_party: State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners
stakeholders: Licensed physical therapists, licensed physical therapist assistants, and members of the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, board special fund expenditures increase by $1,500 annually for compensation for the additional board member, but decrease by an estimated $5,000 annually from switching default renewal notices to electronic delivery, resulting in net annual special fund savings of up to $3,500. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill alters board composition, modifies definitions, and updates electronic notification procedures affecting the board's operations and special fund expenditures.
The bill expands the State Board of Physical Therapy Examiners from 8 to 9 members, requiring the Governor to appoint an additional licensed physical therapist assistant member.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, and will handle the additional physical therapist assistant seat created by this legislation.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a restriction on land use that increases the cost of installing a solar collector system by at least 5% over a certain cost or that reduces the efficiency of the system by at least 10% under a certain energy generation level; authorizing a community association to impose certain restrictions on the installation of solar collector systems in common areas or common elements; authorizing a community association to install a solar collector system in common areas or common elements under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Restrictions on Use - Solar Collector Systems - Alteration

NarrowSubjects.Name: Energy Matters -see also- Fuel; NuclearMatt; PwrPlnts; etc.

bill_summary: Defines an unreasonable land use restriction on solar collector systems as one that increases installation costs by at least 5% or reduces projected energy generation by at least 10% compared to the initially proposed installation. The bill requires property owners to submit supporting documentation from a certified or experienced solar panel design specialist and clarifies the authority of community associations to regulate, restrict, or install solar systems in common areas or elements.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Property owners, community associations (homeowners associations and condominiums), and solar energy designers and installers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially impact State or local government operations or finances, and has a minimal effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Energy Administration (MEA) advises on state energy policy and promotes the adoption of renewable energy technologies, including residential solar. MEA is also cited as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy analysis.

The Maryland Department of Planning oversees the Maryland Historical Trust, whose director is statutorily responsible under Section 2-119(d) for determining whether a historic property is listed in or eligible for the Maryland Register of Historic Properties, thereby exempting it from these solar collector restrictions.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative support to the state judiciary, which handles civil litigation and disputes between property owners and community associations regarding real property restrictions and solar easements; the agency was consulted as an information source in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Altering certain definitions related to the Food Resiliency Council; defining what constitutes "healthy food priority areas" as predominantly lower-income areas that have limited access to retail outlets that sell affordable, healthy foods; defining "wasted food" as food not used for its intended purpose; requiring the Council to make recommendations to increase the availability of local foods, create market opportunities for Maryland food businesses, and expand access to small scale food production infrastructure; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 9 updates the duties and definitions pertaining to the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council. It establishes definitions for 'healthy food priority areas' and 'wasted food,' incorporates local food production and procurement goals into ongoing resiliency policy recommendations, eliminates outdated one-time reporting requirements, and mandates the inclusion of policy and legislative change recommendations in the Council's annual report.
responsible_party: Maryland Food System Resiliency Council (within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management)
stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing food insecurity or living in healthy food priority areas, local food businesses and agricultural producers, and local food council organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local government operations and finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Food System Resiliency Council is housed within the Office of Resilience in the Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), and MDEM staffs the council and implements the bill's reporting and operational updates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory definitions, specific policy goals, and ongoing annual reporting requirements of the Maryland Food System Resiliency Council.

The Maryland State Department of Education is specifically mentioned in the bill's statutory provisions as the recipient of the Council's recommendations regarding student nutrition and the federal Community Eligibility Provision.

Synopsis: Repealing the June 30, 2025, termination date for certain provisions of law related to referrals to and reimbursement of specialists and nonphysician specialists who are not part of a carrier's provider panel; prohibiting certain carriers from imposing utilization review requirements other than would be required if the covered benefit was provided by a provider on the carrier's provider panel under certain circumstances; etc.

bill_summary: This bill permanently extends and expands requirements for health insurance carriers regarding member access to out-of-network specialists and nonphysician specialists. It requires carriers to provide referrals and additional assistance to arrange coverage for mental health and substance use disorder services at in-network cost-sharing levels for the duration of a treatment plan when network access standards are not met, and prohibits carriers from imposing utilization review requirements beyond those applied to in-network providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance policyholders and members seeking specialized care (particularly mental health and substance use disorder services), commercial health insurance carriers, and nonparticipating healthcare specialists and behavioral health providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) increase minimally in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees. MIA can handle any additional regulatory workload using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, and no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs affected by this bill. MIA will oversee compliance with the revised referral and utilization review procedures, review rate and form filings, and collect associated filing fees.

The bill regulates coverage and referral access for mental health and substance use disorder services and references behavioral health programs licensed by MDH under § 7.5-401 of the Health - General Article.
DBM oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; the fiscal note evaluated the program's operations and determined there is no fiscal impact.

Synopsis: Authorizing the officers and employees of the Field Enforcement Division of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission to issue a citation for a violation of §10-108 of the Criminal Law Article; prohibiting the sale or distribution of certain products that contain tetrahydrocannabinol or are advertised as containing tetrahydrocannabinol; authorizing the Executive Director of the Commission to seize, destroy, or confiscate a certain unlawful product; etc.
Title: Cannabis - Sale and Distribution - Tetrahydrocannabinol Offenses

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale or distribution of products containing tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) that violate potency, packaging, or labeling requirements, or that are advertised as containing THC exceeding statutory thresholds. It authorizes the Field Enforcement Division of the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) to issue citations for underage sales and other THC-related offenses, allows the ATCC Executive Director to seize and confiscate illicit THC products, establishes that displaying or offering THC for sale without a license is prima facie evidence of selling it, and sets misdemeanor fines up to $5,000 for unlicensed violators while subjecting licensees to administrative disciplinary action.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission (ATCC) and Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA)
stakeholders: Licensed cannabis businesses, unlicensed retailers and distributors of THC and hemp products, consumers, and law enforcement agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may experience a minimal increase beginning in FY 2026 from penalties and citations heard in District Court. ATCC, MCA, and the District Court can implement the bill and handle any associated caseload with existing budgeted resources. There is no material impact on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Maryland Cannabis Administration (MCA) by subjecting licensed cannabis entities that violate THC packaging, labeling, potency, or advertising restrictions to disciplinary action by the Administration pursuant to § 36-202. The bill also relies on potency and product standards promulgated and overseen by MCA.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor offense punishable by a fine up to $5,000, authorizes law enforcement to charge certain violations via citation, and establishes evidentiary rules regarding prima facie evidence of unlicensed THC sales in prosecutions handled by the District Court.
The bill specifically references cooperative arrangements between the Field Enforcement Division and the Office of the Comptroller regarding enforcement of cannabis and tax provisions.
State and local law enforcement officers collaborate with the Field Enforcement Division on peace officer duties, criminal enforcement, and the issuance of citations for prohibited THC sales.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office was consulted regarding potential impacts on criminal charging and defense caseloads resulting from the new misdemeanor THC citations and penalties.

bill_summary: Enacts the Maryland Limited Worker Cooperative Association Act, authorizing the creation, operation, governance, conversion, and dissolution of limited worker cooperative associations (LWCAs) and collective worker cooperatives as limited liability companies under Maryland law.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Workers, small business owners, entrepreneurs seeking cooperative business structures, and commercial insurers providing workers' compensation.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $278,400 in FY 2027 only for one-time computer programming costs at the State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT). State revenues may see a minimal increase from business document filing fees. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article and Corporations and Associations Article to specifically mandate that the Maryland Insurance Commissioner enforce statutory provisions regarding how insurers calculate workers' compensation insurance premiums for covered employee members of limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill amends multiple sections of the Tax - General Article governing admissions and amusement tax, motor fuel tax, income tax withholding, and sales and use tax to extend personal liability for unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties to individuals with direct fiscal control over limited worker cooperative associations.

The bill explicitly exempts membership interests and equity instruments of limited worker cooperative associations from the registration and broker-dealer requirements of the Maryland Securities Act (Title 11), which is administered and enforced by the Securities Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill establishes legal and judicial standards for limited worker cooperative associations, including provisions for judicial dissolution and service of process, and the Judiciary/Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted for the bill's fiscal and policy analysis.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain provisions of law relating to the inspection of recorded images apply to recorded images produced by a noise abatement monitoring system; and extending by 2 years the reporting and termination dates of the noise abatement monitoring systems pilot programs in Montgomery County and Prince George's County.

bill_summary: This bill extends the noise abatement monitoring system pilot programs in Montgomery County and Prince George's County by two years, setting a new termination date of June 30, 2028, and moving the program reporting deadline to December 1, 2027. It also applies public records inspection restrictions to recorded images from noise abatement systems, requiring record custodians to deny public inspection of the images except to cited individuals, their attorneys, or authorized agency employees.
responsible_party: Montgomery County and Prince George's County governing bodies, alongside the District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Motorists and residents in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, local law enforcement agencies, and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally in FY 2027 and FY 2028 from contested citations collected in District Court, which can absorb the caseload within existing resources. Local revenues and expenditures for Montgomery and Prince George's counties will increase in FY 2027 and FY 2028 if the pilot programs are continued. Montgomery County previously estimated annual expenditures of $99,400, while fine revenues (capped at $75 per violation) are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the noise abatement monitoring pilot program through June 30, 2028. Contested citations are heard in the District Court, and the District Court is responsible for prescribing a uniform citation form and collecting fine revenues from contested citations.
The bill extends the pilot reporting deadline to December 1, 2027, requiring participating counties to submit comprehensive operational and fiscal evaluation reports directly to the Governor.

Synopsis: Expanding the purpose of the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff; requiring the Department to prioritize funding for nurses or nursing support staff who practice in an area with a shortage of nurses or nursing support staff or who practice in a specialty where a shortage has been identified; altering certain education requirements for licensure; repealing a certain requirement that the State Board of Nursing approve certain nursing assistant training program sites within a certain time period; etc.

bill_summary: The Building Opportunities for Nurses Act of 2025 extends the State Board of Nursing and the Secretary of Health's authority over its infrastructure operations through July 1, 2030, allowing board special funds to cover infrastructure costs. It expands the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff to include for-profit employment in workforce shortage areas, modifies education and endorsement pathways for registered nurses, delays the implementation dates for certified nursing assistant tier credentials to 2026, and extends several healthcare preceptor income tax credit programs through 2030 while reducing required rotation training hours from 100 to 90.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the State Board of Nursing
stakeholders: Registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, nurse practitioners, certified nursing assistants, healthcare preceptors, nursing students, and healthcare facilities located in designated workforce shortage areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by approximately $440,000 in FY 2025 as the Board of Nursing resumes paying for infrastructure operations from its special fund. General fund revenues decrease by up to $100,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2030 due to the extension of the physician preceptorship tax credit. General fund expenditures increase by up to $100,000 annually from FY 2026 through FY 2030 to fund the nurse preceptorship tax credit. Special fund revenues and expenditures for preceptorship funds increase by up to $100,000 in FY 2026 and up to $300,000 annually thereafter through FY 2030. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the sunset termination date for the State Board of Nursing (housed within MDH) to 2030, continues the Secretary of Health's authority over the Board's infrastructure operations, expands MDH's Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program (MLARP) for Nurses and Nursing Support Staff, and extends preceptorship tax credit programs administered by MDH.

The bill extends several income tax credits for preceptors (nurse practitioners, physicians, physician assistants, LPNs, and RNs) through tax year 2029, which the Comptroller must administer and which will impact State general fund revenues.

The bill maintains the requirement under Health Occupations § 8–6A–14 that the State Board of Nursing, in conjunction with the Maryland Higher Education Commission, approve nursing assistant training programs and develop regulations for those programs.

Under the Tax - General provisions amended and extended by the bill (§ 10–739 and § 10–739.1), the Department of Health must consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board to identify geographic areas in Maryland with health care workforce shortages for preceptorship tax credit eligibility.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to conduct an annual study examining and comparing certain data regarding an individual's residence prior to incarceration and on release from a State correctional facility; and requiring the Department by October 1, 2026, and each October 1 thereafter, to report the results of the study to certain committees of the General Assembly.

bill_summary: Requires the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to conduct an annual study examining data on the location and county of residence of individuals before and after incarceration in a State correctional facility, and to submit an annual report to specified legislative committees beginning October 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, individuals released from State correctional facilities, and local county communities receiving returning citizens.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not impacted as the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services can conduct the study and prepare the annual reports using existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS) conduct an annual study tracking the location of individuals before and following incarceration in State correctional facilities and submit annual reports to specified legislative committees beginning October 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program in the Maryland Department of the Environment to permit and regulate the planned placement of treated reclaimed water into surface water reservoirs used as drinking water sources, while extending the termination date of the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program to June 30, 2030.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Local governments operating public water systems, drinking water utilities, and Maryland residents receiving public drinking water.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $97,300 in FY 2026, $85,800 in FY 2027, and $89,500 in FY 2028 for contractual staff to establish the program and develop regulations before terminating at the end of FY 2028. Special fund revenues increase by an estimated $75,000 in FY 2030 from a permit application fee. Local expenditures increase for participating local governments (such as the City of Westminster) to pay the application fee and fulfill water treatment and permitting requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Reservoir Augmentation Program within MDE, requiring the department to adopt regulations, review applications, issue and enforce permits, collect fees, manage a dedicated special fund, and report periodically to the General Assembly and the Governor.
MDE is required to submit implementation reports on the Indirect Potable Reuse Pilot Program and the Reservoir Augmentation Program to the Governor on specified recurring statutory schedules.

bill_summary: This bill replaces the statutory commission rate schedules for trustees with a standard of compensation that is reasonable under the circumstances when the trust agreement does not specify compensation. It sets forth factors for courts to consider when assessing reasonableness, requires regular trustee compensation to be split equally between trust income and trust principal, and maintains the existing statutory commission rate structure for guardians of property.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts) and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation
stakeholders: Trustees, trust beneficiaries, guardians of the property of minors or disabled persons, financial institutions, and estate and trust attorneys
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund income tax revenues may be impacted if trust income or principal shifts to personal or business income of trustees via increased compensation, but the impact cannot be reliably estimated and is likely to be limited. State expenditures are not materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the state court system, providing criteria and procedures for circuit courts to review, increase, decrease, or determine the reasonableness of compensation and allowances for guardians of property and trustees.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and probate matters in Maryland and was consulted as an information source regarding modifications to statutory commissions and compensation under the Estates and Trusts Article.

The Comptroller may be affected fiscally to the extent that shifting trust income or principal into trustees' personal or taxable business income alters state income tax collections, as identified in the fiscal note.
The Department of Labor houses the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, the statutory regulatory repository where qualifying institutional trustees and attorneys file schedules of rates.

bill_summary: Establishes 'right to repair' requirements for powered wheelchairs, requiring manufacturers to provide documentation, parts, embedded software, firmware, and tools on fair and reasonable terms to independent repair providers and wheelchair owners for specified components. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Powered wheelchair owners and individuals with physical disabilities, independent wheelchair repair providers, authorized repair providers, and wheelchair manufacturers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances and operations are not materially impacted. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can handle enforcement and implementation with existing resources, and the bill's application of existing civil and criminal penalty provisions is not expected to have a material financial effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill makes a violation of the powered wheelchair right-to-repair requirements an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.

The bill directly impacts the maintenance and repair of assistive technology (powered wheelchairs) used by individuals with physical disabilities, which falls squarely within the Department's policy focus areas of community living, accessibility, and assistive technology support.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to establish a forensic review board at facilities that have charge of persons who have been committed to the facility as not criminally responsible; authorizing a forensic review board to make recommendations relating to the release or rehabilitation of a committed person; requiring the board to give notice at least 10 days before a meeting concerning the committed person; requiring the board to give consideration to a written statement offered by the committed person to the board; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to establish a forensic review board at each facility housing individuals committed as not criminally responsible (NCR). The boards, composed of licensed healthcare providers, must conduct reviews at least annually to determine whether to recommend to the court that a committed person be granted conditional release or discharge, formulate plans to overcome release barriers, and allow committed individuals to be represented by authorized nonlegal agents at meetings.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals committed to state facilities after being found not criminally responsible (NCR), facility treatment teams and healthcare providers, defense representatives and authorized agents, state courts, and State's Attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, as State forensic hospitals and the Community Forensic Aftercare Program already operate forensic review boards. The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Local effect: No material effect on local finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to establish forensic review boards at each facility housing individuals committed as not criminally responsible (NCR), adopt regulations to carry out the provisions, and implement treatment and rehabilitation recommendations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents committed indigent individuals in criminal commitment and release proceedings. The bill requires notice to counsel of record, grants access to board records, and permits social workers or nonlegal representatives from the attorney's office to serve as authorized agents during board meetings.

The forensic review boards make formal recommendations regarding discharge or conditional release to the court, board records must be provided to the court upon request, and board representatives may testify at judicial release hearings.

Administrative Law Judges at the Office of Administrative Hearings routinely conduct administrative hearings regarding the release and discharge eligibility of committed persons under Title 3 of the Criminal Procedure Article.

bill_summary: This bill revises the Maryland Corps Program and its service pathways (Young Adult Service Year Option and Maryland Service Year Option), updating participant eligibility, age requirements, and compensation structures. bill_summary: This bill consolidates three aging services programs—Senior Care, the Senior Assisted Living Subsidy (SALS), and the Congregate Housing Services Provider (CHSP) programs—into a unified system administered by the Maryland Department of Aging (MDOA). It repeals the Interagency Committee on Aging Services, transferring and clarifying its duties under MDOA, and updates statutory terminology from "seniors" to "older adults." Additionally, it requires MDOA and Area Agencies on Aging to conduct transition planning and person-centered assessments for currently enrolled individuals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Older adults in Maryland, their family caregivers, Area Agencies on Aging, assisted living facility providers, and congregate housing service providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational requirements can likely be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. The fiscal 2026 state budget includes $20.1 million in general funds across the three consolidating programs ($13.2 million for Senior Care, $4.9 million for SALS, and $1.9 million for CHSP), which are assumed to fund the consolidated program beginning in fiscal 2027. State expenditures and local revenues/expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal 2027 to the extent MDOA enters into new agreements or contracts with local governments or other entities to coordinate services. Area Agencies on Aging can conduct required person-centered transition assessments using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reorganizes and consolidates the Department of Aging's major programs (Senior Care, Senior Assisted Living Subsidy, and Congregate Housing Services Provider programs) under a unified statutory framework, transfers the responsibilities of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services directly to the Department, and charges it with program transition planning and administering the single points of entry network.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services, and the bill alters and consolidates senior housing and supportive living service frameworks.
The Secretary of Human Services was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services.
The Secretary of Disabilities was a statutory member of the repealed Interagency Committee on Aging Services.
The Department of Aging plans to coordinate with DBM to consolidate three distinct budget lines (Senior Care, SALS, and CHSP totaling over $20 million) into a single unified budget program.

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland's Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS) framework administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). It excludes hospitals and certain manufacturing facilities from the definition of covered buildings and establishes exemptions and special accounting credits for on-site renewable energy, biomethane use, steam sterilization, emergency backup power, and sensitive compartmented information facilities. The bill establishes an annual reporting fee of $100 per covered building, requires MDE to certify qualifying county-level BEPS programs (exempting buildings in those counties from the State program), and directs MDE to complete a comprehensive cost-benefit study and policy recommendations regarding BEPS options by December 31, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners and commercial tenants of commercial and multifamily residential buildings (35,000 square feet or larger), hospitals, manufacturing facilities, defense and intelligence facilities, local governments (notably Montgomery County), and energy auditors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $690,000 in FY 2026, increasing to $746,900 by FY 2030 due to a $100 annual reporting fee (adjusted for inflation) assessed on an estimated 6,900 covered buildings. MDE administrative expenditures increase by $1,033,837 in FY 2026 (5 regular positions plus contractual tracking and study costs); because fee revenue covers $690,000, general fund expenditures increase by $343,837 in FY 2026 to fund the initial shortfall. State and local agencies owning covered buildings will incur minor annual costs to pay the reporting fee starting in FY 2026. Future alternative compliance pathway fee revenues collected by the State may decrease beginning in FY 2031 due to added exemptions and county certifications.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary regulatory and implementing agency responsible for adopting regulations, establishing and enforcing Building Energy Performance Standards (BEPS), certifying county BEPS programs, collecting reporting fees, and completing the mandated cost-benefit study.

DGS oversees the operation, maintenance, and energy management of state-owned facilities. State-owned buildings meeting the size threshold are covered buildings subject to the BEPS requirements and the annual reporting fee.

MEA coordinates state energy efficiency and renewable energy policy, which intersects directly with building energy performance metrics, energy use intensity, and on-site clean energy standards addressed by the bill.

Multifamily residential buildings of 35,000 square feet or more are covered buildings under BEPS, directly intersecting with DHCD's oversight and financing of residential housing and energy efficiency initiatives.
USM owns and operates numerous campus facilities meeting the covered building threshold (35,000 sq ft or greater) that must comply with BEPS standards and pay the annual reporting fee.
As an independent state university owning substantial campus facilities, Morgan State University is subject to BEPS reporting requirements and fee payments for its eligible covered buildings.
MDOT operates and maintains significant state-owned administrative and operational facilities that are subject to the BEPS standards and annual reporting fees as covered state buildings.
OAG provides legal counsel and enforcement support to MDE for regulatory promulgation and compliance enforcement, including additional legal staffing noted in the fiscal analysis.

fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues and expenditures for HSCRC increase by an estimated $1.6 million in FY 2026, growing to $4.8 million in FY 2030 compared to current law. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to HSCRC by repealing the sunset on the statutory formula used to calculate the maximum user fees it assesses on hospitals, preserving higher special fund revenues needed to support commission operations and the AHEAD Model.

HSCRC is an independent agency located within MDH, and this was introduced as an MDH departmental bill. Additionally, the higher hospital user fees will increase MDH Medicaid expenditures by hundreds of thousands of dollars annually due to associated hospital rate adjustments.

bill_summary: This bill revises Maryland's tax sale process by requiring local collectors statewide to withhold owner-occupied residential properties and homes occupied by heirs of deceased owners from tax sale if unpaid taxes and liens are under $1,000. It caps the annual redemption interest rate on owner-occupied residential properties at 10%, excludes post-sale taxes, interest, and penalties from redemption payments for owner-occupied properties statewide, requires counties to establish a registry for properties to be withheld from sale, mandates notice of foreclosure proceedings on owner-occupied properties to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, enhances tenant notice requirements prior to eviction, and expands the Homeowner Protection Program to include heirs and personal representatives of deceased homeowners.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Maryland homeowners (especially low-income, senior, disabled homeowners, and heirs of deceased homeowners), tenants in foreclosed residential properties, local governments and tax collectors, and private tax lien purchasers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State Annuity Bond Fund (ABF) revenues are delayed and/or reduced by up to an estimated $92,000 annually due to limits on the redemption rate for owner-occupied properties; State expenditures are not materially affected. Local government revenues are also delayed or reduced, potentially by up to $1.1 million annually from the redemption rate cap and the $1,000 tax sale withholding threshold. Local government expenditures may increase for administrative, personnel, and IT programming costs to track owner-occupied properties and maintain the required withholding registry.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 59 was requested as a departmental bill by the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). The bill aims to protect vulnerable homeowners, prevent displacement, assist heirs in retaining inherited family homes, and facilitate the return of abandoned properties to productive redevelopment.

The bill directly impacts circuit court foreclosure proceedings by modifying procedures to foreclose the right of redemption, adding required notice to the State Tax Sale Ombudsman, and altering procedural rules and notice timelines regarding writs of possession for tenant-occupied properties.

The bill has a minor fiscal impact on Annuity Bond Fund revenues (reducing or delaying state property tax receipts by up to $92,000 annually), which are managed by the Treasurer's Office to pay debt service on the State's general obligation bonds.

bill_summary: This bill alters the scheduling and administration requirements for special elections to fill vacancies in a county council or the office of county executive. It requires the election date to be at least 90 days after the adoption of the county council resolution and not within 120 days of a regularly scheduled election. It also provides that if a conflict exists between local charter laws and State election law or regulations, the State Administrator must conduct the election under State law. Additionally, for vote-by-mail special elections, it expands the ballot mailing deadline from 14 to at least 30 days before election day, permits ballot drop box returns, and eliminates the requirement for local boards of elections to mail specimen ballots.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections (State Administrator of Elections) and local boards of elections
stakeholders: Registered voters in counties holding special elections, local boards of elections, county councils, county executives, and candidates for local office.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected. Local government finances may be indirectly affected depending on the timing of special elections, as the restrictions may alter whether a county must conduct a special election independent of a regularly scheduled election or concurrently, with independent special elections entailing substantial local expenditures (e.g., Prince George's County spent $2.1 million on a countywide mail-in special primary in 2024).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 75 was introduced at the request of the State Board of Elections (SBE) and directly affects the administration of special elections in Maryland. The bill alters special election timelines, authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to enforce state law and regulations over conflicting local charters, eliminates the specimen ballot mailing requirement for vote-by-mail special elections, adjusts ballot mailing deadlines, and authorizes ballot drop boxes for mail-in special elections.

The Register of Wills oversees estate administration and serves as clerk to the Orphans' Court; although decanting primarily pertains to trusts, procedural changes under the Estates and Trusts Article directly intersect with their domain of probate and fiduciary administration.

The Office of the Attorney General enforces consumer protections, oversees charitable trusts that may be subject to decanting notices, and provided input as an information source during the bill's review.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain crimes relating to animals do not include certain activities; establishing that each animal harmed in a violation of a prohibition against animal cruelty is a separate offense and shall be deemed an individual victim for purposes of the sentencing guidelines stacking rule; establishing that a conviction for a crime relating to animals may not merge with a conviction for any other crime based on the act establishing the violation; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes that each animal harmed in an animal cruelty violation constitutes a separate offense and is considered an individual victim for the sentencing guidelines stacking rule. It prevents animal crime convictions from merging with convictions for other crimes based on the same act, authorizes consecutive or concurrent sentencing, and clarifies exemptions for humane hunting and fishing conducted under State law.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Maryland State Commission on Criminal Sentencing Policy
stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of animal cruelty crimes, state and local judicial and correctional systems, law enforcement officers, hunters, and anglers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues may increase minimally due to additional fine collections in District Court and circuit courts. State and local expenditures may increase minimally due to potential longer periods of incarceration resulting from separate convictions and consecutive sentencing under the sentencing guidelines stacking rule. Incarceration costs average $5,339 per month for State facilities and $140 to $350 per day for local facilities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the judicial system by establishing that each harmed animal constitutes a separate offense for sentencing guidelines stacking, prohibiting merger of convictions, and permitting consecutive sentencing in District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill allows for multiple separate convictions and consecutive sentences for animal cruelty violations, potentially increasing sentence lengths and expenditures for State correctional facilities and supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts criminal defense caseloads and representation for indigent defendants who face expanded charges, non-merging convictions, and stacked sentencing for each animal harmed.
The bill clarifies that animal cruelty provisions do not apply to hunting and fishing activities conducted in compliance with Title 4 and Title 10 of the Natural Resources Article.
The bill maintains statutory exemptions for customary agricultural husbandry practices, veterinary practices, and farming operations overseen and supported by the department.

responsible_party: State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, and refrigeration contractors and licensees in Maryland with expired licenses
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of HVACR Contractors can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and expenditures are not expected to be materially affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the licensing restoration timeframe for the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, which is an occupational licensing board housed within and administered by the Maryland Department of Labor.

It also authorizes local health departments and community-based organizations to appeal adverse program authorization decisions to the Secretary of Health or their designee instead of the Deputy Secretary.

stakeholders: Local health departments, community-based organizations operating or seeking to operate Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs, and members of the Standing Advisory Committee.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact, as the changes are technical in nature and do not directly affect governmental finances.

It shifts the authority to hear appeals of program authorization denials and to chair the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs from the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services to the Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition and leadership of the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs by replacing the Deputy Secretary for Public Health Services with the Secretary of Health or the Secretary's designee as a member and chair.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy is responsible for nominating a law enforcement representative to serve on the Standing Advisory Committee on Opioid-Associated Disease Prevention and Outreach Programs.

Synopsis: Establishing a population ratio quota for certain Class A (off-sale) and Class D (off-sale) licenses in Anne Arundel County; specifying a certain official map to be used to identify certain tax assessment districts for purposes of the population ratio quota; and prohibiting the Board of License Commissioners for Anne Arundel County from approving the transfer of certain alcoholic beverages licenses under certain circumstances.
Title: Anne Arundel County - Class A (Off-Sale) and Class D (Off-Sale) Licenses - Population Ratio Quota
bill_summary: Establishes a population ratio quota for Class A and Class D off-sale alcoholic beverages licenses in Anne Arundel County, prohibiting the issuance of new licenses if the ratio exceeds one license per 3,500 individuals in a tax assessment district (excluding the 6th assessment district). It also restricts the transfer of these licenses outside of their original assessment district, with exemptions for existing licenses and certain brewery on-site consumption permits.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class A and Class D off-sale alcoholic beverages license holders and applicants, local businesses, and residents of Anne Arundel County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Anne Arundel County revenues and expenditures are not affected; while new off-sale licenses are temporarily restricted in several assessment districts until population increases, existing licenses are grandfathered, resulting in no change to current county license fee revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article regarding retail alcoholic beverages licenses and references State-issued Class 5 brewery licenses. While retail licensing is administered locally by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller regulates Maryland's alcohol industry and state-level alcohol manufacturer licenses.

bill_summary: Expands the definition of a 'public entity' in Maryland insurance law to include Resilience Authorities, thereby allowing them to pool together with other public entities to purchase casualty, property, or health insurance or to self-insure against those risks.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Resilience authorities, local governments that incorporate resilience authorities, and other public entities participating in insurance pools.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are unaffected. Local expenditures may decrease to the extent that resilience authorities participate in insurance pooling and achieve lower premium or insurance costs; local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 19-602 of the Insurance Article to expand the definition of 'public entity' to include resilience authorities for the purpose of insurance pooling and self-insurance. As the primary regulatory agency overseeing Maryland's insurance laws and market practices, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees compliance with statutory insurance provisions.

Synopsis: Defining "anchor date" to establish certain reference points for the calculation of a certain covered employee's average weekly wage and eligibility for increases in weekly benefits under the Family Medical Leave and Insurance Program; requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt regulations establishing an optional self-employed enrollment program governing the participation of self-employed individuals in the Program; repealing certain requirements related to  contributions made by certain participating individuals; etc.
Title: Family and Medical Leave Insurance Program - Revisions

bill_summary: This bill alters and delays key implementation dates and administrative requirements for the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. It delays the start date of required employer and employee contributions by 18 months to January 1, 2027, and delays the start of benefit payments to a date between January 1, 2027, and January 3, 2028, as determined by the Secretary of Labor. It also establishes the term "anchor date" to govern average weekly wage calculations and benefit increases, modifies the definition of an application year, delays the inflation indexing of maximum weekly benefits to 2029, and postpones the optional self-employed enrollment program until regulations are adopted by July 1, 2028.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Maryland employers (especially those with 15 or more employees), Maryland workers/covered employees, self-employed individuals, community service providers reimbursed by the State, and the Maryland Department of Labor.
fiscal_impact_summary: State FAMLI special fund revenues decrease by approximately $1,272.5 million in FY 2026 and $1,316.9 million in FY 2027 due to the 18-month delay in contributions. Special fund expenditures for benefit payments decrease by up to $1,753.5 million in FY 2027 and $946.7 million in FY 2028. For FY 2026, special fund administrative expenditures decrease by $66.8 million, general fund expenditures increase by $37.3 million for non-deferrable program administration, and provider reimbursement expenditures through the Maryland Department of Health decrease by $14.8 million in general funds and $14.9 million in federal funds (a net FY 2026 general fund increase of $22.5 million). The bill also eliminates a mandated appropriation for FY 2026. Local government expenditures decrease in FY 2026 and FY 2027 due to delayed employer contributions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor administers the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) Program. HB 102 is a departmental bill that directly modifies the program's statutory implementation dates, contribution schedules, benefit calculation rules, reporting requirements, and mandates the adoption of regulations for self-employed individuals.

Under state law and Section 8.3-601 of the Labor and Employment Article, the Maryland Department of Health is required to reimburse certain licensed community providers for employer FAMLI contributions. The delay in contributions directly reduces MDH general and federal fund reimbursement expenditures by nearly $30 million in FY 2026.

The Board of Public Works is statutorily designated under the FAMLI law to monitor state employment data and determine whether negative economic conditions exist to pause the annual Consumer Price Index adjustments to maximum weekly benefits.

As the state's budget and personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and state agency appropriations. The bill effectuates contingent budget provisions in the FY 2026 state operating budget, resulting in adjustments to general and special fund expenditures.

Synopsis: Altering the purpose and use of the Maryland Farms and Families Fund to match purchases made with FMNP, SNAP, and WIC benefits at certain farmers markets and farm stands, support nonprofit farmers markets by providing logistical and marketing support to increase the use of federal nutrition programs at these markets, and to support nonprofit  organizations or other responsible persons to implement the Program.

bill_summary: Alters the purpose and authorized uses of the Maryland Farms and Families Fund by allowing the Maryland Department of Agriculture to implement the program internally or provide funds to qualified nonprofit organizations or other responsible persons to match federal nutrition benefits (FMNP, SNAP, and WIC) at farmers markets and farm stands.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Food-insecure Maryland residents utilizing federal nutrition benefits (SNAP, WIC, and FMNP), Maryland farmers and farmers market operators, and nonprofit organizations managing food incentive programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances, as it only alters the allowable uses and administration of the existing Maryland Farms and Families Fund (which receives an ongoing mandated annual appropriation of $300,000). The Maryland Department of Agriculture can implement the bill using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Agriculture (MDA) requested the bill and is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the Maryland Farms and Families Program and Fund, including directly managing program funds and overseeing partnerships with farmers markets.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO has historically served as the grant applicant and fiscal pass-through entity to manage the program statewide with the Southern Maryland Agricultural Development Commission; this bill directly streamlines the process by eliminating the need to route funds through MARBIDCO.

Synopsis: Requiring a person who makes an automatic renewal offer to consumers to allow a consumer to cancel the automatic renewal in a cost-effective, timely, and easy-to-use manner; requiring automatic renewal offers to be displayed in a certain manner and contain certain information; establishing that compliance with certain regulations or a certain license shall be considered to be compliance with the Act; establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice; etc.

bill_summary: Regulates automatic renewal and continuous service offers for subscriptions and purchasing agreements by requiring businesses to clearly disclose renewal terms, obtain consumer consent before recurring credit card charges, provide advance notice before renewal or the end of a free trial, and offer simple, cost-effective cancellation mechanisms. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Maryland consumers enrolled in or entering into subscription services and businesses offering automatic renewal contracts
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill's penalty provisions will not materially affect State or local finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can administer and enforce the requirements using existing resources. No private right of action for damages is authorized.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill defines violations of the automatic renewal requirements as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is enforced by the Consumer Protection Division within the Office of the Attorney General.

The bill specifically mentions and exempts businesses or entities whose contract renewal practices are subject to rules, regulations, procedures, or guidelines established by the Maryland Insurance Administration.
The bill specifically mentions and exempts services regulated by the Maryland Public Service Commission from the new automatic renewal statutory requirements.

Synopsis: Establishing requirements for the commercial application of general use pesticides, the commercial application of restricted use pesticides, and the private application of restricted use pesticides; requiring a certified private applicator to ensure that certain individuals working under the certified applicator's supervision meet certain requirements; specifying the responsibility and liability of certified applicators for the application of certain pesticides; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires that commercial applications of restricted use pesticides be performed directly by certified applicators, eliminating the option for noncertified individuals to apply them under supervision. It establishes federal compliance and direct supervision standards for noncertified individuals applying restricted use pesticides privately in agriculture, specifies liability for certified applicators, and repeals obsolete statutory provisions regulating cyclodiene termiticides and tributyltin antifouling paint.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Commercial pest control businesses, certified and registered pest control applicators, private agricultural pesticide applicators, and public agency applicators.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues for the Maryland Department of Agriculture's Pesticide Fund increase by at least $140,000 annually starting in FY 2026 due to an estimated 2,000 registered employees upgrading to certified applicators and paying higher annual certification fees. State expenditures are unaffected as administrative tasks can be absorbed with existing resources, and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill was requested by the Maryland Department of Agriculture and directly alters the Pesticide Applicator's Law under Title 5 of the Agriculture Article, requiring the department to administer new certification requirements and examinations, as well as collect increased annual certification fee revenues for the State Pesticide Fund.

DNR employs public agency applicators who perform pest and vegetation management on state-owned lands and waterways, and must ensure its personnel comply with the updated certification and supervision standards for restricted and general use pesticides.

MDOT employs public agency applicators to perform pest control along highways and transit rights-of-way, and must ensure that personnel applying pesticides meet the revised applicator certification requirements.

bill_summary: Enacts the Utility Transparency and Accountability Act, requiring electric companies (excluding municipal electric utilities) to submit an annual report to the Public Service Commission by February 1 detailing all recorded votes cast by the company or its State affiliates at regional transmission organization meetings during the preceding calendar year.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Maryland electric companies (excluding municipal electric utilities), their State affiliates, regional transmission organizations such as PJM Interconnection, LLC, and Maryland electricity consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State finances or operations and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission (PSC) is the primary regulatory body designated to receive and oversee the annual reports submitted by electric companies detailing recorded votes cast at regional transmission organization meetings.

The Office of the People's Counsel advocates on behalf of Maryland's residential utility consumers before the PSC and federal regulatory bodies regarding utility operations, rates, and transmission issues, and is actively involved in monitoring RTO stakeholder voting and transparency.

fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not significantly affected, as any expense reimbursements for the two additional commission members can be handled with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the statutory composition and membership requirements of the Maryland Correctional Training Commission.
The bill authorizes the Governor to appoint an employee of the Division of Parole and Probation to the Maryland Correctional Training Commission.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, recruiting, and processing appointments to state boards and commissions, which includes the newly established gubernatorial appointee from the Division of Parole and Probation.

If the required disclosures are not provided, property owners and assignees are authorized to rescind the contract without penalty before closing, and assignees are entitled to a refund of any deposit paid.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Owners of residential property, wholesale real estate buyers and sellers, and assignees of residential purchase contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General, through its Consumer Protection Division, monitors and enforces laws protecting residential property owners and consumers against unfair or deceptive business practices, including improper disclosures in wholesale real estate contract assignments.

The Maryland Department of Labor oversees the regulation and licensing of real estate professionals and industry practices; it was consulted regarding the impact of contract assignment disclosures and consumer protections.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judiciary, which may adjudicate civil disputes relating to the rescission of residential sales contracts and the return of earnest money deposits.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 127 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It expands eligibility for administering local rehabilitation programs under DHCD's Maryland Housing Rehabilitation Program (MHRP) to include nonprofit sponsors, authorizing DHCD to certify, allocate funds to, train, and provide technical assistance to these entities.

Synopsis: Updating the funding priorities for failing sewage systems and holding tanks; requiring as a second priority those located within the Maryland Chesapeake Bay 8-digit watershed that have a relative effectiveness for total nitrogen reduction of 9.24 or higher based on the Chesapeake Bay watershed model; requiring as a third priority funding for failing systems within the 500-year floodplain, and fourth to certain other failing systems; and expanding certain funding eligibility criteria for on-site and community sewage systems.
Title: Environment - Bay Restoration Fund - Septic System Upgrade Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut

bill_summary: House Bill 131 modifies the prioritization and eligibility criteria for financial assistance awarded from the Bay Restoration Fund's Septics Account. It updates the funding priority order for repairing or replacing failing septic systems to prioritize systems in the Critical Area, systems in high-effectiveness nitrogen-reduction watersheds, and systems located within 500-year floodplains. Additionally, it expands eligibility for system repair and replacement funding to moderate-income homeowners in addition to low-income homeowners, and shifts the eligibility cutoff date for community sewerage system conversions and municipal wastewater connections from a fixed 2008 date to a rolling standard requiring installation or occupancy at least 15 years before the application year.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners of on-site sewage disposal systems (septic systems), low- and moderate-income homeowners, local governments, local health departments, and septic installation and maintenance contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected overall, as the bill only shifts project prioritization and eligibility without altering overall Bay Restoration Fund revenues or expenditures; the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the changes with existing resources. Local government grant totals remain unchanged, but funding distribution across jurisdictions may shift based on the new criteria, and local health departments may experience a minor operational workload increase.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) administers the Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account, establishes priority rankings, determines funding criteria for septic upgrades and community sewerage connections, and oversees grant distribution to local jurisdictions.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutorily tasked with maintaining the separate Bay Restoration Fund Septics Account and disbursing funds in accordance with the statutory formula.

The bill impacts the administration and prioritization of block grants distributed through local health departments, which operate under the state public health framework to evaluate and approve septic systems and health concerns.

The Department of Agriculture receives a statutory 40% transfer of Bay Restoration Fund septic fee revenues for the Maryland Agricultural Water Quality Cost Share Cover Crop Program, referenced directly within the amended section.

stakeholders: Local taxing authorities (county councils, county commissioners, Baltimore City, and municipal governing bodies) and property taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State administrative expenditures may decrease minimally for the State Department of Assessments and Taxation beginning in fiscal 2026 because the department will calculate constant yield tax rates only upon request rather than for all jurisdictions. responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Victims of alleged rape, sexual offenses, or child sexual abuse, and the physicians, qualified health care providers, and hospitals providing them with forensic examinations and treatment.

It codifies current practice, in which the Sexual Assault Reimbursement Unit within the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy already processes and pays these reimbursements.

bill_summary: Authorizes a trustee of a trust under the Maryland Trust Act to resign without seeking court approval by providing at least 30 days' notice to qualified beneficiaries, the settlor (if living), any co-trustees, and any individual with the authority to appoint or replace a successor trustee.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Trustees, trust settlors, qualified beneficiaries, co-trustees, and persons authorized to appoint successor trustees.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under current law, a trustee typically must seek court approval to resign. The bill permits trustees to resign upon giving 30 days' notice to specified parties without court approval, which directly affects civil caseloads and proceedings in Maryland courts.

bill_summary: Renames the Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program to the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program and lowers the eligible participant age from 65 to 60 for older adults at risk of social isolation. It expands allowable communications beyond telephone calls to include texts, web-based, video, and in-person outreach accessible to individuals with disabilities, authorizes service integration with Telecommunications Access of Maryland, and allows contracts and agreements with local agencies, Area Agencies on Aging, and Senior Villages.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Maryland older adults aged 60 and older who are at risk of social isolation (including deaf, hard-of-hearing, and disabled seniors), Area Agencies on Aging, local government agencies, and community Senior Villages.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The bill primarily alters the purposes for which existing funds may be used, with the fiscal 2026 budget including $419,967 in special funds from the Universal Service Trust Fund (USTF). Administrative duties can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources, though special fund expenditures may increase if new service agreements are executed. Local Effect: Local government revenues and expenditures may increase to the extent that local entities or Area Agencies on Aging contract with the Maryland Department of Aging to provide program services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly renames, restructures, and expands the Department of Aging's Senior Call-Check Service and Notification Program into the Senior Call-Check and Social Connections Program, authorizing new forms of direct communication, expanding participant eligibility, and establishing new contracting and interagency partnership mechanisms.

The bill mandates integration of the program with the Telecommunications Access of Maryland (TAM) program, which is housed within the Department of Disabilities, requiring the promotion of accessible equipment and the use of TAM's educational outreach materials.

bill_summary: Requires each county board of education to adopt curriculum guides and courses of study aligned with content standards established by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). It establishes a formal process for the State Superintendent of Schools to identify discrepancies, require corrective action plans, mandate the adoption of State curriculum standards and resources upon noncompliance, and withhold State education funds if a county board fails to comply.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education (State Superintendent of Schools)
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, public school educators, and local county boards of education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not materially affected, as MSDE can develop content standards and manage discrepancy notices using existing resources, though broader review duties may require staff redirection. Local school system expenditures may increase, likely minimally, to update curriculum guides to align with MSDE standards. Noncompliant school systems risk having State education funds withheld, though such occurrences are anticipated to be rare.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MSDE and the State Superintendent of Schools are the primary entities responsible for implementing the bill, including developing state content standards, monitoring local school board curriculum guides for discrepancies, approving corrective action plans, and enforcing compliance by directing the withholding of state funds if necessary.

Under the enforcement provisions of the bill and current law referenced in §§ 2-303 and 5-205 of the Education Article, the State Comptroller is responsible for withholding state education aid disbursements to noncompliant local school boards upon direction from the State Superintendent of Schools.

responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration

fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. Local Effect: The bill does not affect local government operations or finances.

The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees vehicle administration, licensing, and regulatory compliance under the Transportation Article.
