bill_summary: Extends the date through which the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund may be used from December 31, 2025, to December 31, 2027, allowing the Maryland Department of Health to spend any remaining funds on maternal and child health initiatives for two additional years.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Pregnant women, mothers, infants, and young children in Maryland (particularly Medicaid recipients and those receiving maternal morbidity, asthma, home visiting, and doula care services), as well as participating healthcare providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: No new special fund revenues are collected. Allows up to an estimated $24.1 million in remaining special funds to continue to be expended across FY 2026 through the first half of FY 2028 in lieu of State general funds. Funds expended through Medicaid continue to leverage federal matching funds. In the absence of the bill, unspent balances would remain locked and general funds would be required to sustain programs. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health co-administers the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund, requested this departmental legislation, and directly expends the fund's monies through its Medical Care Programs Administration and Prevention and Health Promotion Administration.
The Health Services Cost Review Commission co-administers the Fund, establishes the hospital rate assessment that finances it, and must approve all expenditures made from the Fund.
Statute designates the State Treasurer to hold the Fund separately and invest its moneys on behalf of the State.
Statute requires the Comptroller to account for the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund.
The statute explicitly notes that the Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

bill_summary: The Davis Martinez Public Employee Safety and Health Act establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health (PESH) Unit within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Labor and Industry to oversee and enforce workplace safety and health standards for public bodies. The bill removes the previous exemption of public bodies from Maryland Occupational Safety and Health (MOSH) civil penalties, requires standards to prevent workplace violence against public employees, and establishes regulations and legal exceptions for the use of body-worn cameras by correctional officers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor (Division of Labor and Industry)
stakeholders: Maryland public sector employees, state and local government agencies (public bodies), correctional officers, and participants in the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State expenditures increase by $604,785 ($535,390 in general funds and $69,385 in special funds) for 1 MD Labor administrative officer ($69,385), 1 Assistant Attorney General ($106,659), and $428,790 in contingent general funds for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services to acquire body-worn cameras. State special fund revenues for the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program increase by an estimated $30,000 in FY 2026 and $40,000 annually thereafter from civil penalties assessed against public bodies. Local government expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 for compliance and potential MOSH penalties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency. The bill establishes the Public Employees' Safety and Health (PESH) Unit within the Division of Labor and Industry, requires the Commissioner to adopt workplace violence regulations for public bodies, conduct inspections, issue citations, and dedicate civil penalty revenues to the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is directly impacted by the bill's body-worn camera (BWC) provisions and the Correctional Training Commission's regulations. The bill also triggers contingent funding in the FY 2026 state budget providing $428,790 to DPSCS for the acquisition and implementation of BWCs for correctional and supervision personnel.

The bill mandates the Attorney General to expedite review of administrative search warrant applications, provide required notices when proceeding to enforce citations or collect penalties against public bodies, and represent MOSH in an expected increase of contested citation proceedings, requiring an additional Assistant Attorney General position.

As a state agency operating juvenile detention facilities and employing officers meeting the definition of correctional units/officers, DJS is required to develop and maintain written policies consistent with the regulations for body-worn cameras.

The operational costs and administrative staffing of the MOSH program within MD Labor are funded via appropriations from the State Workers' Compensation Commission, which supports the new administrative personnel required under the bill.

The District Court of Maryland is designated as the court where applications for administrative search warrants are submitted and where actions to enforce payment of civil penalties may proceed, along with court application of the bill's wiretap exceptions.

The bill requires the Attorney General and the Commissioner of Labor and Industry to formally notify the Governor whenever legal enforcement action is initiated or when a public body fails to pay assessed workplace safety civil penalties within 30 days.

Synopsis: Providing that multiple thefts committed by the same person in multiple counties under one scheme or continuing course of conduct may be joined and prosecuted in any county in which any one of the thefts occurred; prohibiting one or more persons from committing a series of thefts from retail merchants over a 90-day period with an aggregate value exceeding $1,500; requiring a court to make a finding as to whether a certain crime is organized retail theft under certain circumstances for a certain purpose; etc.
Title: Organized Retail Theft Act of 2025

bill_summary: The Organized Retail Theft Act of 2025 creates the felony offense of organized retail theft for committing a series of retail thefts over a 90-day period with an aggregate value exceeding $1,500, setting tiered penalties and restitution requirements. It allows multiple thefts across different counties under a single scheme or continuing course of conduct to be joined and prosecuted in any county where one theft occurred, merges convictions with general theft for sentencing, and requires courts to make findings on whether certain crimes constitute organized retail theft for criminal record reporting.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (District and Circuit Courts), State's Attorneys, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (including the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository)
stakeholders: Retail merchants, individuals accused or convicted of retail theft, criminal defense attorneys/Office of the Public Defender, prosecutors, and state and local correctional facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is expected to have a minimal fiscal impact. State general fund revenues may decrease minimally as fine revenues shift from District Court to circuit courts, while state incarceration expenditures may increase minimally due to longer sentences or additional state facility commitments. Local fine revenues in circuit courts may increase minimally, with no material impact on local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense of organized retail theft, alters venue provisions allowing multi-county theft charges to be consolidated, shifts certain theft cases from the District Court to the circuit courts, and mandates that courts make specific findings of fact for reporting purposes upon request by a State's Attorney.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department is impacted by potential increases in state incarceration costs resulting from new felony penalties and longer sentences. Additionally, DPSCS operates the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives the court findings of organized retail theft required under the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The agency will be required to defend indigent clients facing the new felony charges and notes that aggregating multi-county cases into circuit court felony prosecutions shifts caseload demands from District Court attorneys to more experienced circuit court defense attorneys.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency investigating criminal offenses across county lines, MSP will investigate organized retail theft rings operating across multiple Maryland jurisdictions under the unified venue provisions of the bill.

bill_summary: House Bill 181 authorizes the Adjutant General of the Maryland Military Department, rather than the Governor, to appoint the department's chief of staff and aides, and establishes that these staff members serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General.
responsible_party: Maryland Military Department (Adjutant General)
stakeholders: Chief of staff, aides, and leadership within the Maryland Military Department, as well as the Office of the Governor.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations because it conforms statute to current practice. It has no effect on local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly grants the Adjutant General statutory authority to appoint the chief of staff and aides within the Military Department, and specifies that these individuals serve at the pleasure of the Adjutant General.
The bill transfers the appointment authority and supervisory 'at-pleasure' status of the Military Department's chief of staff and aides away from the Governor to the Adjutant General.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor with executive appointments; removing these positions from gubernatorial appointment authority eliminates them from the office's portfolio.
The Military Department directs the Maryland National Guard, and the chief of staff and aides subject to the appointment authority changes are full-time personnel serving in State active-duty status.

bill_summary: House Bill 182 replaces the flat $40 maximum civil penalty for speed camera violations with an escalating tiered fine structure ranging from $40 to $425 based on the recorded speed over the posted limit. Additionally, the bill requires the State Highway Administration to convene a stakeholder workgroup to study best practices for speed monitoring systems in school zones and report its findings by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists and vehicle owners cited by speed monitoring systems, student pedestrians and school communities, local law enforcement agencies, local governments, and the District Court.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund and Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues are expected to increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 due to higher fines and more contested court cases; TTF expenditures increase correspondingly for authorized purposes through FY 2029. In FY 2026, one-time State costs include $75,000 in TTF expenditures for a consultant to assist the SHA workgroup and $33,600 in general fund expenditures for District Court computer programming. Local government revenues and public safety expenditures are also projected to increase, potentially significantly (e.g., Baltimore City fine revenues could net an estimated $1.7 million annually).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the State Highway Administration (SHA) convene a workgroup to study best practices for speed monitoring systems in school zones and submit a report with recommendations by December 1, 2025. Additionally, SHA receives fine revenues from speed cameras on MD Route 210, which will experience fiscal impacts.

MDOT is the parent department of the State Highway Administration. The bill affects Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures, including $75,000 in FY 2026 for consultant staffing costs and adjustments to fine revenues from MD Route 210.

The District Court must prescribe a revised uniform citation form reflecting the tiered penalty schedule. The Judiciary incurs $33,596 in FY 2026 computer programming expenditures and anticipates an increase in contested citation trials due to higher fines.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a temporary study workgroup convened by SHA to evaluate best practices, incident rates, and camera placement policies in school zones.
The State Highway Administration must submit the final study report and recommendations of the school zone speed monitoring workgroup to the Governor by December 1, 2025.
Under current statute governing speed monitoring systems, any local revenue remaining after cost recovery exceeding 10% of a jurisdiction's total revenue must be remitted to the Comptroller.

DBM is responsible for state budget preparation and long-term fiscal planning, and this bill establishes a statutory mandated general fund appropriation of $3.7 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.
The bill places a statutory mandate on the Governor to include a $3.7 million appropriation to the Program in the annual state budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2029.

bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration to disqualify an individual from driving a commercial motor vehicle for one year if the individual holds a commercial driver's license or commercial instructional permit and drives or attempts to drive any motor vehicle with a blood or breath alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Commercial driver's license (CDL) and commercial instructional permit holders
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. Reprogramming and procedural changes can be absorbed with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) disqualify commercial driver's license (CDL) or commercial learner's permit holders from operating commercial motor vehicles for one year if they drive any motor vehicle with a BAC of 0.08 or greater.
As the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT requested this departmental legislation and oversees state transportation policies and CDL compliance with federal standards.
Administrative Law Judges at the OAH adjudicate administrative per se driver's license hearings and appeals resulting from chemical test failures and MVA disqualification actions.
The Maryland State Police enforces impaired driving statutes, conducts chemical testing, and submits test results and administrative paperwork to the MVA that trigger disqualification actions.
The state court system handles underlying drunk driving citations and transmits conviction records that interface with MVA driver licensing and commercial driver disqualification records.

responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Vehicle owners whose vehicles are towed or impounded, towing companies, police departments, and vehicle insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local operations or finances. The Motor Vehicle Administration will develop a web portal for electronic notifications and plans to charge a nominal fee to towers to completely offset development and maintenance costs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency charged with adopting regulations, sending electronic notices to vehicle owners using email addresses in its records, and developing/maintaining the web portal and insurer database.

The Motor Vehicle Administration is a principal modal administration of the Department of Transportation, and the bill amends the Transportation Article regarding vehicle towing, abandoned vehicle processing, and electronic notice.

The Governor's Office receives the required report from the Maryland State Department of Education regarding the comprehensive plan for the establishment of Restorative Practices Schools by December 1, 2026, as well as the annual student discipline data report.

It also adjusts the requirement for attempting to reach a voter through an alternative communication method if the voter cannot be reached using their selected method.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters on the permanent absentee ballot list
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State finances and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental bill was introduced at the request of the State Board of Elections (SBE). It directly governs SBE's statutory obligations and timeline for contacting and confirming voter information for individuals on the permanent absentee ballot list prior to elections.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person that is a seller from advertising or offering for sale a digital good using certain terminology unless, before executing the sale, a certain affirmative acknowledgment is received from the purchaser or a certain clear and conspicuous statement is provided by the seller; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to certain enforcement and penalty provisions.
Title: Consumer Protection – False Advertising – Digital Goods

bill_summary: Prohibits sellers from advertising or offering digital goods for sale using terms that suggest unrestricted ownership unless the seller provides a clear and conspicuous disclosure or obtains an affirmative acknowledgment from the buyer that only a license is being acquired. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General, Consumer Protection Division
stakeholders: Consumers of digital media and software, as well as digital retailers, publishers, and platforms offering digital goods for purchase or licensing.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not have a material impact on State or local government finances or operations. The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division can enforce the bill's provisions using existing resources, and the application of existing penalties will not yield a significant financial effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Consumer Protection Act through its Consumer Protection Division. The bill establishes that advertising or offering digital goods without required ownership/license disclosures is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to civil enforcement by the division.

The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the Maryland Judicial Branch, which would adjudicate any civil enforcement actions, injunctions, or civil penalties pursued under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act for violations of this digital goods disclosure statute.

Synopsis: Repealing a duplicative provision of law requiring each county government, local school system, and local health department, in consultation with the local emergency manager, to create or update a cybersecurity preparedness and response plan and complete a cybersecurity preparedness assessment in a manner and frequency established by the Department of Information Technology.
Title: State Finance and Procurement - Local Cybersecurity Preparedness and Response Plan and Assessment - Repeal
bill_summary: Repeals a duplicative statutory provision requiring county governments, local school systems, and local health departments to create or update a cybersecurity preparedness and response plan and complete an assessment, resolving redundancy with an identical requirement preserved elsewhere in state law.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: County governments, local school systems, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact. It is technical in nature and simply eliminates a redundant requirement that remains codified in another section of state law.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 209 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) to repeal a duplicative statutory provision regarding local government cybersecurity preparedness and response plans under Title 3.5 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Assistive Technology Program in the Department of Disabilities; providing the purpose of the Program is to increase access to assistive technology services and devices for individuals with disabilities, support the State's efforts to provide assistive technology services and devices to persons with disabilities of all ages, including underrepresented populations, and ensure statewide access to assistive technology lending libraries; establishing the Assistive Technology Services Fund; etc.
Title: Human Services - Maryland Assistive Technology Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Accessibility - see also- Blind; Deaf; Disabilities; etc
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.

bill_summary: This bill codifies the Maryland Assistive Technology Program within the Maryland Department of Disabilities to provide assistive technology devices and services to individuals with disabilities. It also establishes the Assistive Technology Services Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to receive revenues generated from program services—such as assistive technology assessments and digital accessibility trainings—and support the program's operations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities
stakeholders: Individuals with disabilities of all ages, their families, caregivers, support providers, educators, employers, and local government entities utilizing assistive technology services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $25,000 in FY 2026 from fee-for-service activities, growing to $38,300 by FY 2030; special fund expenditures increase correspondingly to support program operations. General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 due to interest earnings credited to the General Fund before shifting to the special fund in FY 2029. Existing federal funding of approximately $1.3 million continues. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to the extent local entities purchase program services or training.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes the Maryland Assistive Technology Program and the Assistive Technology Services Fund within the Department of Disabilities, making it the primary implementing agency responsible for operating the program and administering the fund.
The bill explicitly requires the State Treasurer to hold the newly established Assistive Technology Services Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The bill statutorily designates the Comptroller to account for the newly established Assistive Technology Services Fund.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the sale, offer for sale, transfer, or distribution of non-arc-resistant jacketed corrugated stainless steel tubing; providing a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for a violation of the Act; and requiring the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal, by September 1, 2026, to submit a final report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly with recommendations related to preventing the fire hazards associated with commonly used fuel gas piping systems.
Title: Public Safety - Fuel Gas Piping Systems and Corrugated Stainless Steel Tubing - Prohibitions and Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Codes -see also- Annotated Code of Md; Building Codes
Equipment -see also- Charging; Med. Equip.; MV Equip; etc.
Goods and Services -see also- Retail Sales; TermnSvc; TrfGds
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: This bill prohibits the sale, offer for sale, transfer, or distribution of non-arc-resistant jacketed corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST) that does not meet specified standards, establishes a civil penalty of up to $1,000 for violations, and establishes a penalty for using non-compliant tubing in certain fuel gas piping systems. It also directs the Maryland Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal to conduct a study and report recommendations on mitigating fire hazards related to fuel gas piping systems.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor and Office of the State Fire Marshal
stakeholders: Manufacturers, retailers, wholesalers, and distributors of CSST and fuel gas piping systems; plumbers and construction contractors; residential and commercial property owners; and local gas fitting inspectors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $101,983 in FY 2026 and $22,124 in FY 2027 for the Maryland Department of Labor to hire a contractual engineer to conduct the required study and submit interim and final reports through October 2026. General fund revenues may increase minimally from civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation. Local governments can consult on the study using existing resources with no effect on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is one of the primary agencies tasked with implementing the bill. It is co-responsible with the Office of the State Fire Marshal for conducting a comprehensive study on fuel gas piping fire hazards, hiring a contractual engineer, and submitting interim and final reports to the Governor and General Assembly.

The Office of the State Fire Marshal and the State Fire Prevention Commission are entities within the Department of State Police. The Office of the State Fire Marshal is explicitly mandated to co-lead the study, consult with the commission, and formulate safety recommendations and reports.

The bill mandates that the Department of Labor and the Office of the State Fire Marshal submit both an interim report and a final report on their findings and recommendations directly to the Governor.

The bill creates civil penalties of up to $1,000 for unlawful sales, distribution, or installation of non-compliant tubing, which are adjudicated through the District Court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Creating an exception for vehicles carrying fluid milk products to the prohibition against driving a vehicle subject to an exceptional hauling permit on the interstate highway system; altering certain weight limits and tolerances under an exceptional hauling permit; altering the preventive maintenance documents that an individual operating under an exceptional hauling permit must possess; and altering certain record-keeping requirements and the application of certain administrative penalties under an exceptional hauling permit.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Exceptional Hauling Permits for Farm Products

NarrowSubjects.Name: Farmers and Farming -see also- Agriculture; Farmland
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 225 modifies regulations for exceptional hauling permits for farm products. It permits vehicles carrying fluid milk products under an exceptional hauling permit to operate on the interstate highway system, updates weight limits and axle requirements while removing weight limit tolerances, revises preventive maintenance inspection documentation standards, and gives the State Highway Administration discretion over permit revocations for weight violations.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Farmers, dairy haulers, agricultural producers, and commercial motor carriers transporting farm products in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund revenues are expected to increase starting in FY 2026 due to additional permit applications, though the total increase is not expected to be significant and specific dollar estimates cannot be reliably determined. The State Highway Administration can implement the bill with existing resources. State and local highway preservation and maintenance expenditures may experience minimal long-term impacts resulting from changes to vehicle weight limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administration is the primary implementing agency under the bill, responsible for issuing, regulating, monitoring, suspending, and revoking exceptional hauling permits for farm and milk products, as well as conducting record audits and adopting regulations.

The bill is a departmental initiative sponsored by MDOT, which oversees the State Highway Administration and administers the Transportation Trust Fund into which exceptional hauling permit fees accrue.

The State Highway Administration must adopt implementing regulations in consultation with the Secretary of State Police, and Maryland State Police officers and authorized civilian employees are empowered to confiscate exceptional hauling permits for significant weight violations.
Maryland Transportation Authority Police officers are authorized under the bill to confiscate exceptional hauling permits when vehicles violate weight restrictions by more than 5,000 pounds.

The bill modifies hauling parameters and weight limits specifically for farm products (as defined in the Agriculture Article) and fluid milk products, directly affecting agricultural producers and commodity transport.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to operate all schools within the county using a scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days to allow for less than 180 school days if the minimal hours of attendance are met; requiring the board, if it elects to use a scheduling model that results in a school in the county being open for less than 180 days, to offer certain school employees an opportunity to make up the lost wages; and requiring the Board to make a report on the schools using an alternative scheduling model.
Title: Anne Arundel County – Public Schools – School Schedule Options

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Schools -see also- Primary Schools; Secondary Sch
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Authorizes the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to operate all public schools within the county using an alternative scheduling model that eliminates early dismissal days and allows for fewer than 180 school days, provided that minimum attendance hour requirements are met. It requires the board to offer hourly employees the opportunity to make up lost wages and submit annual reports to the State Board of Education and the General Assembly.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County public school students, parents and families, teachers, and hourly school employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. There is no direct fiscal effect on Anne Arundel County, as the bill is authorizing in nature; if Anne Arundel County Public Schools implements an alternative schedule, it can do so using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts public school calendar and attendance standards governed by Maryland education laws and State Board of Education regulations (COMAR), and requires the Anne Arundel County Board of Education to submit annual reports on the alternative scheduling model to the State Board of Education.

Synopsis: Providing that certain unclaimed money held by an electric cooperative and due to a past member is not considered abandoned property; and authorizing an electric cooperative to use this money only to assist members of the cooperative or make donations to nonprofit, charitable organizations.
Title: Corporations and Associations - Electric Cooperatives - Nonescheat Capital Credits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Corporations -see also- Municipal Corps; Public Corps & Inst
Financial Institutions -see also- Banks; Credit Unions; etc.
Utilities -see also- Recycl; Refuse; Sewage; Teleph; Water

bill_summary: Exempts unclaimed capital credits owed to past members of electric cooperatives from being classified as abandoned property under State law, allowing cooperatives to retain these nonescheat capital credits to assist cooperative members or make donations to approved charitable organizations, provided past members may still claim their refunds upon application.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Electric cooperatives, past and current electric cooperative members, and nonprofit charitable organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Unclaimed Property Fund) and general fund revenues may decrease by an indeterminate amount because nonescheat capital credits will no longer be remitted to the State as presumed abandoned property. State expenditures and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland administers the state's unclaimed/abandoned property program. Because the bill exempts certain nonescheat capital credits held by electric cooperatives from being presumed abandoned, those funds will no longer be reported and transferred to the Comptroller, resulting in a potential reduction in revenues for the Unclaimed Property Fund and General Fund.

Synopsis: Expanding the purposes of the Maryland Veterans Trust to include providing monetary and other assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families; and authorizing the Maryland Veterans Trust to expend money from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to provide loans and grants to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families.
Title: Maryland Veterans Trust – Assistance to Members of the Maryland National Guard

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans

bill_summary: Expands the scope of the Maryland Veterans Trust and the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund to provide grants, loans, and other monetary assistance to members of the Maryland National Guard and their families.
responsible_party: Maryland Veterans Trust (staffed by the Department of Veterans and Military Families)
stakeholders: Members of the Maryland National Guard and their families
fiscal_impact_summary: State nonbudgeted expenditures from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 as additional grants and loans are distributed. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Veterans and Military Families staffs the Maryland Veterans Trust, administers the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund, and processes the grant and loan applications expanded under this bill to include National Guard members.

The bill directly benefits members of the Maryland National Guard and their families by making them eligible to receive loans, grants, and monetary assistance from the Maryland Veterans Trust Fund during temporary financial difficulties.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General requested this departmental legislation to ensure support and financial relief resources are accessible for Maryland National Guard personnel and their families.

Synopsis: Altering the format and content of training on the requirements of the Maryland Public Ethics Law provided by the State Ethics Commission to certain State employees and regulated lobbyists to be either through online training or live presentation on the conflict of interest, financial disclosure, relevant administrative, and other applicable requirements of the law; and altering the scope of disclosure for the employment of an individual or a member of the individual's immediate family reported in a financial disclosure statement.
Title: Maryland Public Ethics Law - Training and Financial Disclosure Requirements - Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland Public Ethics Law by removing the minimum two-hour requirement for ethics training courses provided by the State Ethics Commission, clarifying that trainings may be conducted online or via live presentations, and expanding financial disclosure requirements to report any source of compensated employment rather than only salaried employment for individuals and their immediate family members.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: State officials, public officials, candidates for State office, regulated lobbyists, and local ethics authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none, as the State Ethics Commission can implement the bill using existing budgetary resources. Local fiscal impact is minimal, primarily involving potential updates to local ethics laws to conform with the financial disclosure revisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 230 is a departmental bill requested by the State Ethics Commission. It directly amends the requirements for ethics training programs administered by the Commission for public officials and regulated lobbyists, providing flexibility in format and duration, and modifies the employment reporting requirements on financial disclosure statements overseen by the Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the duties of the Cyber Preparedness Unit in the Maryland Department of Emergency Management; altering the duties of the Office of Security Management in the Department of Information Technology; requiring the Office to submit a yearly report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly on the State's cybersecurity expenditures and recommendations for changes to the budget; and altering the responsibilities of the Secretary of Information Technology with regard to information technology policies.
Title: State Government - Information Technology - Cybersecurity Revisions

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 235 revises Maryland's cybersecurity governance framework by reallocating and clarifying duties between the Department of Information Technology's Office of Security Management and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management's Cyber Preparedness Unit. Specifically, it transfers responsibility for assisting local governments with cyber vulnerability assessments to the Office of Security Management, updates the duties of the Secretary of Information Technology regarding statewide cybersecurity strategy implementation, and establishes a separate January annual reporting requirement for cybersecurity expenditures and budget recommendations.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology (including the Office of Security Management) and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (including the Cyber Preparedness Unit)
stakeholders: State agencies, local governments, local school boards, local school systems, and local health departments
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected as the bill's requirements can be handled using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 235 directly alters the statutory responsibilities of the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), its Secretary, and the Office of Security Management (OSM). It transfers specific cybersecurity assessment support responsibilities from MDEM to DoIT, clarifies threat mitigation authority on the State network, and modifies annual reporting requirements.

The bill directly modifies the statutory duties of the Cyber Preparedness Unit within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), transferring certain vulnerability assessment responsibilities to DoIT and updating requirements related to cybersecurity training and local plan development.

The bill requires DoIT's Office of Security Management to submit two annual reports directly to the Governor concerning cybersecurity activities, preparedness, multi-year state expenditures on cybersecurity, and budget recommendations.
The Maryland National Guard is specifically designated to coordinate with MDEM and DoIT in conducting regional cybersecurity preparedness exercises as necessary.

Synopsis: Expanding the relief that may be included in a final peace order; altering the acts that constitute criminal harassment to include certain visual surveillance of an area of another person's residence where the other has a reasonable expectation of privacy; and providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction for a first offense is subject to imprisonment of up to 90 days or a fine of $500 or both, and for a second or subsequent offense, imprisonment of up to 180 days or a fine of $1,000 or both.
Title: Peace Orders and Criminal Harassment - Intentional Visual Surveillance
bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal harassment statute to prohibit visual surveillance of an area of another person's residence where the person has a reasonable expectation of privacy, provided it is done with the intent to harass, alarm, or annoy, without legal purpose, and after a warning to stop. It also expands the relief a court may order under a final peace order to include requiring the respondent to remove or reposition a visual surveillance device within 15 days and refrain from further visual surveillance.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts)
stakeholders: Maryland residents experiencing nonconsensual visual surveillance of their residences, individuals accused of visual surveillance or harassment, and the state court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $29,600 in FY 2026 only for the Judiciary to make programming adjustments to update relief options for peace orders. State revenues and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the relief that can be granted in peace orders, requiring the Judiciary to implement programming and software updates to interim, temporary, and final peace order forms at an estimated cost of $29,600 in FY 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands the misdemeanor offense of criminal harassment to include certain visual surveillance of a residence, which carries penalties of imprisonment and falls under the purview of public defender representation for indigent defendants.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Secretary of State to suspend payment of certain late fees assessed to certain charitable organizations that fail to file an annual report under certain circumstances; and authorizing the Secretary of State to cancel a charitable organization's registration or reinstate a charitable organization's canceled registration under certain circumstances.
Title: Charitable Organizations - Late Fees and Registration - Suspension and Cancellation Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Secretary of State to suspend or waive late filing fees for charitable organizations under specified regulations or settlement agreements, clarifies that these late fees are not delinquent accounts requiring referral to the Central Collection Unit, and establishes procedures for canceling and reinstating charitable organization registrations.
responsible_party: Maryland Secretary of State
stakeholders: Charitable organizations operating or soliciting contributions in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State finances, as the provisions regarding the suspension or waiver of late fees conform statutory law to the Secretary of State's existing practice. The bill has no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly regulates the Secretary of State's oversight of charitable organizations, authorizing the agency to waive or suspend late fees, adopt implementing regulations, and cancel or reinstate charitable registrations.

The bill specifies that late fees assessed against charitable organizations are not delinquent accounts requiring referral to the Central Collection Unit (CCU), a unit administered under the Department of Budget and Management.

The Office of the Attorney General coordinates with the Secretary of State on charitable enforcement and receives funding support from the Charitable Enforcement Fund, which is financed through charitable organization fees addressed in this bill.

Synopsis: Clarifying that "spouse" includes a former spouse for purposes of disclosure of confidential communications occurring during marriage; and establishing that a spouse, who is the alleged victim, is competent to disclose a confidential communication between spouses occurring during their marriage in a criminal action in which one spouse is charged with a crime against the other spouse.
Title: Marriage - Confidential Communication

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.

bill_summary: This bill specifies that 'spouse' includes a former spouse regarding confidential marital communications and establishes that a spouse who is the alleged victim is competent to disclose confidential communications between the spouses in a criminal case where one spouse is charged with a crime against the other. It also specifies that an alleged victim spouse may not be compelled to testify.
responsible_party: The Maryland Judiciary and State courts
stakeholders: Spouses and former spouses involved in criminal cases involving crimes committed against a spouse, crime victims, criminal defendants, prosecutors, and defense counsel.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is procedural and is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the marital communications privilege in criminal court proceedings by allowing an alleged victim spouse to disclose confidential spousal communications. The Administrative Office of the Courts supports the judicial branch where these evidentiary rules and proceedings are administered.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters criminal trial evidence rules regarding spousal privilege when one spouse is charged with a crime against the other, which impacts the defense strategies and litigation handled by public defenders representing indigent defendants.
The Office of the Attorney General represents the State in criminal appeals where statutory evidentiary privileges and trial court admissibility decisions under § 9-105 are litigated.

Synopsis: Limiting the requirement that a petitioner's spouse join in the petition for adoption to apply only when the prospective adoptee is a minor; authorizing a petitioner's spouse to join in the petition for adoption if the prospective adoptee is an adult; establishing that certain provisions of law requiring the issuance and service of a show-cause order on a prospective adoptee's parents do not apply if the prospective adoptee is an adult; etc.
Title: Family Law - Adoption of an Adult

NarrowSubjects.Name: Adoption - see also- FamLaw; FosterCare; ParentsGuardians
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland adoption law when the prospective adoptee is an adult by eliminating requirements for parental consent, issuance of a show-cause order to biological parents, and mandatory spousal joinder in the adoption petition. It also restricts pre-ruling court investigations in adult adoption cases to instances where good cause is shown.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts)
stakeholders: Adult adoptees, petitioners seeking to adopt an adult, spouses of petitioners, and biological parents of prospective adult adoptees
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters judicial procedures in independent adoption cases involving adult adoptees, including removing mandatory spousal joinder, eliminating parental show-cause order and consent requirements, and limiting court-ordered investigations to circumstances where good cause is shown.

The Department of Human Services oversees state adoption policies and family services under the Family Law Article; this bill streamlines independent adult adoptions and removes certain notice and investigation requirements that may involve the department or child placement agencies.

Synopsis: Specifying that certain provisions of law relating to confidentiality do not prohibit the disclosure of certain information relating to adult protective services or the disclosure of the identity of certain persons making certain reports under certain circumstances; expanding the definition of "health practitioner" to include certain emergency medical providers; and authorizing individuals who are required in specific instances to report information regarding alleged vulnerable adults to make a report by calling the statewide reporting hotline.
Title: Human Services - Adult Protective Services

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Medical Services -see also- Ambul; RescSqd
Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Vulnerable Adults -see also- DevDisab; EldPers; PhysDisab

bill_summary: This bill permits the disclosure of Adult Protective Services records and reporter identities to government investigators conducting official investigations. It also authorizes mandatory reporters to report suspected abuse, neglect, self-neglect, or exploitation of vulnerable adults through the statewide reporting hotline, and expands the definition of 'health practitioner' under mandatory reporting laws to include certain emergency medical services personnel, excluding emergency medical dispatchers.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Vulnerable adults, Adult Protective Services investigators, law enforcement and government investigative personnel, and emergency medical services providers designated as mandatory reporters.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local finances. State and local entities involved in investigations regarding vulnerable adults may experience operational efficiencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DHS requested this departmental bill and oversees the Adult Protective Services (APS) program and local departments of social services that investigate allegations of abuse, neglect, and exploitation of vulnerable adults.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS oversees and certifies emergency medical services providers under § 13-516 of the Education Article, who are now brought under the definition of 'health practitioner' and designated as mandatory reporters for vulnerable adult maltreatment.
The Department of Aging advocates for older and vulnerable adults, coordinates with local APS offices during investigations, and was a primary informational source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
MDH regulates health occupations and public health agencies whose personnel are mandatory reporters of vulnerable adult abuse under the Health Occupations Article.
State law enforcement officers investigate crimes involving vulnerable adult abuse and exploitation and are authorized to receive disclosed APS information necessary for official investigations.
The Judiciary and court system process court orders permitting disclosure of records and adjudicate related legal proceedings regarding vulnerable adults.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a local jurisdiction from enforcing a law or ordinance that limits the summoning of law enforcement or emergency services to a residential property by establishing a certain threshold or penalty.
Title: Residential Real Property - Local Limits on Summoning Law Enforcement or Emergency Services

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Prohibits counties and municipalities from enforcing local laws or ordinances that establish a threshold of emergency or police calls as grounds for designating a residential property as a nuisance, or that penalize residential property owners, operators, or tenants for summoning law enforcement or emergency services.
responsible_party: Local governments (counties and municipalities) and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Residential tenants, property owners, owner-occupants, rental property operators, and local governments and emergency responders.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 249 establishes legal defenses and affirmative claims that tenants, operators, and property owners can bring in court against local jurisdictions attempting to enforce prohibited nuisance laws, allowing courts to award damages, attorney's fees, and other relief.

Synopsis: Altering the frequency, from once every 3 years to an interval of once every 4 years unless it is determined on a case-by-case basis that an audit occur at an interval of 3 years, with which the Office of the Inspector General in the Department of Human Services conducts or contracts for financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services.
Title: Human Services – Local Departments of Social Services – Audits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the frequency of financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services conducted or contracted by the Department of Human Services Office of the Inspector General from at least once every three years to an interval of four years, while permitting three-year audits on a case-by-case basis based on risk and prior audit findings.
responsible_party: Office of the Inspector General in the Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Local departments of social services, local boards and governing authorities, and personnel within the Department of Human Services Office of the Inspector General.
fiscal_impact_summary: Any operational efficiencies are not anticipated to materially impact State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 251 is a departmental bill requested by the Department of Human Services. It directly alters the statutory timeframe and risk-based criteria that the DHS Office of the Inspector General uses to conduct or contract for financial and compliance audits of local departments of social services.

bill_summary: This bill extends the statutory termination (sunset) dates for several health occupations licensing boards under the Maryland Program Evaluation Act: the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists to July 1, 2031; the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners to July 1, 2031; the State Board of Pharmacy to July 1, 2030; and the State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists (including its Behavior Analyst Advisory Committee) to July 1, 2028. It also increases the membership of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners from seven to nine members by adding one licensed massage therapist and one consumer member.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Licensed massage therapists, pharmacists, pharmacy technicians, audiologists, hearing aid dispensers, speech-language pathologists, music therapists, professional counselors, behavior analysts, consumers, and regulated health occupations boards.
fiscal_impact_summary: No impact in FY 2025. Special fund revenues and expenditures are maintained for the affected boards through their respective extension years (FY 2028, FY 2030, and FY 2031). Beginning in FY 2026, special fund expenditures for the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners increase by $3,500 annually for per diems for two additional board members. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly reauthorizes and extends the termination dates for several health occupations licensing boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health (including the State Board of Pharmacy, State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners, State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists, and State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists) and alters the board composition of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners.

The bill expands the membership of the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners from seven to nine members, requiring the Governor to appoint the additional licensed massage therapist and consumer members with the advice and consent of the Senate.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointees for state boards, which includes the two newly established seats on the State Board of Massage Therapy Examiners.

bill_summary: This bill alters the structure, powers, and governance of the West North Avenue Development Authority (WNADA) to align with a State economic development authority. It designates WNADA as a body politic and corporate and an instrumentality of the State, establishes the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund to support operations, grants extensive development, financing, and property acquisition powers, exempts the authority from certain state procurement and tax laws, requires it to become self-sustaining starting in fiscal year 2028, and extends its termination date to September 30, 2029.
responsible_party: West North Avenue Development Authority
stakeholders: Residents, property owners, community organizations, and commercial businesses located within the West North Avenue Corridor and surrounding buffer zones in Baltimore City.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $82,614 in FY 2026 due to a contingent appropriation for personnel. Discretionary general fund expenditures may increase by at least $21.2 million and special fund expenditures by at least $260,000 in FY 2027 based on FY 2026 budget levels; however, the authority must be self-sustaining by FY 2028. State and local tax revenues may decrease due to WNADA exemptions from transfer, recordation, and property taxes, though long-term redevelopment may expand the tax base. Baltimore City local expenditures could increase if discretionary municipal contributions continue.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The President of Coppin State University, an institution within the University System of Maryland, is designated by statute to serve as the Chair of the Board of Directors of the West North Avenue Development Authority.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Economic Development Corporation (or their designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Authority's Board of Directors, and the bill aligns the Authority's powers and operating model with State economic development authorities.

The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a member of the Authority's Board of Directors, and the Authority's statutory mandate directly involves residential development and housing rehabilitation.
The Secretary of Commerce (or designee) is designated to serve on the Authority's Board of Directors, supporting commercial development and business attraction along the corridor.
The Secretary of Transportation (or designee) is designated as a member of the Board of Directors of the Authority to coordinate transportation and infrastructure revitalization along the corridor.
The bill establishes the West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and requires the State Treasurer to hold the fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established West North Avenue Development Authority Fund and administer statutory provisions exempting fund interest from General Fund sweeps.
The Governor is authorized to appoint a member to the Authority's Board of Directors and is authorized to include discretionary appropriations to the Authority in the annual state budget bill.

The bill impacts state budgeting and personnel administration by explicitly exempting the Authority from Title 3 of the State Finance and Procurement Article and authorizing staff salaries outside the State Personnel and Pension System.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain DNA sample to be collected in a certain manner from an individual who is required to register as a sex offender; requiring a DNA sample to be collected by a certain individual or at a certain location under certain circumstances; requiring a custodial agency or correctional facility to ensure a DNA sample is collected in a certain manner; prohibiting a DNA sample from being tested and placed in a certain statewide DNA database system until certain conditions are met; etc.
Title: Public Safety - Statewide DNA Database System, DNA Collection, and Penalties - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Alters statewide DNA database system procedures by requiring DNA sample collection from registered sex offenders and mandating that custodial facilities ensure an individual's DNA sample is collected before release. It establishes specific legal determinations required before testing samples from charged individuals, criminalizes the refusal to submit a required DNA sample with a fine up to $1,000, and updates timelines and conditions for automatic destruction and expungement of DNA records.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of qualifying crimes, registered sex offenders, law enforcement agencies, correctional and booking facilities, and State's Attorney offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not expected to be materially affected and requirements will be handled with existing budgeted resources. Local revenues are unaffected, and most local jurisdictions can handle implementation within existing resources, though Montgomery County estimated an expenditure increase of approximately $200,000 annually for additional correctional staff.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland State Police. MSP's Forensic Sciences Division (Crime Laboratory) administers the Statewide DNA Database System, establishes DNA collection regulations and training, handles the testing and backlog of DNA samples, and executes expungements and destruction of records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS operates state correctional facilities and supervising authorities. The bill requires correctional facilities and custodial agencies to collect DNA samples at intake, verify collection before releasing individuals from custody, and collect samples upon sex offender registration.

The bill establishes that DNA testing and entry into the database depends on judicial or commissioner probable cause determinations, arrest warrants, or indictments in District and Circuit Courts, and impacts court expungement notices and sentencing procedures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD represents indigent defendants whose DNA may be collected, tested, or expunged under the altered statutory standards, and defends individuals facing new misdemeanor charges and fines for refusing to provide required DNA samples.

Title: Criminal Law - Drug Paraphernalia - Prohibitions and Penalties

bill_summary: This bill reduces the penalties for offenses related to the use, possession, delivery, or sale of drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia. For subsequent drug paraphernalia offenses, maximum penalties are lowered from two years imprisonment and/or a $2,000 fine to one year imprisonment and/or a $1,000 fine. For controlled paraphernalia violations, penalties are reduced from up to four years imprisonment and/or a $25,000 fine to a maximum fine of $500 for a first offense and up to one year imprisonment and/or a $1,000 fine for subsequent offenses. It also removes the prohibition on possessing controlled paraphernalia to illegally administer a controlled dangerous substance.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Individuals charged with or convicted of drug paraphernalia and controlled paraphernalia offenses, law enforcement officers, state prosecutors, and public defenders.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. While maximum fines are reduced, District and Circuit Court revenues are not significantly impacted due to a historically low number of convictions. Similarly, State and local incarceration expenditures are not materially affected. Caseload reductions for the Office of the Public Defender and operational time savings for local law enforcement from issuing citations instead of arrests are expected to be redirected to other cases and duties.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill reduces penalties for drug and controlled paraphernalia offenses and makes a first-time violation of § 5-620 a fine-only offense. Because the Office of the Public Defender only provides representation in cases where incarceration is possible, the bill directly reduces or alters OPD caseloads.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS oversees the Division of Correction and the Division of Parole and Probation, which receive individuals convicted of and sentenced for drug paraphernalia offenses. The reduction of maximum incarceration terms impacts potential sentence lengths and supervision requirements.
The Maryland Judiciary handles the charging, adjudication, and sentencing for misdemeanor violations under Criminal Law §§ 5-619 and 5-620 across the District and Circuit Courts.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing state criminal laws, MSP troopers investigate CDS paraphernalia offenses and will have to issue criminal citations rather than effectuate arrests for first-time § 5-620 violations.

Synopsis: Prioritizing the payment of unpaid child support over certain other claims on an estate of a decedent with insufficient assets to pay all claims in full.
Title: Estates and Trusts - Priority of Claims on an Estate - Unpaid Child Support

NarrowSubjects.Name: Family Law -see also- Adoption; Alimony; Annulment; etc.

bill_summary: Prioritizes the payment of unpaid child support owed by a deceased individual when an estate has insufficient assets to pay all claims in full, placing child support claims directly after family allowances and ahead of taxes owed by the decedent and other lower-priority claims.
responsible_party: Personal representatives of decedents' estates and the Registers of Wills
stakeholders: Individuals and families owed unpaid child support, decedents' estates and personal representatives, and creditors of estates (including small businesses and state and local government entities)
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government revenues may decrease to the extent that placing unpaid child support higher in the priority list results in lower-priority government claims—such as unpaid taxes or Public Assistance to Adults program reimbursements—going unpaid or receiving smaller disbursements. The decrease cannot be reliably estimated but is expected to be limited. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Register of Wills oversees the administration of decedents' estates and probate proceedings, which includes ensuring that personal representatives pay valid claims against insolvent estates according to the statutory order of priority.

DHS administers child support enforcement services and the Public Assistance to Adults (PAA) program. The bill elevates unpaid child support claims above several categories, while pushing PAA reimbursement claims down in priority.

The Comptroller is responsible for collecting state taxes. The bill places unpaid child support claims above taxes due by the decedent, potentially reducing state tax recoveries from insolvent estates.
The Maryland Judiciary adjudicates estate disputes, claims against estates, and child support judgments, and may see procedural impacts in estate and child support proceedings.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Maryland Agricultural Commission; establishing the Committee on Young Farmers for purposes of  communicating to the Maryland Agricultural Commission on issues relating to young and beginning farmers in the State; repealing the provisions of law establishing and governing the Young Farmers Advisory Board; and requiring the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation to be governed and administered by a board of trustees composed in a certain manner.
Title: Department of Agriculture - Maryland Agricultural Commission and Young Farmers

bill_summary: This bill updates the membership composition and appointment process of the Maryland Agricultural Commission, repeals the Young Farmers Advisory Board, and establishes a 10-member Committee on Young Farmers within the Maryland Department of Agriculture to identify, address, and advise on issues impacting young and beginning farmers.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Maryland farmers, young and beginning farmers, agricultural industry representatives, and members of the Maryland Agricultural Commission
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Any changes in staffing costs or travel expense reimbursements for the Maryland Department of Agriculture are assumed to be minimal. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill is a departmental request that directly impacts the Department of Agriculture by altering the composition and structure of the Maryland Agricultural Commission, repealing the Young Farmers Advisory Board, and establishing and staffing the new Committee on Young Farmers within the department.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new advisory body (the Committee on Young Farmers), alters the composition and membership categories of the Maryland Agricultural Commission, and repeals the statutory authority for the Young Farmers Advisory Board.

The Governor is responsible for appointing members representing various agricultural sectors to the Maryland Agricultural Commission as well as appointing members to the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation board of trustees.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting, vetting, and processing gubernatorial appointments for the updated positions on the Maryland Agricultural Commission and the Maryland Agricultural Land Preservation Foundation board of trustees.

The Chancellor of the University System of Maryland designates the principal administrative official for agricultural affairs at the system to serve as an ex officio member of the Maryland Agricultural Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the eligibility criteria for Higher Education Loan Assistance Grants under the Maryland Dent-Care Program to include part-time employment.
Title: Dental Services - Qualification for Maryland Dent-Care Program

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Dent-Care Program to allow part-time dentists and part-time dental hygienists to receive Higher Education Loan Assistance Grants, and directs the Office of Student Financial Assistance and the Maryland Department of Health to establish prorated grant amounts for part-time participants.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance, in collaboration with the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Part-time dentists, part-time dental hygienists, and Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) recipients receiving oral healthcare services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase minimally by approximately $6,000 in FY 2026 for one-time Maryland Higher Education Commission IT system upgrades to calculate prorated award amounts. Expanding eligibility does not inherently mandate new grant spending, as awards depend on existing Janet L. Hoffman Loan Assistance Repayment Program appropriations ($4.1 million budgeted for FY 2026). The Maryland Department of Health can likely process additional applications with existing resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the eligibility criteria and award structure for Higher Education Loan Assistance Grants under the Maryland Dent-Care Program, which is administered by the commission's Office of Student Financial Assistance (OSFA). OSFA is required to collaborate with the Maryland Department of Health to establish prorated grant amounts for part-time dentists and dental hygienists and adopt regulations.

The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees the Office of Student Financial Assistance, which administers the Maryland Dent-Care Program and will need to update its systems and adopt regulations to establish prorated grant awards for part-time professionals.

The Maryland Department of Health (specifically the Office of Oral Health) collaborates with OSFA to set grant amounts, determine program participation limits, and process and verify applicant eligibility for the Maryland Dent-Care Program.

Synopsis: Altering provisions of law related to a hospital's financial assistance and collection of debts policies; specifying the percentage by which a hospital is required to reduce a patient's out-of-pocket expenses under certain circumstances; adding to the notice requirements relating to a hospital's financial assistance policy; prohibiting a hospital from filing a civil action to collect a debt against a patient whose outstanding debt is at or below $500; etc.
Title: Hospitals - Financial Assistance and Collection of Debts - Policies

NarrowSubjects.Name: Debt Collection -see also- Attachments and Garnishments

bill_summary: House Bill 268 modifies hospital financial assistance and medical debt collection policies in Maryland. It establishes mandatory sliding-scale reductions in out-of-pocket expenses for medically necessary care for low- and moderate-income patients, extends the waiting period before hospitals can assess interest or initiate civil debt-collection actions from 180 to 240 days, prohibits filing lawsuits to collect medical debt of $500 or less, caps monthly income-based payment plans at 5% of household adjusted gross income, and excludes hospital debt contracts from the 12-year statute of limitations for specialties.
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Hospital patients (particularly low-income, underinsured, or uninsured patients facing medical debt), acute and chronic care hospitals, medical debt collectors, health insurers, and Medicaid recipients.
fiscal_impact_summary: Workload for the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) can be absorbed with existing budgeted resources. Local governments experience no fiscal impact. To the extent hospital rates rise to offset higher uncompensated care resulting from debt collection limitations, state Medicaid expenditures (40% general funds, 60% federal matching funds) and corresponding federal matching revenues will increase, potentially beginning in FY 2026. The exact financial impact is indeterminate.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HSCRC is the primary regulatory body responsible for overseeing hospital financial assistance and debt collection policies, developing income-based payment plan guidelines, reviewing hospital compliance, and compiling annual medical debt reports.

HSCRC is an independent commission housed within MDH. Furthermore, the fiscal note highlights that MDH's Medicaid program expenditures and federal matching revenues may increase if hospital rates rise due to expanded uncompensated care.

The bill mandates that hospitals provide patients with contact information and access to the Health Education and Advocacy Unit (HEAU), a division within the Office of the Attorney General, to assist patients with mediation and reconsideration of financial assistance denials.

The bill amends the statute of limitations under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article for certain consumer hospital debts, restricts when hospitals may file civil debt collection actions (prohibiting actions on debts under $500 and within 240 days), and imposes specific affidavit requirements on court complaints.
