bill_summary: This bill modernizes and streamlines various statutory responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). Among other provisions, it requires the State Administrator of Elections to transmit precinct boundary changes electronically to MDP; limits Department of the Environment referrals of county plans to MDP to water and sewerage proposals only; requires MDP to prepare municipal population projections only upon request; narrows MDP's real property repository obligations to State-owned property; and repeals obsolete provisions regarding capital facilities planning access, geographic classification standards, regional planning project budget authorizations for M-NCPPC, and reporting requirements for the defunct State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Commission.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: State agencies (including the Maryland Department of Planning, Maryland State Board of Elections, and Maryland Department of the Environment), local governments (county and municipal planning entities), and the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Department of Legislative Services, the bill does not directly affect State or local government finances, and it has minimal or no economic impact on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: This departmental modernization bill directly updates and clarifies statutory duties of the Department of Planning, including its population projection requirements, real property repository functions, annual reporting requirements, and interagency review roles.

The bill alters statutory requirements for the Department of the Environment regarding the submission of county plans, limiting the requirement to submit proposals to the Department of Planning to water and sewerage proposals only (excluding solid waste disposal plans).

The bill establishes a new procedural requirement for the State Administrator of Elections to electronically transmit descriptions and maps of new or changed election precinct boundaries to the Secretary of Planning upon receipt from local boards.

Synopsis: Altering a prohibition concerning the maximum penalty for the late payment of rent that a landlord may charge in a residential lease to prohibit a penalty in excess of 5% of the amount of the unpaid rent rather than of the amount due.
Title: Residential Leases - Late Payment Penalties - Calculation
bill_summary: Alters the maximum penalty a landlord may charge for late payment of rent in a residential lease by capping it at 5% of the amount of unpaid rent due, rather than 5% of the total rent due for the rental period.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts) and the Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords, and property management companies
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It may have a meaningful impact on small business landlords and property management companies prohibited from assessing late penalties based on the full rent amount rather than the unpaid portion.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General enforces state consumer protection laws, including statutory tenant protections and prohibitions against unlawful lease terms and improper fee assessments under the Real Property Article.

The District Court of Maryland regularly adjudicates landlord-tenant disputes, failure to pay rent actions, and damages claims regarding residential leases and allowable late fees governed by this statute.

As the primary state department dedicated to affordable and secure rental housing, state statutory changes regulating late fees and tenant lease conditions are relevant to its overarching housing mission and programs.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "adjusted actual income" under the State child support guidelines by requiring the deduction, from actual income, of an allowance for support for each child in the parent's home for whom the parent owes a legal duty of support but who is not subject to a support order; requiring that the amount of a certain allowance be subtracted from a parent's actual income before the court determines the amount of a child support award; etc.
Title: Family Law - Child Support - Multifamily Adjustment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'adjusted actual income' under the Maryland child support guidelines to allow a deduction for support of other children living in a parent's home for more than 92 overnights per year to whom the parent owes a legal duty of support, calculated at 75% of the basic child support obligation using only that parent's actual income. It also adjusts the factors courts may evaluate when deciding whether applying the child support guidelines would be unjust or inappropriate.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Parents paying or receiving child support, particularly those supporting children from other relationships residing in their household, and the affected children.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures for the Department of Human Services (DHS) increase by up to $297,600 in FY 2026 for initial IT programming ($101,200 general funds, $196,400 federal funds), followed by ongoing annual maintenance expenditures of approximately $56,500 ($19,200 general funds, $37,300 federal funds) beginning in FY 2027. Federal fund revenues match federal expenditures at a 66% match rate. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Human Services administers Maryland's Child Support Administration. DHS will experience a direct fiscal impact of up to $297,600 in FY 2026 for IT system programming costs to implement the multifamily adjustment into child support calculation systems, followed by ongoing annual maintenance costs.

The bill alters statutory child support guidelines, calculations for adjusted actual income, and judicial standards and required written findings used by judges and magistrates across the state court system in establishing and modifying child support awards.

bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that Maryland State government departments and independent units submit an annual report regarding forms management to the Records Management Division of the Department of General Services.
responsible_party: Department of General Services (Records Management Division)
stakeholders: Maryland State departments and independent government units
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and has no local fiscal impact. It removes an administrative reporting mandate for State agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 276 was introduced as a departmental bill at the request of the Department of General Services. It repeals the statutory requirement that all state departments and independent units submit an annual forms management report to DGS's Records Management Division, eliminating unnecessary report collection and administrative burden for the agency.

Synopsis: Requiring a water bottle filling station or a combined water bottle filling station and drinking fountain to be installed in certain new construction or as part of certain renovations beginning October 1, 2025, subject to certain exceptions; requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt regulations to carry out the provisions of the Act; and applying the Act prospectively.
Title: Environment - Water Bottle Filling Stations - Requirement

NarrowSubjects.Name: Environmental Matters -see also- Conserv; Nat Resrce; Pollut
Water -see also- Coastal Bays; Riv,Str,Lks; Wastewater; etc.

bill_summary: Requires that at least one water bottle filling station or combined water bottle filling station and drinking fountain be installed in new construction and specified renovations wherever drinking fountains are required by applicable plumbing codes, with certain commercial and industrial exemptions, and directs the Maryland Department of Labor to adopt implementing regulations.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Property owners, developers, contractors, and occupants or visitors of newly constructed or renovated buildings in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not anticipated to be significantly affected, and revenues are not affected. The Maryland Department of Labor can adopt implementing regulations using existing budgeted resources. The impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates that the Maryland Department of Labor adopt regulations to carry out the provisions requiring water bottle filling stations in qualifying new construction and renovations.

The bill codifies the new subtitle within Title 9 of the Environment Article of the Annotated Code of Maryland, an area of statutory code generally administered by MDE, and MDE was consulted in the bill's analysis.

Synopsis: Adding the Department of Planning to the list of entities to which a municipality must send a copy of an annexation resolution with the new municipal boundaries.
Title: Municipalities - Annexation Resolutions - Submission to Department of Planning

NarrowSubjects.Name: Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC

bill_summary: Requires the chief executive and administrative officer of a municipality that has annexed property to send a copy of the annexation resolution and the new boundaries to the Maryland Department of Planning within 10 days after the resolution takes effect, and requires the department to keep it on record and available for public inspection.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Maryland municipalities, the Maryland Department of Planning, members of the public, and businesses or property owners in newly annexed municipal areas.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances and does not materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 279 is a departmental bill requested by the Maryland Department of Planning (MDP). It requires municipalities to send copies of annexation resolutions with new boundaries to MDP within 10 days of taking effect, and mandates that MDP keep the resolutions on record and make them available for public inspection.

bill_summary: Clarifies that only fees collected for the use of electronic procurement systems that are due to the State, rather than fees due to third-party vendors, must be deposited into the Operations Revenue Fund.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation and Department of General Services (Office of State Procurement)
stakeholders: State procurement agencies, third-party electronic procurement service providers (such as BidX), and prospective bidders and contractors utilizing electronic procurement systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is clarifying in nature and has no direct effect on State or local governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT requested this departmental legislation to resolve legal ambiguity regarding its use of the third-party electronic bidding platform BidX, ensuring vendor subscription fees are not improperly classified as State revenues requiring deposit into the Operations Revenue Fund.

DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer, who must approve reasonable electronic procurement fees, and administers the Operations Revenue Fund where state-due electronic procurement fees are deposited to support the Office of State Procurement.

The Board of Public Works possesses statutory authority to approve fees charged for electronic procurement systems under this section and previously notified MDOT that continued usage of third-party platforms might be prohibited without this statutory clarification.

bill_summary: This bill updates Maryland's planning framework by replacing the 12 existing planning visions with 8 core planning principles (land, transportation, housing, economy, equity, resilience, place, and ecology) that local planning commissions must implement in their comprehensive plans and that constitute the State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Maryland residents, local governments and planning commissions, underserved communities, and small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances, and it is not expected to have a direct, material impact on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Department of Planning requested this departmental legislation and serves as the primary state agency responsible for overseeing state growth policy, comprehensive land use planning principles, and reviewing local comprehensive plans.

Smart, Green & Growing is a multi-agency state initiative that is statutorily and programmatically grounded in the state planning visions that this bill repeals and replaces with eight new planning principles.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Maryland Department of Transportation's joint determinations with the Department of Planning regarding whether transportation projects outside of priority funding areas comply with the updated State Economic Growth, Resource Protection, and Planning Policy.
The bill updates the statutory standards under which the Board of Public Works may approve funding for certain growth-related transportation projects outside of priority funding areas.

Synopsis: Increasing from 180 days to 300 days the maximum duration of an emergency status determination authorizing the temporary adjustment of tolls, fees, or other charges by the Maryland Transportation Authority.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum duration of an emergency status determination by the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) from 180 days to 300 days, allowing temporary emergency adjustments to tolls, fees, and other charges to remain in effect longer while permanent rate-setting procedures are carried out.
responsible_party: Maryland Transportation Authority
stakeholders: Motorists, commercial carriers, and public and private entities using MDTA toll facilities, as well as MDTA bondholders.
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted revenues for MDTA may increase, potentially significantly, starting in FY 2026 if temporary emergency toll increases stay in effect up to 120 days longer than permitted under current law. State and local government expenditures across all funds may also increase to pay higher toll rates for a longer duration. Specific dollar estimates cannot be determined because the timing, frequency, and scale of future emergencies are unpredictable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA), extending the maximum duration of its emergency status determinations for temporary toll and fee adjustments from 180 to 300 days.
The Maryland Department of Transportation requested this departmental bill on behalf of the transportation sector and oversees the State's transportation network and financing coordination with MDTA.

bill_summary: This bill modifies reserve account and study requirements for common ownership communities, including cooperative housing corporations, residential condominiums, and homeowners associations. It extends the timeline from three to five years for a community to reach recommended reserve funding levels following an initial reserve study, requires governing bodies to develop and annually review a reserve funding plan using approved accounting methods, and allows communities to temporarily deviate from funding requirements for up to one year (renewable by a two-thirds vote) if experiencing financial hardship.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Cooperative housing corporations, residential condominiums, homeowners associations (common ownership communities), unit and lot owners, and reserve study professionals.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division oversees consumer protection matters, including inquiries and disputes related to common ownership communities (cooperatives, condominiums, and homeowners associations), and served as an information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Altering a certain requirement under which a court is authorized to order that the testimony of a child victim be taken outside a courtroom and shown in the courtroom by closed circuit television in certain child abuse cases; requiring the testimony of a child victim taken by closed circuit television within the courthouse be in a setting that reasonably mitigates the likelihood the child victim will suffer emotional distress; etc.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Child Victims - Testimony in Child Abuse Cases

bill_summary: Alters the standards for permitting child abuse victims to testify outside of a courtroom via closed-circuit television by removing the requirement that a court find the child unable to reasonably communicate due to serious emotional distress. The bill also requires that such testimony take place within the courthouse in a setting that mitigates emotional distress and guarantees the defendant or child respondent private, real-time oral communication with their attorney during the testimony.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Administrative Office of the Courts and state trial courts)
stakeholders: Child victims of abuse, criminal defendants and juvenile respondents, defense attorneys, prosecutors, and judges.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations, as the Judiciary's existing technology and practices for private communication and out-of-court testimony can effectuate implementation.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters court procedures and courtroom technology requirements for taking child victim testimony via closed-circuit television in criminal, juvenile, and child abuse proceedings administered by the Maryland Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts defense practice in child abuse and juvenile delinquency cases by modifying standards for child victim testimony outside the courtroom and establishing explicit requirements for private, real-time oral communication between defendants and their defense counsel.

Synopsis: Renaming the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Pilot Program to be the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program; repealing the termination date of certain provisions of law that establish and govern the funding for the Program; authorizing rather than requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to establish and implement the Program; and prohibiting the Exchange from implementing the Program if certain funds are not available.

bill_summary: This bill makes the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program permanent by repealing its June 30, 2026 sunset date and renaming it from a pilot program. It authorizes the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) to implement the program and designate funds for subsidies to eligible young adults in calendar year 2026 and subsequent years, provided that funding from the health insurance provider fee assessment is available.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Young adults (ages 18 to 40) purchasing health insurance coverage in Maryland's individual market and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund continue to fund young adult health insurance subsidies at an estimated $26.0 million per calendar year through calendar 2028, reflecting $13.0 million in FY 2026, $26.0 million in both FY 2027 and FY 2028, and $13.0 million in FY 2029. The FY 2026 State budget includes $13.0 million in contingent funding. Special fund revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MHBE is the primary agency responsible for administering and implementing the State-Based Young Adult Health Insurance Subsidies Program, adopting necessary regulations, establishing subsidy eligibility and payment parameters, tracking expenditures and market impacts, and designating funds from the MHBE Fund.

The Insurance Commissioner is statutorily required to be consulted by MHBE when establishing and implementing the subsidy program, determining subsidy eligibility and payment parameters, and designating funds from the MHBE Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the rate at which nonprofit organizations receiving State-funded grants or contracts may be reimbursed for indirect costs to match the rate established under relevant federal guidelines; requiring the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council to study and make certain recommendations to the Department of Budget and Management regarding the entire grants life cycle; requiring the Council to submit a report on its full recommendations to the Department and the General Assembly by July 1, 2027; etc.
Title: State Government - Grants and Contracts - Reimbursement of Indirect Costs

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: Increases the rate at which nonprofit organizations receiving State-funded grants or contracts can be reimbursed for indirect costs (if they do not already have a negotiated rate) from at least 10% to the greater of 15% or the federal de minimis rate established in OMB Uniform Guidance.
responsible_party: Maryland State grant-making agencies and the Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Nonprofit organizations receiving State-funded grants or contracts, and local governments that act as pass-through entities for State grant funds.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State revenues or the overall total value of State contracts and grants awarded to nonprofit organizations. However, nonprofit organizations that currently reimburse indirect costs at 10% will be able to allocate at least 5% more of their award to indirect costs, with no material diminution in services expected. Local governments serving as pass-through entities can incorporate the change with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DBM is the principal fiscal agency of the state and is explicitly referenced in the bill (§ 2-210) to receive recommendations and reports regarding the grants life cycle and uniform administrative requirements for state grant-making entities.

The Governor's Grants Office coordinates grant management practices, training, and compliance across Maryland state agencies and nonprofits, directly aligning with the bill's updates to indirect cost reimbursements and federal OMB Uniform Guidance alignment.

As the state's central procurement authority responsible for policies governing the procurement of services and State contracts, DGS must ensure procurement contracts with nonprofit service providers incorporate the updated indirect cost rate minimums.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references § 2-210 governing the Maryland Efficient Grant Application Council, a statutory council tasked with examining grant processes and making recommendations on adopting uniform guidance.
The Board of Public Works oversees and approves significant state procurement contracts and expenditures, which must comply with state statutory terms governing nonprofit cost reimbursement.

MDH relies heavily on contracts and grants with nonprofit organizations to deliver public health, behavioral health, and developmental disability services, requiring grant and contract terms to reflect the 15% de minimis indirect cost rate.

DHS frequently awards state-funded grants and contracts to nonprofit service providers for social services, requiring adjustments to indirect cost reimbursement calculations for qualifying nonprofit recipients.
DHCD regularly administers state grants and contracts to nonprofit community and housing organizations, which will be eligible to claim the increased indirect cost rate under the legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DSCI works extensively with nonprofit host organizations through paid service programs and partnerships that may involve state grants and contract reimbursements.

Synopsis: Altering and clarifying the requirement that a sworn affidavit for judicial authorization to initiate forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search (FGGS) assert that the reasonable investigative leads have been pursued and failed to identify the perpetrator and instead requiring that a sworn affidavit for judicial authorization assert that identity of the perpetrator is unknown.
Title: Criminal Procedure - Forensic Genetic Genealogical DNA Analysis and Search - Affidavit for Judicial Authorization

bill_summary: This bill modifies the affidavit requirements for law enforcement seeking judicial authorization to initiate a forensic genetic genealogical DNA analysis and search (FGGS). It replaces the requirement to show that reasonable investigative leads have been pursued and failed with an assertion that the perpetrator's identity is unknown, and clarifies that investigators are not required to have exhausted all investigative leads.
responsible_party: Law enforcement agencies, State's Attorney offices (prosecutors), and the Judiciary (Maryland courts)
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, prosecutors, criminal suspects and defendants, and victims of murder, rape, and felony sexual offenses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency in Maryland, the Maryland State Police investigates serious crimes such as homicides and sexual offenses, maintains forensic samples and DNA database submissions, and submits affidavits to the courts for judicial authorization to conduct FGGS.
Judges in the Maryland court system are required to review the sworn affidavits and grant judicial authorizations for FGGS under the altered statutory criteria set forth in the bill.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Defender represents indigent criminal defendants in felony cases where FGGS evidence may be utilized, directly impacting trial advocacy, evidence suppression motions, and discovery review.

The Office of the Attorney General prosecutes certain state criminal matters and represents the State in appellate proceedings where the legality and standards of FGGS authorizations and affidavits may be challenged.

Synopsis: Expanding certain provisions of law relating to a certain investigation and recommendation by a State's Attorney concerning the filing of a statement of charges against certain professionals to include certain human service workers.
Title: Courts and Judicial Proceedings - Statement of Charges - Human Service Workers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Investigations and Inquiries -see also- Crim Bckgrnd Invest

bill_summary: Expands existing protections to include adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers, requiring that an application for a statement of charges filed in District Court for an offense allegedly committed in the course of their duties must first be investigated by the State's Attorney before charges can be filed.
responsible_party: State's Attorneys and the District Court of Maryland (Judiciary)
stakeholders: Adult protective services workers, child welfare caseworkers, State's Attorneys, and District Court Commissioners.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect the operations or finances of the Judiciary, State's Attorneys' offices, or local circuit courts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies District Court procedures under Courts and Judicial Proceedings § 2-608 by requiring District Court Commissioners and judges to forward applications for statements of charges against adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers to the State's Attorney for investigation and recommendation prior to filing.

The bill provides procedural protections for adult protective services workers and child welfare caseworkers when criminal charges are sought against them for actions in the scope of their employment, directly impacting the workforce employed and overseen by the Department of Human Services and its local departments.

Title: Public Safety - Law Enforcement Agencies - Peer Support Programs

bill_summary: This bill establishes confidentiality requirements for communications within law enforcement peer support programs. It prohibits peer support specialists and participating officers from disclosing written or oral peer support communications, subject to specific exceptions such as explicit threats of suicide or serious bodily harm, admissions of criminal conduct, mandated reports of abuse or neglect, participant consent, or court orders. It also requires specialists to provide written notice of these confidentiality rules before an initial interaction.
responsible_party: Maryland State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Law enforcement officers, trained peer support specialists, law enforcement agencies, and the Fraternal Order of Police.
fiscal_impact_summary: State law enforcement agencies can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources, with no impact on State revenues. Local government expenditures may see a potential minimal increase if local law enforcement agencies need to modify existing peer support programs. Local revenues are not affected. Specific dollar amounts were not estimated.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary state law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police directly employs law enforcement officers and operates peer support and employee assistance programs subject to the bill's confidentiality requirements and written notification mandates.

DNR oversees the Maryland Natural Resources Police, a statewide law enforcement entity whose officers and peer support specialists are directly impacted by the mandatory confidentiality and disclosure rules.

MDOT oversees state law enforcement forces including the Maryland Transportation Authority (MDTA) Police and Maryland Transit Administration (MTA) Police, whose peer support programs must adhere to the bill's provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS employs state law enforcement and public safety personnel and maintains peer support and wellness initiatives governed by the bill's confidentiality protections.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Institute for Emergency Medical Services Systems
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MIEMSS operates the State Critical Incident Stress Management (CISM) team, which provides trained peer support to law enforcement and other first responders following traumatic incidents.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP administers the Officer and Community Wellness Training Grant Fund, which finances mental health first aid and CISM peer support training for law enforcement agencies across the state.
USM institutions maintain sworn police departments that qualify as law enforcement agencies and must implement the bill's peer support confidentiality requirements for their officers.
Morgan State University operates an independent sworn police department that constitutes a law enforcement agency impacted by the peer support program guidelines.
The Comptroller's Office employs sworn law enforcement officers within its Field Enforcement Division who are eligible for peer support programs and covered by the bill's confidentiality standards.
The Judiciary and state courts are responsible for issuing subpoenas or court orders that qualify as statutory exceptions to the peer support confidentiality protections.

Synopsis: Repealing the time limitation within which the Motor Vehicle Administration is required to make available specially designed vintage reproduction registration plates; and requiring the Administration to charge a fee of $100 for the initial issuance and $25 for the renewal of a specially designed vintage reproduction registration plate.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Specially Designed Vintage Reproduction Registration Plates

bill_summary: Permanently reinstates the Motor Vehicle Administration's authority to issue specially designed vintage reproduction registration plates resembling Maryland's 1910 black and yellow plates for qualifying vehicles, repeals the previous one-year limit on their availability, and establishes an initial issuance fee of $100 and a renewal fee of $25.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Owners and lessees of qualifying vehicles (passenger, light truck, historic, multipurpose, and street rod) who apply for vintage reproduction registration plates.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) fee revenues increase by an estimated $135,000 in FY 2026 and between $100,000 and $156,250 annually through FY 2030. MVA cost recovery expenditures are estimated at $10 per plate ($12,500 in FY 2026 and $10,000 annually thereafter). Remaining net revenues (estimated at $122,500 in FY 2026) are credited to the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, providing a negligible increase in local highway user revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to permanently make available specially designed vintage reproduction registration plates, establish and collect initial ($100) and renewal ($25) fees, recover its production costs, and credit remaining revenues to the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT oversees the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and the Gasoline and Motor Vehicle Revenue Account, both of which will experience increased revenues and expenditures from the issuance of these registration plates.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland to examine and analyze the efficiency, uniformity, and quality of fiduciary adjudication in Maryland and make recommendations; requiring the orphans' courts, circuit courts, registers of wills, and Administrative Office of the Courts to comply with certain requests of the Task Force; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and make recommendations on or before January 1, 2026.
Title: Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland to study and make recommendations regarding the efficiency, uniformity, and quality of fiduciary and probate adjudication in Maryland's orphans' courts and circuit courts, requiring a final report of its findings and recommendations by January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services
stakeholders: Orphans' court and circuit court judges, registers of wills, estate and trust attorneys, and Maryland citizens involved in probate, trust, guardianship, or other fiduciary matters.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The bill can be implemented with existing resources by the Department of Legislative Services and participating entities; task force members are not compensated but may be reimbursed for travel expenses as provided in the State budget. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the administration of probate matters, includes two registers of wills on the Task Force, and explicitly mandates that registers of wills comply with all reasonable requests from the Task Force for information and data.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Task Force to Study Fiduciary Adjudication in Maryland, a temporary body charged with examining court jurisdiction, judicial qualifications, and procedures regarding fiduciary and probate matters.

The bill explicitly mandates that the Administrative Office of the Courts comply with all reasonable requests by the Task Force for information and data necessary for its work studying court adjudication of fiduciary matters.
The Governor is responsible for appointing one member to the Task Force, designating the Task Force chair from among the legislative members, and receiving the final report and recommendations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Administrator of Elections to enter into memoranda of understanding with municipal corporations that allow the State Administrator to work collaboratively with a municipal corporation to support the administration of the municipal corporation's elections; authorizing the State Administrator to lease a voting system or other equipment used to administer an election for use in a municipal election; repealing the authority of a local board to lease a voting system to certain entities within the county; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Administrator of Elections to enter into memoranda of understanding with municipal corporations to support municipal election administration and lease voting systems or election equipment to them, with lease proceeds distributed to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. The bill also repeals local election boards' authority to lease voting systems and modifies the deadline and certification requirements for municipalities requesting their offices and questions be included on a statewide ballot.
responsible_party: State Administrator of Elections
stakeholders: Municipal corporations, municipal candidates and voters, local boards of elections, and the Maryland State Board of Elections
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund (Fair Campaign Financing Fund) revenues may increase annually beginning in FY 2025 from equipment lease proceeds (estimated illustratively at $23,400 for a single municipal election such as Annapolis), while State expenditures remain unaffected. Municipal expenditures may increase to pay for leased election equipment under memoranda of understanding. Local county board revenues and finances are not expected to be affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 322 directly empowers the State Administrator of Elections (the executive head of the State Board of Elections) to enter into memoranda of understanding with municipal corporations, lease voting systems and election administration equipment, set lease terms, and distribute lease proceeds to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund. It also alters the timeline and requirements for municipal requests to have municipal offices and questions included on state-prepared ballots.

Synopsis: Clarifying required information for registering a domestic partnership or obtaining a marriage license; and requiring a declaration of domestic partnership filed with the register of wills to include the Social Security number of each domestic partner who has a Social Security number.
Title: Domestic Partnership and Marriage - Required Information

bill_summary: Clarifies requirements for registering a domestic partnership or obtaining a marriage license by requiring applicants to provide their full legal name and date of birth rather than just age. It also requires declarations of domestic partnership filed with a register of wills to include each partner's Social Security number (if they have one) and protects those numbers from public disclosure, subject to limited statutory exceptions.
responsible_party: County Registers of Wills and Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Couples registering a domestic partnership or applying for a marriage license in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect local government operations or finances. At the state level, no direct expenditures or revenues are estimated, but the bill may help protect federal child support enforcement funding by ensuring Maryland statutory procedures comply with federal requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Estates and Trusts § 2–214, requiring registers of wills to collect the full legal name, date of birth, and Social Security number of individuals registering domestic partnerships and to restrict the public disclosure of those Social Security numbers.

The bill amends Family Law § 2–402 governing the information that circuit court clerks must collect and record during marriage license applications, including legal names and dates of birth. The AOC provides operational, legal, and technology support to the circuit court clerks.

The Department of Human Services administers the State Child Support Administration, which accesses Social Security number records to enforce child support obligations under federal compliance requirements mentioned in the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring each member of a county board of education to complete certain antibias training at least once during the member's term.

bill_summary: Requires each member of a local county board of education to complete an antibias training program at least once during their term, conducted separately from the antibias training provided to public school employees.
responsible_party: County Boards of Education and Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Members of county boards of education, local school systems, and public school students and staff
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. Local school systems can implement and comply with the training requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's public education system and establishes the underlying guidelines for the antibias training programs that county board of education members are required to complete under this bill.

The Maryland Commission on Civil Rights enforces anti-discrimination laws and conducts training on bias and civil rights compliance; it served as an informational resource regarding the bill's subject matter.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to allow an individual to choose to take all components of the General Educational Development Test in either English or Spanish; and requiring the Department to study the feasibility and cost of offering the examination in additional languages and to report its findings and recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly on or before December 1, 2026.

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Labor to allow individuals taking the high school diploma by examination (GED) to take all components in either English or Spanish. It also requires the Department to study the feasibility and cost of offering the examination in additional languages and report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Adult education students in Maryland seeking a high school diploma by examination, particularly non-native English speakers and Spanish-speaking test takers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures are not materially affected. The Maryland Department of Labor can implement the Spanish examination option and complete the required study and report using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. It oversees adult education examinations, must allow test takers to complete all examination components in either English or Spanish, and is required to study and report on the feasibility and cost of offering the exam in additional languages.

The Department of Education is referenced in the statute as the administrator of the GED Option Program for English language learner students and the State Board of Education determines the comprehensive nature of high school diploma examinations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Public Access Ombudsman to delegate to a staff member of the Office of the Public Access Ombudsman any of the powers and duties granted to the Ombudsman that are appropriate to the staff member's training and expertise.
Title: Public Information Act - Public Access Ombudsman - Delegation of Powers
bill_summary: This bill authorizes the Maryland Public Access Ombudsman to delegate any of the statutory powers and duties granted to the Ombudsman to a staff member of the Office of the Public Access Ombudsman, provided the delegated tasks are appropriate to the staff member's training and expertise.
responsible_party: Office of the Public Access Ombudsman
stakeholders: Staff of the Office of the Public Access Ombudsman, public records custodians, and individuals seeking access to public records under the Public Information Act.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State governmental operations or finances, and has no local effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Public Access Ombudsman is established within the purview of the Office of the Attorney General, which appoints the Ombudsman and provides office space and staff for the office. The bill permits the Ombudsman to delegate certain powers and duties to staff members provided by and working within this framework.

bill_summary: Establishes the Workgroup on Newborn Home Visiting Services to study, compile data on, and compare operational home visiting programs in Maryland to evidence-based universal nurse home visiting models. The workgroup is tasked with identifying service gaps, funding opportunities, and workforce needs, and must submit a report with findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
responsible_party: Workgroup on Newborn Home Visiting Services and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Families with newborns, postpartum individuals, pediatricians, obstetricians, nurse midwives, registered nurses, hospitals, and early childhood and home visiting service providers.

bill_summary: Establishes a tiered, escalating system of maximum civil penalties ranging from $40 to $425 for speed monitoring system violations on Maryland Route 210 (Piscataway Highway) in Prince George's County, based on how much a driver exceeds the posted speed limit.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland and the Maryland Department of Transportation State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists driving on Maryland Route 210 in Prince George's County, Prince George's County law enforcement and local government, and the District Court of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues and expenditures increase, potentially by more than $100,000 annually from FY 2026 through FY 2029, for State Highway Administration safety improvements on MD Route 210. General fund revenues may increase from contested citations in District Court, while general fund expenditures increase by $21,048 in FY 2026 for Judiciary computer programming updates. Prince George's County local finances are not materially affected due to existing net-revenue remittance requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Pursuant to existing statutory revenue-sharing requirements, net fine revenues collected from speed monitoring systems on MD Route 210 are remitted to the State Highway Administration to cover the costs of studying and implementing infrastructure and roadway safety solutions on MD Route 210, resulting in increased Transportation Trust Fund revenues and expenditures.

The District Court must prescribe the citation form and penalty fee schedules for the tiered fines, incurring $21,048 in programming expenditures in FY 2026, and is expected to handle an increased volume of contested citations resulting from higher penalty amounts.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration and administrator of the Transportation Trust Fund (TTF), MDOT's TTF revenues and expenditures will increase by potentially over $100,000 annually from the higher speed camera fines dedicated to MD Route 210 safety improvements.
The Comptroller of Maryland acts as the conduit receiving net fine remittances from Prince George's County and distributing them to the State Highway Administration for MD Route 210 safety projects.

Local governments and school systems receive significant capital grant revenues and an extended repayment period (from 2 to 5 years) before reimbursing the State for debt service on transferred school buildings.

MES administers capital bond allocations through the State Water and Sewer Infrastructure Improvement Fund for water and wastewater improvements at State institutions.
Commerce administers the Maryland Arts Capital Grant Program ($3 million) through its Division of Marketing, Tourism, and the Arts.

The Department administers the Access Maryland capital program ($1.027 million) to upgrade accessibility at State-owned facilities.
The Commission receives bond funding to design renovations and expansion of its visitor center into an Education and Artisan Center Complex.

As head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General oversees operations, maintenance, and renovations of readiness centers and headquarters facilities funded under the bill.
AOC supports the Maryland Judiciary, whose major capital projects—including the New Supreme Court of Maryland Building and district court multi-service facilities—are financed in this loan act.
MEDCO is named as a grantee and implementing entity for projects including Viva White Oak and the Principio Rail Spur.
SHA is specifically designated alongside Montgomery County to plan, design, and construct crosswalk safety improvements on Route 108.
The Trust oversees maintenance and improvements to the historic State House, grounds, and Old Treasury Building, which are funded through capital authorizations under the Board of Public Works.
The bill enacts the Governor's capital budget legislation and contains programs organized under the Executive Department - Governor.

bill_summary: The Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025 enacts statutory provisions necessary to balance the State budget. Key actions include raising state revenues through tax and fee adjustments (such as adding individual income tax brackets, imposing a capital gains surtax, expanding the sales tax to IT services, and increasing vehicle-related fees and excise taxes), providing mandate relief across various state-funded grant programs, transferring special fund balances to the General Fund, shifting certain teacher pension and property assessment costs to local governments, and implementing expenditure containment measures across state agencies.
responsible_party: Department of Budget and Management and the Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland taxpayers, businesses, vehicle owners, local governments, local school systems, state retirees, Medicaid and social service recipients, and state agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill achieves an estimated total General Fund improvement of $870.2 million in FY 2025 and $2.514 billion in FY 2026 (totaling approximately $3.384 billion across both fiscal years). Specifically, General Fund revenues increase by $765.6 million in FY 2025 and $1.566 billion in FY 2026, while General Fund expenditures decrease by $104.7 million in FY 2025 and $897.9 million in FY 2026. Special Fund revenues increase by $19.5 million in FY 2025 and decrease by $80.1 million in FY 2026, with Special Fund expenditures increasing by $94.5 million in FY 2025 and $366.7 million in FY 2026. Local jurisdictions face net cost increases and revenue losses starting in FY 2026 (including $97.7 million annually in teacher/community college retirement costs, $21.2 million in property valuation reimbursements, and phased-out supplemental retirement grants), partially offset by an estimated $28.2 million increase in local income tax revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers and enforces numerous major revenue and tax provisions in the bill, including individual income tax rates, capital gains surtaxes, sales and use tax expansions to IT and data services, the new tire fee, adult-use cannabis tax changes, and significant fund balance transfers and repayments involving the Local Income Tax Reserve Account.

Responsible for managing state budget execution, implementing mandate relief and cost containment across executive agencies, certifying and reporting on potential federal funding reductions exceeding $1 billion, and executing across-the-board expenditure reductions.

Implements substantial transportation revenue and financing changes, including increasing Consolidated Transportation Bond authorization to $5 billion, increasing vehicle excise tax to 6.5%, imposing excise tax on rental vehicles, receiving new tire fee revenues into the Transportation Trust Fund, and expanding GARVEE bond uses.

Directly implements multiple vehicle-related fee adjustments, including doubling certificate of title fees, accelerating vehicle registration fee increases, increasing VEIP emissions testing fees, altering rental car registrations, and narrowing the definition of historic motor vehicles.

Implements major healthcare financing actions including increasing the Medicaid Deficit Assessment, establishing the Medicaid Primary Care Program Fund, modifying DDA caps and funding uses, utilizing excess SPDAP funds for retiree health accounts, executing health board fund transfers to BHA, and delegating nursing home survey authority in Montgomery County.

Directly establishes and increases regulatory fees across several programs, including sediment and erosion control training certifications, wetlands and waterways authorizations, rental property lead risk registrations, the Voluntary Cleanup Program, tire recycling fees, and surface mining licenses and permits.

Establishes a new 0.15% unemployment insurance administrative fee to fund administrative operations, receives a $37.3 million transfer from the Local Income Tax Reserve Account for the Division of Paid Leave, and absorbs mandated funding reductions for various workforce grant programs.

Directly affected by the redirection of transfer tax revenues from Program Open Space and Rural Legacy to the General Fund, expanded use of the Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays 2010 Trust Fund and Program Open Space balances for operating expenses, and increased Waterway Improvement Fund support for Natural Resources Police.

Increases inspection and certification fees for nurseries, establishes administrative authority to set weights and measures registration fees, alters horse establishment renewal processes, absorbs a reduction in mandated agricultural tree planting funds, and sees MALPP transfer tax revenue redirected to the General Fund.

Reduces the State share of nonpublic placement program costs for educating children with disabilities, modifies Safe Schools Fund and School Resource Officer grant requirements, and reduces State retirement payments for local school system personnel.

Administers programs facing altered funding and caps, including accelerating the reduction in Film Production Activity tax credits, altering More Jobs for Marylanders reserve fund transfers, capping E-Nnovation Initiative allocations, and redirecting SMWOBA funds to other business financing programs.

Impacted by the $97.7 million cost shift of employer pension contributions for teachers and community college personnel to local governments, the permanent repeal of the $50 million annual supplemental pension contribution, and the elimination of the general fund surplus pension sweeper.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers the increase in the mobile sports wagering tax rate from 15% to 20%, redistributes 25% of sports wagering proceeds to the General Fund, clarifies license renewal calculations, and modifies statutory lottery distributions to the Bus Rapid Transit Fund.

SEIF interest and investment earnings are redirected to the General Fund, $230 million in ACP account balances are transferred to the General Fund, SEIF funds are authorized for MDE air quality operations, and ACP funds are expanded to support government clean energy projects.

Replaces general funds with special funds for Consumer Protection Division enforcement, expands the use of the Securities Act Registration Fund to support general OAG operations, and expands allowable uses of Mortgage Loan Servicing Practices Settlement funds to support legal representation and eviction defense.

Designated as the successor entity to MTROA for the planning, design, construction, and ownership of racing and community development projects, and transfers $3 million in interest earnings from the Racing and Community Development Financing Fund to the General Fund.

Designated as the successor entity to MTROA for the ongoing operation and management of thoroughbred racing and community development projects, assuming related responsibilities, assets, contracts, and liabilities.

CREF allowable uses are expanded to support the $5 million mandated appropriation for the Social Equity Partnership Grant Program, and the distribution schedule for cannabis excise tax revenues is altered.

Implements the increased Medicaid Deficit Assessment on hospital rates and is authorized to establish an alternative collection method across fiscal 2025 and 2026; also administers hospital payments capitalizing the new Medicaid Primary Care Program Fund.

Delays the statutory requirement to procure only zero-emission buses for the transit fleet from fiscal 2027 to fiscal 2032 and authorizes the use of GARVEE bond proceeds to finance light rail system rehabilitation.

Administers scholarship and financial assistance programs facing mandate reductions, including the Community College Promise Scholarship, the Police and Probation Agents Scholarship and LARP programs, and a temporary reduction in Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credits.
Administers scholarship and aid programs facing mandated budget reductions, including the Community College Promise Scholarship and the Student Loan Debt Relief Tax Credit.

Holds and manages newly created special funds such as the Medicaid Primary Care Program Fund and is authorized to receive transfers from the Rainy Day Fund into the Annuity Bond Fund if necessary to pay State debt service.

Notifies the Comptroller and local governments regarding the new 50% county cost-sharing obligation for erroneous conviction compensation awards and executes reductions to prior local grant appropriations.

Repeals the mandate requiring a 20% set-aside of Information Technology Investment Fund appropriations for expedited projects and oversees cybersecurity funds transferred from the Dedicated Purpose Account.

Authorizes $340,000 in Program Open Space funds transferred to MHAA to be used for MDP operating expenses and reduces the mandated appropriation to the Historic Revitalization Tax Credit Reserve Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Reduces statutory participant targets for the Young Adult Service Year Option Pathway and reduces the fiscal 2026 mandated appropriation for the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway Fund.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Manages programs with reduced funding mandates (warrant apprehension grants) and transfers funds from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund to support the Office of the Correctional Ombudsman, along with fund transfers from the VIPP fund.
Statutory caps on project reserve contingency funds for the Eastern Correctional Institution Turbine Project and reimbursable projects are substantially increased.
Withdraws a $12 million capital PAYGO grant for Baltimore County's Lansdowne Library and manages DPA fund transfers related to the relocation of State agencies from State Center.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Authorizes Opioid Restitution Fund monies to supplant general funds for inmate opioid use disorder medication and authorizes transfer of $5 million from the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission Fund to the General Fund.

Caps the total restoration of EBT benefits lost due to theft at $30 million annually and is subject to the Interagency Rates Committee rate freeze on foster care maintenance provider rates.
Expands allowable uses of the Maryland Emergency Medical System Operations Fund in fiscal 2025 and 2026 to support the general operations of the MSP Aviation Command.

Eliminates the $1.0 million annual funding mandate for the Maryland Patient Safety Center Fund, making the appropriation discretionary.
Removes the Judicial Branch's exemption from performance reviews conducted by OPEGA and authorizes a $20 million transfer from the Land Records Improvement Fund to the General Fund.
Authorizes the transfer of $9 million from the Resilient Maryland Revolving Loan Fund to the Blueprint for Maryland's Future Fund.
Transfers $62.9 million in capital PAYGO funding originally allocated in the Dedicated Purpose Account for the construction of a new State veterans home to the General Fund.
Transfers $10 million in capital PAYGO funds from the Dedicated Purpose Account for deferred maintenance to the General Fund, offset by replacement GO bond funding.
Subject to the Interagency Rates Committee payment rate freeze for residential child care providers in fiscal 2026.
Serves on the Interagency Rates Committee, which is prohibited from increasing provider payment rates for fiscal 2026.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Oversees small and minority business development policies and program accounts affected by SMWOBA reallocations to MSBDFA and TEDCO.
Consults on the development of the scope and objectives for the required independent audit of the Prince George's County Board of Education and receives the resulting audit report.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Primary recipient of MEMSOF funding, the allowable uses of which are temporarily expanded to support non-medical general operations of the State Police Aviation Command.

University of Maryland Discovery District quantum computing activities receive a specific sales and use tax exemption on IT services, and UMMS cancer center DPA funding is transferred to the General Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the registration fee requirement for the Community Association Registry; permitting the County Executive to establish the registration fee; prohibiting a person or entity who fails to register from filing a dispute; and requiring the Prince George's County Office of Community Relations to provide revenue from annual community association registration fees to fund the administrative hearing process for disputes between community associations and owners in Prince George's County.

bill_summary: This bill requires all common ownership communities (cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations) in Prince George's County to register annually with the county's Community Association Registry. It removes the fixed $100 fee and authorizes the County Executive to establish fees in amounts sufficient to fund the administrative hearing process and technical assistance provided by the Office of Community Relations and the Commission on Common Ownership Communities. Additionally, unregistered or falsely registered persons are prohibited from filing a dispute through the administrative hearing process until properly registered.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Office of Community Relations
stakeholders: Common ownership communities (condominiums, homeowners associations, and cooperative housing corporations), property/unit owners, community association managers, and residential developers in Prince George's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not materially affected. For Prince George's County, annual administrative expenditures increase by approximately $400,000 beginning in FY 2026 to hire three staff members in the Office of Community Relations to investigate cases and manage administrative hearings. These costs are anticipated to be fully offset by increased fee revenues from registry fees and related administrative process charges.

bill_summary: Prohibits Maryland health occupations boards from requiring additional proof of English proficiency from an applicant who holds a valid, unrestricted license from another state requiring English proficiency. It also requires boards to post this policy on their websites, expands acceptable methods for demonstrating English proficiency for nurses, and adjusts licensure by endorsement standards for nursing and pharmacy.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and health occupations licensing boards (including the Maryland Board of Nursing and Maryland Board of Pharmacy)
stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed healthcare professionals applying for Maryland licensure or certification (including registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, and pharmacists) and Maryland health occupations licensing boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational changes can generally be absorbed within existing budgeted resources by the affected health occupations boards. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health houses and oversees the state's health occupations boards, including the State Board of Nursing and the State Board of Pharmacy, which are directly required to implement the bill's changes regarding English proficiency standards, website disclosures, and nursing licensure by endorsement.

Synopsis: Repealing the termination of certain provisions of law establishing the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority.
Title: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority - Sunset Repeal PG 403-25
bill_summary: This bill repeals the statutory termination date for the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, thereby making the authority and its neighborhood revitalization functions in Prince George's County permanent.
responsible_party: Prince George's Gateway Development Authority (in consultation with the Department of Housing and Community Development and supported by the Prince George's County Redevelopment Authority)
stakeholders: Residents, property owners, and businesses in the target area municipalities of Prince George's County (the cities of Mount Rainier and Bladensburg, and the towns of Brentwood, Cottage City, Colmar Manor, and North Brentwood).
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, nor Prince George's County operations or finances, as there is no statutory funding mandate for the authority.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Housing and Community Development (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, and the Authority operates in consultation with the department. Repealing the sunset makes these responsibilities permanent.

Under the Economic Development Article, the Secretary of Commerce (or designee) serves as a statutory member of the Prince George's Gateway Development Authority, a role made permanent by the repeal of the termination date.
The Prince George's Gateway Development Authority is statutorily required to report its comprehensive neighborhood revitalization strategy to the Governor.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person to ride a bicycle, play vehicle, or unicycle on a sidewalk or sidewalk area unless prohibited by local ordinance; and requiring a person riding a bicycle, play vehicle, or unicycle on a sidewalk or sidewalk area or in or through a crosswalk to yield the right-of-way to a pedestrian or a person using an electric personal assistive mobility device.
Title: Bicycles, Play Vehicles, and Unicycles - Authorizations and Requirements (Jay's Law)

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Transportation -see also- Aircraft; Airports; Boats; etc

bill_summary: House Bill 375 (Jay's Law) permits individuals to ride bicycles, play vehicles, or unicycles on sidewalks or sidewalk areas unless prohibited by a local ordinance. It also requires operators of these vehicles on sidewalks or in crosswalks to yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and individuals using electric personal assistive mobility devices.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of State Police and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Bicyclists, unicyclists, operators of play vehicles, pedestrians, and users of electric personal assistive mobility devices
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may see a potential minimal decrease to the extent that fewer citations are issued. State and local law enforcement can handle enforcement with existing resources. Local governments can review and update local ordinances with existing resources, with no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article regarding the operation of bicycles, play vehicles, and unicycles on sidewalks and crosswalks, directly impacting the department's statewide transportation policy and pedestrian/bicycle safety regulations.
The MVA administers driver licensing and records, including assessing points against driving privileges when sidewalk driving or right-of-way violations occur under the Maryland Vehicle Law.
MDOT SHA designs, constructs, and maintains sidewalks, crosswalks, and pedestrian/bicycle facilities along state highways where these rules of the road and right-of-way requirements will apply.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Vehicle Law, MSP officers are responsible for enforcing bicycle and pedestrian right-of-way statutes and issuing citations.

The District Court processes traffic citations, establishes prepayment penalties, and adjudicates violations relating to the unlawful operation of vehicles on sidewalks and failure to yield right-of-way.

Synopsis: Altering the selection of the membership and chair of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council; requiring beginning on October 1, 2025, and every 2 years thereafter, the Council to elect a chair and vice chair from among the members of the Council; requiring the Council, working with certain entities, to assess and address cybersecurity threats and associated risks from artificial intelligence and quantum computing; etc.
Title: Maryland Cybersecurity Council - Alterations

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the membership and leadership structure of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council, establishing biennial elections for a chair and vice chair (one State employee and one non-State employee). It also expands the Council's duties to assess and address cybersecurity threats and privacy risks associated with artificial intelligence and quantum computing across critical infrastructure.
responsible_party: Maryland Cybersecurity Council
stakeholders: State residents, cybersecurity businesses, higher education institutions, critical infrastructure providers (energy, water, banking, and healthcare), and state and federal cybersecurity agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Any reimbursements for additional Council members are minimal and absorbable within existing budgets. State revenues and local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the membership, leadership structure, and statutory duties of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council, an executive advisory and coordinating body.

Under current law, the Attorney General or designee chairs the Maryland Cybersecurity Council; the bill alters the chair structure to an elected position and maintains the Attorney General's council membership.

The Secretary of Information Technology is a statutory member of the council, and the agency is directly impacted by the council's expanded duties concerning artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and critical cyber infrastructure.
The bill explicitly adds the People's Counsel, or their designee, as a designated member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.

The bill explicitly designates multiple USM institution leaders (including the presidents of Bowie State, UMB, UMBC, and UMCP, the Dean of UMGC's cybersecurity school, and two appointments by the Chancellor) as council members. UMGC also historically staffs the council.
The bill explicitly designates the President of Morgan State University, or their designee, as a member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Chief Executive Officer of TEDCO, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of Emergency Management, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council and provided information for the fiscal note.
The Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Homeland Security, or their designee, is a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The State Administrator of Elections, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of State Police, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Adjutant General, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Secretary of Commerce, or their designee, serves as a statutory member of the Maryland Cybersecurity Council.
The Governor's Office oversees executive branch policy and was consulted as an information source regarding the changes to executive council structures.

Synopsis: Imposing assessments of 12 points for certain subsequent drunk and drugged driving violations.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Drunk and Drugged Driving - Points Assessments

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to assess 12 points against the driver's license of an individual convicted of repeat drunk or drugged driving violations under § 21-902(h) or § 21-902(i) of the Transportation Article, subjecting their license to revocation.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Drivers convicted of repeat drunk or drugged driving offenses in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency directly responsible for assessing the 12 points on drivers' licenses following convictions under § 21-902(h) and (i) and issuing corresponding license revocations.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees vehicle laws, driver licensing administration, and highway safety policy.

The Judiciary processes subsequent offender drunk and drugged driving criminal convictions under the Transportation Article, which must then be transmitted to the Motor Vehicle Administration for points assessment.

Individuals subject to license revocation resulting from the accumulation of 12 points have the right to request an administrative hearing, which is typically adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

Synopsis: Exempting personal property used in connection with certain large family child care homes from valuation and taxation; authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or a municipal corporation to grant, by law, a property tax credit against the real property tax owed on the portion of real property used for certain large family child care homes; increasing the maximum amount of a property tax credit that may be granted for certain child care homes and centers and day care centers; etc.
Title: Property Tax - Day Care Centers, Child Care Homes, and Child Care Centers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
