bill_summary: This bill exempts personal property used in connection with large family child care homes from property valuation and taxation. It also expands eligibility for optional local real property tax credits to include large family child care homes, eliminates previous construction completion date requirements for eligibility, and increases or establishes the maximum local real property tax credit limit at $10,000 per year.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Operators and owners of registered large family child care homes, family child care homes, licensed child care centers, adult and elderly day care centers, and county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues may decrease minimally starting in FY 2026 due to the personal property tax exemption for large family child care homes (estimated at approximately $7,500 annually in Worcester County) and to the extent local jurisdictions authorize, expand eligibility for, or increase the value of real property tax credits up to the new $10,000 cap. Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands property tax exemptions and local tax credit eligibility for family child care homes, large family child care homes, and child care centers registered or licensed under Title 9.5 of the Education Article, which is administered and regulated by the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE). MSDE also tracks licensing data for these facilities.

Synopsis: Authorizing an owner of real property used for rental housing and the governing body of a county to enter into a payment in lieu of taxes agreement for maintaining at least 25% of the rental housing units located at the real property as affordable dwelling units for at least 15 years; and authorizing the governing body of the county to require the owner of real property to maintain a higher percentage of rental housing units as affordable dwelling units than the minimum percentage specified in the Act.
Title: Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes

bill_summary: The Affordable Housing Payment In Lieu of Taxes Expansion Act authorizes county governing bodies to exempt rental housing real property from county property taxes if the property owner enters into a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreement. Under the agreement, the owner must agree to pay a negotiated amount and maintain at least 25% of the rental units as affordable dwelling units for at least 15 years.
responsible_party: Governing bodies of Maryland counties
stakeholders: Rental property owners, developers, low-income tenants earning 60% or less of area median income, and county governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal year 2026 to the extent that eligible rental properties are granted property tax exemptions, though any reduction will be mitigated by negotiated PILOT payments. Specific dollar estimates are indeterminate and depend on the number and assessed value of participating properties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes statutory criteria for affordable rental housing payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements to incentivize and preserve affordable housing units, which directly aligns with DHCD's primary mission of expanding and supporting affordable rental housing throughout Maryland.

The bill references definitions codified in the Land Use Article regarding affordable dwelling units and area median income; while the department has no direct administrative mandate under the bill, it provides land use guidance and data to local jurisdictions.

Synopsis: Altering a certain loan program to authorize the Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation to provide loans in an amount up to $25,000 for certain seasonal full-time jobs; and reducing, from 5 years to 3 years, the number of years that a person must have been a licensed seafood dealer in order to be eligible to receive financing under the loan program.
Title: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation - Oyster Shucking House Loan Program

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program administered by MARBIDCO by increasing the maximum loan amount from $10,000 to $25,000 per seasonal full-time job projected to be created or retained, and by reducing the eligibility requirement for licensed seafood dealers from five years of licensure to three years.
responsible_party: Maryland Agricultural and Resource-Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO)
stakeholders: Licensed seafood dealers, oyster processing facilities and shucking houses, and seasonal or full-time seafood industry workers in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: Nonbudgeted expenditures and subsequent revenues for MARBIDCO increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that expanding eligibility and loan limits increases lending activity under the program, which currently has $750,000 in available funds remaining from a prior appropriation. The bill does not alter State general fund appropriations, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Agricultural & Resource-Based Industry Development Corp.
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MARBIDCO is the primary implementing agency for the Oyster Shucking House Loan Program. The bill directly alters MARBIDCO's loan terms by increasing the allowable loan amount per seasonal full-time job to $25,000 and expanding applicant eligibility by lowering the seafood dealer licensing tenure requirement.

DNR oversees the licensing of seafood dealers and tidal fish license holders who are eligible for the program, and acts as the receiving and verifying entity for oyster shells and spat-on-shell plantings tied to statutory loan forgiveness.

bill_summary: Increases the higher education scholarship awarded to a student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education who completes a full term from $8,000 to $15,000.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of Education
stakeholders: Student members of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education who complete a full term
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $7,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2025 to fund the increased scholarship award. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Education Article regarding the scholarship compensation for the student member of the Anne Arundel County Board of Education. The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and local school boards, though the bill has no state fiscal impact and solely affects local county expenditures.

Synopsis: Altering the appointment process for licensed hearing aid dispenser members of the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists by requiring the Board to notify all licensed hearing aid dispensers in the State of the vacancy and to solicit nominations to fill the vacancy.

bill_summary: Alters the appointment process for licensed hearing aid dispenser members of the State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists by requiring the Board, rather than an external professional society, to notify all licensed hearing aid dispensers in Maryland of vacancies and submit a list of nominees to the Secretary of Health and the Governor.
responsible_party: State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists
stakeholders: Licensed hearing aid dispensers in Maryland, members of the Board, and the Hearing Society of Maryland, Washington, D.C., and Delaware.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal impact because it is procedural in nature and does not materially affect State finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Examiners for Audiologists, Hearing Aid Dispensers, Speech-Language Pathologists, and Music Therapists is a health occupations board housed within the Maryland Department of Health, and the Secretary of Health provides advice to the Governor regarding board appointments.
The Governor is statutorily responsible for appointing the hearing aid dispenser members to the board from the list submitted by the board.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in administering appointments to state boards and commissions, including vetting candidates and processing board vacancies.

responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: The part-time deputy chief inspector for Anne Arundel County and the Anne Arundel County government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Anne Arundel County expenditures increase by $9,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to fund the salary increase. Local revenues are not affected.

bill_summary: Designates chromite as the official State mineral of Maryland.
responsible_party: State of Maryland
stakeholders: Maryland residents, educators, historians, and geologists.
fiscal_impact_summary: Designating a State mineral does not materially affect State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Archives is responsible for documenting official State symbols and maintaining the Maryland Manual On-Line, which catalogues official designations such as the State mineral. It was also the primary information source for the bill's fiscal and policy note.

Synopsis: Requiring each local board of elections to make available on its website each open meeting agenda, a summary of any finalized documents, certain written testimony, and other materials on which the  board will be voting; requiring each local board to provide live video streaming of each open meeting and to maintain a complete and unedited archived video recording of each open meeting for 5 years; requiring the State Board of Elections to adopt regulations to ensure that the streaming requirements are met in a certain manner; etc.

bill_summary: Enacts the Local Boards of Elections Transparency Act, requiring each local board of elections to post open meeting agendas and related voting materials online at least 48 hours in advance (or as soon as practicable during emergencies), provide live video streaming of open meetings, and maintain unedited archived recordings for at least five years.
responsible_party: State Board of Elections and Maryland local boards of elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, members of the public seeking access to local election administration proceedings, and local boards of elections across Maryland counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local government expenditures increase for counties whose local election boards do not currently possess the technology or infrastructure to live stream and archive meetings for five years. Reported local one-time equipment and installation costs range from approximately $5,300 to $25,000, along with recurring annual streaming, licensing, or storage fees ranging from $250 to $2,000 for certain counties.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 412 directly tasks the State Board of Elections with adopting regulations by December 1, 2025, to ensure the uniform implementation of enhanced open meeting and live video streaming requirements across all local boards of elections.

Synopsis: Authorizing a person who is at least 21 years of age to manufacture a personal use amount of cannabis products or concentrated cannabis for personal use or adult sharing at a private residence if the manufacturing process does not involve the use of a volatile solvent; specifying that manufacturing, distributing, dispensing, or possessing certain large quantities of certain controlled dangerous substances is a felony; altering the penalties for being a volume dealer and drug kingpin with regard to cannabis; etc.
Title: Criminal Law - Controlled Dangerous Substances and Firearms

bill_summary: House Bill 413 allows individuals 21 years of age and older to manufacture personal use amounts of cannabis products or concentrated cannabis at home without the use of volatile solvents. It establishes reduced penalties and removes mandatory minimums for cannabis-related volume dealer and drug kingpin offenses, while establishing that non-cannabis volume dealer offenses are felonies. In addition, the bill allows certain incarcerated individuals serving mandatory minimum sentences for cannabis or cocaine base offenses to apply for sentence reductions, and reclassifies several firearms-related offenses from misdemeanors to felonies with increased penalties.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
stakeholders: Individuals aged 21 and older producing personal use cannabis, individuals incarcerated or facing charges for volume dealer or drug kingpin offenses involving cannabis or cocaine base, individuals charged with illegal firearm trafficking, manufacturing, or possession of stolen/unserialized firearms, public defenders, prosecutors, and state correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Public Defender increase by up to $95,726 in FY 2026 (and up to $130,500 by FY 2030) to hire one assistant public defender to handle increased workloads from sentence modification applications. Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services expenditures and overall state revenues are not materially affected, though minimal fine revenue shifts may occur between the District Court and circuit courts. Local State's Attorneys' offices and circuit courts may experience minor operational impacts from processing and hearing sentence modification motions, but no material local fiscal impact is expected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Office of the Public Defender by authorizing incarcerated individuals to file applications for sentence modifications and reductions for certain cannabis and cocaine base offenses, leading to increased attorney caseloads and an estimated general fund expenditure increase of $95,700 to $130,500 annually.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters criminal penalties, eliminates mandatory minimums for cannabis volume dealers and drug kingpins, establishes sentence modification procedures for currently incarcerated individuals, and creates felony incarceration penalties for certain firearms offenses, impacting inmate populations and term lengths under DPSCS custody.

The bill requires Maryland courts to process applications and conduct hearings for sentence modifications, while also shifting caseloads between District Court and Circuit Court due to the reclassification of various firearm offenses to felonies and certain cannabis volume dealer offenses to misdemeanors.

The bill alters criminal classifications and penalties for firearms offenses under Title 5 of the Public Safety Article, which includes provisions governing handgun rosters, serial number marking, and regulated firearms trafficking overseen and enforced by the Maryland State Police.

The bill amends statutory thresholds and criminal provisions regarding the manufacturing of cannabis products and concentrated cannabis for personal use and adult sharing, which aligns with the broader regulatory framework overseen by the Maryland Cannabis Administration.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary coordinating body for Maryland's criminal justice policies and public safety strategies, the agency is affected by substantive changes to sentencing laws, mandatory minimums, and firearms offense penalties.

Synopsis: Establishing the Family Literacy Pilot Program administered by the State Library Agency in consultation with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Correctional Education Council to enable certain incarcerated individuals to read aloud to their children by preparing a recording; and requiring the State Library Agency to submit a certain report on or before December 1, 2028.
Title: State Library Agency - Family Literacy Pilot Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Public Safety and Correctional Services, Department of

bill_summary: House Bill 415 establishes the Family Literacy Pilot Program, administered by the Maryland State Library Agency in consultation with the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Correctional Education Council. The program provides children's books to incarcerated individuals at four selected State correctional facility libraries or prerelease centers and enables them to record themselves reading aloud, distributing the book and recording to their children free of charge.
responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in participating Maryland correctional facilities and prerelease centers, along with their children and custodial parents or guardians.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $69,200 in FY 2026, $70,800 in FY 2027, $73,800 in FY 2028, and $38,500 in FY 2029 to support one contractual program administrator within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services as well as supplies, books, and recording equipment for the Maryland State Library Agency. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency is the primary administrator of the newly established Family Literacy Pilot Program, tasked with selecting books, developing program processes, and submitting a final report to the General Assembly.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is required to consult on the program's establishment, host the pilot program across four of its correctional facilities or prerelease centers, and incurs fiscal costs for contractual personnel to administer the program on-site.

The Correctional Education Council, which is required to consult on the selection of facilities and implementation processes for the pilot program, is housed under the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Workforce Development and Adult Learning.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Correctional Education Council, an advisory and governing body under joint jurisdiction of MD Labor and DPSCS, is specifically mandated by the bill to consult on selecting facilities and designing the literacy pilot program.

Synopsis: Altering the defined term "auto-injectable epinephrine" to be "emergency use epinephrine" and to include certain drug delivery devices and products; and altering the name of the Emergency Use Auto-Injectable Epinephrine Program to be the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program.
Title: Education and Health - Emergency Use Epinephrine - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.

bill_summary: Replaces the term 'auto-injectable epinephrine' with 'emergency use epinephrine' across the Education, Health - General, and Health Occupations articles of the Maryland Code, expanding authorization to cover FDA-approved non-injectable epinephrine delivery devices and products (such as nasal sprays). It also renames the Emergency Use Auto-Injectable Epinephrine Program to the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program and extends legal protections and protocols to non-injectable emergency epinephrine use in schools, youth camps, child care facilities, and participating food service facilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals experiencing severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis), public and nonpublic school staff and students, youth camp operators and attendees, child care providers, higher education and food service facilities, and healthcare professionals authorized to prescribe or dispense epinephrine.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can update existing program regulations, procedures, and materials using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) administers the Emergency and Allergy Treatment Program for youth camps and the Emergency Use Epinephrine Program for participating facilities. MDH is responsible for issuing certificates, collecting incident reports, and updating regulations and materials to incorporate newly approved FDA non-injectable epinephrine products.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees public school and child care policies under the Education Article amended by the bill, including developing and disseminating the standard reporting form for emergency epinephrine incidents in public schools and maintaining guidelines for child care settings.

Synopsis: Authorizing the use of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund for certain expenditures that support the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline; and altering a certain restriction on the use of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to prohibit funds from being used for expenses solely related to the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline, instead of preventing the use of funds for any costs associated with the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline.
Title: Public Safety - 9-1-1 Trust Fund - 9-8-8 Suicide Prevention Hotline

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to cover expenditures for activities shared between the 9-1-1 emergency system and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline, such as software interfaces and joint training, while prohibiting 9-1-1 Trust Fund monies from being used for expenses that solely support the 9-8-8 hotline.
responsible_party: Maryland 9-1-1 Board within the Maryland Department of Emergency Management
stakeholders: Emergency telecommunications personnel, 9-1-1 public safety answering points, 9-8-8 crisis response centers, and individuals using Maryland's emergency and crisis hotline services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures from the 9-1-1 Trust Fund will increase minimally to cover shared activities and projects; however, administrative efficiencies are expected and may decrease expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. Revenues are unaffected, and there is no material fiscal or operational impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and manages the 9-1-1 Trust Fund. The bill directly alters the statutory purposes of the 9-1-1 Trust Fund to authorize expenditures for shared operations, software interfaces, and joint training between 9-1-1 systems and the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline.

MDH administers the 9-8-8 suicide prevention hotline and the 9-8-8 Trust Fund. The bill allows joint 9-1-1 and 9-8-8 initiatives to be funded through the 9-1-1 Trust Fund, which creates operational efficiencies and may reduce expenditures from the 9-8-8 Trust Fund.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Maryland 9-1-1 Board to adopt regulations to implement and enforce certain responsibilities of the Board; and authorizing the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to adopt regulations to implement and enforce the responsibilities of the Department.
Title: Public Safety - Maryland 9-1-1 Board and Maryland Department of Emergency Management - Regulatory Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Emergency Services -see also- Ambul; Emergencies; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management to adopt regulations to implement and enforce their respective statutory responsibilities.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Emergency Management and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board
stakeholders: Emergency management personnel, 9-1-1 specialists and operators, local public safety answering points (PSAPs), local governments, and Maryland residents relying on 9-1-1 and emergency services.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The Department of Emergency Management and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board can handle the regulatory responsibilities using existing budgeted resources, and local government operations and finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 423 directly grants statutory regulatory authority to the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM) and the Maryland 9-1-1 Board, which is housed within MDEM, allowing them to adopt regulations to implement and enforce their statutory responsibilities.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council; requiring the Prescription Drug Affordability Board, under certain circumstances, to establish a process for setting upper payment limits for purchases and payor reimbursements of prescription drug products that the Board determines have led or will lead to affordability challenges; authorizing the Board to reconsider an upper payment limit for a drug that becomes a current shortage; and altering requirements related to the setting of upper payment limits.
Title: Prescription Drug Affordability Board - Authority and Stakeholder Council Membership (Lowering Prescription Drug Costs for All Marylanders Now Act)

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill expands and alters the authority of the Maryland Prescription Drug Affordability Board (PDAB) to establish upper payment limits (UPLs) for prescription drug products that present affordability challenges. It updates criteria for setting UPLs (including considerations for drug shortages, rare diseases, and 340B providers), expands the membership of the Stakeholder Council, establishes new reporting requirements on the market impact of UPLs, and creates a contingent process to expand UPLs to commercial purchases and payor reimbursements across the State if specified conditions are met by September 30, 2030.
responsible_party: Prescription Drug Affordability Board
stakeholders: Prescription drug consumers in Maryland, pharmaceutical manufacturers, pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs), health insurance carriers, wholesale distributors, retail and independent pharmacies, 340B covered entities, rare disease patients, and state/local government health programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General increase by $106,700 in FY 2026, rising to $146,300 by FY 2030 for an additional Assistant Attorney General. PDAB special fund expenditures and fee revenues increase by at least $264,900 in FY 2027 (and approximately $273,300 by FY 2030) for personnel and contractual services, funded through an increased annual assessment fee on pharmaceutical manufacturers, PBMs, carriers, and wholesale distributors. Local governments may realize minimal cost savings on prescription drug spending once UPLs take effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly increases general fund expenditures for the Office of the Attorney General (OAG) by $106,700 in FY 2026 and over $128,000 annually thereafter to hire a full-time Assistant Attorney General to provide legal advice, draft regulations, and defend against potential litigation regarding upper payment limits. Additionally, the Attorney General shares approval authority with the Governor over PDAB's plan of action if not approved by the Legislative Policy Committee.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid). The bill explicitly requires the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to confer with Medicaid before setting an upper payment limit applicable to the program to evaluate federal rebate compliance and state budget impacts.

DBM has a designated representative on the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council and administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, whose prescription drug purchasing and formularies are impacted by upper payment limits set by the Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the composition and membership of the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council, adding representatives for the rare disease community, oncologists, and patient advocacy organizations.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members of the Stakeholder Council (including a new patient advocacy representative) and holds statutory authority to approve the Board's plan of action alongside the Attorney General if the Legislative Policy Committee does not approve it.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and processing appointments to state boards and councils, including the newly added gubernatorial appointment to the Prescription Drug Affordability Stakeholder Council.
The bill repeals obsolete statutory language requiring the Prescription Drug Affordability Board to repay start-up funds to the Maryland Health Care Commission, as repayment has been completed.

Synopsis: Exempting certain auctioneers from certain provisions of the State Boat Act.
Title: Natural Resources - State Boat Act - Auctioneers

Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Exempts licensed auctioneers from the definition of a boat dealer under the State Boat Act when they act on behalf of a seller, secured party, or owner, provided title does not pass to the auctioneer and the auction is not intended to evade the provisions of the Act.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Licensed auctioneers, vessel owners, secured parties and lienholders, and Maryland boat dealers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances and has no local effect. While boat dealers pay an annual $25 license fee, the Department of Natural Resources notes there are currently only eight auctioneers licensed as boat dealers, resulting in a negligible fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) administers the State Boat Act, which governs the licensing and regulation of boat dealers and the collection of vessel excise taxes. This bill alters the definition of 'dealer' under the Act to exempt certain licensed auctioneers, directly impacting DNR's licensing jurisdiction and regulatory oversight.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Elections, in collaboration with the local boards of elections, to conduct a risk-limiting audit after each statewide election; authorizing the State Board, in collaboration with the local boards, to conduct a risk-limiting audit after a special general election; authorizing the State Board, in collaboration with the local boards, to conduct an automated software audit after a statewide election; authorizing a local board to conduct a risk-limiting audit of a local contest under certain circumstances; etc.
Title: Election Law - Postelection Tabulation Audits - Risk-Limiting Audits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 426 requires the State Board of Elections, in collaboration with local boards of elections, to conduct a postelection risk-limiting audit of at least one statewide contest and any other selected contests following each statewide election prior to certification. It also authorizes local boards to conduct risk-limiting audits of local contests, allows risk-limiting audits after special general elections, makes postelection automated software audits permissive rather than mandatory, and repeals the requirement for a separate manual audit after each statewide general election.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, local boards of elections, election staff, and candidates running in statewide and local contests.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $77,000 in FY 2026, $72,000 in FY 2027, and $51,000 in FY 2028 and future years to cover software fees and consultant support. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 due to personnel and operational costs to carry out the audits, though some savings may offset costs during general election years from the repeal of previous manual audit requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly tasks the State Board of Elections (SBE), in collaboration with local boards, with implementing and conducting risk-limiting postelection tabulation audits following statewide elections. SBE must adopt regulations establishing criteria, audit methods, and risk limits, and the fiscal note outlines direct general fund expenditures incurred by SBE for software and consulting services.

Synopsis: Authorizing the State Board of Public Accountancy to place a licensee on emeritus status under certain circumstances; and requiring the Board to reinstate the license of an individual who is on emeritus status under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Board of Public Accountancy to place an individual on emeritus status if they meet specified experience, age, and disciplinary standing requirements and attest to being retired. Licensees on emeritus status are exempt from continuing education requirements and reinstatement fees, may use the title "CPA Emeritus," but are prohibited from actively practicing certified public accountancy or offering related services unless properly reinstated.
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
stakeholders: Retired or long-serving certified public accountants in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures for the State Board of Public Accountancy are likely not materially affected, as the bill is assumed to apply in a limited number of cases. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Public Accountancy is a regulatory licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Department of Labor is directly responsible for administering the new emeritus licensing status, processing applications, and issuing certificates.

Synopsis: Establishing certain requirements for a complaint for a money judgment; defining "medical debt" as a debt owed by a consumer to a provider of medical services, products, or devices, but does not include debt charged to a credit card except under certain circumstances; prohibiting the creation of a lien on owner-occupied residential property by contract or as a result of a breach of contract for the payment of medical debt; and applying the Act prospectively.

bill_summary: Prohibits the creation of a lien on owner-occupied residential property by contract or as a result of a breach of contract for the payment of medical debt, and requires courts to remove any lien created in violation. Additionally, requires complaints for a money judgment to indicate whether the judgment sought is for medical debt and include the address of the defendant's primary residence.
responsible_party: Judiciary of Maryland
stakeholders: Consumers and homeowners with medical debt, health care providers, medical debt collectors, and the Maryland court system.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal and Policy Note, the bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is anticipated to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies court procedures under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article by requiring complaints for money judgments to specify if the claim is for medical debt and include the defendant's primary residence, altering judgment lien indexing rules, and mandating that courts remove prohibited liens.

bill_summary: This bill establishes that any provision in a consumer contract that sets a shorter time limitation to bring an action than otherwise required under Maryland law is against public policy, illegal, and void. Violations are classified as unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practices under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, enforceable by civil remedies and penalties. The bill exempts certain regulated utility services, businesses operating under specific state/local authorizations, and licensed security system service providers, and applies prospectively to contracts entered into on or after the effective date.

stakeholders: Maryland consumers entering into consumer contracts, as well as businesses that issue or enter into consumer contracts for personal, family, or household goods and services.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not directly affect State or local government operations or finances. The impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that a violation of its provisions constitutes an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to the enforcement and penalty provisions under Title 13 of the Commercial Law Article, which is administered and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

Synopsis: Altering the definition of "private place" as it relates to the prohibition on conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent of an individual without the consent of the individual to include a residence; and altering the prohibition against conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent.
Title: Criminal Law - Visual Surveillance With Prurient Intent - Modifications
bill_summary: This bill expands the criminal prohibition against conducting visual surveillance with prurient intent by adding residences and other places of private use or accommodation to the definition of a protected "private place." It also clarifies that surreptitious camera surveillance of an individual's private areas without consent is illegal regardless of the person's location.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services and the Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Individuals whose privacy is protected in residences and private accommodations, victims of surreptitious surveillance, criminal offenders, law enforcement, and state and local correctional systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues may experience a minimal increase from fines assessed in the District Court and circuit courts (up to $2,500 per violation). State and local expenditures may experience a minimal increase due to expanded incarceration penalties of up to one year, with local detention per diem costs ranging from approximately $140 to $350 per incarcerated individual. Specific aggregate dollar figures are not specified.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands criminal liability for visual surveillance with prurient intent and maintains a civil cause of action, directly impacting caseloads, trial proceedings, and fine collection within Maryland District and Circuit Courts.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill subjects offenders to penalties including up to one year of imprisonment and probation, impacting the Division of Correction, the Baltimore Pretrial Complex, and the Division of Parole and Probation for supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because violation of the statute carries a potential penalty of incarceration for up to one year, the Office of the Public Defender will be responsible for providing legal representation to indigent defendants charged under the expanded offense.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency enforcing the Maryland Criminal Law Article, the State Police is responsible for investigating allegations of illegal visual surveillance and enforcing criminal penalties.

The Administrative Office of the Courts provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Judiciary, which will hear and adjudicate criminal prosecutions and civil suits arising under the bill's provisions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender

bill_summary: Establishes the Invasive Blue Catfish Pilot Program within the Department of Natural Resources to curb the spread of invasive blue catfish in the Chesapeake Bay and tributaries. The program authorizes eligible participants to conduct for-hire and commercial fishing trips simultaneously, permits the expanded use of finfish trotlines south of the Chesapeake Bay Bridge, directs the department to consider gear and harvest practice modifications such as electrofishing and longer trotlines, and requires a report on findings and recommendations by December 1, 2025.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial fishermen, for-hire fishing charter operators, seafood processors, and Maryland tidal fisheries businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not affected, as the Department of Natural Resources can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources because it establishes programs the department is already in the process of implementing. There is no local government fiscal impact. Small commercial fishing and seafood processing businesses may experience a meaningful positive impact from increased catfish harvest opportunities.

The bill mandates that the Department of Natural Resources report its findings and recommendations regarding the pilot program directly to the Governor by December 1, 2025.

bill_summary: The Modernization of Military Laws Act updates and standardizes military-related definitions across Maryland law by referencing the U.S. Code, expanding classifications of uniformed services to include bodies such as the Public Health Service and NOAA. The act eliminates the state residency requirement for certain veterans seeking burial in State veterans' cemeteries, expands cemetery eligibility to qualified reserve members and their families, updates housing and employment discrimination protections, and requires the Department of Veterans and Military Families to develop transition policies and annual reporting on service members.
responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Veterans, active service members, reserve component members, commissioned officers of the Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and their families.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general and federal fund expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 due to additional burials at State veterans' cemeteries. Costs for burying non-resident veterans are reimbursed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. Burials of qualified reserve members and their dependents require collection of a fee matching the federal plot allowance ($948 as of August 2024), offsetting those expenditures. General fund expenditures for newly eligible PHS and NOAA officers and certain dependents increase by an indeterminate amount because no fee is charged. Local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the Department of Veterans and Military Families as the primary implementing agency, expanding eligibility and altering fee structures for burial in State veterans' cemeteries, removing residency requirements for certain veterans, expanding annual reporting requirements, and requiring the Secretary to develop coordinated policies for service members and veterans undergoing life transitions.

The bill amends the Election Law Article regarding voter registration, absentee voting definitions, use of common access cards, and qualifications for filing certificates of candidacy remotely for members of the uniformed services.

The bill expands the definition of 'military status' under Title 20 of the State Government Article to include reserve components of the uniformed services (such as the Reserve Corps of the Public Health Service), expanding the protected class under state employment and housing anti-discrimination laws enforced by the Commission.

The bill amends statutory language governing the Governor's authority as commander-in-chief of the state militia relative to active service in the uniformed services and requires expanded reporting directly to the Governor regarding active service members.
The bill reenacts provisions governing the acquisition of land for State veterans' cemeteries, which requires the formal approval of the Board of Public Works.

bill_summary: This bill expands existing restrictions on using State funds for permanent outdoor lighting to include lighting on the grounds of State parks and trails, while exempting lighting used for sports facility fields. It requires non-MDOT luminaires installed or replaced with State funds to have a correlated light temperature of 3,000 Kelvins or less (subject to Board of Public Works waivers), directs the Maryland Green Building Council to update or develop outdoor lighting guidance considering American Medical Association recommendations by October 1, 2026, and requires the Maryland Department of Transportation to review highway lighting practices by September 30, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Green Building Council, Board of Public Works, and Maryland Department of Transportation
stakeholders: State agencies acquiring outdoor lighting, Maryland Department of Transportation, visitors to State buildings, parks, and trails, motorists, and outdoor lighting contractors and suppliers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to be materially affected due to existing waiver procedures and the prospective application of the bill. The Maryland Department of Transportation can conduct its review of highway lighting practices using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on State revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT is explicitly tasked with conducting a review of highway lighting practices by September 30, 2026, considering alterations inconsistent with Federal Highway Administration guidelines. The bill also specifies unique statutory exemptions tailored to MDOT operations and equipment.

DGS provides administrative and operational support to the Maryland Green Building Council, which is required to update or develop outdoor lighting guidance by October 1, 2026. DGS also manages state facilities, oversees state procurement of lighting, and exercises delegated waiver authority from the Board of Public Works.

The bill authorizes the Board of Public Works (or its designees) to establish waiver criteria and review and grant waivers for the new correlated color temperature and restricted uplight luminaire requirements.
The bill broadens the restrictions on using State funds for outdoor luminaires to explicitly encompass State parks and trails, which are owned, operated, and maintained by DNR.

As the MDOT administration responsible for state highways and roadway infrastructure, SHA will be directly involved in the required review of highway lighting practices under Federal Highway Administration standards.

The bill creates a specific statutory exemption from the lighting restrictions for luminaires used to illuminate the field of play at sports facilities, directly relevant to MSA's sports venue operations.

USM operates extensive campus grounds and outdoor facilities subject to State building lighting restrictions and holds delegated authority from the Board of Public Works to review and grant lighting waivers.

bill_summary: The James 'Jimmy' Malone Act requires Maryland counties that offer self-insured employee health benefit plans to provide county-employed firefighters with coverage for preventive cancer screenings without copayments, coinsurance, or deductibles, adhering to International Association of Fire Fighters guidelines. Counties may fulfill this requirement through a no-cost annual exam or by applying for a state grant for innovative cancer screening technologies. Counties must collect and report screening and cost data to the Maryland Health Care Commission, which must evaluate expanding coverage to the commercial insurance market.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission and Maryland County Governments
stakeholders: County-employed professional firefighters and Maryland county governments that offer self-insured health plans.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $100,000 in FY 2029 only for the Maryland Health Care Commission to complete a required study; state revenues are unaffected. Local government health insurance expenditures may increase for counties with self-insured plans employing firefighters to provide screenings without cost-sharing, though counties can fulfill the requirement by applying for existing grant funds and data reporting can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 459 directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission receive cancer screening data reports from counties in 2027 and 2028, conduct a study on expanding coverage to the commercial insurance market, and submit a final report to the General Assembly by December 1, 2028, with an estimated $100,000 fiscal impact in FY 2029.

The bill allows counties to satisfy the cancer screening mandate by applying for grants under the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program (Health - General Article Title 13, Subtitle 40), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health. Additionally, the Maryland Health Care Commission operates as an independent commission within MDH.

stakeholders: Certain driver's license applicants (specifically out-of-country drivers qualifying without a learner's permit), students enrolled in driver education, and certified private driver education providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Motor Vehicle Administration can implement the bill's requirements using existing resources, and State revenues are not affected. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MVA is the primary agency responsible for establishing the 3-hour Roadway Safety Driving Education Program, determining course content, and adopting regulations to certify private entities to offer the program.
MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the state's transportation administration and motor vehicle safety policies.
The bill mandates that MVA establish the program in cooperation with the Behavioral Health Administration, an agency within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing public health, the regulation of health occupations, and housing vouchers and assistance to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Health Equality for Service Members Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: The Health Equality for Service Members Act standardizes definitions relating to military and uniformed services across Maryland law by referencing federal definitions. It expands eligibility for certain state benefits, rights, and administrative procedures—such as expedited health occupations licensing, vital records fee waivers, housing voucher prioritization, and continued eligibility for Medicaid and developmental disability waiver services—to encompass all members of the uniformed services, specifically including the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, rather than only the armed forces.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health (including health occupations licensing boards), Maryland Department of Housing and Community Development, and Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Active-duty service members, veterans, and military families, particularly members of the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Officer Corps, as well as health occupation license applicants and licensees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected, as the expansion applies to a relatively small population (primarily PHS and NOAA personnel) relative to the existing veteran population in Maryland. Any operational or workload changes can be absorbed within existing agency resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency for multiple sections of the bill, including vital records fee exemptions, Developmental Disabilities Administration waitlist protections, Medicaid waiver programs, behavioral health coordination and grants, and oversight of health occupations licensing boards.

The bill amends the core definitions in Title 9, Subtitle 9 of the State Government Article governing DVMF, expands the scope of veterans and uniformed service members covered, and requires DVMF collaboration regarding behavioral health coordination and uniformed services culture coursework.

The bill amends the Housing and Community Development Article (§ 4-2906) to alter the definition and prioritization of housing vouchers and assistance payments for veterans and uniformed service members.

MSDE administers the Autism Waiver registry and services program, which is amended by the bill (§ 15-154) to protect the registry status and eligibility of children whose families relocate out of state due to uniformed services assignments.
The bill alters the Certificate of Need (CON) exemption criteria for comprehensive care facilities serving veterans under Health-General § 19-114, which falls under MHCC's regulatory oversight.

The bill explicitly references the Maryland National Guard in provisions requiring interagency collaboration with MDH to provide behavioral health service coordination for eligible veterans and service members.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the Maryland National Guard and Maryland Defense Force (both of which are statutory partners in the behavioral health service coordination provisions), the Adjutant General's operational scope aligns with the bill's expanded service member provisions.

Synopsis: Altering references to the Annapolis and Anne Arundel County Conference and Visitors Bureau to be Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc.
Title: Local Government - Annapolis and Anne Arundel County Conference and Visitors Bureau Designation
bill_summary: Updates statutory references in the Local Government Article regarding Anne Arundel County hotel tax distributions, annual reporting, and county audits by changing the name of the Annapolis and Anne Arundel County Conference and Visitors Bureau to Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County
stakeholders: Visit Annapolis and Anne Arundel County, Inc., the City of Annapolis, Anne Arundel County government, and local tourism organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no State fiscal effect and is not expected to materially affect Anne Arundel County finances or operations, as it solely updates obsolete organizational name references.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from obscuring or modifying any vehicle registration plate in a manner that may prevent identification and enforcing the prohibition as a secondary offense; prohibiting a person from advertising for or promoting the sale of an unlawful registration plate cover by falsely claiming that the registration plate cover is lawful in the State; and establishing that a violation of the Act is an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice subject to certain enforcement and penalties.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Obscured, Modified, or Blocked Registration Plates and Registration Plate Covers

bill_summary: This bill modifies Maryland vehicle laws by prohibiting individuals from obscuring or modifying a vehicle registration plate in a manner that may prevent identification, making enforcement of this violation a secondary offense. It also amends the definition of a registration plate cover, prohibits advertising or promoting the sale of unlawful covers by falsely claiming they are legal in the State, and classifies such false advertising as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division) and State and local law enforcement agencies
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners and drivers in Maryland, retailers and advertisers of vehicle registration plate covers, consumers, and law enforcement officers
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not materially affected, and the bill can likely be implemented and enforced using existing budgeted State resources. Local government finances and operations are also not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the false advertising or promotion of unlawful registration plate covers as an unfair, abusive, or deceptive trade practice under the Maryland Consumer Protection Act, which is investigated and enforced by the Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General.

As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle laws and highway safety, the Maryland State Police is directly responsible for enforcing the bill's provisions on obscured registration plates, including the requirement that it be enforced only as a secondary offense.

The MVA regulates vehicle registration plates and assesses driver's license points for moving violations under § 16-402, which applies to violations of the prohibition on obscuring or modifying registration plates.
The Maryland Department of Transportation is the parent department overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and the administration of the Maryland Vehicle Law altered by this bill.
The District Court and Judiciary process traffic citations, track prepayable fines, and adjudicate cases related to motor vehicle registration plate violations.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in a certain area of the 45th alcoholic beverages district in Baltimore City under certain circumstances; and altering a geographic boundary in the 45th district within which the holder of a Class A or Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor license must operate in accordance with specified hours.
Title: Baltimore City - Alcoholic Beverages - 45th Alcoholic Beverages District - Licenses
bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C beer, wine, and liquor license in the 400 block of East Oliver Street in the 45th alcoholic beverages district under specified conditions, including executing a memorandum of understanding with the Greenmount West Community Association. It also establishes a defined geographic boundary in the 45th district where holders of Class A and Class B-D-7 beer, wine, and liquor licenses are limited to sales between 9:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage license applicants and holders of Class A, Class B-D-7, and Class C licenses in the 45th alcoholic beverages district of Baltimore City, patrons, and the Greenmount West Community Association.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City finances and operations are not materially affected, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland oversees state regulation of the alcohol industry. While the bill specifically alters local licensing and hours of operation administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners, it falls within the broader statutory framework governing alcoholic beverages in the state.

Synopsis: Altering the number of years that a recipient of an award under the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program may hold the award under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program to allow part-time associate's degree students to receive scholarship awards for up to six years, while maintaining a three-year maximum duration for full-time associate's degree candidates. It also clarifies that students pursuing noncredit vocational certificates, certificate sequences leading to licensure or certification, or registered apprenticeship programs may receive the award for up to three years.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland community college students (specifically part-time associate's degree students, vocational and certificate students, and apprenticeship participants) and Maryland community colleges.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase by an estimated $7,000 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) to make system enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System to track differing award lengths. The bill does not change overall statutory funding for the scholarship program, though extending award durations could result in more students on waiting lists or fewer total recipients if funding limits are reached. Local community colleges and Baltimore City Community College can implement the changes with existing resources. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) oversees the State's higher education financial assistance programs, including allocating Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program funding and tracking award durations through software enhancements to the Maryland College Aid Processing System.
The Commission coordinates higher education policy and financial aid administration, including the Maryland Community College Promise Scholarship Program affected by this bill.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing transportation to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only certain uniformed services.
Title: Transportation Equality for Service Members Act

bill_summary: The Transportation Equality for Service Members Act establishes uniform statutory definitions for military and uniformed services terms across Maryland law and expands various transportation-related rights, benefits, and exemptions—such as special registration plates, driver's licensing exemptions, temporary renewals, and emissions inspection exemptions—to encompass all branches of the uniformed services, including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Active-duty service members, reservists, veterans, and military families across all branches of the uniformed services, including the U.S. Armed Forces, the Public Health Service Commissioned Corps, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Officer Corps.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances, including the Transportation Trust Fund, are not materially affected because the bill is expected to apply in a limited number of cases. Local governments experience no fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which substantively updates the Maryland Vehicle Law regarding driver's license expirations, ID renewals, special registration plates, and vehicle emissions inspection exemptions for members of all uniformed services.

The Maryland Department of Transportation oversees the Motor Vehicle Administration and administers the state's transportation laws, which are directly amended by this legislation to standardize privileges and exemptions across all uniformed services.

The bill directly amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article, which sets out foundational definitions for the Department of Veterans and Military Families, standardizing the statutory definitions of veteran, active service member, service member, and military family across state law.

The Department of the Environment jointly establishes and administers the vehicle emissions control inspection program with the Motor Vehicle Administration, and the bill amends statutory inspection exemptions for deployed uniformed service members.

Synopsis: Altering the quota for the number of Class A alcoholic beverages licenses that may be issued in the 8th election district in St. Mary's County.
Title: St. Mary's County - Alcoholic Beverages - Class A License Quota
bill_summary: This bill alters the licensing quota in St. Mary's County by decreasing the allowable concentration of Class A alcoholic beverages licenses in the 8th election district, changing the threshold from one license per 1,350 residents to one license per 4,000 residents.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Current and prospective Class A alcoholic beverage license holders and businesses in the 8th election district of St. Mary's County, as well as local consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. St. Mary's County revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent that fewer Class A licenses are renewed or issued under the restricted quota (which reduces the maximum capacity from 30 to 10 licenses). Local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the statutory quota for Class A alcoholic beverages licenses in the 8th election district of St. Mary's County. While the quota is administered locally by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, the Comptroller is the primary state entity tasked with general regulatory oversight of Maryland's alcohol industry.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Department of Education to conduct a thorough analysis of the State's regulatory framework for child care facilities with particular emphasis on regulations that limit a person's ability to register a child care facility, receive a license to operate a child care center, or operate a child care facility in a profitable manner while providing quality care; and requiring an interim and final report be submitted to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, and September 1, 2026, respectively.
Title: State Department of Education - Family Child Care Homes and Child Care Centers - Regulatory Analysis

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the State's regulatory requirements for child care facilities, including family child care homes and child care centers. The study must assess regulations impacting licensing, registration, staffing, physical standards, and operational profitability while providing quality and affordable care. MSDE must consult with key stakeholders and submit an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report with recommendations by September 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Operators and staff of child care centers, family child care homes, and large family child care homes, as well as children and families seeking child care services in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: MSDE can implement the bill's study and reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact or effect on small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting a comprehensive analysis of the State's child care facility regulations and submitting interim and final reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
The bill requires the Department of Education to submit both an interim report and a final report on the findings and recommendations of the regulatory analysis directly to the Governor.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Department consult with advisory bodies including the Office of Child Care Advisory Council and State and local early childhood advisory councils in conducting the regulatory analysis.

bill_summary: Authorizes Hagerstown Community College police officers to exercise peace and police officer powers on property outside the college within Washington County when responding to an imminent threat to life, property, or public safety, or when complying with a memorandum of understanding with another local law enforcement agency.
responsible_party: Hagerstown Community College Board of Trustees and the Hagerstown Community College Police Force
stakeholders: Hagerstown Community College students, faculty, staff, college police officers, and Washington County residents and law enforcement agencies
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none, as the bill only affects local operations. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill addresses the jurisdictional authority and mutual aid/MOU operations of the Hagerstown Community College Police Force. By statute, the college's police force standards and qualifications are set in consultation with the Secretary of State Police, and State Police operate within Washington County as an allied law enforcement agency.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill references statutory provisions requiring the Hagerstown Community College Board of Trustees to adopt standards, training, and qualifications for its police officers in consultation with the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission, which is housed within DPSCS.

The bill reenacts and updates provisions governing the Hagerstown Community College Police Force's extra-jurisdictional authority, which includes circumstances where officers are ordered to exercise police powers by the Governor.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions relating to the adoption of or revision or amendment to a county plan to county plans in St. Mary's County; and repealing certain provisions relating to public sewerage systems and water supply systems in St. Mary's County.

bill_summary: Repeals specific requirements for St. Mary's County that required additional local reviews, public hearings, and findings of fact by the St. Mary's County Planning Commission before adopting, revising, or amending county water and sewerage plans for new or expanded systems, aligning the county with standard statewide planning procedures.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: St. Mary's County local government officials, planners, developers, and residents affected by public water and sewerage planning and construction.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State operations or finances. The impact on St. Mary's County finances is minimal, primarily resulting in local operational efficiencies without materially altering county revenues or expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 480 amends Title 9, Subtitle 5 of the Environment Article, which governs county water and sewerage plans overseen and approved by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). The bill removes St. Mary's County-specific local review requirements, aligning their plan adoption process with the standard procedures regulated by MDE.

Synopsis: Adding programs, a day reporting program, an in-patient treatment program, and a pretrial release supervision program, that the St. Mary's County Sheriff is authorized to establish; repealing a requirement that the Sheriff or the Sheriff's designee collect the earnings of a certain individual participating in a certain program; and authorizing the Sheriff or the Sheriff's designee to direct an individual participating in a certain program to provide proof that the individual has made payments toward certain obligations.

bill_summary: House Bill 485 expands the types of correctional release programs the St. Mary's County Sheriff is authorized to establish to include day reporting, in-patient treatment, and pretrial release supervision programs. It broadens eligibility criteria by allowing courts to place individuals into these programs during any court proceeding rather than strictly at sentencing. Additionally, the bill repeals the requirement that the Sheriff collect and manage the earnings of participating individuals, instead authorizing the Sheriff to require proof that participants are paying required dependent support, restitution, and court-ordered fees or fines.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Sheriff
stakeholders: Individuals in the custody of or court-ordered to the St. Mary's County Sheriff participating in detention, pretrial, or rehabilitative release programs; the St. Mary's County Sheriff's Office; and local courts.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no State fiscal effect. The bill is not anticipated to materially affect St. Mary's County finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly involves the judiciary by altering court proceedings, authorizing judges to order individuals into newly established correctional and supervision programs in St. Mary's County, and requiring the Sheriff to provide written notification to the court upon program violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys represent indigent criminal defendants in St. Mary's County who may be eligible for court-ordered placement into these alternative correctional and treatment programs, or who face revocation and loss of diminution credits for alleged program violations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is Maryland's primary correctional department overseeing state correctional policy and supervision. While the bill specifically governs local correctional programs administered by the St. Mary's County Sheriff under the Correctional Services Article, DPSCS monitors statewide correctional standards and statutes.

Synopsis: Increasing, from $1,000 to $2,500, the maximum civil penalty that the Board of License Commissioners for St. Mary's County may impose for a violation of a law relating to licensing the sale of alcoholic beverages.

bill_summary: Increases the maximum civil penalty from $1,000 to $2,500 that the St. Mary’s County Board of License Commissioners may impose on a person who violates laws relating to licensing the sale of alcoholic beverages.
responsible_party: St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees, applicants, and businesses selling alcoholic beverages in St. Mary's County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. St. Mary's County local revenues may increase by up to $1,500 per civil penalty imposed beginning in fiscal year 2026, depending on the number of licensing violations. County expenditures are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article concerning civil penalties for alcoholic beverages licensing violations in St. Mary's County. While the penalty is administered locally by the St. Mary's County Board of License Commissioners, the Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for state-level regulation and oversight of the alcohol industry.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Labor to study building code requirements for single-staircase buildings in the State and other States and analyze best practices when drafting building code requirements; requiring the Department to make legislative and regulatory recommendations for the purpose of increasing the affordable housing supply by reducing barriers to multifamily housing development; and requiring the Department to report to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by December 1, 2026.
Title: Maryland Department of Labor - Study on Building Code Requirements for Single-Staircase Buildings
