Cryor Scholarship Fund special fund revenues and expenditures may increase by an estimated $9,200 per additional scholarship award annually beginning in FY 2026, though the total number of additional awards cannot be reliably estimated. Higher education institutions may experience a potential minimal loss of nonresident tuition revenue due to expanded in-state tuition exemptions. Public school enrollments and local finances are not expected to be materially affected.

As an independent public university, Morgan State must implement the bill's expanded nonresident tuition exemptions for active service members and dependents of all uniformed services.
As a public honors college, St. Mary's College must comply with statutory expansions of nonresident tuition exemptions for uniformed services personnel and their families.
The bill amends Education Article § 18-1910 to allow time spent in active duty in the uniformed services to extend the period for exercising benefits under the Maryland Prepaid College Trust.

The bill amends Education Article § 21-309 regarding qualified employees with disabilities, expanding the Maryland Department of Labor's determinations of individuals discharged or released from active duty for service-connected disabilities to include all uniformed services.

responsible_party: Maryland State Library Agency
stakeholders: Deaf and hard-of-hearing individuals, library patrons, and State and county public library staff
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $49,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 to fulfill the $450,000 mandated appropriation, accounting for $401,000 already budgeted for the Maryland Deaf Culture Digital Library. Funding is discretionary in FY 2026 and becomes a statutory mandate beginning in FY 2027. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Library Agency oversees the Deaf Culture Digital Library (DCDL), which is established under its purview and is required by the bill to submit its annual operating budget to the agency on or before June 1 each year.

DBM is responsible for formulating the state budget and managing state expenditures, and will be required to implement the bill's mandated annual appropriation of $450,000 for the Deaf Culture Digital Library.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: ODHH coordinates directly with the Deaf Culture Digital Library on sensitivity training, advisory board appointments, and partnership development to serve deaf and hard of hearing Marylanders.
The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a $450,000 appropriation for the Deaf Culture Digital Library in the annual state budget bill starting in fiscal year 2026.

Synopsis: Altering the circumstances under which the Child Support Administration may notify the Motor Vehicle Administration of an individual's child support arrearages for the purpose of suspending the individual's driver's license or privilege to drive; and requiring the court, after establishing a child support order, to send a copy of the guideline calculation and the order to the Child Support Administration.
Title: Child Support - Driver's License Suspension for Arrearages and Court Orders

NarrowSubjects.Name: Family Law -see also- Adoption; Alimony; Annulment; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters child support enforcement by exempting obligors whose income is at or below 250% of the federal poverty guidelines from driver's license suspensions for arrears, unless judicially determined to be voluntarily impoverished. It also extends the noncompliance threshold for noncommercial license suspensions from 60 to 120 days and requires courts to provide copies of child support orders and guideline calculations to the Child Support Administration.
responsible_party: Child Support Administration (Department of Human Services) and the Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Child support obligors (particularly low-income obligors earning up to 250% of the federal poverty guidelines), child support obligees and children receiving support, and circuit court staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures increase for the Department of Human Services (DHS), including $125,000 in one-time IT programming costs in FY 2026 (34% general funds, 66% federal funds) and potential additional personnel costs for caseworkers (illustratively $49,000 per caseworker in FY 2026 and $73,000 annually thereafter). General fund expenditures for the Judiciary may increase minimally to transmit order and guideline data for over 50,000 additional cases annually, causing a significant operational impact on circuit courts. General fund fine revenues will decrease minimally from fewer citations for driving on a suspended license.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Child Support Administration (CSA) is a division of DHS. The bill directly alters the procedures and criteria under which CSA investigates obligors, determines poverty thresholds, and notifies the Motor Vehicle Administration to suspend driver's licenses for nonpayment of child support, resulting in potential significant operational and IT programming fiscal impacts.

MVA is responsible for executing driver's license suspensions, reinstatements, expungements, and issuing work-restricted licenses based on child support arrearage notifications transmitted from the Child Support Administration.

The bill requires courts, after establishing a child support order, to send copies of child support orders and guideline calculations to the Child Support Administration, resulting in a significant operational impact and increased clerical workload across the court system.

MDOT is the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, and the Secretary of Transportation is specifically tasked by the bill with cooperating with the Secretary of Human Services to adopt regulations implementing the act.

OAH is designated in the statute as the administrative forum for obligors appealing child support investigation findings regarding license suspension actions, and participates in adopting implementing regulations.
OAG provides legal representation and advice to DHS, CSA, and MVA regarding child support enforcement actions, administrative procedures, and statutory compliance.

Synopsis: Establishing certain deluxe complex restaurant and resort complex beer and wine and beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Garrett County; requiring the Board of License Commissioners for Garrett County to hold a hearing for the issuance of certain festival licenses and altering certain notice requirements for the hearing; requiring certain festival license applicants to apply to the Board in a certain manner; clarifying the entities to which the Board may issue certain multiple day and multiple event licenses; etc.
Title: Garrett County Alcoholic Beverages Act of 2025

bill_summary: The bill establishes Class BDR-DC (deluxe complex restaurant) and Class BRC (resort complex) beer and wine and beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Garrett County, along with associated license and issuing fees and catering options. It also updates hearing and application notice requirements for several temporary and festival alcoholic beverages licenses and authorizes nonprofit organizations, rather than clubs, to obtain Class C multiple day and multiple event licenses.
responsible_party: Garrett County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurants, resort complexes, nonprofit organizations, festival/event organizers, and patrons in Garrett County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is none. Garrett County revenues increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that new deluxe complex restaurant, resort complex, and other licenses are issued; the exact revenue increase cannot be reliably estimated because the number of new licenses is unknown. Garrett County can handle administrative and enforcement duties using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and administering alcoholic beverage taxes. While House Bill 790 / Chapter 790 exclusively concerns local retail licenses, festival permits, and hearings administered by the Garrett County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, it relates to the state's overall alcoholic beverages regulatory framework and involves state-licensed wholesalers and manufacturers.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing personnel and taxation to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Tax Relief and State Personnel Equality for Service Members Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: The bill establishes uniform statutory definitions regarding military service across several Maryland Code articles, referencing federal standards under the U.S. Code. It broadens the application of various personnel, reemployment, and tax relief provisions (such as income tax abatements, military subtraction modifications, and property tax relief) to cover all uniformed services—including the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration—rather than only the armed forces.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families, Office of the Comptroller, and the Maryland Department of Budget and Management
stakeholders: Active duty and reserve service members, veterans, and military families—particularly members of the U.S. Public Health Service and National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration—as well as state and local government employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local finances are not materially affected. While the bill expands access to state and local personnel benefits, tax abatements, and property tax relief, the newly eligible population (primarily PHS and NOAA commissioned officers) is small relative to the overall veteran population, allowing any fiscal impact to be absorbed within existing agency and local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article, which establishes the core definitions governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families (including definitions for 'active duty', 'active service member', 'armed forces', 'military family', 'reserve component', 'service member', 'uniformed services', and 'veteran') used across the Maryland Code.

As the state's principal personnel agency, DBM oversees state employee policies and merit systems impacted by the bill, including reemployment and reinstatement rights for returning service members, veteran selection credits in state hiring, and paid leave for uniformed services training.

The Comptroller administers state tax laws and will be responsible for implementing the bill's tax provisions, which alter income tax subtraction modifications for military pay and retirement income, establish income tax abatements for service members dying in active service or public health emergencies, and update sales and use tax exemptions for veterans' organizations.

Members of the Maryland National Guard are directly impacted by the standardized definitions of reserve components and service members, which govern their state personnel reemployment protections, leave rights, and eligibility for state tax subtractions.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department overseeing the state's military forces and National Guard members, the Adjutant General has an administrative interest in statutory updates affecting the rights, service credits, and protections of military personnel.

bill_summary: Requires certain charter, code, and commission counties in Maryland that impose development impact fees, surcharges, or excise taxes to report annually to the Maryland Department of Planning on the collection and expenditure of those revenues, make the report publicly available, and report local authorizing laws and subsequent amendments to the department.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: County governments imposing development impact fees, surcharges, or excise taxes; property developers and homebuilders; and county residents and taxpayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State operations or finances. Local governments can comply with the annual reporting requirements using existing resources, resulting in no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 698 specifically designates the Department of Planning (MDP) as the state entity to which Maryland counties must annually report data on the collection, expenditure, and location of local development impact fees, surcharges, and excise taxes, as well as copies of the local laws authorizing them.

Synopsis: Defining "honorable discharge" with respect to any State program of benefits, rights, or privileges applicable to a veteran to include certain discharges.
Title: General Provisions - Veterans Benefits - Honorable Discharge

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of 'honorable discharge' for any State program of benefits, rights, or privileges to include discharges that are less than honorable if the Department of Veterans and Military Families determines the individual is eligible for State benefits under the criteria established in federal regulations (38 C.F.R. § 3.12).
responsible_party: Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Maryland military veterans with less than honorable discharges who meet federal discharge review criteria, making them eligible for State veteran benefits, rights, and programs.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations will not be materially affected. The Department of Veterans and Military Families can administer eligibility reviews and provide State veterans' benefits using existing budgeted resources. While some State programs may absorb minor costs if federal reimbursements are unavailable for certain non-federally recognized discharges, these costs are expected to be absorbed within existing general funds and no specific dollar amounts are estimated. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 699 directly tasks the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) and its Secretary with reviewing veterans' discharge documentation and determining eligibility for State veterans' benefits, rights, and privileges based on criteria in federal regulations (38 C.F.R. § 3.12).

bill_summary: Requires each local county board of education to develop and publish on its website a list of all special education service delivery models provided to parentally-placed private school students within its jurisdiction, and to provide a written copy of the list upon request.
responsible_party: County boards of education (local school systems)
stakeholders: Parentally-placed private school students with disabilities, their parents or guardians, private and religious schools, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local school systems can handle the publication requirements using existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's 24 local school systems and manages statewide policies, regulations, and federal compliance related to special education under IDEA, which directly pertains to the special education service delivery models local boards must publish.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include certain students attending the Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include eligible Maryland residents attending the Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine.
responsible_party: Maryland Higher Education Commission
stakeholders: Maryland resident graduate students attending the Meritus School of Osteopathic Medicine, as well as students and participating institutions under the Maryland Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program.
fiscal_impact_summary: No net impact on State expenditures or revenues. Program funding is as provided in the State budget ($1.2 million in FY 2026), meaning expanding eligibility redistributes existing scholarship funds across an additional institution rather than requiring new expenditures. Local finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Higher Education Commission (MHEC) administers the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program, determines financial need criteria, establishes award guidelines, and allocates scholarship funds among eligible institutions.

As the administrator of state financial aid programs, the Commission is directly responsible for adopting regulations, establishing guidelines, and reallocating funds for the Graduate and Professional Scholarship Program to include the newly eligible institution.

Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (such as the University of Maryland professional schools and the University of Baltimore School of Law) participate in this scholarship program, and the inclusion of an additional institution will affect their proportionate funding allocations.

Synopsis: Requiring that an original and renewal application for a license, an identification card, or a moped operator's permit allow an applicant to choose to indicate on the document the applicant's nonapparent disability; requiring the Motor Vehicle Administration to ensure that a certain license, identification card, or moped operator's permit include a notation of a nonapparent disability; requiring the immediate implementation of training for law enforcement concerning interactions with persons with nonapparent disabilities; etc.
Title: Vehicle Laws - Licenses, Identification Cards, and Moped Operator's Permits - Notation of Nonapparent Disability (Eric's ID Law)

bill_summary: Known as Eric's ID Law, this bill requires the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) to allow applicants for a driver's license, identification card, or moped operator's permit to indicate if they have a nonapparent disability, such as an intellectual or developmental disability. The MVA must place a notation on the credential without charging a fee or requiring proof of disability, conduct public outreach, restrict unauthorized disclosure of the information, and remove the notation upon request. Additionally, the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission must implement training for law enforcement regarding interactions with individuals who have this notation.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Individuals with nonapparent disabilities (including developmental and intellectual disabilities) applying for or holding Maryland licenses, ID cards, or moped permits, advocacy groups, and law enforcement officers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2026 for one-time vendor costs to update credential templates, plus ongoing credential production costs of $1.39 per change (amounting to $69,500 per 50,000 credential holders). The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can implement the required training with existing resources. State revenues and local government operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Motor Vehicle Administration is the primary implementing agency responsible for updating applications, issuing credentials with the nonapparent disability notation, managing records and deletions, conducting public outreach, and ensuring data privacy protections.

As the parent department of the Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund will incur the expenditures associated with credential redesign, vendor system updates, and card issuance.

The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission to consult with the Department of State Police to implement law enforcement training regarding interactions with individuals who have a nonapparent disability notation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS houses the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC), which is tasked by the bill with implementing training for law enforcement concerning interactions with individuals displaying a nonapparent disability notation.

The department coordinates services and policy for Marylanders with disabilities and serves as a key stakeholder and resource regarding advocacy and outreach for developmental and intellectual disability communities.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County to issue a Class GSF (golf simulator facility) license to a holder of a Class B license; and clarifying that the Class GSF (golf simulator facility) license counts toward the maximum number of nine Class B alcoholic beverages licenses a holder may be issued.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Multiple Licenses - Golf Simulator Facilities
bill_summary: Authorizes the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to issue one Class GSF (golf simulator facility) alcoholic beverages license to a person who holds one or more Class B licenses, with the GSF license counting toward the maximum limit of nine Class B licenses that may be issued to the same individual.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Harford County Class B alcoholic beverages licensees, golf simulator facility businesses, and their patrons
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State finances and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations, with a minimal effect on small businesses. Class GSF licenses have an annual fee of $1,500.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry and collects alcoholic beverage excise taxes. While this bill strictly applies to local licensing administered by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal effect, it falls within the broad subject area of alcohol regulation.

Synopsis: Repealing certain incorrect references to the Comptroller of Maryland in certain provisions of law requiring the holder of a performing arts nonprofit organization license in Harford County to comply with certain record-keeping and reporting requirements; repealing the authority of the Comptroller to suspend the license of a license holder without a hearing under certain circumstances; and authorizing, rather than requiring, the Board to summon a license holder for a hearing and impose a fine under certain circumstances.

bill_summary: This bill removes outdated references to the Comptroller of Maryland concerning recordkeeping and reporting requirements for performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverages licenses in Harford County, repealing the Comptroller's power to suspend licenses without a hearing. It also grants the Harford County Board of License Commissioners discretionary authority, rather than a mandatory requirement, to summon a license holder to a hearing and impose fines or license suspensions for violations.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverage license holders in Harford County, the Harford County Board of License Commissioners, and the Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or Harford County operations or finances. While the local licensing board has discretion to impose fines between $250 and $2,000 for violations, any fiscal impact is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly removes obsolete statutory references to the Comptroller of Maryland regarding record-keeping, reporting, and audit requirements for performing arts nonprofit organization alcoholic beverage licenses in Harford County, and repeals the Comptroller's former authority to suspend such licenses without a hearing.

Synopsis: Altering the quota used to determine the maximum number of certain alcoholic beverages licenses that the Board of License Commissioners for Harford County may issue from every 4,000 to every 4,750 individuals in the county.
Title: Harford County - Alcoholic Beverages - Alteration of License Quota
bill_summary: Increases the population quota threshold from 4,000 to 4,750 individuals per license used by the Harford County Board of License Commissioners to determine the maximum number of Class A, Class A-1, and Class A-2 off-sale alcoholic beverages licenses issued.
responsible_party: Harford County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage retail establishments, prospective license applicants, and residents of Harford County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Harford County finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is explicitly referenced in the statutory text as the entity that specifies the county population figures used to calculate the alcoholic beverages license quota for Harford County.

Synopsis: Including the Department of Housing and Community Development in the definition of "public housing agency" for the purposes of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program; authorizing a public housing agency to administer the Program in accordance with a local administrative plan; authorizing the Department to project-base up to 100% of its authorized voucher units; altering the manner in which the Department and each public housing agency shall prioritize vouchers and housing assistance payments for certain families; etc.
Title: Housing and Community Development - Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program Eligibility - Alterations

Housing -see also- Apartments; Condos; Mobile & Manuf  Homes
Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst

bill_summary: This bill alters the administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program by including the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD) under the definition of a public housing agency (PHA), permitting PHAs to administer the program under local administrative plans, and allowing DHCD to project-base up to 100% of voucher units. It also removes the requirement that priority categories of families be prioritized equally, adjusts inspection frequency requirements from annual to at least biennial, and increases the share of program funding distributed to local PHAs for administrative staffing costs from 6% to 15% (or the federal de minimis rate, whichever is greater).
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development
stakeholders: Low-income households and families eligible for rental assistance (including children, young adults transitioning out of foster care, veterans, individuals experiencing homelessness, individuals with disabilities, and the elderly), local public housing agencies, and participating rental property owners.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected because overall program funding remains unchanged. Local government revenues for public housing agencies increase due to higher administrative cost distributions (increasing from 6% to the greater of 15% or the federal de minimis rate of direct costs) to defray staffing expenses, while local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 716 is a departmental bill directly concerning the Department of Housing and Community Development (DHCD). It alters the administration of the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program housed within DHCD, including defining DHCD as a public housing agency, allowing project-basing of voucher units, adjusting inspection requirements, and modifying the distribution of administrative funds to local public housing agencies.

bill_summary: This bill modifies various provisions governing the Maryland Department of Natural Resources (DNR) and public lands management. It establishes the Land and Property Management Program to process property transactions and employee housing, authorizes DNR to create affiliated nonprofit foundations to solicit contributions and support public land initiatives, and mandates annual budget requests for at least one permanent staff position per 400 acres of newly acquired fee-simple land. Additionally, it permits the transfer of Program Open Space (POS) land acquisition balances over $80 million to cover operating, maintenance, and Natural Resources Police costs, while granting local jurisdictions greater flexibility and revised matching requirements for local POS development projects.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Visitors to Maryland public lands, local governments managing parks and recreation, Department of Natural Resources personnel, and commercial contractors and vendors providing conservation and park development services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $212,543 in FY 2026 to fund two positions in the newly codified Land and Property Management Program (funds are included in the FY 2026 budget contingent on this legislation). Beginning in FY 2027, expenditures escalate as additional staff are requested and hired based on land acquisition formulas, reaching an estimated $1,875,970 in FY 2030 for a cumulative 18 positions. Additional special fund expenditures may occur if excess POS acquisition fund balances over $80 million are transferred to operational uses. State revenues are not directly affected. Local governments benefit from increased flexibility to direct up to 100% of local POS allocations toward development projects, reduced local matching requirements on projects receiving federal or other state funds, and the ability to apply up to $125,000 in acquisition funding toward 5-year recreation plan updates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which establishes a Land and Property Management Program within DNR, authorizes DNR to create affiliated foundations, modifies real property interest acquisition processes, mandates budget requests for land management positions, and alters the use of Program Open Space funds.

The Board of Public Works has direct statutory authority under the bill to approve DNR's real property acquisitions, authorize real property interest disposals/exchanges, approve an easement valuation system, and supervise appropriations for land acquisitions.

DNR is statutorily required to submit funding requests to DBM in its annual budget requests to create new permanent, classified positions based on acres of fee simple real property interests acquired.

The Maryland Department of Planning, in conjunction with DNR, is responsible for certifying whether local jurisdictions have met their land acquisition goals under approved local land preservation and recreation plans to allow use of Program Open Space funds for development projects.
The Attorney General is required to review policies developed by DNR for operating affiliated foundations for form and legal sufficiency and, if appropriate, approve them.

The State Ethics Commission is required to review and approve affiliated foundation policies concerning conflicts of interest, receive notification of DNR officials/employees serving on foundations, evaluate potential concerns, and receive annual reports on foundation governance.
DNR must consult with the Department of General Services to develop a system for appraisal reviews for real property interest acquisitions as part of its regulatory implementation.

The bill authorizes the Governor to transfer funds from the Program Open Space State land acquisition balance to DNR under specified conditions and mandates that DNR submit an annual report on affiliated foundations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor and assess the impact of potential and actual federal changes to specified health care programs and to provide recommendations for State and local action to protect the access of residents of the State to affordable health coverage; and requiring the Commission to submit a report of its findings and recommendations, including any legislative proposals, to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31 each year.
Title: Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission - Established

bill_summary: Reestablishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission to monitor and assess potential and actual federal changes to the Affordable Care Act, the Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act, Medicaid, the Maryland Children's Health Program, Medicare, and the Maryland All-Payer Model, and to make recommendations for state and local actions to maintain access to affordable health coverage.
responsible_party: Department of Legislative Services, Maryland Department of Health, and Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Maryland residents enrolled in or seeking health insurance coverage (including Medicaid, Medicare, MCHP, and ACA marketplace plans), health insurance carriers, healthcare providers, employers, and state health regulatory agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Department of Legislative Services, Maryland Department of Health, and Maryland Insurance Administration can jointly staff the commission and prepare required reports using existing budgeted resources. Commission members are entitled to standard travel expense reimbursement, but receive no compensation. State revenues are not affected. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of Health (or designee) is designated as a member of the Commission, and the Maryland Department of Health is explicitly required to jointly provide staff and operational support for the Commission.
The Maryland Insurance Commissioner (or designee) serves on the Commission, and the Maryland Insurance Administration is mandated to jointly staff the Commission alongside MDH and DLS.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Maryland Health Insurance Coverage Protection Commission, a temporary advisory commission authorized to study health coverage issues and make legislative recommendations through June 30, 2029.
The Executive Director of HSCRC (or designee) is named as a Commission member, and the Commission is specifically tasked with monitoring and assessing impacts on the Maryland All-Payer Model.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (or designee) serves on the Commission, which is tasked with monitoring and addressing potential changes to the ACA and state health insurance markets.
The Governor is responsible for appointing four members to the Commission and receives the Commission's annual reports and legislative proposals.
The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as a statutory member of the Commission.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in recruiting and vetting candidates for the four gubernatorial appointments to the newly created Commission.

bill_summary: This bill updates the State Boat Act by revising the definitions of personal watercraft and personal flotation devices, eliminating newspaper advertising and petition hearing requirements for proposed boating regulations, and establishing authority to set speed zones by public notice for emergent or restricted situations. It also increases several vessel-related fees—including certificates of title, two-year certificates of number, Maryland use stickers, and manufacturer/dealer licenses—creates a voluntary nonmotorized vessel decal, and expands funding thresholds and expenditure flexibility under the Waterway Improvement Fund.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Recreational boaters, vessel owners, boat dealers and manufacturers, livery vessel operators, and local governments applying for waterway improvement funding.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Department of Natural Resources increase by approximately $4.9 million annually beginning in FY 2026 due to increased vessel registration, titling, and dealer fees. Federal fund revenues may increase modestly starting in FY 2027 based on vessel counts. Special fund expenditures are projected to increase by $100,000 or more annually due to higher expenditure limits for small Waterway Improvement Fund (WIF) projects, slightly offset by minor savings from eliminated newspaper publication requirements. Local governments benefit from expanded access to 100% and 50% WIF grants for marina construction and small emergency projects.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 719 is a departmental bill sponsored on behalf of the Department of Natural Resources (DNR). It directly alters provisions of the State Boat Act administered by DNR, including fee structures for vessel titling, certificates of number, dealer licenses, Maryland use stickers, and the Waterway Improvement Fund, resulting in an estimated $4.9 million annual increase in DNR special fund revenues.

Synopsis: Repealing provisions of law relating to the Somers Cove Marina Commission, the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund, and the operation of Somers Cove Marina; requiring the Secretary to develop a master plan for the operation and improvement of services at Somers Cove Marina by October 1, 2027; requiring all revenue received by the Department from activities associated with Somers Cove Marina be deposited in the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund; establishing the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission; etc.

bill_summary: Repeals provisions establishing the Somers Cove Marina Commission and the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund, transferring the management, operations, and property oversight of the marina directly to the Department of Natural Resources. It authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to lease property, procure operating contracts, employ staff, and assess fees, while directing marina revenues into the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund and establishing the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Boaters, slip holders at Somers Cove Marina, marina employees and contractors, the commercial fishing industry, tourism and business communities in Somerset County and the City of Crisfield.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State special fund revenues and expenditures may increase significantly (potentially exceeding $1,000,000 annually if DNR operates the marina directly, or less if operations are leased out to a third party). Special fund revenues also increase in FY 2026 from the transfer of the remaining balance of the Somers Cove Marina Improvement Fund (estimated illustratively at $336,671). General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 due to interest earnings. Local finances for Somerset County and the City of Crisfield are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which repeals the independent Somers Cove Marina Commission and transfers full management, operations, maintenance, leasing, fee-setting, and staffing authority of the Somers Cove Marina to the department and the Secretary of Natural Resources. DNR also administers the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund, which receives all marina revenues.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the existing Somers Cove Marina Commission and creates a new advisory body, the Somers Cove Marina Advisory Commission within DNR, tasked with advising the Secretary on marina operations, management, and development.

The bill statutorily requires the State Treasurer to hold the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund separately, invest money of the fund, and allocate interest earnings back to the fund as exempted under the State Finance and Procurement Article.
The bill specifically designates the Comptroller to account for the Natural Resources Property Maintenance Fund.

DBM was consulted as an information source on the bill regarding fiscal and personnel impacts, as the bill authorizes new state employee compensation structures, potential new state positions, and alterations to special fund expenditures through the state budget.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports on or before December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, to the Senate Finance Committee, the Senate Budget and Taxation Committee, the House Health and Government Operations Committee, and the House Appropriations Committee on the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs and recovery residences.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports to specified General Assembly committees by December 1, 2025, and December 1, 2026, regarding the revision of COMAR 10.63, improvements to the oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs, and enhanced procedures for the certification, monitoring, and oversight of recovery residences. The reports must also analyze how regulatory revisions and other departmental actions will prevent incidents such as patient relapse and death in provider-owned housing.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Substance use disorder treatment program operators, recovery residence operators, and individuals receiving substance use disorder treatment or living in recovery residences.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Health can likely fulfill the bill's reporting requirements using existing budgeted resources. Although the department advised it would require four staff members costing $318,716 in fiscal 2026, the Department of Legislative Services determined that additional personnel are not necessitated by the bill because it mandates reporting rather than implementation. State revenues are unaffected. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to submit reports to General Assembly committees regarding the revision of COMAR 10.63, improvements to oversight of substance use disorder treatment programs, and certification and monitoring procedures for recovery residences.

Synopsis: Requiring the State Board of Dental Examiners to issue a license or certification to certain applicants licensed or certified by another state within 15 business days after receiving the completed application; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to develop a plan for a temporary or permanent authorization to practice a health occupation in the State for certain individuals who left employment with a federal agency after January 20, 2025; requiring the Department to submit the plan by October 1, 2025 to certain committees; etc.

bill_summary: This bill requires the State Board of Dental Examiners to issue licenses or certifications within 15 business days to qualified dentists, dental hygienists, and dental radiation technologists who are licensed or certified in another state. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop and submit a plan to authorize certain individuals who left federal employment after January 20, 2025, and hold equivalent out-of-state licenses, to practice health occupations in Maryland.
responsible_party: State Board of Dental Examiners and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Out-of-state licensed dentists, dental hygienists, dental radiation technologists, and former federal health occupation employees seeking authorization to practice in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Dental Examiners and the Maryland Department of Health can handle the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. Any impact on special fund revenues from application fees is indeterminate but anticipated to be minimal. There is no direct effect on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Dental Examiners and the health occupations boards. Under the bill, the department is directly required to develop and submit a plan for authorizing certain former federal employees licensed in other states to practice health occupations in Maryland, and its Board of Dental Examiners must issue licenses and certifications within 15 business days to qualified out-of-state applicants.

bill_summary: This bill expands the allowable uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to include covering operating expenses and personnel costs for investigations, enforcement actions, and related activities conducted by the Opioids Enforcement Unit within the Office of the Attorney General to recover opioid-related judgments and settlements. It also requires an annual activity and case disposition report by the Attorney General.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Office of the Attorney General (Opioids Enforcement Unit), Maryland's Office of Overdose Response, local health departments, community recovery organizations, and individuals receiving opioid prevention and treatment services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The FY 2026 budget includes a $1.5 million special fund appropriation from the Opioid Restitution Fund (ORF) for the Office of the Attorney General's Opioids Enforcement Unit, an allocation assumed to continue through FY 2029. While this shifts $1.5 million annually from discretionary opioid abatement grant programs managed by the Maryland's Office of Overdose Response to the Attorney General, there is likely no net impact on total ORF expenditures, and state revenues are unaffected. Local government finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund to support the operating expenses and personnel costs of the Opioids Enforcement Unit within the Office of the Attorney General (OAG), authorizing an estimated $1.5 million annually in special fund expenditures from FY 2026 through FY 2029, and establishes annual reporting requirements for OAG.

The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) manages and distributes Opioid Restitution Fund revenues. Expanding the fund's allowable uses to support OAG's enforcement unit reduces the amount of discretionary grant funding available for MDH and community-level substance use disorder abatement programs by $1.5 million annually.

The bill mandates that the Office of the Attorney General submit an annual report to the Governor by October 1 detailing the status, investigations, lawsuits, and case dispositions of the Opioids Enforcement Unit.

Synopsis: Altering the training that the Maryland Department of Health is authorized to provide under the Overdose Response Program to include emphasis on the restoration of breathing, avoiding withdrawal, and compassionate postoverdose support and care; clarifying that the use of the Opioid Restitution Fund is subject to certain restrictions; and altering the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund so as to include the addressing of racial disparities in access to prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services.

bill_summary: This bill aligns the authorized uses of the Opioid Restitution Fund with the purposes specified in settlement agreements and court judgments involving the opioid industry, including addressing racial and socioeconomic disparities in access to prevention, harm reduction, treatment, and recovery support services. It also updates the Maryland Department of Health's Overdose Response Program training to emphasize restoring breathing, avoiding withdrawal, and providing compassionate post-overdose support and care.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals with substance use disorders or at risk of opioid overdose, communities facing racial and socioeconomic healthcare disparities, harm reduction and treatment providers, and community-based nonprofit recovery organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal or operational impact on State or local finances. It modifies the permissible uses of existing Opioid Restitution Fund monies to align with allowable uses under national settlement agreements without affecting existing funded programs.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health directly administers the Overdose Response Program (ORP), is authorized to alter training components under the program, and manages and distributes monies from the Opioid Restitution Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references and assigns decision-making authority to the Opioid Restitution Fund Advisory Council to review and approve distributions for non-evidence-based pilot programs and demonstration studies.

The Office of the Attorney General negotiates and enforces the settlement agreements and judgments against the opioid industry that dictate the terms and allowable expenditures of the Opioid Restitution Fund, and served as an information source on the bill.
The Comptroller of Maryland is statutory custodian tasked with accounting for the Opioid Restitution Fund pursuant to the reenacted provisions of the bill.
The State Treasurer is statutory custodian responsible for holding the Opioid Restitution Fund separately pursuant to the reenacted provisions of the bill.

bill_summary: Establishes the Maryland Connectivity Coalition to improve wildlife habitat connectivity, protect threatened and endangered species, and reduce collisions between vehicles and wildlife. The bill gives the State Highway Administration final decision-making authority over wildlife crossing projects, requires reporting on wildlife crossings in the Consolidated Transportation Program, and mandates that local jurisdictions consider wildlife movement and habitat connectivity in their comprehensive plans.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Motorists, wildlife populations (especially threatened and endangered species), local governments, and transportation and conservation agencies.
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund special fund expenditures increase by an estimated $50,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 for the State Highway Administration to hire consultant services for coalition research and staffing. The Department of Natural Resources and the Maryland Department of Planning can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and local government operations and finances are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Highway Administrator (or designee) serves as Chair of the newly created Maryland Connectivity Coalition, co-adopts rules for the coalition with DNR, maintains final decision-making authority over the placement, funding, and design of wildlife crossings, and must report on wildlife crossings in each Consolidated Transportation Plan, resulting in an estimated $50,000 annual fiscal impact from the Transportation Trust Fund.

The Secretary of Natural Resources is a designated statutory member of the Maryland Connectivity Coalition, co-adopts coalition rules with the State Highway Administration, and coordinates with the Department of Planning to supply local governments with wildlife connectivity and crossing information.

As the parent agency of the State Highway Administration, MDOT's Consolidated Transportation Program must incorporate required wildlife crossing reports, and the bill results in ongoing expenditures from the Transportation Trust Fund.

The bill mandates the Department of Planning to coordinate with the Department of Natural Resources and the State Highway Administration to provide updated information on habitat connectivity and planned wildlife crossings to charter counties and local jurisdictions for their comprehensive plans.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The legislation formally establishes the Maryland Connectivity Coalition as a permanent interagency and stakeholder body tasked with setting project criteria, performance metrics, and funding recommendations for wildlife habitat connectivity.

Under existing Land Use provisions referenced in the bill, the Department of the Environment reviews local comprehensive plan sensitive areas elements, which now must incorporate wildlife movement and habitat connectivity considerations.

bill_summary: This bill alters the statutory framework governing the funding, management, and oversight of major information technology (IT) development projects across Maryland State executive branch agencies. It establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience (MODE), along with the Maryland Digital Service Unit and the Major IT Development Project Oversight Division within the Department of Information Technology (DoIT), and creates the Information Technology Advisory Board to advise the General Assembly while repealing the Modernize Maryland Commission. Additionally, the bill strengthens oversight and reporting requirements, mandates a public online dashboard for major IT projects, and authorizes the withholding or reallocation of project funds under specified conditions.
responsible_party: Department of Information Technology
stakeholders: State executive branch agencies, State IT personnel and contractors, and Maryland residents accessing State digital services
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund expenditures from the Information Technology Investment Fund (ITIF) increase by at least $4,300,000 in FY 2026 to support staffing for the new Maryland Office of Digital Experience, with out-year expenditures likely increasing by at least that amount. General funds could be required if ITIF resources are insufficient. Potential cost reductions from IT efficiencies and economies of scale across agencies cannot be reliably estimated. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DoIT is the primary agency responsible for implementing the bill. The legislation substantially alters and expands DoIT's oversight over major IT development projects, establishes the Maryland Office of Digital Experience (MODE), the Maryland Digital Service Unit, and the Major IT Development Project Oversight Division within the department, and mandates the creation of a public project dashboard.

The Secretary of Budget and Management is directly tasked with fiscal oversight alongside DoIT, including withholding and reallocating major IT project funds upon recommendation, approving compensation levels for MODE staff, and executing budget amendment transfers of ITIF funds.

DGS is required to consult on the procurement assessment for IT modernization projects and submit recurring reports to legislative committees on projects over $1,000,000 under the Statewide Agile Resources and Teams master contract.

Managing units must provide notice to the Board of Public Works within 30 days of awarding contracts for major IT development projects affirming project team identification, DoIT approval, and agency head accountability.

The Governor is authorized to transfer up to 50 positions to the newly created Maryland Office of Digital Experience, approves budget amendment transfers with the Secretary of Budget and Management, and receives reports when IT project funding is withheld.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally repeals the Modernize Maryland Commission and alters statutory advisory frameworks regarding state IT modernization.

Members of the newly established Information Technology Advisory Board are made subject to the Public Ethics Law and must submit specific employment and financial interest disclosures to the State Ethics Commission.

Synopsis: Altering the penalties and points assessments related to the offenses of reckless, negligent, and aggressive driving; and adding certain motor vehicle offenses as elements that may contribute to charges for reckless or aggressive driving.
Title: Motor Vehicles - Reckless, Negligent, and Aggressive Driving (Sergeant Patrick Kepp Act)

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

NarrowSubjects.Name: Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Known as the Sergeant Patrick Kepp Act, this bill alters penalties, offenses, and point assessments for reckless, negligent, and aggressive driving. It classifies driving 30 miles per hour or more over the posted speed limit as reckless driving, designates reckless driving as an incarcerable offense punishable by up to 60 days in jail and/or a $1,000 fine, increases maximum fines for negligent driving ($750) and aggressive driving ($1,000), increases driver's license points for negligent driving and extreme speeding, and expands the list of violations that qualify toward an aggressive driving charge.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) and the Office of the Public Defender (OPD)
stakeholders: Maryland motorists, individuals cited for traffic infractions (specifically speeding 30+ mph, reckless driving, negligent driving, or aggressive driving), indigent defendants facing traffic-related criminal charges, pedestrian and bicycle road users, and law enforcement.
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by at least $534,800 in FY 2026 (growing to $725,500 by FY 2030) for the Office of the Public Defender to add staff for reckless driving cases, which become incarcerable must-appear offenses. General Fund revenues increase minimally from higher District Court fines. State correctional expenditures may see a minimal increase for Baltimore City detentions. Local governments may experience minimal increases in revenues from circuit court fines and minimal increases in detention facility expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the points assessed by MVA against individuals' driver's licenses for negligent driving convictions and speeding 30 mph or more above the posted speed limit, leading to increased license suspensions and revocations.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Because the bill makes reckless driving an incarcerable offense (up to 60 days imprisonment), indigent defendants charged with reckless driving become eligible for public defender representation, resulting in a substantial caseload increase and a fiscal impact of over $534,000 annually for additional attorneys and staff.

Reckless driving becomes a must-appear violation in District Court and Circuit Courts due to potential incarceration, eliminating prepayment options and increasing court appearances and trials managed by the Judiciary.
MDOT is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration and oversees the administration of Maryland's Vehicle Law and the Transportation Trust Fund.
As the primary state law enforcement agency enforcing motor vehicle and criminal laws on Maryland roadways, MSP will enforce the expanded definitions of reckless and aggressive driving.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The addition of a 60-day incarceration penalty for reckless driving may result in a minimal increase in commitments to State-operated correctional facilities, primarily the Baltimore Pretrial Complex.
OAH adjudicates administrative appeals of driver's license suspensions and revocations initiated by the MVA following points assessments.

responsible_party: State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
stakeholders: Applicants for behavior analyst licensure and practicing behavior analysts in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists can implement the bill's requirements using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists is a health occupations licensing board operating under the Maryland Department of Health. The bill directly impacts the board's licensure application processing times and notification requirements for behavior analysts.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Baltimore County Board of License Commissioners to approve the transfer of up to five existing Class B or Class D alcoholic beverages licenses from an eligible transferor election district to other election districts in the county between June 1, 2025, and May 31, 2028, subject to certain economic and district caps and requirements.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Farm owners and agricultural business operators in Washington County, agritourism visitors, and Washington County local code and permitting authorities.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect Maryland State or Washington County finances or operations. The effect on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor adopts and oversees the Maryland Building Performance Standards (MBPS) under the Public Safety Article and is responsible for adopting regulations governing building permit and occupancy exemptions for agritourism buildings.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture promotes and supports agribusiness and the economic viability of farms, including agritourism operations affected by the building code exemptions in Washington County.

responsible_party: Governing body of Washington County

fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Washington County property tax revenues are estimated to increase by approximately $710,000 annually beginning in fiscal year 2026 due to the reduction in tax credits provided under the adjusted credit schedules and higher qualification thresholds. Local fire departments and companies may experience increased grant revenues and operational expenditures to conduct innovative cancer screenings.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Professional and Volunteer Firefighter Innovative Cancer Screening Technologies Program, manages the grant distribution, handles program administrative requirements (including hiring additional personnel), and is authorized to allocate up to 20% of program funds to research centers.

The bill explicitly authorizes the Secretary of Health to allocate up to 20% of program funds (potentially up to $200,000 annually) to support academic medical research centers, specifically naming the University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing for data collection, analysis, and processing.

The bill amends statutory provisions that govern the amount the Governor is authorized to include in the annual state budget for the program, increasing the authorization from at least $500,000 to at least $1,000,000.

As the principal agency overseeing state budget development and fiscal planning for the executive branch, DBM is responsible for implementing the altered discretionary budget authorization for the program.
Program appropriations, expenditures, and grant funds remain subject to statutory audit by the Office of Legislative Audits under the Health - General Article.

bill_summary: House Bill 761 updates the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act by making virtual currency subject to abandoned property laws and requiring holders to liquidate it after five years of inactivity. The bill also establishes standards for determining apparent owner interest and addresses, requires life insurers to run annual comparisons against the Death Master File, lowers the threshold for publishing unclaimed property notices from $100 to $50, permits the Comptroller to apply unclaimed property toward outstanding state and local debts, and authorizes the Comptroller to retain up to $5 million for IT and cybersecurity modernization.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Owners and apparent owners of abandoned property, financial organizations, insurers, virtual currency holders, businesses holding unclaimed funds, and the Comptroller's Office.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are expected to increase by an indeterminate amount beginning in FY 2026 due to expanded abandoned property categories such as virtual currency, partially balanced by provisions recognizing additional account activity as continued ownership. Special fund expenditures will increase as the Comptroller's Office is authorized to retain up to $5.0 million from proceeds for information technology and cybersecurity costs, as well as an amount reasonably sufficient to pay claims. Local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland acts as the Administrator of the Maryland Uniform Disposition of Abandoned Property Act, requested the legislation, and is the primary implementing agency. The bill alters definitions, establishes procedures for handling virtual currency and retirement accounts, adjusts claim processes, and authorizes the Comptroller to retain up to $5 million from unclaimed property proceeds for information technology and cybersecurity.

The bill establishes statutory criteria and requirements for life insurance and annuity holders regarding the Social Security Administration Death Master File and presumptions of abandonment, directly referencing rules and policies adopted by the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

The bill alters statutory deadlines and timeframes under which claimants aggrieved by the Comptroller's determinations regarding abandoned property may file actions in the circuit courts to establish their claims.

The Department of Labor regulates state financial institutions and banking organizations that hold customer deposits and are subject to the revised dormancy, communication, and abandonment provisions under the Act.

bill_summary: Authorizes Maryland hospitals to sell patient medical debt to a governmental unit, a contractor of that unit, or a tax-exempt nonprofit organization for the sole purpose of canceling the debt. It establishes eligibility criteria for debt that can be sold, requires hospitals to dismiss pending collection actions and cease collection activities on sold debt, requires purchasers to notify patients and vacate adverse credit reports or judgments, and mandates related reporting to the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC).
responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC)
stakeholders: Hospitals, qualifying patients with outstanding medical debt (family income at or below 500% of the federal poverty level or medical debt exceeding 5% of family income), nonprofit organizations purchasing medical debt, and state and local governmental units.
fiscal_impact_summary: HSCRC can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. State and local government expenditures increase to the extent that any governmental unit elects to purchase patient medical debt for cancellation from FY 2026 through FY 2028. Any impact on the uncompensated care pool and hospital rates is indeterminate but expected to be minimal overall, and specific dollar estimates are unavailable.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC) is the primary regulatory body responsible for implementing the bill's provisions, including receiving hospital debt collection policies and reports, monitoring hospital compliance, offsetting uncompensated care amounts, and posting reporting data on its website.

HSCRC is an independent commission housed within the Maryland Department of Health (MDH). Additionally, MDH administers the Medicaid program, which participates in the state's hospital all-payer rate-setting system and could experience indirect rate adjustments resulting from changes to hospital uncompensated care balances.

The Office of the Attorney General (specifically its Consumer Protection Division) enforces Maryland consumer protection and debt collection laws and served as an information source for the legislation.

bill_summary: House Bill 767 establishes additional procedures and notice requirements following the issuance of a warrant of restitution in residential eviction cases (failure to pay rent, breach of lease, and tenant holding over). Landlords must provide written notice of scheduled repossession at least six days in advance by mail, door posting with a timestamped photograph, and electronic communication, while permitting landlords to charge up to $5 for notice expenses. It also details sheriff verification procedures, court actions for noncompliance, and tenant civil remedies for violations.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland and county sheriffs or constables
stakeholders: Residential landlords, residential tenants facing eviction, and county sheriffs and constables executing warrants of restitution
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances. Landlords may charge tenants up to $5 for expenses incurred in providing notice. Small business landlords may experience meaningful operational impacts and exposure to civil remedies for noncompliance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters judicial procedures in the District Court regarding summary ejectment, warrants of restitution, and eviction notice filings, requiring court clerks to receive documentation, the court to vacate warrants if proper notice was not given, and notices to include information about the District Court Help Center.

bill_summary: This bill updates, clarifies, and standardizes provisions of the Maryland Medical Practice Act and the Maryland Physician Assistants Act governing the State Board of Physicians and allied health professionals. It alters licensure requirements, reporting and notification mandates, and disciplinary grounds and procedures; standardizes the structure, membership, and duties of allied health advisory committees; authorizes new administrative penalties and raises existing civil penalties for violations such as employing unlicensed individuals or knowingly failing to report adverse actions; and expands the physician rehabilitation program into a comprehensive program covering all licensees.
responsible_party: State Board of Physicians
stakeholders: Physicians, physician assistants, allied health professionals (such as respiratory care practitioners, polysomnographic technologists, athletic trainers, perfusionists, naturopathic doctors, and genetic counselors), healthcare employers and facilities, and Maryland healthcare patients.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues to the Board of Physicians Fund and General Fund revenues may increase by an indeterminate amount beginning as early as FY 2026 due to new administrative penalties and increased civil fines. The Maryland Board of Physicians and the Office of Administrative Hearings can implement the bill's provisions using existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Physicians and its advisory committees operate within the Department of Health. The bill substantially revises the Maryland Medical Practice Act and the Maryland Physician Assistants Act, modifying licensing requirements, disciplinary panel procedures, reporting mandates, and administrative penalties for physicians, physician assistants, and allied health professionals.

The bill alters disciplinary hearing procedures and explicitly mandates that complaints proceeding to an evidentiary hearing be referred to the Office of Administrative Hearings (OAH). The fiscal note highlights that this will increase hearings delegated to OAH and necessitate Administrative Law Judge training.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the statutory requirement that the Board of Physicians include a blank panel data sheet supplied by the Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office with every license renewal notice.

The bill governs the collection and distribution of licensing fees and civil penalties paid to the Comptroller, specifically detailing the allocation between the Board of Physicians Fund and the Maryland Loan Assistance Repayment Program for Physicians and Physician Assistants.

The bill maintains statutory provisions directing the Legislative Auditor to audit the accounts and transactions of the Board of Physicians Fund and the Rehabilitation Program, as well as access records upon request.

stakeholders: Maryland public middle and high school students, teachers, administrators, local school systems, and law enforcement agencies.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Center for School Safety (MCSS) to conduct a comprehensive study and evaluation on detecting deadly weapons in public middle and high schools, evaluate current security infrastructure across all public school systems, assess weapons detection technologies, and submit interim and final reports to the General Assembly.

The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) oversees the state's 24 public school systems that are subject to the evaluation, houses the Maryland Center for School Safety as an independent unit within the department, and served as an information source for the fiscal analysis.

bill_summary: Regulates the use of artificial intelligence, algorithms, and software tools in health insurance utilization reviews by carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and private review agents. bill_summary: House Bill 839 qualifies a voter to cast a provisional ballot if the voter claimed a political party affiliation differing from their affiliation on record, provided the voter made a selection in a nonpartisan board of education contest. responsible_party: Local boards of elections and the Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Registered Maryland voters who cast provisional ballots due to party affiliation discrepancies, candidates running in nonpartisan local board of education elections, and election administrators.

bill_summary: The Pregnant and Parenting Student Support Act requires specified Maryland public senior higher education institutions to adopt and post on their websites a plan supporting pregnant and parenting students. The plan must comply with Title IX and include referrals to government assistance programs, adoption resources, and healthcare service providers, as well as institutional accommodations such as priority registration and flexible scheduling.
responsible_party: Maryland public senior higher education institutions (University System of Maryland constituent institutions, Morgan State University, and St. Mary's College of Maryland, excluding UMCES, UMGC, and the University of Baltimore)
stakeholders: Pregnant and parenting students enrolled at Maryland public senior higher education institutions, along with the universities and their administrative and student support offices.
fiscal_impact_summary: State higher education institutions can adopt and publish the required plans using existing resources. Expenditures may increase by an unknown, minimal to moderate amount if institutions provide additional services. Furthermore, State general and federal fund expenditures could increase, potentially significantly, if referrals result in increased enrollment in entitlement programs such as Medicaid and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), with federal fund revenues increasing correspondingly. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Constituent institutions of the University System of Maryland (with specified exceptions) are directly mandated by the bill to develop, adopt, and post on their websites comprehensive support plans for pregnant and parenting students.
Morgan State University is explicitly required to adopt and publish on its website a plan providing accommodations, referrals, and resources for pregnant and parenting students.
St. Mary's College of Maryland is explicitly required to adopt and publish on its website a plan providing accommodations, referrals, and resources for pregnant and parenting students.

The bill mandates that institutional plans refer students to the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), and WIC, which may notably increase enrollment and expenditures for these MDH-administered programs.
The bill specifically requires institutions to include referrals to the Child Care Scholarship Program, which is administered by the Maryland State Department of Education.
The bill requires institutional plans to include referrals and resources regarding adoption services and public assistance programs, which fall under the purview of DHS.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact. It also has no local fiscal impact on Charles County, as the Charles County Attorney has already assumed the duties and responsibilities of the Gaming Permit Review Board.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill repeals the Charles County Gaming Permit Review Board, which under existing law specifically required a member of the Department of State Police to serve on the board, thereby removing that statutory service requirement.

Synopsis: Requiring that certain adverse decision and grievance decision notices include certain information in a certain manner; requiring that the information regarding criteria and standards for utilization review that a private review agent is required to post on its website or the carrier's website be posted on the member's and provider's pages of the websites; requiring that certain information submitted to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner be aggregated by zip code; etc.
