bill_summary: House Bill 848 updates requirements regarding adverse decision and grievance notices, reporting, and examinations for health insurance carriers and private review agents. It mandates specific disclosures and unique identifiers on denial notices, requires private review agents to post utilization review criteria on member and provider webpages and maintain dedicated contact channels, requires carriers to report appeals and grievances data aggregated by zip code and explain significant increases in adverse decisions, and authorizes the Insurance Commissioner to examine carriers using this data.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance policyholders/members, health care providers, health insurance carriers, and private review agents
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected, and any administrative impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. There is no local government fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for administering and enforcing the bill's requirements, which include receiving and analyzing enhanced quarterly adverse decision reports by zip code, regulating private review agents, and authorizing the Insurance Commissioner to initiate market conduct examinations based on reported data.

The bill mandates that health carrier denial and grievance notices prominently provide contact information and statements regarding the assistance available through the Health Advocacy Unit, a division housed within the Office of the Attorney General that mediates consumer health coverage disputes.
The bill requires the Insurance Commissioner to provide copies of the annual summary report on health insurance appeals, grievances, and adverse decisions to the Governor.

The Governor is responsible for appointing six members representing various industry associations and unions to the Workgroup, and the Workgroup must submit its final findings and recommendations to the Governor by January 7, 2027.

bill_summary: The Maryland Second Look Act expands the provisions of the Juvenile Restoration Act to permit individuals who committed offenses between the ages of 18 and 24 to file a motion to reduce their sentence duration, provided they have served at least 20 years of confinement, were not sentenced to life without parole, are not registered sex offenders, and were not convicted of murdering an on-duty first responder. It also establishes procedural rules, factors courts must consider before granting a reduction, and specific victim protections.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary (Circuit Courts), Office of the Public Defender, and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals who committed crimes between ages 18 and 24 and have served at least 20 years, crime victims and their families, public defenders, and State's Attorneys.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase for the Office of the Public Defender by at least $538,100 in FY 2026 (growing to $730,300 by FY 2030) to hire six staff members, with additional indeterminate costs for panel attorneys. Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services expenditures will decrease by an indeterminate amount as individuals are released (saving approximately $312 per month per inmate in variable costs). Local expenditures for State's Attorneys' offices may increase minimally to respond to sentence reduction motions. Revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands eligibility for sentence reduction motions under the Maryland Second Look Act, directly increasing caseloads for the Office of the Public Defender and requiring significant additional staff and funding to evaluate case files and represent eligible incarcerated individuals.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill impacts individuals serving sentences within Division of Correction facilities; court decisions granting sentence reductions or releases will directly affect inmate population management, institutional record reporting for hearings, and departmental correctional expenditures.
Circuit courts are tasked with receiving petitions, holding hearings, receiving victim impact statements, issuing written determinations on statutory factors, and ordering release conditions.

bill_summary: This bill alters the membership of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network by decreasing the number of appointed members across several categories, extends the deadline for its final report to December 1, 2026, and extends the termination date of the workgroup to June 30, 2027.
responsible_party: University of Maryland, Baltimore County
stakeholders: Maryland citizen scientists, researchers, higher education institutions, private and nonprofit sector technology experts, and the Workgroup members.
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The University of Maryland, Baltimore County can staff the workgroup for two additional years using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates a representative from the University of Maryland, Baltimore County (UMBC)—a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland—as a member and specifically requires UMBC to provide administrative and operational staff support for the workgroup through its extension.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the Executive Director's designee, is statutorily designated as a member of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the membership composition, reporting requirements, and operating timeline of the Workgroup on Establishing a Science and Technology Best Practices and Innovation Network.

The Governor is responsible for appointing several members representing higher education and community-based science and technology applications, and the workgroup must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and coordinating gubernatorial appointments to state task forces, advisory councils, and workgroups, which are altered under this legislation.

responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Licensed deer hunters in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances, and there is no local fiscal impact.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange, in collaboration with the Maryland State Department of Education and other organizations, to promote access to health insurance for child care professionals through targeted outreach, enrollment assistance for health coverage and Medicaid, and conducting a survey on health care access among child care providers.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Child care professionals, child care employers, and child care providers
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Department of Commerce increase by $250,000 in FY 2026 to transfer funds from the Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE). MHBE special fund revenues and expenditures correspondingly increase by $250,000 in FY 2026 for the outreach campaign and survey. Ongoing MHBE expenses and MSDE partnership responsibilities will be absorbed with existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) to lead the implementation of the act by conducting outreach to child care professionals, assisting them in obtaining coverage through the exchange or Medicaid, and conducting a survey on health care access across the child care community.

The bill explicitly requires MHBE to partner with the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), utilize prekindergarten provider hubs established by MSDE, and consult with MSDE in developing the required child care health care access survey.

The fiscal note identifies a direct fiscal impact on the Department of Commerce, requiring a $250,000 transfer in special funds from Commerce's Child Care Capital Support Revolving Loan Fund to MHBE in FY 2026 to fund the outreach and survey activities.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees the state's Medicaid program, which is specifically targeted by the bill's outreach and enrollment assistance initiatives for child care professionals.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain common carriers from damaging certain public infrastructure necessitating the closure of the infrastructure; establishing that a violation of the Act is a public nuisance; authorizing the State or a local government to bring a civil action against a common carrier for a violation under the Act; and providing that a common carrier that commits a violation may be liable to the State or local government for civil penalties of $1,000 per day for each day the public nuisance continues.
Title: Public Nuisance - Common Carriers - Damage to Public Infrastructure

NarrowSubjects.Name: Motor Vehicles -see also- Aband Veh; Ambulances; Buses; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Prohibits common carriers engaged in transporting passengers by land from damaging state or locally owned bridges or highways resulting in their closure, defining such damage as a public nuisance. Authorizes the State or local governments to bring civil actions against common carriers for injunctive relief, declaratory relief, compensatory damages for repair or replacement costs, and civil penalties of up to $1,000 per day until the infrastructure is restored or replaced.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Transportation, Maryland Transportation Authority, and the Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Land-based passenger common carriers (including bus companies, rail companies, taxicab services, and transportation network companies), local governments, and the traveling public.
fiscal_impact_summary: The fiscal impact is indeterminate because incident frequency cannot be predicted. When violations occur, state general fund revenues and local revenues may increase from civil penalties of $1,000 per day. Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) and local government finances may recoup costs through compensatory damages for infrastructure repair or replacement, partially offset by increased legal and litigation expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDOT oversees the state's highways and bridges, which constitute the public infrastructure protected under this bill. MDOT and the Transportation Trust Fund are directly affected as the department would initiate civil actions to recover costs, receive compensatory damages for repairs, and incur potential litigation expenses.

As the MDOT modal administration responsible for designing, maintaining, and repairing state non-toll highways and bridges, SHA would directly suffer infrastructure damages, conduct necessary repairs or closures, and provide documentation to recover repair and replacement costs from responsible common carriers.

MDTA finances, operates, and maintains state toll bridges and highways. The fiscal note explicitly notes that MDTA may engage in litigation to pursue compensatory damages and civil penalties, incurring nonbudgeted expenditures and potentially recouping infrastructure repair costs.

The OAG provides legal representation to the State and MDOT. It would be responsible for initiating and litigating public nuisance civil actions against common carriers for injunctive relief, compensatory damages, and civil penalties.

The bill creates a new civil cause of action and statutory remedy under the Courts and Judicial Proceedings Article, which would be filed and adjudicated within the Maryland court system managed by the AOC.

fiscal_impact_summary: The Public Service Commission can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission regulates transportation network companies (TNCs) in Maryland and is the primary state agency tasked under the bill with receiving annual aggregated reporting regarding operator fares, hours driven, and earnings.

bill_summary: Authorizes the transfer of funds from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund by budget amendment if the fund's balance is depleted or if estimated disaster relief costs exceed the fund's balance, and reduces the Legislative Policy Committee's review and comment period for transfers from 15 days to 10 days.

stakeholders: State and local government agencies responding to emergencies, and Maryland residents and communities impacted by natural disasters or catastrophic events
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no net effect on overall State finances. If transfers occur, special fund expenditures from the Catastrophic Event Account and special fund revenues to the State Disaster Recovery Fund increase correspondingly. Interest revenues to the Revenue Stabilization Account (Rainy Day Fund) may decrease minimally if substantial funds are transferred. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDEM administers the State Disaster Recovery Fund, which under the bill is authorized to receive fund transfers from the Catastrophic Event Account when funds are depleted or disaster relief costs exceed the fund's balance.
DBM administers the Catastrophic Event Account within the State Reserve Fund and oversees the execution of budget amendments and state fund transfers governed by this legislation.

The bill directly amends the statutory procedure and timeframe under which the Governor may transfer funds by budget amendment from the Catastrophic Event Account to the State Disaster Recovery Fund following a reduced 10-day review period.

bill_summary: The Preserve Telehealth Access Act of 2025 permanently includes certain audio-only telephone conversations under the definition of telehealth and makes permanent the requirement that Medicaid and commercial health insurers reimburse telehealth services on the same basis and at the same rate as in-person services. It also alters the circumstances under which health care practitioners may prescribe Schedule II opiates for the treatment of pain via telehealth and requires the Maryland Health Care Commission to submit a telehealth report every four years beginning December 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Care Commission
stakeholders: Patients receiving telehealth services (including Medicaid enrollees and commercially insured individuals), health care providers and practitioners, and commercial health insurers and managed care organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures for the Maryland Health Care Commission increase by an estimated $100,000 in FY 2027, and every four years thereafter, to complete required telehealth reporting. Maryland Insurance Administration special fund revenues decrease minimally in FY 2026. Medicaid expenditures and federal matching funds continue beyond FY 2025 with an indeterminate net effect. Local government health expenditures may increase to continue reimbursing certain telehealth services.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates that the Maryland Health Care Commission submit a quadriennial report to the Governor and General Assembly starting in 2026 on telehealth advances, modalities, and cost changes, resulting in a recurring $100,000 fiscal impact.

The bill permanently mandates telehealth coverage and payment parity (including audio-only telephone conversations) under the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), which is administered by the Maryland Department of Health.

The bill permanently requires commercial health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations regulated by the Maryland Insurance Administration to provide telehealth coverage and reimbursement parity.
The bill amends provisions in the Health Occupations Article establishing clinical requirements and permissions for prescribing Schedule II controlled dangerous substances (CDS) via telehealth.

The bill specifically clarifies that telehealth payment parity requirements do not supersede the authority of the Health Services Cost Review Commission to set hospital rates and hospital facility fees for hospital-provided telehealth.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which was evaluated in the fiscal analysis regarding commercial insurance telehealth coverage requirements.
The Governor's Office receives the mandated four-year telehealth status report from the Maryland Health Care Commission.

responsible_party: Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Nonprofit hospitals, community-based organizations, community health workers, and hospital patients
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local governmental operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the hospital community benefit statute (§ 19-303 of the Health - General Article) administered by the Health Services Cost Review Commission (HSCRC). It expands the definition of 'community benefit' to include community health worker workforce programs that nonprofit hospitals report in their annual community benefits filings to HSCRC.

The bill references statutory definitions of community health workers governed under the Health - General Article and impacts public health workforce partnerships. In addition, HSCRC is an independent commission established within the Maryland Department of Health.

Synopsis: Clarifying the circumstances under which liability for the failure to comply with certain requirements relating to a tenant's right of first refusal to purchase residential property is restricted to the owner of the property and does not attach to the property.
Title: Residential Real Property - Tenants' Right of First Refusal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers
Transfer of Goods -see also- Goods&Svc; Leas&Rnt; RetailSale

bill_summary: Clarifies that following the closing of a contract of sale between a property owner and a third party, liability for noncompliance with statutory requirements regarding a tenant's right of first refusal is restricted solely to the owner and does not attach to the residential rental property.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development (Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs)
stakeholders: Residential rental property owners, residential tenants, and third-party property buyers
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends provisions governing the tenant's right of first refusal process under Real Property Section 8-119. The Office of Tenant and Landlord Affairs (OTLA), which receives required notices and oversees administrative aspects of this statute, is housed within the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill clarifies legal liability and title encumbrances arising from noncompliance with the tenant's right of first refusal law, which may be referenced in judicial litigation regarding residential real property transactions.

Synopsis: Extending the time for submission of the interim report and final report of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by 3 years; and extending the termination date for the Commission by 3 years.
Title: Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission - Reporting and Sunset Extension

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill extends the termination date and reporting deadlines of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by three years. The commission's interim report deadline is extended to June 1, 2028, the final report deadline to January 1, 2029, and the sunset date to June 30, 2029.
responsible_party: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals, individuals involved in the criminal and juvenile justice systems, and commission members.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $28,500 in FY 2026, $65,600 in FY 2027, $68,400 in FY 2028, and $42,100 in FY 2029 for the Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy to maintain one contractual program coordinator to support the commission through its extended duration. There is no effect on revenues, and local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP is the primary staffing agency for the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission and incurs direct general fund expenditures from FY 2026 through FY 2029 to maintain contractual staff to support the commission's extended operational timeline.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly extends the termination date (sunset) and interim and final reporting deadlines of the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission by three years.
The bill mandates that the Prison Education Delivery Reform Commission submit both its extended interim report and final report of findings and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools for the purpose of studying and making recommendations on practices to identify, prevent, and eliminate chronic absenteeism by students from schools in the State; and requiring the Task Force to report its findings and recommendations to the Governor and the General Assembly by December 31, 2025.
Title: Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Primary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Schools
Secondary Schools -see also- Private Schools; Public Sch

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools to study, analyze data on, and recommend culturally responsive and nonpunitive practices to identify, prevent, and reduce student chronic absenteeism. Requires the Maryland State Department of Education to update attendance regulations and distribute guidance and an absenteeism toolkit to local school systems.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education
stakeholders: Maryland public school students, parents, teachers, school administrators, and local school systems
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues are not affected. The Maryland State Department of Education can provide staff support for the task force and update regulations using existing budgeted resources. Local school finances are not expected to be materially affected, although local school operations may be impacted if new regulations impose additional requirements.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education is the primary implementing agency required to staff the Task Force, update student attendance regulations based on the Task Force's findings, and distribute chronic absenteeism toolkits and guidance to local school systems.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory, temporary body known as the Task Force to Improve Attendance and Reduce Chronic Absenteeism in Schools to study best practices, analyze attendance data, and make recommendations.
The Task Force includes a designated representative of the Governor's Office among its membership and must submit its final report and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Phasing in a requirement that all child support received in a month pass through to a family seeking assistance under the Family Investment Program and prohibiting the consideration of child support in computing the amount of assistance received.
Title: Family Investment Program - Child Support

NarrowSubjects.Name: Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst

bill_summary: This bill phases in an increase in the amount of child support collected each month that passes directly to families receiving Temporary Cash Assistance under the Family Investment Program, rather than being retained by the State. Starting in fiscal 2028, the passthrough increases progressively until fiscal 2031, when 100% of collected child support passes through to families and is disregarded when computing benefit amounts.
responsible_party: Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Families and children receiving assistance under the Family Investment Program / Temporary Cash Assistance
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $138,067 in FY 2027 for one-time technology updates (matched by $268,013 in federal funds), and then increase by $2.4 million in FY 2028, $6.2 million in FY 2029, $10.1 million in FY 2030, and $13.9 million annually beginning in FY 2031 to offset the loss of retained child support revenue and reimburse the federal government's share. Special fund revenues and expenditures decrease correspondingly. Local governments are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 881 directly amends the Human Services Article governing the Family Investment Program (FIP) and child support pass-through calculations. The Department of Human Services (DHS)—specifically its Family Investment Administration and Child Support Administration—is the primary agency responsible for administering these programs, updating eligibility and child support IT systems, and managing the associated fiscal adjustments.

Synopsis: Establishing that an individual who, after earning service credit sufficient for a vested allowance in the State Police Retirement System, the Correctional Officers' Retirement System, or the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System, separates from service, and subsequently returns to service in a position in the same system under certain circumstances, is subject to the same requirements to which certain members of the same system are subject.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System – Deferred Vested Former Members – Return to Service

NarrowSubjects.Name: Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Allows certain former members of the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers' Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who were members on or before June 30, 2011, separated from service, and later return to service under specified conditions to be subject to the pre-2011 pension benefit structure rather than the post-2011 reformed structure.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Returning members of the State Police Retirement System, Correctional Officers' Retirement System, and Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System who were enrolled on or before June 30, 2011, and had a qualified break in service.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is likely no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates, as the State Retirement Agency identified only 16 members of the Law Enforcement Officers' Pension System and no members of the other systems who would benefit. The bill has no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency directly administers the State Retirement and Pension System, including SPRS, CORS, and LEOPS, and is responsible for implementing the altered benefit tiers and record-keeping for returning members.
The bill directly impacts the State Police Retirement System (SPRS), affecting pension rules and benefit eligibility for re-employed State Police personnel.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters retirement system rules for the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS), affecting correctional staff employed by the department who separate and subsequently return to service.

As the principal personnel and state employee benefits administration agency for Maryland, DBM oversees state workforce policies and personnel regulations that interact with re-employment and pension provisions.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for an individual licensed as a certified public accountant in another state to practice certified public accountancy in the State by requiring that the individual must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination when qualifying for the license in the other state.
Title: Accountants - Licensed Out-of-State Practice Privileges - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications allowing out-of-state certified public accountants (CPAs) to practice in Maryland without obtaining a Maryland license. It repeals requirements for the National Association of State Boards of Accountancy (NASBA) to verify substantial equivalence to the Uniform Accountancy Act, establishing instead that an individual qualifies for practice privileges if they hold a valid CPA license from another state and were required to pass the Uniform CPA Examination to obtain that license.
responsible_party: State Board of Public Accountancy
stakeholders: Certified public accountants licensed in other states who wish to practice in Maryland, accounting firms, and their Maryland clients.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Board of Public Accountancy can implement the bill with existing resources. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the board are not materially affected. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Labor houses and supports the State Board of Public Accountancy, which directly regulates the practice and licensing privileges of certified public accountants in the state.

Synopsis: Altering the qualifications for an initial teacher certificate to include passing a portfolio-based assessment of a nationally accredited teacher preparation program.
Title: Education - Initial Teacher Certification - Qualifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters the qualifications for an initial teacher certificate by allowing candidates to qualify by passing a portfolio-based assessment from a nationally accredited teacher preparation program as an alternative to existing portfolio assessment or induction program requirements.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and the State Board of Education
stakeholders: Teacher candidates graduating from approved or alternative teacher preparation programs, accredited teacher preparation institutions, and local school systems.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material fiscal effect on State finances or local school systems, though it may expand the pool of licensed teachers available for local school systems to hire.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE) certifies and licenses educators in Maryland. This bill directly amends the qualifications and assessment requirements for individuals seeking an initial teacher certificate.

Synopsis: Requiring the Department of Natural Resources to suspend for up to 5 years for a first violation, rather than revoke, a person's oyster authorization for knowingly committing certain violations; providing for the reinstatement for certain persons of an oyster authorization and an entitlement to engage or work in the oyster fishery; altering a certain offense related to the use of prohibited gear; and repealing the 90-day time period within which a certain administrative hearing must be held.
Title: Tidal Fish Licenses - Oyster Authorizations - Administrative Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fish and Fishing -see also- Aquaculture; FishNets&Dev
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill modifies administrative penalties for commercial oyster harvesters, replacing the mandatory revocation of an oyster authorization for a first violation with a suspension of up to 5 years, while retaining revocation for second or subsequent violations. It adjusts the violation criteria for using prohibited gear by specifying that the gear must be used while more than 200 feet within a prohibited area, repeals the 90-day deadline for holding an administrative penalty hearing, and allows individuals whose authorizations were revoked prior to July 1, 2025, to have their entitlement to work in the fishery reinstated and reapply for an authorization 5 years after revocation.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Commercial oyster harvesters, individuals whose oyster authorizations have been suspended or revoked, and individuals on the commercial license waiting list.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State expenditures increase by an estimated $11,500 annually ($5,300 in general funds and $6,200 in special funds) for the Department of Natural Resources to cover the cost of holding additional administrative hearings with the Office of Administrative Hearings. Special fund revenues may decrease minimally as suspended authorizations are held rather than revoked and reissued to paying applicants on the waiting list. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary regulatory agency responsible for issuing tidal fish license oyster authorizations, conducting administrative penalty proceedings, suspending or revoking authorizations, and processing reinstatements.

The Office of Administrative Hearings conducts contested administrative penalty hearings under the Administrative Procedure Act on behalf of the Department of Natural Resources, with caseload and hearing volumes expected to increase under the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Secretary of Natural Resources to issue an incidental taking permit for the Indiana bat, the northern long-eared bat, the tricolor bat, or the eastern small-footed bat if an applicant submits a certain conservation plan and the Secretary makes certain findings.
Title: Endangered and Threatened Species - Incidental Taking - Bats

NarrowSubjects.Name: Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to issue incidental taking permits for the Indiana bat, northern long-eared bat, tricolored bat, or eastern small-footed bat, provided an applicant submits an approved conservation plan and the Secretary makes specific determinations regarding species survival and mitigation.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Land developers, businesses, and contractors operating in habitats of endangered bats, as well as wildlife conservation groups and threatened/endangered bat populations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and has no local government fiscal effect. It may provide meaningful relief to small businesses by offering an incidental taking permit process rather than requiring full adherence to activity and time-of-year restrictions in areas supporting endangered bats.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 894 directly authorizes the Secretary of Natural Resources to review conservation plans, make required statutory findings, issue incidental taking permits for specified bat species, and adopt implementing regulations.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of law governing the regulation of business, economic development, insurance, and labor and employment to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Employment and Insurance Equality for Service Members Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: The Employment and Insurance Equality for Service Members Act establishes uniform statutory definitions across Maryland law to align with federal standards, broadening protections, economic development programs, professional licensing accommodations, insurance provisions, and employment benefits from applying solely to the armed forces to include all uniformed services (such as the Public Health Service and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Corps), reserve components, veterans, and military spouses.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Department of Commerce, and Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Members of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, Public Health Service, and NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps), reserve components, veterans, military spouses and families, regulated employers, and insurers
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues increase minimally in FY 2026 only due to form filings submitted to the Maryland Insurance Administration. Otherwise, State finances and operations are not materially affected since the expansions apply to a limited number of individuals. Local government finances and operations are not materially impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill substantially amends the Labor and Employment, Business Regulation, and Financial Institutions Articles, directly impacting the department's administration of unemployment insurance benefits, the Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) system, apprenticeship credits, workforce development, occupational licensing units, and mortgage loan originator licensing.

The bill amends Section 9-901 of the State Government Article—which establishes the statutory framework and definitions governing the department—and requires the Department of Commerce to consult with DVMF in administering the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program.

The bill amends multiple provisions of the Insurance Article concerning insurance producer licensing, reinstatement fee waivers for deployed personnel, underwriting rules, and policy exclusions, which the administration regulates and for which it will process policy and form filings.

The bill amends the Economic Development Article to update the scope, definitions, and naming of the Uniformed Services Personnel and Veteran-Owned Small Business No-Interest Loan Program administered by Commerce.

The bill amends Section 20-502 of the Insurance Article to broaden the eligibility exceptions for motor vehicle liability insurance coverage provided by MAIF to all active-duty uniformed services members.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office monitors and implements the State's Veteran-Owned Small Business Enterprise (VSBE) Program across state agencies, which is affected by the bill's update to the definition of 'veteran' under Section 14-601 of the State Finance and Procurement Article.

The bill amends Commercial Law Section 14-1212.2 regarding protected consumer status under credit reporting laws for active service members, which is subject to enforcement by the Consumer Protection Division of the OAG.

Synopsis: Increasing the amount of a certain property tax exemption for dwelling houses owned by blind individuals or their surviving spouses from $15,000 to $40,000.
Title: Property Tax - Exemption for Blind Individuals - Alteration
bill_summary: Increases the property tax exemption on dwelling houses owned by qualified blind individuals or their surviving spouses from $15,000 to $40,000 of assessed value.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Legally blind homeowners and their unremarried surviving spouses, as well as county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Annuity Bond Fund revenues decrease by approximately $40,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 due to the increased exemption, resulting in an average state tax savings of $28 per homeowner. Local property tax revenues decrease by an estimated $450,000 annually beginning in FY 2026, saving homeowners an average of $320 each. State and local expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board hears appeals regarding property valuations and disputes over property tax exemptions and credits, which includes the statutory real property tax exemption for blind individuals altered by this bill.

The Department of Disabilities coordinates state programs, advocacy, and policies supporting Maryland residents with disabilities, including blind homeowners impacted by this property tax relief measure.
The Maryland Tax Court serves as the highest administrative body adjudicating appeals from the Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board concerning real property tax assessments and exemptions.

State property tax collections fund the Annuity Bond Fund, which the Treasurer oversees to pay debt service on State general obligation bonds; the bill reduces Annuity Bond Fund revenues by approximately $40,000 annually.

Synopsis: Increasing from two to four the number of speed monitoring systems that may be placed on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City; limiting to not more than one speed monitoring system in each direction that may be in operation at the same time on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City; and making permanent the authorization to place speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City.
Title: Baltimore City - Speed Monitoring Systems - Interstate 83

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Increases the number of speed monitoring systems authorized on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City from two to four, while limiting operation to no more than one camera in each direction at a time, and permanently eliminates the program's June 30, 2026 sunset date.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Department of Transportation
stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City and the Baltimore City local government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund revenues may increase starting as early as FY 2026 from contested citations decided in District Court, which will handle any added caseload with existing budgeted resources. Baltimore City revenues and expenditures may increase beginning in FY 2026 from installing additional cameras (with procurement and installation expenditures potentially beginning in FY 2025). Making the program permanent prevents the authorization from expiring at the end of FY 2026, preserving significant annual city fine revenues (which generated $5.6 million in FY 2024 from the two existing I-83 cameras) and associated operating expenditures beginning in FY 2027.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill expands and makes permanent speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City. Individuals receiving citations may contest them in the District Court of Maryland, which is administered and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts, resulting in a potential increase in contested caseloads and general fund revenues.

The bill amends the Maryland Transportation Article governing speed monitoring systems on interstate highways and affects highway speed enforcement and signage compliance within the state's broader transportation network.
Under the governing statute for speed monitoring systems, speed camera signage and speed display devices must conform to traffic control device standards adopted by the State Highway Administration.

Under state speed monitoring system laws, any net revenues generated by jurisdictions in excess of statutory caps must be remitted to the Comptroller of Maryland, which also tracks speed camera revenues and citation data.

Synopsis: Specifying that an individual may consent to the issuance of a permanent protective order against the individual.
Title: Family Law - Permanent Protective Orders - Consent
bill_summary: This bill allows an individual to consent to the issuance of a permanent protective order against themselves, expanding the statutory circumstances under which a court must issue a permanent protective order.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Victims of abuse seeking protective relief and respondents in protective order proceedings who choose to consent to a permanent protective order.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Judiciary increase by $30,300 in FY 2026 only for one-time computer programming costs. The bill is not anticipated to materially impact local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory criteria under which courts may issue permanent protective orders by allowing orders to be issued by consent. The Administrative Office of the Courts will incur a direct fiscal impact of $30,300 in FY 2026 for one-time judicial programming and system modifications.

Synopsis: Establishing the Public Health Abortion Grant Program to provide grants to improve access to abortion care clinical services for individuals in the State; establishing the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund to provide grants under the Program; and requiring that certain premium funds collected by health insurance carriers be used to provide certain coverage and to support improving access to abortion care clinical services under certain circumstances.
Title: Public Health Abortion Grant Program - Establishment

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Health Maintenance Organizations -see also- Manage Care Orgs
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund within the Maryland Department of Health to provide operating grants to eligible organizations to improve access to abortion care clinical services for uninsured, underinsured, or vulnerable individuals. The program is financed by transferring excess balances and accrued interest from health insurance carriers' ACA-mandated segregated abortion coverage accounts.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Individuals seeking abortion care clinical services who are uninsured, underinsured, or facing privacy risks; health care providers and clinics offering abortion services; and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $19.3 million in FY 2026 and $2.5 million annually thereafter from the transfer of excess funds in carriers' segregated accounts. Special fund expenditures increase by $2.0 million in FY 2026 via a required budget amendment and by $2.5 million annually beginning in FY 2027 from a mandated appropriation to fund grants (at least 90%) and administrative personnel costs (1.0 FTE). General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 from fund interest earnings. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 930 establishes the Public Health Abortion Grant Program and the associated special fund within the Maryland Department of Health. The Secretary of Health is responsible for administering the fund, developing grant standards, and awarding operating grants to eligible organizations.

The Maryland Insurance Administration and the Insurance Commissioner are tasked with collecting annual accountings of carriers' segregated accounts under the ACA, establishing reporting forms, and ordering the transfer of tens of millions of dollars in excess balances to the new special fund.
The bill explicitly mandates that the State Treasurer hold the Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund separately and invest the money of the fund in accordance with state investment procedures.
The bill explicitly designates the Comptroller of Maryland to account for the newly established Public Health Abortion Grant Program Fund.

The bill requires the Governor to allocate $2,000,000 to the program by budget amendment on or before October 1, 2025, and mandates the inclusion of specific annual appropriations in the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2027.

As the state's budget agency, DBM must facilitate the Governor's mandated budget amendment in fiscal year 2026 and incorporate the ongoing mandated appropriations for the fund into the state budget beginning in fiscal year 2027.
Under the Insurance Article provisions, carriers aggrieved by an order of the Insurance Commissioner have hearing and appeal rights that may be adjudicated by the Office of Administrative Hearings.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to place certain interests into a certain certified blind trust or divest of certain interests within 6 months after taking the oath of office; requiring the Governor to enter into a nonparticipation agreement with the State Ethics Commission for any interests not included in a blind trust; authorizing the Ethics Commission to impose a fine of up to $5,000 for each violation of the Act; requiring the Commission to adopt regulations to carry out the Act including standards for types of interests that be exempted; etc.
Title: Public Ethics - Conflicts of Interest and Blind Trust - Governor

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Governor, within six months of taking the oath of office, to place their financial interests into a certified blind trust approved by the State Ethics Commission or divest interests that pose potential conflicts of interest. For exempted interests not included in a blind trust, the Governor must enter into a nonparticipation agreement prohibiting participation in matters involving those interests. In addition, the bill requires business entities in which the Governor or specified family and household members hold a qualifying interest to report those interests when seeking State grants, awards, or contracts.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: The Governor of Maryland, the Governor-elect, specified relatives and household members of the Governor ('restricted individuals'), and business entities seeking State grants, awards, or contracts in which the Governor or restricted individuals hold qualifying ownership interests.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $95,000 in FY 2026 only for contractual IT services, consisting of $75,000 for the State Ethics Commission to update its electronic training systems and website, and $20,000 for the Department of General Services to add a check-off disclosure box to eMaryland Marketplace. Potential fines assessed on violators are distributed to the Fair Campaign Financing Fund but are not expected to materially affect special fund revenues. Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly establishes ethics requirements and restrictions on the Governor and Governor-elect, requiring them to establish a certified blind trust or divest interests, execute nonparticipation agreements for exempted assets, submit annual compliance certifications, and face potential civil fines for noncompliance.

The State Ethics Commission is the primary implementing and regulatory agency responsible for adopting regulations, approving blind trusts, granting exemptions, executing nonparticipation agreements, receiving disclosures from business entities, publishing records on its website, and assessing fines for noncompliance.

DGS is required to modify the eMaryland Marketplace procurement platform by October 1, 2025, to include a check-off box on procurement notices for bidders or offerors to disclose ownership interests held by the Governor or restricted family members, requiring $20,000 in IT expenditures.

The bill prohibits the Governor from participating in matters before the Board of Public Works involving interests not placed in a blind trust, and mandates that copies of any nonparticipation agreements be formally provided to the Executive Secretary and General Counsel of the Board.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Department of Health to review the cost reports and other data submitted by each nursing home that participates in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program; and requiring the Department to report the findings resulting from the review conducted under the Act to the Governor and certain committees of the General Assembly by October 1, 2025, and each October 1 thereafter through 2029.
Title: Nursing Homes - Cost Reports

NarrowSubjects.Name: Nurses -see also- Nurse Practitioners; Nursing Assistants
Nursing Homes -see also- AsstLiving; ContinCare; LTCare
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data submitted by nursing homes participating in the Maryland Medical Assistance Program—specifically regarding revenues allocated to contracted nursing care and wages for direct care nonadministrative staff—and to report its findings annually to the Governor and relevant legislative committees through 2029.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Medicaid-participating nursing homes, nursing home direct care and nonadministrative staff, and nursing home residents and caregivers
fiscal_impact_summary: State Effect: The Maryland Department of Health can review the required cost reports and data and complete the annual reports using existing budgeted resources. Revenues are unaffected. Local Effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to review cost reports and data submitted by nursing homes participating in Medicaid regarding revenue allocations to contracted nursing care and direct care staff wages, and to submit an annual report of its findings from 2025 through 2029.
The Governor's Office is a designated recipient of the annual report detailing the Department of Health's review and findings on nursing home cost reports through 2029.

Synopsis: Requiring that a carrier provide notice by certain electronic means, in addition to written notice, of cancellation or nonrenewal of a small group market health benefit plan and include information regarding additional health benefit coverage options in the notice; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2026.
Title: Health Insurance - Cancellation and Nonrenewal of Coverage - Required Notice

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Requires health insurance carriers to provide notice of cancellation or nonrenewal of a small employer health benefit plan by electronic means in addition to written notice, and requires the notice to include information regarding additional coverage options such as COBRA and plans available through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, small employers, and enrolled employees of small businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state or local fiscal or operational impact. It has a potential meaningful effect on small businesses and their employees by ensuring employees receive comprehensive written and electronic notice of cancellation or nonrenewal along with alternative coverage options.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurance carriers and enforces state insurance laws, including carrier compliance with notice requirements for cancellation or nonrenewal of small group health benefit plans.

The bill mandates that carrier notices sent to employees upon cancellation or nonrenewal of coverage include information regarding health coverage options available through the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange.

Synopsis: Requiring the appointment of an alternate subscriber member to the governing body of a continuing care provider; and authorizing the alternate subscriber member to attend all meetings of the governing body and vote only if the regular subscriber is unable to fulfill the subscriber's duties as a regular member of the governing body.
Title: Continuing Care Providers - Governing Bodies - Membership

NarrowSubjects.Name: Continuing Care -see also- Long-Term Care; Nursing Homes
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Requires the governing body of a continuing care provider that has only one subscriber member to authorize the appointment of an alternate subscriber member. The alternate subscriber is authorized to attend all meetings and may vote only when the regular subscriber is unable to fulfill their duties.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Aging
stakeholders: Continuing care retirement community providers, governing bodies of continuing care facilities, and facility subscribers/residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Aging can implement the bill's requirements, including modifying existing documents and amending regulations, using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Aging regulates continuing care retirement communities and providers under Title 10 of the Human Services Article. As noted in the fiscal note, the department is responsible for modifying existing documents and amending regulations to implement the bill's governance requirements.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Commission for Women to establish the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control to study access to over-the-counter birth control; and requiring the Collaborative to submit an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Governor and General Assembly by December 1, 2027.
Title: Maryland Commission for Women - Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Education -see also- ContEd; DrvEd; HigherEd; etc.
Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Commission for Women to establish and staff the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control to study access and coverage options for over-the-counter birth control and submit interim and final recommendation reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Commission for Women
stakeholders: Maryland consumers seeking over-the-counter birth control, pharmacies and retailers, health care providers, and health insurers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not impacted; the Maryland Commission for Women can staff the collaborative with existing budgeted resources. Revenues and local government operations are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Commission for Women, which is housed within the Department of Human Services, to establish, lead, and provide staff support for the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control. The Secretary of Human Services is also tasked with appointing numerous collaborative members.

The bill requires the Commissioner of the Maryland Insurance Administration to designate a representative to the Collaborative, which directly examines and recommends regulatory and point-of-sale coverage requirements for state-regulated health insurance plans.

The Secretary of Health is required to designate two representatives to the Collaborative (one from the Maryland Medical Assistance Program and one from public health) to assist in evaluating OTC birth control coverage and public health initiatives.

The Executive Director of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange is required to designate a representative to serve on the Collaborative to address coverage access across individual and small business exchange plans.
The Secretary of Budget and Management must designate a representative with expertise in the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program to serve on the Collaborative.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a multi-stakeholder body, the Maryland Collaborative to Advance Implementation of Coverage of Over-the-Counter Birth Control, which functions as a temporary advisory board to study and report on OTC contraception coverage before abrogating in 2028.

The Collaborative includes a representative from the Consumer Health Information Hub at the University of Maryland School of Public Health and may include representation from a constituent institution providing student health insurance.
The Collaborative is statutorily mandated to submit an interim report by January 1, 2026, and a final report by December 1, 2027, detailing its findings and recommendations to the Governor.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from committing a certain crime of malicious or fraudulent burning that causes the death of or serious physical injury to a firefighter; and establishing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a felony and on conviction is subject to imprisonment not to exceed 10 years.
Title: Criminal Law - Crimes of Malicious or Fraudulent Burning - Prohibitions and Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes a felony offense prohibiting a person from committing a crime of malicious or fraudulent burning that causes the death of or serious physical injury to a firefighter, punishable by up to 10 years of imprisonment.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Firefighters and individuals charged with or convicted of malicious or fraudulent burning crimes resulting in firefighter injury or death.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally due to increased incarceration costs from the 10-year felony penalty. Workload impacts on the Judiciary and the Office of the Public Defender are anticipated to be minimal and absorbable with existing budgeted resources. State revenues and local government finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new felony offense punishable by up to 10 years of imprisonment, which can run consecutively to underlying offenses, directly impacting DPSCS correctional facility populations and incarceration expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: OPD attorneys will be responsible for providing legal defense to indigent individuals facing charges under this new felony provision.
The Judiciary and state courts are responsible for presiding over the filing, trials, and sentencing of individuals charged under the newly established criminal offense.

As the primary state law enforcement agency (which includes the Office of the State Fire Marshal), MSP investigates state criminal violations, including arson and malicious burning incidents resulting in serious injury or death to firefighters.

Synopsis: Altering, from the last Tuesday in June to the fourth Tuesday in June, the date for the primary election in the year of the gubernatorial election.
Title: Election Law - Gubernatorial Primary Election - Date
bill_summary: Alters the date of Maryland's statewide primary election in gubernatorial election years from the last Tuesday in June to the fourth Tuesday in June.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland voters, political candidates, and state and local election officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Board of Elections is the primary agency responsible for administering and supervising statewide elections, and it will be directly responsible for scheduling and conducting the gubernatorial primary election on the newly designated fourth Tuesday in June.

Synopsis: Requiring each collector of taxes that maintains a website to include on the collector's website certain information and a certain link relating to the Homeowner Protection Program; altering the information the State Department of Assessments and Taxation is required to obtain and include in a certain annual report regarding tax sales; requiring the State Tax Sale Ombudsman to take certain actions to maximize enrollment in the Homeowner Protection Program; etc.
Title: Tax Sales - Homeowner Protection Program - Funding and Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill alters provisions related to the Homeowner Protection Program (HPP), which diverts vulnerable homeowners from the private tax lien sale process. It requires local tax collectors with websites to display a program description and application link, mandates that the State Tax Sale Ombudsman actively screen and maximize enrollment, prohibits the State Department of Assessments and Taxation from charging interest on unpaid taxes owed by enrolled homeowners, and expands reporting requirements. It also creates a recurring funding mechanism for the Homeowner Protection Fund consisting of an annual state appropriation of $250,000 from interest on overdue state property taxes and $500,000 collectively from county governments derived from interest on overdue county property taxes.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation (specifically the State Tax Sale Ombudsman)
stakeholders: Homeowners delinquent on property taxes or facing tax sales, local tax collectors, county governments, and tax lien purchasers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State special fund revenues and expenditures for the Homeowner Protection Fund increase by $750,000 annually ($250,000 from State property tax interest and $500,000 from county payments). State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually to replace the State property tax interest diverted from the Annuity Bond Fund for debt service. Local government expenditures increase collectively by $500,000 annually, apportioned among counties based on their share of real property accounts.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the Governor include an annual appropriation of $250,000 from the interest on overdue State property taxes to the Homeowner Protection Fund in the annual budget bill.
DBM prepares the executive budget and oversees state fiscal planning, and this bill establishes a mandated annual state budget appropriation of $250,000 for the Homeowner Protection Fund.
Under Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article, the State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the Homeowner Protection Fund separately and invest the money of the Fund.
Under Section 14-891 of the Tax - Property Article, the Comptroller is statutorily required to account for the Homeowner Protection Fund.

Synopsis: Establishing the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation; requiring the Workgroup to monitor and make recommendations related to the regulation of artificial intelligence, consumer protection, current private sector use of artificial intelligence, enforcement authority for the Office of the Attorney General's Office of Consumer Protection, and impact in the determination of government benefits; and requiring the Workgroup to make its recommendations to certain committees of the General Assembly by July 1, 2026.
Title: Consumer Protection - Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation

General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

bill_summary: This bill establishes the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation to examine issues and provide annual recommendations regarding the regulation of artificial intelligence, consumer and privacy protections, developer obligations, and the impact of AI on employment and government benefits.
responsible_party: University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security
stakeholders: Maryland consumers, private sector AI developers and deployers, labor and workforce organizations, and industries including technology, e-commerce, biotechnology, real estate, healthcare, and education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally in FY 2026 for costs associated with the workgroup. From FY 2027 through FY 2029, general fund expenditures may increase by up to $100,000 annually if the Governor exercises the discretionary authority to include an appropriation to support the workgroup in the state budget. There is no local fiscal effect.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill mandates that the University of Maryland Center for Health and Homeland Security provide staff support for the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, and the fiscal analysis assumes funding up to $100,000 annually will be provided through the USM budget.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Artificial Intelligence Implementation, a temporary multi-stakeholder body tasked with studying AI issues, monitoring implementation, and reporting recommendations to the General Assembly.

The Attorney General (or designee) is designated as a member of the workgroup, and the workgroup is specifically charged with evaluating and recommending enforcement authority for the Office of the Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO), or the CEO's designee, is designated as a statutory member of the workgroup.
The Governor is tasked with appointing 19 members from diverse sectors to the workgroup and is authorized to include an annual appropriation of $100,000 in the State budget to support the workgroup.

Synopsis: Specifying that the scope of the Maryland Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry and Referral System includes private and State inpatient and outpatient mental health and substance use services; requiring the Maryland Department of Health and the Department of Human Services, under certain circumstances, to ensure pediatric hospital overstay patients are placed in the least restrictive setting when clinically indicated and when possible; etc.
Title: Public Health - Pediatric Hospital Overstay Patients and Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Overstays

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
