Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Minors -see also- Age of Majority; Youth
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and the Department of Human Services (DHS) to ensure pediatric hospital overstay patients are transferred to the least restrictive clinically indicated setting and to establish a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator within each department. It allows hospitals to concurrently explore in-state and out-of-state placements, establishes the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays, clarifies the scope of the State's Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry, and authorizes funding to staff five additional beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents (JLG RICA).
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Department of Human Services
stakeholders: Pediatric patients under age 22 experiencing hospital overstays in inpatient or emergency departments, children in out-of-home or unlicensed placements, hospitals, and behavioral health and residential treatment providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by approximately $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026 to fund staffing for five additional beds at the JLG RICA. The FY 2026 budget as passed includes $6.0 million in general funds for pediatric overstays, sufficient to cover initial costs. MDH, DHS, and the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect can implement the coordinator and workgroup responsibilities using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on revenues or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is a primary implementing agency responsible for ensuring pediatric hospital overstay patients are placed in the least restrictive setting, establishing a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, maintaining the Mental Health and Substance Use Disorder Registry and Referral System, staffing five additional beds at John L. Gildner RICA ($3.0 million annual fiscal impact), and serving on the Workgroup.

DHS is a primary implementing agency tasked with establishing a Pediatric Hospital Overstay Coordinator, ensuring children committed to its custody who experience pediatric hospital overstays are placed in the least restrictive setting, and serving on the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays to evaluate bed needs and develop plans to end unlicensed placements and overstays, and tasks the State Council on Child Abuse and Neglect (SCCAN) with staffing the workgroup.

The Governor is authorized to appropriate funding to staff additional beds at RICA, appoints 11 members to the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays, and receives the Workgroup's final report.
The Secretary of Juvenile Services or their designee is designated by statute as an ex officio member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Public Defender or their designee is designated by statute as a member of the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

DBM oversees the state budget and personnel allocations, which is impacted by the bill's estimated $3.0 million annual general fund expenditure and filling of positions to staff five beds at the John L. Gildner Regional Institute for Children and Adolescents.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the 11 specialized stakeholder members to the Workgroup on Children in Unlicensed Settings and Pediatric Hospital Overstays.

Synopsis: Establishing the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove to study how urban renewal caused the displacement of residents from the Emory Grove community and make recommendations on potential remedies to those who were displaced by urban renewal; requiring the Task Force to submit an interim report by December 15, 2025, and a final report of its findings and recommendations to the Montgomery County Council, the Montgomery County Executive, the Montgomery County Delegation, and the General Assembly by December 15, 2026.
Title: Montgomery County - Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove MC 5-25

NarrowSubjects.Name: Historical Matters -see also- Archives; Monumts; Museum; etc
Real Estate -see also- Agents and Brokers

bill_summary: Establishes the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove to study the impacts of the urban renewal program carried out from 1960 through 1985 in the Emory Grove community and to recommend potential remedies for displaced residents and former landowners.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Office of Human Rights
stakeholders: Displaced residents and former landowners of the Emory Grove community, Emory Grove United Methodist Church, and Montgomery County residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state fiscal impact. Montgomery County can implement the bill and staff the task force using existing resources.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: House Bill 964 establishes the Task Force on the Displacement of Residents of Emory Grove, a temporary statutory body created by the General Assembly to study the historic displacement of residents due to urban renewal and recommend potential remedies.

Synopsis: Legalizing the 2025 Edition of the Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement to the extent to which that code or supplement contains laws enacted by the General Assembly.
Title: Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws - 2025 Edition - Legalization
bill_summary: This bill legalizes the 2025 Edition of the Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws and any supplement containing laws enacted by the General Assembly, establishing it as recognized evidence of the law in Maryland courts and by public officials.
responsible_party: Somerset County Government
stakeholders: Somerset County government officials, Maryland state and local courts, legal professionals, and residents of Somerset County.
fiscal_impact_summary: No State fiscal effect. Somerset County local expenditures for publication costs are expected to be minimal in FY 2026 and absorbable within existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill provides that the 2025 Edition of the Somerset County Code of Public Local Laws shall be recognized and admitted as evidence of the law in all Maryland state courts, which are operationally supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

Synopsis: Altering, with respect to business licensing requirements in the State, the definition of "storage warehouse" to exclude a self-service storage facility.
Title: Business Regulation – Licensing – Definition of Storage Warehouse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Commerce and Business -see also- ElectrComm; ForeignTr; etc.
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: This bill alters the definition of "storage warehouse" under Maryland's business licensing laws to exclude self-service storage facilities, thereby exempting them from the requirement to obtain a storage warehouse license and pay associated licensing fees.
responsible_party: Clerks of the Circuit Court
stakeholders: Owners and operators of self-service storage facilities, the Judiciary, and the Comptroller of Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease, likely minimally, beginning in FY 2026 due to self-service storage facilities no longer paying annual warehouse licensing fees ($30 to $150 based on population). State expenditures are not materially affected. Local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Storage warehouse licenses are issued by the clerks of the circuit courts, which receive operational and administrative support from the Administrative Office of the Courts. The bill exempts self-service storage facilities from the requirement to obtain a license from the clerks.

Storage warehouse licensing fees collected by the court clerks are remitted to the Comptroller for deposit into the State's general fund. The exemption will result in a minimal reduction in general fund revenues remitted to the Comptroller.
The Department of Labor regulates businesses and professional licensing under the Business Regulation Article and was consulted as an informational source regarding the licensing scope change.

Synopsis: Authorizing the governing body of a county to enter into a payment in lieu of taxes agreement with a provider of broadband service located in the county for property located in the county and owned by the provider; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
Title: Property Tax - Payment in Lieu of Taxes Agreements - Broadband Service Providers

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes county governments to enter into payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT) agreements with broadband service providers for provider-owned real and personal property in the county, exempting all or specified portions of that property from county property tax in exchange for negotiated annual payments.
responsible_party: County governing bodies
stakeholders: Broadband service providers and county governments
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. County property tax revenues may decrease beginning in fiscal 2026 to the extent counties enter into PILOT agreements and exempt provider property; however, any tax revenue reduction will be mitigated by the negotiated payments in lieu of taxes. Specific revenue impacts are indeterminate and depend on individual agreements. Local expenditures are unaffected.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing a step therapy or fail-first protocol for insulin or an insulin analog used to treat an insured's or enrollee's Type 1, Type 2, or gestational diabetes; and applying the Act to all policies, contracts, and health benefit plans issued, delivered, or renewed in the State on or after January 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from requiring step therapy or fail-first protocols for FDA-approved insulin or insulin analogs prescribed to treat Type 1, Type 2, or gestational diabetes.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Individuals with Type 1, Type 2, or gestational diabetes, health insurance carriers, pharmacy benefits managers, and healthcare prescribers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 resulting from $125 rate and form filing fees, with form reviews managed using existing resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency tasked with enforcing state health insurance mandates. It is responsible for reviewing policy and form filings from carriers to ensure compliance with the prohibition on step therapy or fail-first protocols for insulin, and will collect form filing fees associated with updated policies.

The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program. Although the program is already compliant and does not impose step therapy or fail-first protocols on diabetes medications, DBM is directly reviewed for potential state benefit plan impacts.

Synopsis: Establishing the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee to provide advice on the planning of the Park; requiring the Advisory Committee to make recommendations to ensure that the Park focuses on mental and physical health and well-being, is equitable in providing access to the property, is truthful about the history of Crownsville Hospital, and preserves the natural beauty of the site; and requiring the Committee to report its achievements and recommendations to certain entities by February 1 each year.

bill_summary: Establishes the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee to advise on the planning process, collect public input, and make recommendations regarding the development and historical preservation of Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park, with annual reports required through 2030.
responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee
stakeholders: Residents of Anne Arundel County, adjacent communities to Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park, historical and cultural preservationists, and park visitors
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or Anne Arundel County operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Executive Director of the Governor's Office of Community Initiatives (or their designee) as a statutory member of the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee.
The bill requires the Governor to appoint one member representing the Office of the Governor to serve on the newly established advisory committee.
The committee includes a representative of Bowie State University, designated by the university's president. Bowie State University is a constituent institution of the University System of Maryland.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a state-authorized advisory body, the Anne Arundel County Crownsville Hospital Memorial Park Advisory Committee, to advise on site planning, historical preservation, and development.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and appointing the representative of the Office of the Governor to the advisory committee.

Synopsis: Altering certain requirements for continuing education required for the renewal of a license for real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, and real estate salespersons, including the number of clock hours, course topics, course instructors, and course application fees.
Title: Real Estate Commission - Continuing Education Requirements - Alterations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Job Training -see also- Continuing Ed; Vocational Rehab

bill_summary: Alters continuing education requirements for license renewal of real estate brokers, associate brokers, and salespersons in Maryland. The bill modifies required clock hours and topics for courses including fair housing, Americans with Disabilities Act compliance, and broker supervision; repeals the topic of property flipping from required ethics coursework; specifies that course providers select instructors; and authorizes the State Real Estate Commission to set continuing education course application fees rather than keeping the statutory $25 fee.
responsible_party: State Real Estate Commission
stakeholders: Licensed real estate brokers, associate real estate brokers, real estate salespersons, and real estate continuing education course providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The State Real Estate Commission can implement the bill's changes with existing resources. State revenues are likely not materially affected, as the Commission does not plan to change the course application fee from its current $25 level. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Real Estate Commission is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor's Division of Occupational and Professional Licensing. The Department is directly responsible for administering the licensing, continuing education requirements, and fee schedules for real estate brokers and salespersons.

Synopsis: Clarifying the application of certain health insurance preventive services coverage requirements to certain high deductible health plans; and requiring the Insurance Commissioner to enforce certain provisions of law related to preventive services consistent with the recommendations and guidelines set by certain federal agencies in effect on December 31, 2024.
Title: Health Insurance - Preventive Services - High Deductible Health Plans and Enforcement Authority

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs
Intergovernmental Cooperation -see also- AdmAgn; Cmts; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 974 requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce coverage mandates for preventive health services without cost-sharing consistent with federal guidelines and recommendations in effect on December 31, 2024. The bill permits the Commissioner to adopt regulations expanding coverage or incorporating future recommendations, and clarifies how deductibles apply to preventive services under high deductible health plans.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, Maryland insureds and enrollees (including those enrolled in high deductible health plans), healthcare providers, and religious organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can adopt required regulations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article and directly mandates the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce health insurance preventive services coverage requirements without cost-sharing and authorizes the Commissioner to adopt regulations to implement and enforce these standards.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain operator of a certain self-service storage facility to notify at least 10 days prior to conducting a sale of an occupant's personal property stored in certain leased space at the self-service storage facility of the time, place, and terms of the sale by hand delivery, verified mail, or electronic mail at the occupant's last known address.
Title: Maryland Self-Service Storage Act - Sale of Personal Property in Satisfaction of Lien - Notice Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer

bill_summary: Requires self-service storage facility operators to notify occupants of the time, place, and terms of a public sale at least 10 days before selling stored personal property to satisfy a lien. If the operator sends the notice via email and does not receive a response or delivery confirmation at least 5 days before the sale, the operator must promptly send a second notice by verified mail.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Operators of self-service storage facilities and occupants leasing storage space.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General houses the Consumer Protection Division, which enforces statutory provisions under the Commercial Law Article concerning consumer protections, notices, and commercial transactions like self-service storage lien sales.

Synopsis: Establishing the Language Assistance Program; requiring a local board of elections to participate in the Program if the State Board determines that there is a significant need for language assistance to voters in the county in a language other than English; requiring the State Board to designate, not later than February 1 of the year of the election, certain languages other than English in which a local board that is required to participate in the Program must provide assistance to voters; etc.
Title: Election Law - Local Boards of Elections - Language Assistance Program

Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Establishes the Language Assistance Program requiring the State Board of Elections (SBE) to determine counties where there is a significant need for language assistance for voters in languages other than English based on specific demographic thresholds. Local boards of elections in designated counties must provide translation services at early voting centers and polling places, post notices in designated languages, provide online voting materials in those languages, and make reasonable efforts to recruit bilingual election judges.
responsible_party: Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Voters with limited English proficiency, local boards of elections, and county election officials.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $122,000 in FY 2026, reflecting $50,000 for a demographics consultant and $72,000 for translation software service licenses, with ongoing costs of at least $50,000 in FY 2028 and FY 2030. Local government expenditures increase beginning in FY 2026 for qualifying counties to cover hardware, software usage fees, polling place signage, and written translation of materials. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 983 establishes the Language Assistance Program under the oversight and administration of the Maryland State Board of Elections (SBE). SBE is directly responsible for determining county need, designating languages, publishing lists on its website, adopting regulations, and procuring licensed translation software services, resulting in direct general fund expenditures.

The bill creates a new misdemeanor criminal offense punishable by fines and up to 90 days imprisonment, authorizes civil penalties, and establishes civil liability for damages, which impacts court dockets and judicial operations.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the Objective Criteria Committee of the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) and establishes a new Compensation and Staffing Committee in its place. It transfers responsibilities regarding the establishment of objective criteria for staffing levels, qualifications, compensation, and incentive pay to the new committee. Additionally, it clarifies the conditions under which the Chief Investment Officer and Investment Division personnel can receive awarded incentive compensation if they retire directly from the division after a separation or furlough.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Chief Investment Officer and professional staff of the Investment Division of the State Retirement Agency, and the Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by $10,000 annually beginning in FY 2026 (with the exception of FY 2029, when a consultant would have been hired under current law) to retain a consultant assisting the Compensation and Staffing Committee. Expenditures may increase further if the consultant is engaged to provide executive search services. The State Retirement Agency can otherwise staff the committee with existing resources. There is no effect on revenues and minimal local impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly governs the Board of Trustees and the Investment Division of the State Retirement Agency, altering committee structures (replacing the Objective Criteria Committee with the Compensation and Staffing Committee), setting rules for CIO and investment staff compensation and incentives, and requiring special fund expenditures for a consultant.
The Secretary of Budget and Management (or the Secretary's designee) is statutorily designated as a required member of the newly created Compensation and Staffing Committee of the Board of Trustees.
The State Treasurer (or the Treasurer's designee) is explicitly identified as an official who may be appointed to the Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

The Comptroller of Maryland (or the Comptroller's designee) is explicitly identified as an official who may be appointed to the Compensation and Staffing Committee by the Chairman of the Board of Trustees.

Synopsis: Clarifying the membership in the Correctional Officers' Retirement System for certain employees of certain Maryland Department of Health facilities; and clarifying that certain participating employees who are appointed, promoted, or transferred are members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System as a condition of employment.
Title: Correctional Officers' Retirement System - Membership - Clarifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill makes certain Maryland Department of Health employees at specified facilities members of the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) as a condition of employment rather than the Employees' Pension System or Employees' Retirement System. It also provides for the transfer of prior service credit and clarifies membership, vesting, and retirement allowance calculations for affected employees.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees of the State Retirement and Pension System
stakeholders: Up to 30 Maryland Department of Health employees in specified supervisory and managerial positions across seven state health and psychiatric facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State pension liabilities increase by $470,000, resulting in an increase in State pension contributions of $53,600 in FY 2028 (allocated 60% general funds, 20% special funds, and 20% federal and other funds), with annual increases thereafter according to actuarial assumptions. The State Retirement Agency can administer transfers using existing resources. There is no effect on revenues or local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency administers the State Retirement and Pension System, which includes the Correctional Officers' Retirement System (CORS) and Employees' Pension System (EPS). The agency is directly responsible for administering the transfer of service credit, calculating retirement and disability benefits, and processing opt-out elections under the bill.

The bill specifically applies to designated positions and facilities within the Maryland Department of Health (such as Eastern Shore Hospital Center, Spring Grove Hospital Center, and others), moving certain supervisory and direct care staff into CORS as a condition of employment.

As the state's central personnel and budget agency, DBM oversees state employee benefits and personnel classifications, and is responsible for incorporating the increased state employer pension contributions into future state budgets.

Synopsis: Clarifying that the maximum average final compensation that certain retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System is to be based on the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale as of January 1 of the preceding calendar year in order to be exempt from a certain reemployment earnings limitation; and adding an average final compensation reemployment exemption for the temporary suspension of a retirement allowance for disability retirees.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Reemployment Earnings Limitations - Maximum Average Final Compensation

NarrowSubjects.Name: Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: This bill updates the threshold for exempting certain State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS) service and disability retirees from reemployment earnings limitations and benefit suspensions. Instead of a fixed average final compensation (AFC) cap of less than $25,000, the bill establishes that retirees are exempt if their AFC was less than the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale as of January 1 of the preceding calendar year.
responsible_party: State Retirement and Pension System Board of Trustees
stakeholders: Reemployed service and disability retirees of the State Retirement and Pension System whose average final compensation was below the minimum annual salary on the standard State pay scale, as well as participating public employers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no discernible effect on State or local pension liabilities or contribution rates because the State Retirement and Pension System does not account for foregone benefit offsets. It has no effect on State or local revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency is the primary implementing agency responsible for administering the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), including calculating average final compensation, enforcing reemployment earnings limitations, and applying exemptions from benefit offsets or suspensions.

As the state's central personnel agency, DBM establishes and maintains the standard State pay scale, the minimum annual salary of which serves as the statutory benchmark for the reemployment earnings limitation exemptions in the bill.

Synopsis: Altering certain due dates of certain reports from the State Retirement and Pension System; and clarifying the eligibility requirements of State Police Retirement System members to participate in the Deferred Retirement Option Program.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System – Alterations and Clarifications
bill_summary: House Bill 1034 extends the statutory due dates for two annual reports prepared by the State Retirement Agency regarding minority business enterprise utilization and Maryland-based venture capital investments. It also clarifies eligibility for the State Police Retirement System's Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) by basing the participation duration on years of employment in an eligible position rather than years of eligibility service credit.
responsible_party: State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: Members of the State Police Retirement System (including Maryland State Troopers and State Police Cadets), minority business enterprise brokerage and investment management services firms, and the State Retirement and Pension System.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material effect on State governmental operations or finances, and no local fiscal effect. Linking DROP eligibility to years of employment rather than service credit restores eligibility to intended levels, affecting an estimated single individual, and has no material effect on State pension liabilities or contribution rates.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1034 directly alters reporting deadlines for reports issued by the State Retirement and Pension System's Investment Committee and Board of Trustees, and clarifies statutory eligibility criteria for the State Police Retirement System's Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP), which the agency administers.

The bill directly modifies eligibility standards for participation in the Deferred Retirement Option Program (DROP) for members of the State Police Retirement System, including Maryland State Troopers and the Secretary of State Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters the annual statutory deadline from September 1 to November 1 for a report submitted to this office regarding minority business enterprise (MBE) brokerage and investment management utilization by the State Retirement and Pension System.

bill_summary: The Next Generation Energy Act comprehensively alters Maryland's regulation and procurement of electricity and gas infrastructure. Among other provisions, the act authorizes the Department of Housing and Community Development to issue loans for emissions-reduction projects; establishes competitive solicitation and expedited Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) processes for dispatchable generation, energy storage, and nuclear energy; sets specific rate schedule requirements for large load customers; restricts utility cost recovery for certain expenses; excludes waste-to-energy and refuse-derived fuel from Tier 1 of the Renewable Energy Portfolio Standard (RPS); and directs Strategic Energy Investment Fund compliance fees to provide electric bill credits to residential customers in fiscal 2026.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Maryland residential, commercial, and industrial electric and natural gas customers; investor-owned utilities, municipal electric utilities, and electric cooperatives; clean energy, nuclear, and energy storage developers; and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, special fund expenditures for the Public Service Commission (PSC) increase by $200 million to distribute residential electric customer bill credits funded by a transfer from the Strategic Energy Investment Fund. PSC and Office of People's Counsel administrative special fund expenditures increase by at least $2.9 million annually beginning in FY 2026, matched by assessment revenues on utilities. Department of Natural Resources expenditures increase by $0.8 million in FY 2026 and at least $1.2 million annually thereafter. Local finances are impacted, including an estimated $12.2 million annual revenue loss for Montgomery County starting in FY 2027 due to the removal of waste-to-energy from the RPS.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: PSC is the primary regulatory and implementing agency under the bill. It is responsible for overseeing utility rates, reviewing gas infrastructure replacement plans, regulating large load tariffs, conducting procurements for energy storage and nuclear generation, administering expedited Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) reviews, and overseeing the distribution of $200 million in ratepayer relief credits.

MEA is tasked with pursuing interstate cost-sharing and federal siting agreements for nuclear energy in coordination with PSC and DNR, reporting on those efforts, and managing the Strategic Energy Investment Fund (SEIF), which is significantly impacted by the transfer of up to $200 million for ratepayer refunds.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is assigned key statutory duties to review, evaluate, and recommend proposals for dispatchable energy and large capacity energy resources, evaluate CPCN application completeness under expedited timelines, and coordinate on regional nuclear agreements.

OPC represents residential utility consumers in proceedings before the PSC. The numerous new complex regulatory proceedings, multi-year rate cases, and procurement dockets established by the bill require OPC to expand staff and consultant capacity, and OPC is granted fast-track procurement authority.

DHCD is authorized to issue loans in addition to grants for multifamily residential building greenhouse gas reduction projects and can count expanded funding sources toward its EmPOWER Maryland energy reduction targets, significantly altering its program financing and ratepayer funding needs.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOSBA is specifically required by the bill, in consultation with the Office of the Attorney General, to assist potential applicants and minority investors in nuclear energy projects and establish clear plans for setting MBE participation goals and procedures.
DGS houses the Chief Procurement Officer (CPO), who is required under new fast-track procurement provisions to review and approve specified consultant procurement contracts within five business days.

MD Labor's Commissioner of Labor and Industry is tasked with determining prevailing wage rates and enforcing prevailing wage and labor standards required for underground infrastructure contracts, energy storage construction, and community benefit agreements under the bill.

DHS is mandated to submit a report to the Governor and the General Assembly by January 1, 2026, detailing legislative and regulatory changes needed to consolidate all State energy assistance programs into a single program.

The Comptroller administers Maryland's income tax and will be responsible for implementing the new income tax subtraction modification for legislative energy relief refunds received by residential utility customers.

The OAG is required to consult with GOSBA to provide assistance to potential applicants and minority investors and to establish minority business enterprise plans and procedures for approved nuclear generation projects.

As the State's MBE certification agency, MDOT is identified in the fiscal note as needing to conduct a disparity study to evaluate MBE participation in nuclear energy facilities to support GOSBA's goal-setting requirements.

MDE is granted fast-track consultant procurement authority for climate and greenhouse gas matters, provides greenhouse gas emissions data used to set baseline reduction targets, and handles air and water quality permitting for new generation and storage facilities.

The Governor is specifically authorized to transfer up to $200 million by budget amendment from SEIF to PSC for electric bill refunds and receives multiple mandated reports from state agencies under the bill.
BPW maintains overarching constitutional and statutory oversight of State procurements, including reviewing contracts exceeding $200,000 that may arise under the fast-track procurement provisions.

Synopsis: Altering the factors the Public Service Commission must consider before taking final action on a certificate of public convenience and necessity; establishing a distributed generation certificate of public convenience and necessity to authorize the construction and operation of a certain distributed solar energy generating system; requiring the Power Plant Research Program, by July 1, 2026, to develop and submit to the Commission proposed siting and design requirements and licensing conditions; etc.
Title: Public Utilities - Generating Stations - Generation and Siting (Renewable Energy Certainty Act)

bill_summary: The Renewable Energy Certainty Act establishes a standardized framework for the siting, review, and approval of solar energy generating stations and front-of-the-meter energy storage devices. It creates a Distributed Generation Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (DGCPCN) for community solar systems between 2 and 5 megawatts, restricts local governments from banning these facilities or denying conforming site plans, and requires expedited local reviews. Additionally, it establishes consumer protections and a special contractor license for residential rooftop solar installations, updates state solar mapping tools, and directs the Public Service Commission to conduct studies on energy procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Solar and energy storage developers, electric companies and suppliers, residential rooftop solar customers and contractors, community solar subscribers (including low- to moderate-income households), and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State expenditures increase by approximately $2.41 million across agencies: $403,385 in special funds for the Public Service Commission (PSC), $1,816,564 in general/special funds for the Department of Natural Resources (DNR) Power Plant Research Program, and $187,270 in general funds for the Maryland Department of Labor. PSC special fund revenues increase correspondingly by $403,385 in FY 2026 and by at least $0.7 million annually beginning in FY 2027 from utility assessments and DGCPCN application fees. MD Labor general fund revenues increase beginning in FY 2027 from licensing fees. Local government operations and finances may be significantly impacted through altered zoning authority, administrative permitting workloads, and changes in local tax and permit revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission is the primary regulator and implementing agency under the bill, responsible for establishing and issuing Distributed Generation Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (DGCPCNs), approving front-of-the-meter energy storage devices, adopting associated regulations, jointly setting application fees, and conducting two major studies on generation procurement models and community solar automatic enrollment.

The department's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is tasked with developing proposed standard siting and design requirements and licensing conditions for DGCPCNs, reviewing DGCPCN applications, jointly setting application fees, updating the SmartDG+ tool, and assessing State-owned land for solar suitability, requiring significant additional staff and budget.

The Maryland Department of Labor is required to establish and administer a new special solar contractor license for individuals installing and maintaining residential rooftop solar energy generating systems, establish minimum qualifications, and handle licensing enforcement.

The Maryland Energy Administration is statutorily required to consult with the Department of Natural Resources to update the SmartDG+ screening tool with State-owned land and complete an analysis identifying State land suitable for solar energy development.

The Department of Planning is required to consult with the Department of Natural Resources on updating the SmartDG+ tool and analyzing State-owned land for solar development, and is involved in land use coordination concerning Priority Preservation Areas.
The Department of Transportation must consult with the Department of Natural Resources to update the SmartDG+ tool and evaluate State-owned land suitable for solar energy development.

The Department of the Environment must be notified of power plant construction CPCN applications, is required to expedite regulatory processes under electricity procurement models, and oversees environmental and stormwater standards referenced in the bill.

The bill mandates that herbicide use on solar and energy storage sites comply with the Department of Agriculture's weed control program and references agricultural activities recognized by the department for agrivoltaics.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents residential utility customer interests in proceedings before the Public Service Commission regarding CPCN/DGCPCN approvals, utility rate impacts, and the mandated generation procurement and community solar studies.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel and enforcement support for state agencies, with the fiscal note budgeting for legal staffing to assist the Department of Labor with developing and enforcing the new solar contractor licensing program.

Synopsis: Updating references to federal law related to family planning services, grandfathered plans, explanation of benefits, summaries of benefits and coverage, medical loss ratios, catastrophic plans, annual limits for cost sharing, prescription drugs, and rescissions; altering the definitions of "legally protected health care" and "sensitive health services" to include gender-affirming care for purposes of law governing the disclosure of information regarding sensitive health services; etc.
Title: Health Insurance, Family Planning Services, and Confidentiality of Medical Records - Consumer Protections - Updates

bill_summary: This bill updates statutory references to federal law across several health insurance consumer protection standards and the State Family Planning Program to reflect federal regulations in effect on December 31, 2024. It expands the definitions of 'legally protected health care' and 'sensitive health services' to include gender-affirming care under medical record confidentiality laws, and establishes concurrent enforcement jurisdiction between the Maryland Insurance Commissioner and the Maryland Commission on Civil Rights regarding nondiscrimination in health insurance.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration, Maryland Commission on Civil Rights, and Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals receiving family planning, reproductive health, or gender-affirming services; health insurance carriers; health insurance policyholders; and health care providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations, and has no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill updates numerous insurance consumer protection provisions under Title 15 of the Insurance Article, grants the Insurance Commissioner concurrent jurisdiction to enforce anti-discrimination laws in health insurance, and authorizes the Commissioner to adopt corresponding regulations.

The bill directly amends provisions governing the Family Planning Program and the Maryland Medical Assistance Program administered by MDH, and alters statutory definitions of 'legally protected health care' and 'sensitive health services' regarding medical records and health care protection under the Secretary of Health.

The bill establishes concurrent jurisdiction between the Commission on Civil Rights and the Insurance Commissioner to enforce statutory prohibitions against discrimination by health insurance carriers.

The bill updates federal reference dates governing the Exchange's statutory requirement to adopt regulations establishing processes for hardship and affordability exemptions, and requires the Insurance Commissioner to consult with the Exchange regarding summary of benefits and coverage standards.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a mechanical repair contract from containing a provision precluding coverage for service to a motor vehicle solely for issues identified in a technical services bulletin and prohibiting the denial of a service claim solely for such an issue by a guarantor or provider.
Title: Mechanical Repair Contracts - Technical Service Bulletins

NarrowSubjects.Name: Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Prohibits motor vehicle mechanical repair contracts from including provisions that preclude coverage solely for vehicle issues identified in a technical service bulletin, and prohibits guarantors or providers from denying claims solely because the diagnosed issue was identified in such a bulletin.
responsible_party: Office of the Attorney General (Consumer Protection Division)
stakeholders: Motor vehicle owners who purchase mechanical repair contracts or extended warranties, as well as vehicle dealers, contract obligors, guarantors, and providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Consumer Protection Division of the Office of the Attorney General enforces the Maryland Service Contracts and Consumer Products Guaranty Act under Title 14 of the Commercial Law Article, which the bill amends to prohibit excluding coverage or denying claims based on technical service bulletins.
The Motor Vehicle Administration licenses and regulates motor vehicle dealers who sell mechanical repair contracts governed by § 15-311.2 of the Transportation Article referenced in the bill.
As the parent agency overseeing the Motor Vehicle Administration and transportation-related commerce, MDOT provided analysis on vehicle repair contract regulations.
Obligors who issue mechanical repair contracts are required to register annually with and submit required documentation to the Maryland Insurance Commissioner.

Synopsis: Establishing rules of interpretation related to the uniformed services; altering the rule of interpretation for "veteran"; and altering the application of certain provisions of judicial proceedings, corrections, criminal, family, public safety, and real property laws to apply to all uniformed services, rather than only the armed forces.
Title: Judicial and Public Safety for Service Members Act

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.

bill_summary: The Judicial and Public Safety for Service Members Act establishes uniform statutory definitions for military and uniformed services terms across several articles of the Maryland Code. It broadens various existing rights, exemptions, protections, and benefits—including those relating to court records, jury service, firearms licensing, militia service, residential leases, and civil relief—to encompass all uniformed services, including the Commissioned Corps of the Public Health Service (PHS) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA), rather than solely the armed forces.
responsible_party: Department of State Police
stakeholders: Active-duty service members, reserve component members, and veterans of the uniformed services (including the armed forces, PHS, and NOAA), as well as their families.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $50,000 in FY 2026 only to update the Department of State Police licensing portal to accommodate uniformed services identification. Other agencies and the Judiciary can absorb any operational or minimal programming costs within existing resources. Local government finances and operations are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters firearm licensing exemptions and acceptable identification to include uniformed services, requiring a $50,000 update to the Maryland State Police licensing portal in FY 2026. It also governs the reappointment of police employees who resign to enter uniformed service.

The bill amends the Department's governing statute (State Government § 9-901) to establish standard definitions for veterans and military families, and tasks the Department with presenting State flags to the families of deceased service members.

The bill amends provisions governing the organized militia, appointment and commissioning standards in the Maryland Defense Force, and the Adjutant General's authority to organize uniformed honor guards for deceased veterans.

The bill updates definitions, enlistment, and Maryland Code of Military Justice provisions impacting Guard members, and references information to be posted on the Maryland National Guard website under the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act.

The bill impacts judicial operations by expanding fee exemptions for court records to all service members of the uniformed services, updating the juror qualification form, and altering provisions on CINA court jurisdiction.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends Correctional Services § 2-109, requiring the Secretary to adopt regulations exempting honorably discharged reserve component members of the uniformed services from the minimum age requirement for correctional officers.
The bill updates eligibility terminology regarding uniformed services duty for out-of-home placement programs administered for former CINAs under the Family Law Article.
The bill amends the statutory definition of 'emergency management' in Public Safety § 14-101 to exclude functions for which the uniformed services are primarily responsible.
The bill amends Public Safety § 1-202 regarding the Secretary of State's duty to issue State flags to the families of uniformed service members killed in the line of duty.

The bill expands contract termination rights and consumer protections under the State's Servicemembers Civil Relief Act, which falls within the enforcement jurisdiction of the Consumer Protection Division.

Synopsis: Establishing that certain project site visits and educational field tours do not constitute open meetings subject to the requirement that the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, respectively, stream live video or audio of their open meetings.
Title: Montgomery County Planning Board and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission - Open Meetings - Live Streaming Requirement MC/PG 101-25
bill_summary: Establishes that project site visits and educational field tours do not constitute open meetings subject to live video or audio streaming requirements for the Montgomery County Planning Board and the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, provided that no organizational business is conducted.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Planning Board and Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission
stakeholders: Members and staff of the Montgomery County Planning Board, Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC), and members of the public seeking access to their meetings.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal impact and does not materially affect the operations or finances of the Montgomery County Planning Board or the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of the Attorney General provides legal interpretation and advice regarding the Open Meetings Act and statutory compliance across Maryland public bodies, and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the board of appeals in Prince George's County to be at least three members; and altering the number of members of the board required to concur in any resolution to a simple majority.
Title: Prince George's County - Board of Appeals - Membership MC/PG 106-25
bill_summary: Alters the membership of the Prince George’s County Board of Appeals by requiring the County Council to appoint at least three members rather than exactly three, and establishes that a simple majority of members must concur in any resolution rather than a fixed minimum of two.
responsible_party: Prince George's County Council
stakeholders: Prince George's County residents, members of the Prince George's County Board of Appeals, and individuals or entities appealing local zoning and administrative decisions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Prince George's County expenditures may increase beginning in fiscal year 2026 if additional members are appointed to the Board of Appeals (compensation, fringe benefits, and operating expenses). Prince George's County revenues are not affected.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access to establish a workgroup dedicated to improving health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use. The workgroup must evaluate the availability and outcomes of substance use disorder treatment, criminal justice involvement and its associated costs, and regulations governing patient discharge from treatment programs, and recommend policy changes to mitigate harms related to criminalization.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
stakeholders: Individuals with substance use disorders, justice-involved individuals, patients in treatment programs, and substance use disorder treatment providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures for the Maryland Department of Health increase by $38,000 in FY 2026 and $39,600 in FY 2027 to hire one part-time contractual health policy analyst to staff the workgroup until the commission's scheduled termination on June 30, 2027. State revenues and local government finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health (MDH) provides administrative and staffing support to the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access. The bill requires the new workgroup to review MDH's regulations concerning patient discharge standards from substance use treatment programs, and MDH incurs general fund expenditures to hire contractual staff to support the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill statutorily establishes a new workgroup under the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access focused on the improvement of health, social, and economic outcomes related to substance use, requiring regular meetings, evaluation, and annual reporting.

Synopsis: Prohibiting the use of discretionary clauses in life insurance policies, health insurance policies, annuity contracts, and health maintenance organization contracts.

bill_summary: Prohibits insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from selling, delivering, or issuing health insurance policies, life insurance policies, annuity contracts, or HMO contracts that contain discretionary clauses reserving sole discretion to the carrier to interpret policy terms or establish review standards inconsistent with Maryland law.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Insurance carriers (including insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations) and consumers/policyholders holding health insurance, life insurance, annuities, or HMO contracts.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee as carriers update forms. The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill with existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for reviewing and approving insurance policies, contracts, and form filings, as well as enforcing compliance with state insurance laws prohibiting discretionary clauses in life, health, annuity, and HMO contracts.

The bill amends the Health - General Article (§ 19-706) to apply the discretionary clause prohibition to health maintenance organizations (HMOs), which fall under statutory provisions codified within the Department of Health's governing article.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System to certify certain employer contribution rates each fiscal year; requiring the employer contribution rates to include recognition of certain administrative and operational expenses; repealing a requirement that certain administrative and operational expenses of the State Retirement and Pension System and the State Retirement Agency be funded by charging each participating employer an administrative fee for each system participant; etc.
Title: State Retirement and Pension System - Administrative Fees - Repeal

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: Repeals the requirement that the State and participating local employers pay separate administrative fees to the State Retirement and Pension System (SRPS), instead funding administrative and operational expenses directly through the accumulation fund in fiscal year 2026 and incorporating those expenses into the actuarially certified employer normal contribution rates beginning in fiscal year 2027.
responsible_party: Board of Trustees for the State Retirement and Pension System and the State Retirement Agency
stakeholders: State agencies, participating local governmental employers (such as local school boards, community colleges, and participating governmental units), and the State Retirement and Pension System
fiscal_impact_summary: In FY 2026, State Retirement Agency (SRA) special fund revenues decrease by an estimated $21.8 million due to the cancellation of local employer administrative fee payments, resulting in an identical $21.8 million expenditure reduction for local participating employers. State general fund expenditures decrease by $5.7 million ($5,691,206) in FY 2026 due to a planned budget reversion, accompanied by an equal reduction in reimbursable fund revenues for SRA. Beginning in FY 2027, the inclusion of administrative and operating expenses in the employer normal contribution rate fully offsets the repeal of administrative fees, resulting in no material net effect on State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland State Retirement Agency (SRA) and its Board of Trustees are the primary entities governed by the bill, which restructures the funding mechanism for SRA's administrative and operational expenses by repealing per-participant administrative fees and incorporating those costs directly into actuarially certified employer contribution rates.

The Board of Trustees is required to annually certify the employer contribution rates to the Secretary of Budget and Management. DBM also oversees state personnel retirement benefit budgeting, which is fiscally impacted in fiscal 2026 through general fund expenditure decreases and budget reversions.
The bill requires the Board of Trustees to annually certify the recommended employer contribution rates directly to the Governor for the formulation of the annual state budget.

The bill repeals Section 21-316 of the State Personnel and Pensions Article, which previously required the Comptroller to exercise the right of setoff against delinquent local employers for unpaid administrative fees.

Synopsis: Requiring a landlord to provide a tenant with certain written notice in a certain manner at least 24 hours in advance of when the landlord intends to enter a leased premises, except in the event of a certain emergency; and authorizing the court to issue a certain injunction or assess certain damages under certain circumstances.
Title: Residential Real Property - Landlord and Tenant - Notice of Landlord Entry

NarrowSubjects.Name: Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: House Bill 1076 requires residential landlords to provide tenants with at least 24 hours of written advance notice before entering a leased premises, limits entry to between 7:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday (except during emergencies or by mutual agreement), specifies permitted reasons and delivery methods for entry notices, and authorizes courts to grant injunctive relief and assess damages for violations.
responsible_party: Judiciary (Maryland Courts)
stakeholders: Residential tenants, residential landlords, and property managers in Maryland
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The small business effect is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a statutory civil cause of action allowing residential tenants to seek injunctive relief and damages against landlords in court for unlawful entry or improper demands for entry, which directly impacts the court system supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

The Office of the Attorney General, specifically through its Consumer Protection Division, oversees statewide consumer protection and landlord-tenant rights, and was consulted regarding the legal and operational impact of this legislation.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include $200,000,000 in the annual operating or capital budget bill for site redevelopment and transportation infrastructure improvements if the U.S. General Services Administration applies to Prince George's County or the State for a permit associated with the relocation of the Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters to Prince George's County.
Title: Prince George's County - Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters - Mandated Appropriation
bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $200 million in the annual operating or capital budget bill for site redevelopment and transportation infrastructure improvements related to the relocation of the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) headquarters to Prince George's County, contingent upon the U.S. General Services Administration applying for a relocation permit from Prince George's County or the State.
responsible_party: Governor of Maryland
stakeholders: Residents, commuters, and businesses in Prince George's County (specifically the Greenbelt area), as well as the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the U.S. General Services Administration.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect is estimated to be zero assuming $200 million in previously authorized General Obligation (GO) bond funding satisfies the bill's mandate over fiscal years 2026 through 2028. If interpreted as requiring an additional $200 million, Pay-As-You-Go Transportation Trust Fund expenditures and/or GO bond expenditures would increase by up to $200 million in fiscal 2027. Local effect is zero.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a statutory requirement mandating the Governor to include an appropriation of at least $200,000,000 in the annual operating or capital budget bill for the FBI headquarters relocation project if the specified condition is met.

As the principal agency responsible for developing and administering the state operating and capital budgets on behalf of the Governor, DBM is directly impacted by the mandated appropriation requirement and was consulted for the fiscal analysis.

The mandated appropriation is dedicated to transportation infrastructure improvements and site redevelopment, which are programmed in MDOT's Consolidated Transportation Program (CTP) and could impact Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) or General Obligation bond funding allocations.

The funding supports highway infrastructure improvements, specifically the construction of an interchange along I-95/I-495 at the Greenbelt Metro Station under the jurisdiction and operational scope of MDOT SHA.

Synopsis: Establishing that governmental units may provide disaster service leave with pay to certain employees; establishing that an employee of a governmental unit of a county or a municipality in the State may be entitled to disaster service leave with pay under certain circumstances; authorizing certain governmental units to waive certain requirements for disaster service leave; and authorizing a governmental unit of a county or a municipality to provide leave with pay under certain circumstances.
Title: Local Government - Local Personnel - Leave With Pay

Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

Municipal Corporations -see also- Annap; Balt; Hager; OC
Rescue Squads -see also- Emergency Medical Serv
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 1080 authorizes county and municipal governmental units in Maryland to provide paid disaster service leave (up to 30 days in a 12-month period) to employees who are certified disaster service volunteers or members of specified volunteer emergency response organizations. It also authorizes local governments to grant paid leave for jury service, approved employee organization events, uniformed services training or active reserve duty, subpoenaed court or administrative appearances, certain administrative removals, and any other purpose deemed necessary by the local government head.
responsible_party: Governmental units of Maryland counties and municipalities
stakeholders: County and municipal government employees—especially volunteer emergency responders, disaster service volunteers, and military reservists—and local governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local expenditures may increase, potentially significantly, for overtime, substitute coverage, and payroll costs if local governmental units choose to provide additional paid leave to their employees. Because the provisions are discretionary and require approval from the local government, specific dollar estimates are indeterminate. Local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes paid disaster service leave for local government employees who volunteer with disaster relief organizations, including Maryland VOAD, CERT, and volunteer fire and rescue entities, which directly support emergency response and disaster resilience efforts coordinated statewide by MDEM.

The bill authorizes local government units to provide up to 30 days of leave with pay for employees participating in uniformed services training or active duty in the organized militia, which is overseen and commanded by the Adjutant General.

The Maryland National Guard constitutes the organized militia referenced in the bill; local government personnel who are Guard members may be granted up to 30 days of paid leave for training or active duty deployments.

Synopsis: Establishing the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program to provide subsidies to individuals in the State to mitigate the impact of a reduction in certain federal advance premium tax credits for calendar years 2026 through 2028; and requiring the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to implement the Program under certain circumstances.
Title: Health Insurance - Individual Market Stabilization - Establishment of the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program

NarrowSubjects.Name: Health Insurance -see also- ACA; HMOs; MCOs

bill_summary: Establishes the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program within the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange to provide subsidies to individuals purchasing health coverage in the individual market in calendar years 2026 and 2027, mitigating the potential loss or reduction of federal advance premium tax credits.
responsible_party: Maryland Health Benefit Exchange
stakeholders: Maryland residents purchasing health benefit plans through the individual health insurance market, particularly those facing reduced federal premium tax credits.
fiscal_impact_summary: If federal advance premium tax credits are not extended for calendar years 2026 and 2027, special fund expenditures from the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund increase by a significant but indeterminate amount (estimated up to $75.0 million in FY 2026, $150.0 million in FY 2027, and $75.0 million in FY 2028) to provide state subsidies. Administrative costs can be absorbed using existing budgeted resources. If federal credits are extended, the bill terminates and no state expenditures are incurred. Local governments are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange (MHBE) to establish, administer, and adopt regulations for the State-Based Health Insurance Subsidies Program, as well as administer and expend from the MHBE Fund.

The Maryland Insurance Commissioner must be consulted by MHBE in establishing the program and setting its eligibility and payment parameters, and is tasked alongside MHBE with notifying the Department of Legislative Services if federal tax credits change.
The Comptroller accounts for the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, the purposes and allowed uses of which are modified under this legislation.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the moneys of the Maryland Health Benefit Exchange Fund, which is expanded to accommodate funding and disbursements for the new subsidy program.

Synopsis: Requiring the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, through its workgroup, to implement Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment requirements; requiring the workgroup to provide recommendations to implement recommendations in a certain Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services State Health Official letter; and requiring the Maryland Department of Health to report its findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
Title: Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access - Plan to Implement Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment Requirements

NarrowSubjects.Name: Communications -see also- ElecComm; Intergov; Telecom; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.

bill_summary: Requires the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access, through its workgroup on youth behavioral health, individuals with developmental disabilities, and individuals with complex behavioral health needs, to develop recommendations for implementing federal Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services best practices for Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) requirements for children. It also requires the Maryland Department of Health to submit a report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health, Behavioral Health Advisory Council, and Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access
stakeholders: Medicaid-eligible children and youth, particularly those with behavioral health conditions, complex needs, or developmental disabilities, along with their families, caregivers, and pediatric behavioral health providers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The advisory council and commission can provide recommendations and the Maryland Department of Health can submit the required report using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are not affected. Local effect: None.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers Maryland's Medicaid program and Early and Periodic Screening, Diagnostic, and Treatment (EPSDT) services, supports behavioral health policy, and is statutorily mandated to submit the final report of findings and recommendations to the General Assembly by January 1, 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly mandates the Behavioral Health Advisory Council and the Commission on Behavioral Health Care Treatment and Access (through its youth behavioral health workgroup) to convene stakeholders and formulate recommendations implementing CMS best practices for EPSDT requirements.

Synopsis: Exempting certain real property owned by certain nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities from State and local property taxation; directing certain nonprofit entities created by public housing authorities to make payment in lieu of taxes that may be set by mutual agreement with a political subdivision; and applying the Act to all taxable years beginning after June 30, 2025.
Title: Housing Authorities - Tax-Exempt Status - Modifications

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: This bill standardizes the tax treatment of real property owned by nonprofit entities established by public housing authorities across Maryland by expanding a property tax exemption statewide. Previously limited to Baltimore City, Howard County, and Montgomery County, qualifying property used for housing persons of eligible income is exempt from State and local property taxes, and the housing authority entities may make payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT) to local jurisdictions pursuant to mutual agreements.
responsible_party: Maryland Public Housing Authorities
stakeholders: Public housing authorities, nonprofit housing entities, local governments, and individuals and families of eligible income seeking affordable housing
fiscal_impact_summary: Beginning in FY 2026, State and local property tax revenues may experience a potential minimal decrease to the extent that public housing authorities establish qualifying nonprofit entities. State and local expenditures are not significantly affected. Any revenue loss may also be partially offset by negotiated payments in lieu of taxes (PILOT).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: HB 1085 amends the Housing and Community Development Article to extend property tax exemptions to nonprofit entities established by public housing authorities statewide, facilitating affordable housing financing mechanisms such as Low-Income Housing Tax Credits (LIHTC). The Department of Housing and Community Development was also consulted as an information source for the bill's fiscal analysis.
As the State's chief tax collection and financial agency, the Comptroller is impacted by changes affecting State property tax revenues and was consulted in the preparation of the fiscal note.

Synopsis: Requiring, beginning January 1, 2026, the Maryland Medical Assistance Program, managed care organizations, and certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations, if providing coverage for the delivery of anesthesia for a procedure for which a licensed medical professional issues an order, to provide the coverage for the duration of the procedure; prohibiting the establishment, implementation, or enforcement of policies or practices  that place time limitations on the delivery of anesthesia; etc.
Title: Maryland Medical Assistance Program and Health Insurance - Coverage for Anesthesia - Prohibiting Time Limitations

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
