bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), managed care organizations, and private health insurers from imposing time limits on coverage for anesthesia delivery when ordered by a licensed medical professional. Insurers and Medicaid must cover anesthesia for the full duration of the procedure as well as related care provided immediately before and after.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Patients undergoing procedures requiring anesthesia, healthcare providers and anesthesiologists, health insurance carriers, and Medicaid managed care organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Medicaid expenditures increase by an indeterminate but minimal amount starting in FY 2026 (funded 50% general funds and 50% federal funds), matched by an equivalent increase in federal fund revenues. No impact on the Maryland Insurance Administration, the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Health - General Article governing the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), requiring MDH to cover anesthesia without time limitations and resulting in an indeterminate but minimal fiscal impact on Medicaid expenditures.

The bill adds § 15–861 to the Insurance Article, establishing coverage requirements and prohibiting time limitations on anesthesia for private health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs regulated by the Administration.

DBM administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while evaluated for potential fiscal and coverage impacts relating to health plan mandates, the bill does not impact the State plan.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing a step therapy or fail-first protocol for certain prescription drugs prescribed by a treating physician to treat a symptom of or side effect from the treatment of stage four metastatic cancer and use of the prescription drug is consistent with best practices for treatment of the condition.
Title: Health Insurance - Step Therapy or Fail-First Protocols - Drugs to Treat Associated Conditions of Advanced Metastatic Cancer

NarrowSubjects.Name: Drugs -see also- Cannabis; ControlDangSubst; Pharm; etc.
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.

Medical Conditions -see also- AIDS; COVID-19; rabies
Physicians -see also- MedExmnrs; Pediatr; Psychiatrists etc.

bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from imposing step therapy or fail-first protocols on FDA-approved prescription drugs prescribed to treat symptoms or side effects of stage four advanced metastatic cancer, provided the treatment follows best practices, is supported by peer-reviewed literature, and is covered under the policy.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Patients diagnosed with stage four advanced metastatic cancer, treating physicians, health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, health maintenance organizations, and pharmacy benefits managers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees, with reviews handled using existing resources. No anticipated impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, and minimal assumed impact on local governments with fully insured plans.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing the Insurance Article, reviewing carrier form and rate filings for compliance with the prohibition on step therapy protocols, and collecting associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management manages the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate compliance and benefit design regarding prescription drug protocols.
The Maryland Department of Health oversees broad state health policies and programs and provided information on clinical standards and impacts related to cancer treatment protocols.

Synopsis: Expanding eligibility for a certain beauty salon license in Montgomery County to include a holder of a certain barbershop permit; authorizing a holder of the license to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption in addition to beer and wine; and authorizing the holder to provide not more than 12 ounces of beer, 5 ounces of wine, or 1.7 ounces of liquor for on-premises consumption by a beauty salon or barbershop customer; and requiring an annual license fee of $100.
Title: Montgomery County - Alcoholic Beverages - Beauty Salon and Barbershop License MC 3-25
bill_summary: Expands eligibility for a beauty salon alcoholic beverages license in Montgomery County to include licensed barbershops, renames it the beauty salon and barbershop beer, wine, and liquor license, allows licensees to provide up to 1.7 ounces of liquor, and increases the maximum amount of beer that may be provided to a customer for on-premises consumption from 5 to 12 ounces.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Beauty salon and barbershop owners, employees, and customers in Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect. Montgomery County revenues are not affected, and any additional enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing local resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes that eligibility for the license requires holding a barbershop or beauty salon permit issued under Titles 4 and 5 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article, which are licensed and regulated by boards under the Maryland Department of Labor.

The Comptroller serves as the state's principal alcohol regulator and tax collector; while licensing is administered locally by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners, the bill alters allowable alcoholic beverage service parameters.

Synopsis: Requiring the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund to calculate and report its risk based capital level in accordance with certain provisions of insurance law and maintain total adjusted capital in a certain amount; establishing that certain provisions of insurance law regarding prior approval rate making apply to the Fund during a certain time period and under certain circumstances; requiring the Maryland Insurance Administration to establish a workgroup to study automobile insurance affordability; etc.
Title: Insurance - Automobile Insurance - Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund and Affordability Study

NarrowSubjects.Name: Fees -see also- Attys' Fees; Devt Fees & Taxes

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF) to calculate and report risk-based capital levels, maintain total adjusted capital at or above company action level requirements beginning December 31, 2026, and adhere to prior approval ratemaking standards during specified periods. Additionally, directs the Maryland Insurance Administration to establish a workgroup to study private passenger automobile insurance affordability and excess insurer profits.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration and Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund
stakeholders: Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), private passenger automobile insurance companies, insurance producers, and Maryland motor vehicle policyholders
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Insurance Administration can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources with no impact on State general revenues. MAIF nonbudgeted revenues may be impacted if meeting risk-based capital thresholds requires reducing higher-yield equity investments in favor of lower-risk assets, which could affect investment income and potentially influence future industry assessments. No local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly applies to the Maryland Automobile Insurance Fund (MAIF), requiring it to calculate and report risk-based capital (RBC) levels, maintain a specified total adjusted capital level, submit an RBC plan under certain conditions, and comply with prior approval rate-making provisions. Its Executive Director also serves on the study workgroup.

The Maryland Insurance Administration (MIA) is tasked with reviewing and determining the adequacy of MAIF's RBC plans, overseeing prior approval rate filings, establishing and staffing a workgroup to study automobile insurance affordability, and having the Insurance Commissioner chair the workgroup.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a specialized temporary workgroup tasked with studying the affordability of private passenger automobile insurance in Maryland and reporting findings and recommendations.
The workgroup established under the bill is required to submit a report of its findings and recommendations regarding automobile insurance affordability to the Governor on or before January 1, 2026.

bill_summary: Requires the Maryland Department of Health, in collaboration with the Commission on Health Equity, to develop and maintain an easy-to-understand graphic data dashboard tracking age-adjusted health disparity data disaggregated by race, ethnicity, and gender across various health indicators, updated quarterly on its website.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland residents, public health researchers, healthcare policymakers, and demographic communities affected by health disparities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures and revenues are not affected; the Maryland Department of Health can develop and update the dashboard using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health to develop, maintain, quarterly update, and host a comprehensive health equity data dashboard on its website.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly requires the Maryland Department of Health to develop the graphic health equity data dashboard in collaboration with the Commission on Health Equity.

Synopsis: Clarifying that electronic health care transactions information may be used to support the participation of the State in the States Advancing All-Payer Health Equity Approaches and Development (AHEAD) Model and any successor models; establishing the Population Health Improvement Fund to support the statewide population health targets under the AHEAD Model and any successor models; authorizing the Health Services Cost Review Commission to assess a uniform, broad-based, and reasonable amount in hospital rates to be credited to the Fund; etc.
Title: Maryland Department of Health - AHEAD Model Implementation - Electronic Health Care Transactions and Population Health Improvement Fund

NarrowSubjects.Name: Electronic Commerce -see also- Electronic Funds Transfer
Health -see also- COVID19; EnvHlth; MedCon; etc.
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Establishes the Population Health Improvement Fund jointly administered by the Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission to invest in population health improvements and support health equity targets under the federal AHEAD Model. The bill permits the use of electronic health care transaction data for state participation in the model, authorizes a temporary hospital rate assessment through 2027 to finance the fund, and requires annual progress reporting.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and the Health Services Cost Review Commission
stakeholders: Maryland hospitals, health care providers, electronic health networks, Medicaid beneficiaries, and Maryland residents receiving care under population health initiatives.
fiscal_impact_summary: Special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $25.0 million in FY 2026 from an HSCRC hospital rate assessment credited to the Population Health Improvement Fund, with indeterminate increases in FY 2027 and FY 2028 if assessments continue. State Medicaid expenditures increase by $5.0 million in FY 2026 ($2.0 million in general funds and $3.0 million in federal matching funds) due to higher hospital rates. Minimal general fund revenue increase from interest earnings through FY 2028. No local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDH is the primary executive department responsible for jointly administering the newly established Population Health Improvement Fund with the HSCRC, managing expenditures aligned with the Statewide Health Equity Plan, and submitting required annual reports to the General Assembly.

HSCRC is given direct authority to assess uniform amounts in hospital rates to fund the Population Health Improvement Fund, jointly administer the Fund with MDH, and provide monthly updates to designated General Assembly members.

The bill impacts MHCC's regulatory oversight and standards regarding electronic health networks and the State-designated health information exchange (CRISP), specifying that its regulations may not restrict State use of financial claims information for AHEAD Model purposes.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund separately and manage the investment of the Fund's balances.
The Comptroller is required to account for the newly established special, nonlapsing Population Health Improvement Fund.
The bill explicitly provides that the newly created Population Health Improvement Fund is subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.

Synopsis: Altering the minimum age for employment in Allegany County for alcoholic beverages license holders that do not derive more than half of their revenues from the sale of food from 16 years of age to 18 years of age.
Title: Allegany County - Alcoholic Beverages - Minimum Age for Employment of Underage Individuals

bill_summary: Increases the minimum employment age from 16 to 18 years for alcoholic beverage license holders in Allegany County that do not derive more than half of their revenue from food sales, while maintaining the minimum age of 16 for establishments where food sales exceed 50% of revenue.
responsible_party: Allegany County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverage licensees in Allegany County and individuals aged 16 to 17 seeking employment at these establishments.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Allegany County operations or finances. Any impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill modifies the legal minimum age of employment for certain alcoholic beverage license holders in Allegany County, touching on youth employment and labor standards enforced by the Department of Labor.
The Comptroller regulates the state's alcohol industry, although day-to-day retail alcoholic beverage licensing and local enforcement in Allegany County are handled primarily at the local level.

Synopsis: Providing that solar energy generating systems located on or over certain water retention ponds or quarries are eligible for the Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program; and authorizing the Mayor and City Council of Baltimore City or the governing body of a county or municipal corporation to grant by law, a certain property tax credit against the county or municipal corporation property tax imposed on certain nonresidential solar energy generating systems.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility under Maryland's Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program to include solar energy generating systems located on or over industrial water retention ponds or quarries. It also authorizes Baltimore City and county or municipal governments to grant an optional property tax credit for nonresidential solar energy generating systems built on brownfields, industrial water retention ponds, or quarries.
responsible_party: Public Service Commission
stakeholders: Nonresidential solar energy system developers and owners, owners of industrial brownfields, quarries, and water retention ponds, local governments, and electric utility customers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not materially affected; the Public Service Commission, the State Department of Assessments and Taxation, and the Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources. Local property tax revenues may decrease beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that local governments elect to grant the optional property tax credit.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Public Service Commission administers the Small Solar Energy Generating System Incentive Program and is directly responsible for certifying eligible solar energy generating systems, which the bill expands to include systems located on or over certain water retention ponds or quarries.

The department regulates brownfields, industrial sites, and nontidal wetlands and waterways; its Water and Science Administration reviews and handles environmental approval processes for floating solar installations on water retention ponds and quarries.
MEA oversees the state's clean energy policies, solar incentive programs, and land assessment studies regarding solar siting on brownfields and industrial sites.

bill_summary: This bill alters the medical and geriatric parole processes in Maryland. It requires the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC) to consider an incarcerated individual's age and its effect on recidivism, alters criteria and evaluation procedures for medical parole, and repeals the Governor's authority to disapprove medical parole for individuals serving life sentences. It also establishes a standardized geriatric parole review process for incarcerated individuals who are at least 65 years old, have served at least 20 years, are not sex offenders, have parole-eligible sentences, and have no serious recent infractions. Additionally, it directs any incarceration savings to parole-related assessments and reentry services, and authorizes the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board to recommend distributing funds to MPC to hire psychologists for risk assessments.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Parole-eligible incarcerated individuals (specifically individuals aged 65 and older and individuals with chronic debilitating or terminal medical conditions), victims and their representatives, and correctional system staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,494 in FY 2026 (reflecting the October 1, 2025 effective date) and rise to $654,500 by FY 2030, covering salaries and operating expenses for three psychologists and one administrative officer to conduct risk assessments and comply with reporting requirements. This estimate does not reflect potential savings in incarceration costs, which are indeterminate. To the extent funding is distributed to MPC from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund via GOCPP/JROB, the need for general funds would decrease. Local operations and finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy

The bill repeals the statutory authority of the Governor to disapprove a decision by the Maryland Parole Commission to grant medical parole to an incarcerated individual serving a life sentence.

bill_summary: This bill prohibits a person from knowingly selling or offering to sell heating, ventilation, air-conditioning, or refrigeration (HVACR) equipment unless the purchaser holds a specified license issued by the State Board of Heating, Ventilation, Air-Conditioning, and Refrigeration Contractors, employs a licensed individual, operates a business reselling equipment to licensed individuals, or qualifies for an exemption. bill_summary: Expands the authority of municipal corporations and governed special taxing districts in Montgomery County to impose additional or stricter building requirements (such as setbacks, bulk, parking, and lot coverage) beyond county or regional standards. It allows these jurisdictions to regulate buildings with four or fewer dwelling units—including duplexes, triplexes, quadplexes, cottage clusters, and townhouses—and accessory structures without regard to underlying zoning, provided requirements for buildings with two to four units are not more restrictive than those for single-unit houses.
responsible_party: Legislative bodies of municipal corporations and governed special taxing districts within Montgomery County
stakeholders: Property owners, residents, and construction/remodeling contractors and developers of small residential properties (up to four units) in Montgomery County municipalities and governed special taxing districts.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no direct effect on State or local government finances. It may have a meaningful impact on small businesses involved in the construction, repair, or remodeling of residential buildings with two to four dwelling units if local jurisdictions enact stricter requirements.

It also eliminates requirements to report specific percentages and classes of partnership or membership interests in articles of merger involving limited partnerships, limited liability companies, or general partnerships.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances. It may potentially have a meaningful impact on small businesses by streamlining asset transfers and corporate merger filings.

Synopsis: Requiring the Board of License Commissioners for Baltimore City to impose a fee of not more than $250 for expedited processing of certain Class C per diem licenses; requiring the Board to adopt regulations related to the application process for Class C per diem licenses, including for the denial or revocation of the licenses, and limiting the number of licenses that may be issued to a person for the same location within a certain period of time; etc.

bill_summary: House Bill 1172 requires the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to charge a fee of up to $250 for expedited processing of Class C per diem license applications submitted less than two weeks prior to an event, and authorizes the Board to regulate, deny, revoke, or limit such licenses. The bill also authorizes the issuance of specific Class B and Class C alcoholic beverages licenses at designated locations in the 40th alcoholic beverages district under certain conditions, establishes daily sales hour restrictions for specified areas within the 40th district, and exempts Class M-F (municipal family fun center) licenses from certain hour restrictions.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Alcoholic beverages license applicants, event organizers seeking per diem licenses, designated businesses and venues in Baltimore City's 40th legislative district (including restaurants, campus event venues, and barbershops), neighborhood community associations, and local patrons.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Baltimore City revenues will increase beginning in FY 2026 to the extent that new alcoholic beverage licenses are issued and expedited application processing fees of up to $250 are collected. Specific dollar totals are unavailable. Baltimore City expenditures are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners to issue a Class C beer and light wine license for on-campus events in the 2500 block of West North Avenue, which is the campus location of Coppin State University, a member institution of the University System of Maryland.

The Comptroller is responsible for regulating Maryland's alcohol industry and collecting state alcoholic beverage taxes, although primary administration and licensing under this bill is carried out locally by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners.

Synopsis: Authorizing the placement and use of speed monitoring systems on highways in Montgomery County that are at high risk for certain motor vehicle crashes; prohibiting the placement and use of speed monitoring systems on certain highways in Montgomery County; requiring the fines collected by Montgomery County or by a municipal government in Montgomery County as a result of violations enforced by a speed monitoring system to be used to fund the study, design, and construction of certain safety-related projects; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the placement and operation of speed monitoring systems on highways in Montgomery County identified in Strategic Highway Safety Plans or Vision Zero Plans as high-risk for severe or fatal crashes, while prohibiting their use on controlled access highways, expressways, and interstates. The bill also dedicates net revenues from these systems to safety-related roadway projects and requires system evaluations every five years.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Drivers, pedestrians, Montgomery County government, and municipal governments within Montgomery County
fiscal_impact_summary: State General Fund expenditures increase by approximately $12,208 in FY 2026 for District Court computer programming changes, with minimal potential revenue increases from contested citations. Local government revenues and expenditures in Montgomery County may increase, potentially significantly, beginning in FY 2026 depending on the number of speed monitoring systems deployed; excess fine revenues after cost recovery must be spent on road safety projects on high-risk roadways.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The District Court of Maryland (supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts) is responsible for prescribing uniform citation forms, processing fine payments, and adjudicating contested citations resulting from newly authorized speed monitoring systems, with an estimated programming cost of $12,208 in FY 2026.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding speed monitoring on highways and safety-related projects, which directly intersects with MDOT's oversight of statewide transportation infrastructure and traffic safety planning.

The MVA houses the Maryland Highway Safety Office (MHSO), which develops and administers the State's Strategic Highway Safety Plan and Vision Zero program—the exact plans the bill uses to qualify high-risk roadways eligible for speed camera placement.

SHA partners closely with MHSO to implement traffic safety plans and policies, maintains state non-toll roadways, establishes traffic control device standards, and may be involved in the design or coordination of safety-related roadway projects funded by fine revenues.
The Comptroller receives and deposits into the General Fund any excess fine revenues remitted by political subdivisions if net speed monitoring revenues exceed 10% of total local revenues.

Synopsis: Increasing to two the number of Class BD-BWL alcoholic beverages licenses in Montgomery County that the same person may hold; and specifying that the establishment for which a second class BD-BWL license is issued shall have average daily receipts from the sale of food that exceed the average daily receipts from the sale of alcoholic beverages.

bill_summary: This bill permits an individual or entity in Montgomery County to hold up to two Class BD-BWL alcoholic beverages licenses, an increase from the previous limit of one. For an establishment operating under a second Class BD-BWL license, average daily receipts from food sales must exceed average daily receipts from alcohol sales, and off-premises sales are restricted to private-label products manufactured exclusively for the license holder.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Current and prospective Class BD-BWL alcoholic beverages license holders and restaurant and bar owners in Montgomery County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Montgomery County revenues will increase depending on how many licensees obtain a second Class BD-BWL license ($3,500 annual fee, $600 initial application fee, and $100 annual renewal fee). For illustrative purposes, if all 52 existing licensees apply for and maintain a second license, county revenues would increase by $213,200 in fiscal 2026 and by $187,200 annually thereafter. Montgomery County can handle any additional enforcement activities with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry and collecting state excise and sales taxes on alcoholic beverages. While this bill specifically addresses local Class BD-BWL retail licensing limits administered by the Montgomery County Board of License Commissioners with no direct state fiscal impact, it relates generally to alcohol regulation under the Comptroller's broader industry purview.

bill_summary: The Maryland Housing Data Transparency Act requires counties with at least 150,000 residents that issue at least 50 residential building permits annually to submit quarterly reports to the Maryland Department of Planning on residential building and development permits. It permits municipalities to voluntarily submit the same data, requires counties to make reports publicly available, and directs the Maryland Department of Planning to publish the data on an interactive, searchable website and submit annual reports to the Governor and General Assembly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Planning
stakeholders: Counties with at least 150,000 residents, local planning and zoning departments, municipalities, residential housing developers, and the general public.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $86,109 in FY 2026 for the Maryland Department of Planning to hire one GIS administrator to build and maintain the permit database and online dashboard, increasing to $116,500 by FY 2030. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures for reporting counties and voluntary municipalities are expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Planning is the primary implementing agency for the bill, tasked with collecting quarterly housing development permit reports from local jurisdictions, maintaining an interactive and searchable public website to display the data, reporting annually to the Governor and General Assembly, and adopting implementing regulations. It also incurs general fund expenditures to hire staff for these duties.

The Department of Housing and Community Development is a co-recipient of annual residential building permit application reports under existing provisions of the amended statute, and the bill directly affects statewide housing supply and development data relevant to its core mission.
The Department of Planning is mandated to submit an annual report on the building permit data collected under the bill to the Governor.

bill_summary: The Maryland Values Act requires federal law enforcement officers to notify designated local or State officials prior to taking immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations, such as public schools, libraries, courthouses, and government healthcare facilities. It directs public schools, libraries, and State and local executive agencies at sensitive locations to bar federal immigration enforcement from nonpublic areas without a valid federal judicial warrant or exigent circumstances. Additionally, the Act mandates that the Attorney General publish guidance regarding immigration enforcement at sensitive locations, requires covered entities to adopt conforming policies by October 1, 2025, and directs governmental entities, in consultation with the Department of Information Technology, to establish procedures by July 1, 2026, to prevent the commercial sale and redisclosure of personal records and geolocation data.
responsible_party: Maryland Office of the Attorney General, Department of Information Technology, and State and local governmental entities
stakeholders: Maryland residents, immigrant communities, federal law enforcement officers, State and local law enforcement, and staff and visitors at public schools, libraries, courthouses, and State/local healthcare facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill requires the Attorney General to develop and publish guidance regarding immigration enforcement at sensitive locations and grants the Attorney General the authority to designate additional locations that require special consideration.

The bill requires all governmental entities to consult with the Department of Information Technology to develop and publish procedures preventing the sale and redisclosure of personal records and geolocation data.

Facilities operated by the Comptroller are explicitly defined as sensitive locations, requiring the agency to implement policies restricting nonpublic access by federal immigration authorities and adopting policies consistent with Attorney General guidance.
Federal law enforcement officers conducting immigration enforcement actions at sensitive locations are required to provide notice to the Department of State Police barrack commander.

Public schools are designated as sensitive locations under the bill, requiring them to restrict nonpublic access to federal immigration enforcement officers without a federal court warrant and implement policies aligned with Attorney General guidance.

Public libraries are explicitly designated as sensitive locations, requiring public library systems overseen by the agency to deny access to nonpublic areas to immigration enforcement officers without a warrant and implement required policies.

State-operated health care facilities are defined as sensitive locations, requiring facilities managed by the Department of Health to restrict access to nonpublic areas and implement corresponding policies by October 1, 2025.

Federal law enforcement officers conducting immigration enforcement actions on property owned, leased, operated by, or under the control of the Department of Natural Resources must notify the Secretary of Natural Resources or the Secretary's designee.
Federal law enforcement officers conducting immigration enforcement on MDTA, MAA, or MPA property are required to notify the chief of police of the Maryland Transportation Authority.

The bill explicitly references property owned, leased, operated by, or under the control of the Maryland Aviation Administration regarding notification requirements for federal immigration enforcement actions.

The bill explicitly references property owned, leased, operated by, or under the control of the Maryland Port Administration regarding notification requirements for federal immigration enforcement actions.
Courthouses are categorized as sensitive locations under the bill, which impacts court facilities, operations, and policies regarding access by federal immigration enforcement.

Special fund revenues to the State Barbers and Cosmetologists Boards' Fund increase beginning in FY 2026 from new biennial limited license fees (anticipated at $56 per license), though the exact total revenue is indeterminate. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Cosmetologists is housed within the Maryland Department of Labor. The department is directly responsible for implementing the new limited license for eyelash extension services, adopting regulations, updating licensing software, and collecting license fee revenues.

The bill requires the State Board of Cosmetologists to establish curriculum standards for use by the State Department of Education in approving cosmetology school applications and programs for instruction in eyelash extension services in public schools.
The bill requires curriculum standards to be used by the Maryland Higher Education Commission in approving applications and programs for eyelash extension instruction at private career schools.

Synopsis: Applying certain provisions of law regarding school bus stops located on certain highways in Montgomery County to a school bus stop at a location for which at least 400 citations were issued in the preceding fiscal year to drivers traveling in the opposite direction of the bus stop; and prohibiting, beginning on December 31, 2028, locating a school bus stop on any highway with five or more undivided traffic lanes, except under certain circumstances.
Title: Montgomery County - School Bus Stops on Highways - Alterations MC 8-25

BroadSubjects.Name: Vehicle Laws - Rules of the Road

bill_summary: Alters regulations concerning school bus stop locations in Montgomery County by delaying the requirement that prohibits bus stops on undivided highways with five or more lanes (unless a crossing guard or red-signal traffic control device is present) from December 31, 2026, to December 31, 2028. The bill also narrows the restriction to only apply to bus stops where at least 400 citations were issued in the preceding fiscal year to motorists traveling in the opposite direction.
responsible_party: Montgomery County Public Schools and Montgomery County Government
stakeholders: Montgomery County public school students, school bus drivers, motorists, and school crossing guards in Montgomery County.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Montgomery County expenditures may be reduced and delayed due to narrowing the scope of restricted school bus stop locations and extending the compliance deadline from December 31, 2026, to December 31, 2028. For context, the county estimated that hiring up to 13 crossing guards under current law requirements could cost more than $500,000 annually if bus stops could not be relocated. County revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends § 7–801.1 of the Education Article concerning the placement and safety requirements of school bus stops on multi-lane highways in Montgomery County. The Maryland State Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and statewide standards for student transportation.

The legislation alters rules regarding school bus stops and traffic control devices on undivided highways with five or more lanes in Montgomery County, which encompasses state-maintained roadways and traffic signal systems under SHA's jurisdiction.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Commerce
stakeholders: Tourists, visitors, residents, and owners of small businesses, agricultural operations, historic sites, and recreation facilities within the Montgomery County Agricultural Reserve.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures are not significantly affected, as the Department of Commerce, the University of Maryland Extension, and Montgomery County can complete the study and report with existing budgeted resources. Revenues are not affected, and the impact on small businesses is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Commerce is the lead agency designated to conduct the study on economic development and the tourist and visitor economy of the Montgomery County Agricultural Reserve, synthesize data, and submit the final report by June 30, 2026.
The bill explicitly mandates that the study be conducted in coordination with the University of Maryland Extension - Montgomery County, an entity within the University System of Maryland.

The Maryland Office of Tourism Development operates within the Division of Tourism, Film, and the Arts at the Department of Commerce and focuses on visitor economies and tourism attraction, which is the core subject of the required study.

bill_summary: This bill mandates that the Montgomery County Council and Prince George's County Council grant full or partial exemptions from the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission (WSSC) system development charge for specified properties and revitalization projects located in Montgomery County. It prohibits requiring applicants for Montgomery County exemptions to own the property, directs Montgomery County to approve exemptions on a first-come, first-served basis up to the annual limit including carryovers, and establishes annual reporting requirements for both Montgomery and Prince George's counties.
responsible_party: Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission, Montgomery County Council, and Prince George's County Council
stakeholders: Property developers, community-based youth organizations, child care providers, programs for developmentally disabled individuals, elderly housing facilities, biotechnology/manufacturing businesses in Montgomery County, and WSSC ratepayers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are unaffected. Local finances for the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission are not directly affected by expanding exemption eligibility, as both Montgomery and Prince George's counties operate under an existing $500,000 annual cap on exemptions with rollover provisions, and both counties currently retain substantial unused capacity under those limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Public Utilities Article concerning water and sewer system development charge exemptions administered by the Washington Suburban Sanitary Commission and the local county councils. While the Public Service Commission was consulted as an information source for the fiscal note, it has no direct administrative or regulatory responsibilities under the bill and experiences no fiscal impact.

bill_summary: Authorizes municipalities in Queen Anne's County to lower the maximum speed limit on highways within their jurisdiction to as low as 15 miles per hour without conducting an engineering and traffic investigation.
responsible_party: Municipal governments in Queen Anne's County
stakeholders: Motorists, pedestrians, residents, and municipal governments in Queen Anne's County
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues may increase minimally if lower speed limits result in additional speeding citations, with no significant operational impact on the District Court. Queen Anne's County municipal expenditures decrease minimally due to savings from not conducting engineering and traffic investigations before lowering speed limits.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Under Maryland transportation law, any alteration of speed limits by a local authority on a State highway or extension thereof requires approval by the State Highway Administration. The bill amends local speed-setting authority on highways within Queen Anne's County municipalities.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding speed limit regulations and traffic investigations, falling directly under MDOT's statutory domain and oversight of highway safety and regulations.
The fiscal note notes that general fund revenues and District Court caseload may be minimally affected by citations resulting from any lowered speed limits implemented under the bill.

bill_summary: This bill establishes a liquor tasting license in Somerset County, authorizing the Board of License Commissioners to issue the license to holders of a Class A beer, wine, and liquor license. It permits complimentary liquor tastings with per-person limits of one-half ounce per offering and up to five offerings per day, and establishes tiered license fees based on the number of tasting days.
responsible_party: Board of License Commissioners for Somerset County
stakeholders: Holders of Class A beer, wine, and liquor licenses in Somerset County, Somerset County retail consumers, and Somerset County local government.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Somerset County revenues will increase to the extent that liquor tasting licenses are issued, with tiered fees of $20 for 1 day, $200 for 26 days, $300 for 52 days, and $400 for 104 days per licensing period. Any additional local enforcement activity can be absorbed within existing county resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Comptroller of Maryland regulates the state's alcohol industry. While this bill is implemented locally by the Somerset County Board of License Commissioners and has no state fiscal impact, it relates to the regulation and licensing of alcoholic beverages within the state.

Synopsis: Prohibiting certain insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations from excluding coverage for certain specialty drugs that are administered or dispensed by a provider that is an in-network provider of covered medical oncology services and complies with State regulations for the administering and dispensing of specialty drugs, if the specialty drugs meet certain qualifications; and requiring the reimbursement rate for certain specialty drugs to meet certain criteria.

bill_summary: Prohibits health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and health maintenance organizations—including pharmacy benefits managers acting on their behalf—from excluding coverage for certain specialty drugs administered or dispensed by qualified in-network medical oncology providers, and sets criteria for reimbursement rates.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, pharmacy benefits managers (PBMs), in-network medical oncology providers dispensing specialty drugs, and patients receiving specialty oncology medications.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal special fund revenue increase for the Maryland Insurance Administration in FY 2026 from the $125 rate and form filing fee. Any regulatory workload can be absorbed within existing budgeted resources. No impact on local finances or the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: As the primary regulator of private insurance plans, health maintenance organizations, and pharmacy benefits managers in Maryland, the Maryland Insurance Administration is responsible for enforcing the bill's coverage and reimbursement mandates and reviewing insurer form filings.

The bill explicitly references the Health Services Cost Review Commission to clarify that the new coverage and reimbursement restrictions do not supersede the Commission's statutory authority to set rates for specialty drugs administered in regulated hospital settings.

The Department of Health houses the Health Services Cost Review Commission and oversees regulations governing health care practitioners authorized to administer and dispense specialty drugs under the Health Occupations Article.

The Department of Budget and Management was analyzed during the legislative review to evaluate the bill's potential fiscal effect on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, though it was determined to have no impact.

Synopsis: Establishing the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration Waiver Advisory Council to advise and provide recommendations to the Developmental Disabilities Administration on system design, service delivery, and quality enhancement strategies for the Medicaid waiver programs operated by the Administration.

bill_summary: This bill formally establishes and codifies the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration Waiver Advisory Council within the Developmental Disabilities Administration. The council is tasked with advising and providing recommendations regarding system design, service delivery, federal waiver assurances, and quality enhancement strategies for Medicaid waiver programs, while prioritizing input from individuals with lived experience.
responsible_party: Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration within the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities participating in Medicaid waiver programs, their families, service providers, and disability advocacy organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures can likely be absorbed with existing budgeted resources (such as member expense reimbursements and travel arrangements), as the bill generally codifies the existing council. State revenues are not affected, and there is no material fiscal effect on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill formally establishes the Waiver Advisory Council within the Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA), an administration of the Department of Health. The Secretary of Health appoints voting members and designates nonvoting members, DDA provides staff support, and MDH hosts the council's webpage.

The Secretary of Disabilities designates a representative to serve as a nonvoting member on the newly established advisory council, which aligns closely with the department's mission to coordinate and improve services for individuals with disabilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new permanent advisory council, the Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration Waiver Advisory Council, to provide ongoing advice and recommendations on Medicaid waiver programs.

The State Superintendent of Schools is required to designate a representative from the Division of Rehabilitation Services within the Department of Education to serve as a nonvoting member of the council.
The Secretary of Housing and Community Development is required to designate a representative to serve as a nonvoting member of the advisory council.
The Secretary of Human Services is required to designate a representative to serve as a nonvoting member of the advisory council.

Synopsis: Requiring certain hospitals to adopt certain policies relating to obstetric services and to provide evidence to the Maryland Department of Health that the hospital has the policies; requiring the Maryland Department of Health to provide certain policies to the public on request; and requiring insurers that issue or deliver medical professional liability insurance policies in the State to provide the Maryland Department of Health, on request, with information regarding the insurer's policy regarding coverage of obstetric services.
Title: Hospitals and Medical Professional Liability Insurers - Obstetric Services Policies (Doula and Birth Policy Transparency Act)

bill_summary: The Doula and Birth Policy Transparency Act requires Maryland hospitals providing obstetric care to adopt and submit to the Maryland Department of Health policies concerning doula access, informed consent for significant medical interventions, and acceptance of patient transfers from home birth settings and licensed direct-entry midwives. It also directs the Department of Health to make these policies available to the public upon request and requires medical professional liability insurers to provide coverage information on obstetric services to the department upon request.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Birthing parents and their families, doulas, direct-entry midwives and home birth practitioners, hospitals providing obstetric services, and medical professional liability insurers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $90,800 in FY 2026, which accounts for the bill's October 1, 2025 effective date and covers the hiring of one health facilities nurse surveyor within the Office of Health Care Quality to adopt regulations, track compliance, and investigate complaints. Annualized expenditures range from $108,400 in FY 2027 to $123,300 in FY 2030. State revenues and local finances are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health is the primary implementing agency for the bill. It is responsible for adopting regulations, receiving evidence of hospital policies regarding doulas, informed consent, and patient transfers, making these policies available to the public upon request, and requesting obstetric coverage information from medical professional liability insurers.

The bill amends the Insurance Article by enacting requirements related to medical professional liability insurers providing obstetric care coverage policies. As the state agency regulating the insurance industry and insurers operating in Maryland, the Maryland Insurance Administration oversees compliance and was consulted on the legislation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Health Care Alternative Dispute Resolution Office handles medical malpractice claims and was consulted as an information source regarding the bill's provisions on informed consent for significant medical interventions and medical professional liability insurance.

Synopsis: Establishing the Department of Social and Economic Mobility; providing for the Secretary of Social and Economic Mobility; providing the purpose of the Department is to provide support for units of State government, individuals, and businesses for the maintenance of social equity policies in the State; establishing the Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund; requiring the Governor to include in the annual budget bill a certain appropriation from the Transportation Trust Fund to the Fund; etc.
Title: Department of Social and Economic Mobility - Established

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Establishes the Department of Social and Economic Mobility (DoSEM) as a principal department within the Executive Branch, headed by a Secretary appointed by the Governor. The bill consolidates and acts as the successor to three existing offices: the Governor's Office of Small, Minority, and Women Business Affairs, the Office of Social Equity in the Maryland Cannabis Administration, and the Office of Minority Business Enterprises in the Maryland Department of Transportation. It establishes the Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund to fund the operations and administrative expenses of the Office of Social Equity and Office of Minority Business Enterprises, and directs coordination and reporting on statewide social equity programs.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Social and Economic Mobility
stakeholders: Small, minority-, and women-owned business enterprises, individuals and communities disproportionately impacted by the enforcement of cannabis laws, state agency procurement staff, and transferred State personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $2.3 million in FY 2026 ($2,298,254, of which $2.2 million is pre-budgeted) for 9 new administrative and legal staff, one-time moving costs ($1.0 million), rent, and operating expenses, with ongoing general fund costs ranging from $1.6 million to $1.8 million annually. Additionally, 57 existing positions and associated special and general funds are redirected from MDOT, MCA, and the Executive Department, with special fund revenues and expenditures flowing through the newly established DoSEM Special Fund ($5.4 million in FY 2026 and $4.2 million to $4.4 million annually thereafter). There is no direct local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Small, Minority & Women Business Affairs
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the office and all of its staff, funding, and statutory responsibilities to become a constituent unit within the newly established Department of Social and Economic Mobility.

The bill transfers the Office of Social Equity out of the Maryland Cannabis Administration to the new department, while requiring ongoing coordination and consultation between MCA and the office on regulations and technical assistance.
The bill transfers the Office of Minority Business Enterprises out of MDOT into the new department and mandates that the Transportation Trust Fund continue to fund OMBE's operations.

DBM is tasked alongside the Governor with managing the transfer of personnel, positions, and funding to the new department, as well as overseeing budget and classification for newly created agency positions.

The bill establishes a new principal executive department, requires the Governor to appoint the Secretary and Executive Director of Social Equity, authorizes the transfer of budgeted positions and funds, and requires annual reports to the Governor.
The bill designates the Attorney General as the legal adviser to the new department and requires the assignment of Assistant Attorneys General and a designated principal counsel to the agency.

The Comptroller must account for the new Special Fund, administer the quarterly distribution of cannabis sales and use tax revenues to the fund, and consult with the Office of Social Equity regarding the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.
The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the newly created Department of Social and Economic Mobility Special Fund.
The bill requires Commerce to collaborate with the Office of Social Equity in assisting businesses with obtaining financing under the Capital Access Program and the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund.
The bill requires annual MBE reporting to be submitted to the Board of Public Works.

responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Restaurants, bars, and hospitality businesses near the Annapolis Mall, patrons seeking entertainment and alcoholic beverages, and the school located at the Annapolis Mall.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. The bill does not materially affect Anne Arundel County finances and operations, though minimal permit fee revenues ($200 to $400 annually per permit) may be collected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill alters local alcoholic beverages licensing and permit distance requirements in Anne Arundel County. While local licensing and enforcement are handled by the county's Board of License Commissioners and there is no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller is broadly responsible for regulating the state's alcohol industry.

responsible_party: Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Anne Arundel County alcoholic beverages license holders (Class B, BLX, C, D, and H), patrons, and local performers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: The bill does not materially affect Anne Arundel County operations or finances, though it establishes permit fees of $15 per day for beer and wine licensees, $25 per day for beer, wine, and liquor licensees, and no fee for Class C licensees. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to authorize a limited special event permit in Anne Arundel County. While the permit is administered and issued locally by the Anne Arundel County Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller regulates the alcohol industry in the state.

responsible_party: Charles County Government
stakeholders: Owners and operators of off-highway recreational vehicles in Charles County, local law enforcement, and Charles County residents.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State finances or operations. Because the bill is authorizing, it has no immediate local fiscal impact; however, if Charles County implements registration requirements and fees, county revenues will increase minimally, with no material impact on local expenditures.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law within the Transportation Article (§ 25-102) to grant Charles County specific regulatory, registration, and impoundment authority over off-highway recreational vehicles.

The Motor Vehicle Administration oversees statewide vehicle titling and registration. The bill establishes an exception allowing Charles County to implement county-level registration and fees for off-highway recreational vehicles.

Maryland State Police officers enforce the Maryland Vehicle Law and criminal laws throughout the state, including the reckless driving, impaired driving, and trespassing statutes referenced in the vehicle impoundment provisions.

The court system is responsible for adjudicating alleged violations of the Transportation Article and Criminal Law Article that could give rise to vehicle impoundment proceedings under local regulation.

responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Commissioner
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, dental plan carriers, healthcare providers, and health benefit plan enrollees and prospective enrollees in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: No state or local fiscal impact. The bill pertains to private-sector requirements conforming to federal law. The Maryland Insurance Administration can complete the required report to the General Assembly using existing budgeted resources, and revenues are not affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding provider directory requirements for health insurance carriers regulated by the state, and requires the Maryland Insurance Commissioner to enforce these standards and report to the General Assembly on regulatory changes related to directory accuracy by January 1, 2026.

bill_summary: This bill regulates earned wage access (EWA) products under the Maryland Consumer Loan Law and related consumer credit laws. responsible_party: Office of Financial Regulation (Maryland Department of Labor)
stakeholders: Earned wage access providers, consumer lenders, employers, and consumers/employees who use earned wage access or consumer credit products.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill generally codifies existing practice and is not anticipated to materially affect State finances or operations. The Office of Financial Regulation can implement and enforce the provisions using existing resources. There is no local government fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill regulates earned wage access products under the Maryland Consumer Loan Law, overseen by the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, which is a division within the Maryland Department of Labor. The Department is responsible for licensing providers, receiving required annual reports, adopting implementing regulations, and conducting enforcement.

The Office of the Attorney General provides legal counsel to the Department of Labor and the Commissioner of Financial Regulation, and enforces state consumer protection laws regarding consumer credit practices.

bill_summary: Establishes the Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program within the Maryland Department of the Environment, prohibiting unauthorized groundwater augmentation while authorizing the department to review, permit, and regulate a single demonstration facility using treated reclaimed water to test groundwater augmentation.

stakeholders: Local governments, public water systems, private well owners near potential project sites, and water treatment or engineering businesses.
fiscal_impact_summary: MDE can implement the program and issue the single permit using existing resources. General fund expenditures and revenues for MDH Laboratories Administration may increase by approximately $17,000 annually beginning as early as FY 2026 for water testing reimbursed by MDE. Local government expenditures may increase significantly if a local entity voluntarily applies for the permit and constructs a demonstration facility.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Managed Aquifer Recharge Pilot Program within MDE. MDE is the primary regulatory body responsible for accepting applications, issuing the managed aquifer recharge permit, setting water quality and monitoring requirements, conducting inspections, adopting regulations, and submitting annual reports.

MDH's Laboratories Administration provides analytical testing support for MDE and is anticipated to conduct water testing for the pilot program under an existing memorandum of understanding, resulting in an estimated $17,000 annual impact on expenditures and reimbursable revenues.

MDE is required to submit an annual report to the Governor beginning December 31, 2028, on the status and scientific results of the pilot program and recommendations regarding permanent statutory or regulatory authorization.

bill_summary: Prohibits the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid), the Maryland Children's Health Program, managed care organizations, and certain commercial health insurance carriers from requiring prior authorization for a patient transfer to a special pediatric hospital.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health and Maryland Insurance Administration

fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration increase minimally in FY 2026 from $125 rate and form filing fees. Medicaid expenditures (general and federal funds) may increase by an indeterminate but likely minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 to the extent the bill increases nonmedically necessary inpatient days, with federal fund revenues increasing accordingly. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of Health administers the Maryland Medical Assistance Program (Medicaid) and the Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP), both of which are directly prohibited under the bill from requiring prior authorization for transfers to special pediatric hospitals.

The Maryland Insurance Administration regulates health insurers, nonprofit health service plans, and HMOs subject to the new prior authorization prohibition, and will review policy form filings and collect associated filing fees.

The Department of Budget and Management administers the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program; while reviewed as an information source, the fiscal note determined the bill has no fiscal impact on the State plan.

bill_summary: This bill revises Maryland's Prescription Drug Repository Program by allowing entities located in other states to participate as drop-off sites and repositories, and expanding the program to include over-the-counter (OTC) drugs in addition to prescription drugs. responsible_party: State Board of Pharmacy
stakeholders: Eligible patients (individuals who are indigent, uninsured, underinsured, or enrolled in public health benefit programs), participating in-state and out-of-state pharmacies and repositories, pharmacy staff and volunteers, and drug donors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Board of Pharmacy special fund expenditures increase by $53,844 in FY 2026 to hire one full-time licensing specialist to handle registration and oversight of out-of-state participating entities, increasing to $69,800 by FY 2030 due to ongoing operational costs. agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Board of Pharmacy, which regulates and administers the Prescription Drug Repository Program, is housed within the Maryland Department of Health. The bill expands the program to include out-of-state entities and over-the-counter drugs, requiring MDH/the Board of Pharmacy to adopt regulations, register out-of-state participants, and incur special fund expenditures for staffing.
The State Board of Pharmacy is statutorily required to submit an annual report to the Governor on the operation of the Prescription Drug Repository Program.

It also requires insurers and nonprofit health service plans to cover childhood and adolescent immunizations recommended by ACIP or the American Academy of Pediatrics as of December 31, 2024, without a deductible.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding mandated child wellness and immunization coverage, granting the Insurance Commissioner regulatory authority and resulting in rate and form filings submitted to the Administration.

The bill directly governs the scope of pharmacist-administered vaccinations, establishes criteria for vaccination protocols in consultation with health occupations licensing boards, and references reporting requirements to the Department's ImmuNet system.
As the agency overseeing the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, DBM assesses health insurance coverage mandates for potential fiscal and benefit design impacts.

bill_summary: Known as Matthew's Law, this bill prohibits operating a gasoline-powered vessel manufactured after July 31, 2007, that has accommodation spaces, swim platforms, or aft lounging areas on Maryland waters unless carbon monoxide warning labels are conspicuously affixed near the transom and helm. It also specifies that the Department of Natural Resources may not impose a penalty for violations.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Owners and operators of qualifying gasoline-powered vessels, boat passengers, and maritime recreationists in Maryland waters
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances, and has a minimal effect on small businesses. The Department of Natural Resources is prohibited from imposing penalties for violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a safety requirement to the State Boat Act in the Natural Resources Article requiring carbon monoxide warning labels on certain gasoline-powered vessels on State waters, and explicitly prohibits the Department of Natural Resources from imposing penalties for violations.

fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: May result in minimal cost savings for Garrett County from reduced advertising expenses and improved operational efficiencies.

Synopsis: Establishing the special event venue beer, wine, and liquor license in Caroline County; authorizing the Board of License Commissioners of Caroline County to issue the license to the owner of a venue with a certain zoning classification; authorizing holders of certain multiple event licenses in Caroline County to store alcoholic beverages on the licensed premises between individual events in a certain manner; requiring the license holder to keep complete records of all alcoholic beverages purchased and sold on the premises; etc.

It also permits multiple event license holders to store alcoholic beverages securely on premises between events, subject to specific inventory and recordkeeping requirements.
responsible_party: Caroline County Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Owners and operators of special event venues and holders of multiple event licenses (including volunteer fire companies) in Caroline County, alcohol wholesalers, and event attendees.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: None. Local effect: Caroline County revenues will increase beginning in FY 2026 depending on the number of licenses issued, with fees set at $250 (up to 10 events), $500 (up to 20 events), $750 (up to 30 events), and $1,000 (up to 40 events) per year. County enforcement can be handled with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly authorizes personnel of the Comptroller of Maryland to inspect the alcoholic beverage inventory records and premises of multiple event license holders in Caroline County.

It also authorizes Anne Arundel County and its municipalities to grant a real property tax credit of up to $10,000 for qualifying portions of real property dedicated exclusively to licensed or registered child care centers, large family child care homes, or adult and elderly day care centers.
responsible_party: State Department of Assessments and Taxation
stakeholders: Operators of large family child care homes, child care centers, and adult/elderly day care facilities in Anne Arundel County; businesses with 25 or more employees offering child care facilities; and Anne Arundel County and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances are not affected. Local property tax revenues in Anne Arundel County and its municipalities will decrease beginning in FY 2026 due to the personal property tax exemption (expected to be minimal as only one such home was licensed as of January 2025) and local property tax credits of up to $10,000 per qualifying property to the extent local governments authorize and grant them. Local expenditures are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill bases eligibility for local property tax exemptions and credits on child care facilities and family child care homes registered or licensed by MSDE under Title 9.5 of the Education Article.
The bill references day care centers for the elderly and adults licensed under Title 14 of the Health - General Article, which falls under MDH regulatory oversight.

responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: Child care providers, Maryland working families and children, and State agencies occupying State-owned facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $96,000 in FY 2026 and $35,500 in FY 2027 to hire one contractual program manager to review facilities, conduct site visits, and prepare the required report. No impact on revenues or local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency tasked with conducting the assessment of all State-owned facilities across 16 supported agencies to determine their suitability and availability for leasing to child care centers, and reporting its findings to the General Assembly.

MSDE oversees early childhood development and child care center licensing standards (under § 9.5–401 of the Education Article), requiring extensive collaboration with DGS to assess whether facility physical plants meet child care center regulatory criteria.

bill_summary: Exempts certified security guards employed by or providing services to cannabis licensees or registrants from having to complete a separate criminal history records check to register as cannabis agents with the Maryland Cannabis Administration. Additionally, alters the definition of "security guard employer" to exclude video lottery operators, sports wagering facility licensees, and health care facilities from security guard employer regulations.
responsible_party: Department of State Police and the Maryland Cannabis Administration
stakeholders: Security guards, cannabis licensees and registrants, video lottery operators, sports wagering facility licensees, and health care facilities
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $75,000 in FY 2026 for one-time IT costs for the Department of State Police to update its online licensing portal. General fund revenues decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2026 from reduced security guard certification and renewal fees. Special fund revenues and expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services decrease indeterminately beginning in FY 2026 due to fewer criminal history records checks and associated pass-through FBI fees. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Secretary of State Police is responsible for licensing security guard agencies and certifying security guards under Title 19 of the Business Occupations and Professions Article. The bill directly impacts MSP's regulatory scope by altering the definition of 'security guard employer,' requiring $75,000 in IT expenditures to update its application portal and resulting in reduced certification fee revenues.

The bill directly amends § 36-501 of the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article by exempting certain cannabis agents who are already authorized security guards from the requirement to obtain a separate State and national criminal history records check to register with the MCA.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department houses the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository (CJIS-CR), which processes criminal history records checks. The bill will reduce the volume of CHRCs processed, resulting in minor decreases in special fund fee revenues and FBI pass-through expenditures.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland State Lottery & Gaming Control Agency
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly references video lottery operators and sports wagering facility licensees licensed and regulated by the agency, exempting them from the definition and regulatory requirements of 'security guard employers.'

bill_summary: This bill shortens the timeframe within which health insurance carriers must accept or reject certain behavioral health care professionals—including licensed master social workers, certain graduate-level counselors and therapists, registered psychology associates, licensed certified social workers-clinical, and licensed clinical professional counselors—for participation on a provider panel to within 60 days after receiving a completed application. It also updates the statutory list of community-based behavioral health providers whom carriers may not reject solely based on practicing within their scope of license by removing licensed graduate social workers to reflect current licensing titles.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, behavioral health care professionals (such as licensed master social workers, graduate counselors and therapists, psychology associates, and clinical counselors), accredited community-based behavioral health programs, and patients seeking behavioral health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations, and local government finances and operations are not directly affected. Small business community-based health care providers may experience a meaningful impact by being able to credential providers faster and obtain insurance reimbursement more quickly.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Insurance Article regarding health insurance carriers' credentialing timelines and requirements for behavioral health care provider panels, which are regulated and enforced by the Maryland Insurance Administration through existing statutory penalties.

The bill affects provider panel credentialing for behavioral health professionals licensed by health occupations boards housed within MDH (such as social workers, professional counselors, and psychology associates) and references community-based health service programs accredited under MDH regulations.
