bill_summary: Expands health insurance coverage requirements for medically appropriate and necessary adult hearing aids to include those that are ordered, fitted, and dispensed by a licensed hearing aid dispenser, in addition to licensed audiologists.
responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Adult health insurance policyholders needing hearing aids, licensed hearing aid dispensers, and health insurance carriers.
fiscal_impact_summary: Minimal increase in special fund revenues for the Maryland Insurance Administration from $125 rate and form filing fees in FY 2026 only, with additional workload managed using existing budgeted resources. There is no impact on the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program and no material effect on local government finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Insurance Administration is the primary regulatory agency responsible for enforcing health insurance mandates and reviewing rate and form filings submitted by insurers to comply with the altered hearing aid coverage requirements.
The Department of Budget and Management oversees the State Employee and Retiree Health and Welfare Benefits Program, which must evaluate changes to state health insurance coverage mandates.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange oversees qualified health plans and essential health benefits offered on the individual and small business marketplaces, which are subject to state coverage mandates.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing coordinates policies and advocates for improved accessibility and resources, including hearing health coverage and devices, for hard of hearing residents across Maryland.

bill_summary: Establishes a civil penalty of up to $50,000 per day for any person who falsifies information submitted in a lead-contaminated dust testing or visual inspection report required under the Reduction of Lead Risk in Housing law.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Accredited lead paint inspectors and risk assessors, rental property owners, and tenants residing in affected rental housing.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues to the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund may minimally increase beginning in FY 2026 from civil penalties assessed under the bill. State expenditures and local government finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) administers the Lead Poisoning Prevention Program and receives the verified inspection and testing reports under Title 6, Subtitle 8 of the Environment Article. The bill establishes a civil penalty of up to $50,000 for falsifying information in these reports, which will be collected and deposited into the Lead Poisoning Prevention Fund.

The bill provides that the civil penalty is to be collected via a civil action, which directly involves the Maryland state court system managed and supported by the Administrative Office of the Courts.

As the chief legal representative for state agencies, the Office of the Attorney General would represent the Department of the Environment in filing and litigating civil actions to collect civil penalties for falsified lead inspection reports.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration to enter into agreements through a national association of motor vehicle agencies to facilitate the issuance, use, and verification of electronic credentials, and allows individuals to present a valid electronic credential (mobile ID) instead of a physical driver's license when renting a vehicle.
responsible_party: Motor Vehicle Administration
stakeholders: Drivers utilizing electronic credentials or mobile IDs, nonresidents renting vehicles in Maryland, and vehicle rental companies and lessors.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no material impact on Transportation Trust Fund revenues or expenditures. To the extent the Motor Vehicle Administration enters into facilitation agreements, it can do so using existing resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends laws governing the Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA), authorizing it to enter into agreements through a national association of motor vehicle agencies to facilitate electronic credentials and permitting electronic credentials to be used in rental vehicle transactions.

The Department of Transportation is the parent agency of the Motor Vehicle Administration, and the bill impacts Transportation Article provisions and operates within MDOT's administrative and budgetary oversight.

Synopsis: Authorizing a tow truck to display a portable variable messaging sign mounted on the tow truck while at the scene of a crash or a disabled vehicle; and requiring the portable variable messaging sign to conform to the standards established in the manual on uniform traffic control devices adopted by the State Highway Administration and display only messages approved by the Administration.

bill_summary: Authorizes tow trucks to be equipped with and display mounted portable variable messaging signs while at the scene of a vehicle crash or disabled vehicle, provided the signs conform to standards in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices and display only messages approved by the State Highway Administration.
responsible_party: State Highway Administration
stakeholders: Tow truck operators, motorists, highway maintenance personnel, and emergency responders.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is authorizing in nature and does not directly affect State or local revenues or expenditures. However, expenditures may increase if State or local agencies voluntarily choose to equip or purchase tow trucks with portable variable messaging signs (for illustrative purposes, the Maryland Transportation Authority estimated fleet purchase costs of $3.0 million for 20 trucks at $150,000 each).

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill explicitly tasks the State Highway Administration (SHA) with adopting the standards in the Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices that portable variable messaging signs must conform to, as well as approving the specific messages authorized for display.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding vehicle equipment regulations and directly affects its modal administrations, including the State Highway Administration and the Maryland Transportation Authority.

MDTA operates highway facilities and tow truck fleets; the fiscal note specifically highlights potential fiscal impacts if MDTA chooses to purchase and deploy tow trucks equipped with portable variable messaging signs.
The Maryland State Police was an information source for the fiscal note and is responsible for enforcing vehicle lighting and equipment laws on Maryland highways.
The bill amends vehicle equipment and lighting provisions under the Maryland Vehicle Law, which is administered and regulated by the Motor Vehicle Administration.

Synopsis: Altering certain provisions relating to the award of noneconomic damages to a claimant in an action for child sexual abuse; altering certain provisions relating to the liability of the State under the Maryland Tort Claims Act and of a local government under the Local Government Tort Claims Act for certain claims of child sexual abuse; and requiring the Maryland Judiciary to report to the General Assembly by January 31, 2027, and each year thereafter, on the amount of each award and a summary of the sexual abuse claims related to the award.
Title: Civil Actions - Child Sexual Abuse

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.
Insurance -see also- Health Ins; MAIF; Motor Vehicle Ins
Torts -see also- Libel and Slander; Med Malp; Wrongful Death

bill_summary: This bill reduces the liability limits and damages caps for previously time-barred civil actions for child sexual abuse filed on or after June 1, 2025. Specifically, it lowers the noneconomic damages cap from $1.5 million to $700,000 for non-governmental defendants, and reduces the liability limits under the Maryland Tort Claims Act, Local Government Tort Claims Act, and for county boards of education from $890,000 to $400,000 for a single claimant. It also limits attorney's fees to 20% of a settlement or 25% of a judgment, bars actions against the State or State units filed on or after January 1, 2026 for previously time-barred claims, and establishes reporting requirements for the Judiciary.
responsible_party: Supreme Court of Maryland and Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Claimants of child sexual abuse, plaintiffs' attorneys, the State of Maryland, local governments, and county boards of education.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local expenditures decrease, potentially significantly, due to lower liability caps ($400,000) for previously time-barred claims filed on or after June 1, 2025, and applying limits per claimant rather than per occurrence. State and local revenues are unaffected. Exact fiscal savings cannot be reliably determined in advance.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Section 3 of the bill directly mandates that the Maryland Judiciary report annually to the General Assembly beginning January 31, 2027, on the amount of each award made under the Act and a summary of the underlying sexual abuse claims. Additionally, Section 2 authorizes the Supreme Court of Maryland to adopt implementation rules.

The OAG represents the State in civil litigation and tort claims under the Maryland Tort Claims Act (MTCA). The bill directly impacts the defense and potential liability for thousands of pending and future Child Victims Act claims filed against the State by setting liability caps and establishing a filing deadline of January 1, 2026, for claims against the State.

The Treasurer's Office administers the State Insurance Trust Fund (SITF), which handles and pays tort claims against the State under the Maryland Tort Claims Act. The bill directly alters MTCA liability caps for child sexual abuse claims, significantly impacting potential state liabilities and SITF expenditures.

The bill amends Section 4-105 of the Education Article, requiring the State Board of Education to update its standards for comprehensive liability insurance coverage carried by county boards of education to conform to the new liability caps for sexual abuse claims.

Under the amended provisions of Education Article § 4-105, county boards of education that elect to self-insure must comply with regulations adopted by the State Insurance Commissioner and submit their self-insurance terms and conditions to the Commissioner for review and approval.
As the State's principal fiscal agency, DBM is affected by potential substantial reductions in State expenditures and liabilities arising from the modified MTCA caps and settlement considerations.

bill_summary: House Bill 1424, titled the Protect Our Federal Workers Act, expands the purposes of the Catastrophic Event Account and renames and expands the Federal Government Shutdown Employee Assistance Loan Fund to provide no-interest loans and financial assistance to Maryland residents who are federal employees facing furloughs, mass layoffs, closures, or relocations. It authorizes loan forgiveness, increases the annual mandated appropriation to the Office of the Attorney General from $1.0 million to at least $2.5 million to protect Marylanders against certain federal actions, and creates a temporary Expedited Hiring Program in the Department of Budget and Management to quickly recruit former federal employees into vacant State positions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor, Department of Budget and Management, and Office of the Attorney General
stakeholders: Current and former federal employees and contractors residing in Maryland who are impacted by federal shutdowns, mass layoffs, or facility closures, as well as State and county agencies seeking to fill vacant government positions.
fiscal_impact_summary: State Rainy Day Fund expenditures increase by $6.5 million in FY 2025 to transfer $5.0 million to the loan fund and $1.5 million to the Office of the Attorney General (OAG). Dedicated Purpose Account expenditures increase by $500,000 in FY 2025 and $1.5 million in FY 2026 to support the Expedited Hiring Program. Catastrophic Event Account expenditures increase by $10.0 million in FY 2026 for loan capitalization, resulting in special fund loan expenditures of up to $15.0 million in FY 2026. General fund expenditures increase by $1.7 million in FY 2026 for Department of Labor administrative and IT costs, and by $1.5 million annually beginning in FY 2027 to satisfy the increased mandated appropriation for OAG. Local fiscal impact is minimal, though counties may benefit from expedited hiring coordination.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Administers the newly renamed and expanded Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund, establishes loan procedures and eligibility, processes loans and loan forgiveness, and conducts research and reports on foreclosure activity among federal workers.

Establishes and administers the temporary Expedited Hiring Program to recruit former federal workers into the State Personnel Management System, develops guidance and regulations, and oversees the Catastrophic Event Account.

Receives expanded authority under the Maryland Defense Act to investigate and litigate federal actions impacting federal employees and federal benefits/entitlements, and receives an increased annual mandated appropriation of at least $2.5 million to employ attorneys.

Authorizes the Governor to execute transfers from the Revenue Stabilization Account and Catastrophic Event Account, mandates funding in the Governor's annual budget for the Attorney General, and establishes notice and review procedures between the Attorney General and the Governor before litigation is filed.

Accounts for the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund, and is authorized to disclose tax information to the Department of Labor to verify eligibility and prevent fraud.
Holds and manages investments for the Catastrophic Event Account and the Federal Government Employee Assistance Loan Fund as specified in the State Finance and Procurement statutory alterations.

The bill modifies the Maryland Homeowners Association Act and places restrictions on private covenants and deed restrictions, which falls within the regulatory and consumer protection interest of the Attorney General's Office regarding homeowners associations and real property law enforcement.

bill_summary: This bill modifies laws governing special taxing districts for erosion prevention and control projects. bill_summary: This bill establishes paid family and medical leave (PFML) benefits for all Executive Branch state employees, including temporary workers, allowing them to take up to 12 weeks (and up to 24 weeks under specific circumstances) of fully paid leave. It permits the State to self-insure rather than participate in the public Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FAMLI) system, repeals the State's existing paid parental leave program, and requires the Department of Budget and Management and public higher education institutions to adopt regulations to administer the program.

FAMLI Fund special fund revenues decrease by twice that amount due to foregone employer and employee contributions. Beginning in FY 2027, FAMLI contribution savings continue, but State expenditures increase to provide fully paid leave and administer the program (including contracting a third-party administrator and hiring additional staff); the net expenditure impact is indeterminate. FAMLI special fund expenditures also decrease beginning in FY 2027 from not paying FAMLI benefits to State employees. No local fiscal impact.

Title: Real Property - Holding Over - Expedited Hearing and Service of Summons for Active Duty Service Members

NarrowSubjects.Name: Armed Forces -see also- Military Department; Veterans
Law Enforcement -see also- SRO; Sheriffs; State Police

bill_summary: Establishes expedited proceedings in tenant holding over actions for active duty U.S. military service members or their spouses who relocate to Maryland and intend to occupy the property. Under the bill, the District Court must order the tenant to appear within 45 days of the complaint, and authorizes service of summons by a private process server if a county sheriff or constable fails to serve it within 10 days.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Active duty U.S. military service members and their spouses who own residential rental property in Maryland, holdover tenants residing in those properties, county sheriffs and constables, and private process servers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the operations and scheduling of the District Court by requiring an expedited hearing within 45 days of a tenant holding over complaint when filed by an active duty service member, and modifies summons procedures.

The bill establishes legal protections and expedited real property repossession procedures specifically for active duty military service members and their families relocating to Maryland, which aligns with the department's mission to support active-duty service members and their families.

Synopsis: Requiring a certain hearing to be held not more than 10 business days after a certain complaint is filed; and altering requirements relating to service of process in a wrongful detainer action.
Title: Real Property - Wrongful Detainer - Time of Hearing and Service of Process

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: This bill alters procedures governing wrongful detainer actions by requiring the District Court to hold a show-cause hearing within 10 business days after a complaint is filed. It also modifies service of process requirements when an occupant cannot be found after two good faith efforts on separate days, requiring an affidavit of efforts, service by both certified and first-class mail, and conspicuous posting on the property within four business days of filing.
responsible_party: District Court of Maryland
stakeholders: Property owners claiming possession of real property, individuals occupying real property without legal right (wrongful detainers), process servers, and county sheriffs.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not anticipated to materially affect State or local government finances or operations. Any impact on small businesses is expected to be minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Senate Bill 46 establishes strict statutory timelines and procedural requirements for wrongful detainer actions in the District Court and Circuit Court. It mandates that hearings occur within 10 business days after a complaint is filed, sets requirements for service of process affidavits and default judgments, and expedites the timeline for appeals. As the central administrative agency for the Maryland Judiciary, AOC is responsible for implementing the necessary court scheduling, case management, and operational adjustments to comply with these statutory court deadlines.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of General Services to include a notation on a certain identification card indicating that the holder is a veteran under certain circumstances; requiring the Department to obtain the consent of a certain holder of an identification card before transmitting certain information to a certain executive agency; and prohibiting the Department from transmitting certain information obtained on an application for an identification card except under certain circumstances.
Title: Department of General Services - Identification Cards - Veteran Status Notation

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

bill_summary: Authorizes the Department of General Services to place a veteran status notation on identification security cards for individuals who provide acceptable proof of veteran status, and allows applicants to consent to having their contact information shared with executive agencies regarding eligibility for veterans' benefits.
responsible_party: Department of General Services
stakeholders: Military veterans who are state employees, contractors, regulated lobbyists, media personnel, local government officials, or volunteers receiving identification cards from the Department of General Services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State effect: The Department of General Services can implement the veteran status notation and manage information transmission using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on revenues. Local effect: No material effect on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DGS is the primary implementing agency responsible for authorizing and issuing the veteran status notation on state identification cards, updating application forms to capture veteran status and contact consent, transmitting consented information to executive agencies, and potentially adopting regulations.

DVMF is explicitly named as an entity providing certifications of veteran status required for the ID card notation, and serves as a primary executive agency that can receive contact information of consented veterans to connect them with state and federal benefits.

Synopsis: Requiring a licensed funeral establishment, crematory operator, or reduction facility to take certain actions if a certain veterans service organization does not take possession of certain unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, or soil remains that qualify for a plot in a veterans cemetery within a certain period of time.
Title: Funeral Establishments, Crematories, and Reduction Facilities - Disposition of Unclaimed Remains - Veterans

NarrowSubjects.Name: Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Forests and Parks -see also- MdNatlCapPkPlnCm; Plants; etc.

bill_summary: Requires licensed funeral establishments, crematory permit holders, and reduction facilities to notify and transfer unclaimed cremated, hydrolyzed, or soil remains of veterans or eligible dependents to the Department of Veterans and Military Families if a veterans service organization does not take possession of them within 10 days of notification, ensuring appropriate disposition and burial in a State veterans' cemetery.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Veterans and Military Families
stakeholders: Deceased veterans and their eligible dependents with unclaimed remains, licensed funeral establishments, crematory operators, natural organic reduction facilities, and veterans service organizations.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures (general and federal funds) for the Department of Veterans and Military Families (DVMF) may increase by an indeterminate but minimal amount beginning in FY 2026 for additional burials in State veterans' cemeteries. Costs for veterans are fully reimbursed by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs through a $978 plot allowance, generating matching federal fund revenue. Costs for burying veterans' dependents are not reimbursed and must be covered by general funds (estimated illustratively at $5,000 annually for five dependents). Local governments are not impacted.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 57 directly impacts the department by requiring licensed funeral establishments, crematories, and reduction facilities to notify and transfer unclaimed cremains, hydrolyzed remains, or eligible soil remains of veterans and their dependents to the department for final disposition and burial in State veterans' cemeteries, which also carries an operational and fiscal impact.

The Maryland Department of Labor houses the Office of Cemetery Oversight, which regulates crematories and reduction facilities under the Business Regulation Article, the primary section of state law amended by this bill.

The Maryland Department of Health oversees the State Board of Morticians and Funeral Directors, which licenses funeral establishments and crematories regulated under Title 7 of the Health Occupations Article amended by the bill.

Synopsis: Authorizing health occupations boards to include a notation indicating veteran status on a license, certificate, registration, or public profile.
Title: Health Occupations Boards - Notation of Veteran Status and Eligibility for Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits

bill_summary: Authorizes health occupations boards under the Maryland Department of Health to establish a process allowing applicants and licensees to include a notation indicating veteran status on their license, certificate, registration, or public profile, and to share relevant information with Executive Branch agencies to assist in determining eligibility for state and federal veterans benefits.
responsible_party: Health Occupations Boards within the Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Military veterans applying for or holding health occupation credentials in Maryland and Maryland health occupations boards
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures may increase by an indeterminate, likely minimal amount to the extent that health occupations boards opt to create the process (primarily for one-time licensing software and IT system updates, which are largely absorbable within existing resources). Revenues are not affected, and there is no material impact on local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the 20 health occupations boards housed within the Maryland Department of Health to establish processes for noting veteran status on licenses, certificates, registrations, and public profiles, and to transmit relevant applicant data to executive branch agencies.

The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status obtained from the Department of Veterans and Military Families and allows applicant information to be shared with executive branch agencies to determine eligibility for and connect veterans to state and federal benefits.

Synopsis: Renaming the Chesapeake Conservation Corps Program to be the Thomas V. Mike Miller, Jr. Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program.

Natural Resources -see also- Coal; For&Pks; Rivers; etc.

bill_summary: Renames the Chesapeake Conservation Corps Program to be the Thomas V. Mike Miller, Jr., Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program.
responsible_party: Chesapeake Bay Trust
stakeholders: Volunteers and young adults participating in the corps, grant-recipient organizations, and communities served by environmental and climate projects.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not directly affect State or local finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Chesapeake Bay Trust is the primary entity that administers the Chesapeake Conservation Corps Program, which is renamed by this bill to the Thomas V. Mike Miller, Jr., Chesapeake Conservation and Climate Corps Program.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Service and Civic Innovation
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department administers the Maryland Service Year Option Pathway under State Government Article § 21-206, which is specifically amended to reflect the renamed Corps Program when using pathway funds to expand service opportunities.

DNR oversees natural resources provisions and the Environmental Trust Fund in the Natural Resources Article, which transfers funds to the Chesapeake Bay Trust for the renamed Corps Program, and DNR provided information on the bill.

Synopsis: Prohibiting a person from committing a violation of the prohibition against abusing or neglecting an animal that results in the death of a domestic animal or livestock or the need to euthanize the domestic animal or livestock; providing that a person who violates the Act is guilty of a misdemeanor and on conviction is subject to imprisonment for up to 1 year or a fine of up to $5,000 or both; and authorizing a court to impost certain conditions of sentencing and probation.
Title: Criminal Law - Animal Abuse or Neglect - Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Abuse -see also- Child Abuse; Dom. Viol.; Elder Abuse; etc
Animals -see also- Birds; Dogs; Domestic An; Horses; Livestk
Courts -see also- AppCt; Circuit; District; Orphans'; etc.
Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Mental and Behavioral Health -see also- Aut; Cogn; Dev; etc.
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Establishes a distinct criminal misdemeanor offense for animal abuse or neglect that results in the death of a domestic animal or livestock, or the need to euthanize it based on the validated recommendation of two licensed veterinarians. The bill sets penalties of up to one year imprisonment and/or a fine up to $5,000, and allows courts to impose conditions of sentencing such as psychological counseling, restitution for care and euthanasia costs, and prohibitions on owning, possessing, or residing with animals.
responsible_party: Judiciary of Maryland
stakeholders: Individuals accused or convicted of animal abuse or neglect, domestic animal and livestock owners, veterinarians, animal welfare organizations, and state and local law enforcement and correctional facilities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $34,600 in FY 2025 for one-time programming costs for the Judiciary. General fund incarceration expenditures for the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services may also increase, while state general fund revenues will be minimally affected. Local revenues may increase from higher fines imposed in circuit courts, while local expenditures may rise due to longer incarceration terms in local detention centers and potential costs to compensate veterinarians for validating euthanasia decisions.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new criminal offense and associated sentencing conditions for animal abuse resulting in death or euthanasia. The fiscal note identifies a direct fiscal impact of $34,558 in FY 2025 for one-time computer system programming costs for the Judiciary.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes misdemeanor penalties of up to one year of imprisonment, which the fiscal note notes may increase state incarceration expenditures for convictions arising in Baltimore City served at state-operated correctional facilities.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes a new criminal misdemeanor penalty punishable by up to one year in prison, impacting caseloads and representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants charged under the statute.

The Maryland Department of Agriculture oversees animal health and livestock welfare in the state. The bill specifically establishes criminal penalties regarding abuse or neglect resulting in the death or euthanasia of livestock.

As the primary statewide law enforcement agency, the Maryland State Police is responsible for investigating and enforcing violations of state criminal law, including criminal animal cruelty and abuse statutes.

Synopsis: Authorizing the Department of the Environment to establish a certain process in collaboration with one or more boards under the Department's direction and control that requires a board to include a notation indicating veteran status on a professional license or certificate.
Title: Department of the Environment - Notation of Veteran Status

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst
Work, Labor, and Employment -see also- JobTrn; Leave; etc.

bill_summary: Authorizes the Maryland Department of the Environment, in collaboration with its licensing boards, to establish a process allowing applicants for professional licenses or certificates to submit proof of veteran status, consent to a veteran notation on their credential, and consent to being contacted by Executive Branch agencies regarding eligibility for state and federal veterans' benefits.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Veterans seeking or holding professional licenses and certificates from boards under the Maryland Department of the Environment (such as marine contractors, well drillers, and waterworks operators).
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of the Environment can implement the necessary updates to forms and databases using existing budgeted resources. The bill is not anticipated to have a material impact on State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill authorizes the Department of the Environment and its licensing boards to establish a process to include a veteran status notation on professional licenses and certificates, collect documentation and consent, transmit information to executive branch agencies, and adopt related regulations.

The bill explicitly references veteran status certification obtained from the Department of Veterans and Military Families, and involves sharing veteran applicant information to assist with determining eligibility for state and federal veterans benefits.

Synopsis: Requiring the local board of elections to send a written notice regarding a request for a State-approved absentee ballot application with a specimen ballot and any other mailings to voters and eligible voters to further awareness of the option of mail-in voting, except under certain circumstances.
Title: Election Law - Absentee Ballots - Notice to Request Application

NarrowSubjects.Name: Voting -see also- Absentee and Mail-In Voting

bill_summary: Requires local boards of elections to include a written notice regarding requests for a State-approved absentee ballot application with mailed specimen ballots and any other mailings to voters or eligible voters to raise awareness of mail-in voting options, excluding voters who have permanent absentee ballot status, voters who have already received the notice for that election, or vote-by-mail elections.
responsible_party: Local boards of elections and the Maryland State Board of Elections
stakeholders: Maryland registered voters, eligible voters, and local election boards
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local government finances, as the notice is sent alongside existing mailings such as specimen ballots.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Election Law Article regarding absentee ballot request notices sent by local election boards to eligible voters. The Maryland State Board of Elections oversees and administers election laws statewide, supervises local boards of elections, and approves the absentee ballot applications referenced in the bill.

Synopsis: Specifying that property damage that results from an accident that involves any vessel subject to the State Boat Act while on the waters of the State includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers for purposes of a certain reporting requirement.
Title: Boating Accidents - Reporting Requirement - Property Damage
bill_summary: Clarifies that property damage resulting from a vessel accident on Maryland waters includes damage to navigational aid markers, lights, or identifiers, requiring the vessel operator or owner to report such accidents to the Department of Natural Resources within 10 days.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Vessel operators and owners on Maryland waters, boaters, and maritime navigation authorities
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations, and it does not directly affect local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Department of Natural Resources is the primary implementing agency under the State Boat Act. Operators or owners of vessels involved in boating accidents on State waters that result in specified property damage are required to file accident reports directly with the department.

The Administrative Office of the Courts was consulted regarding potential judicial impacts of reporting mandates and violations under the Natural Resources Article, though boating accident reports themselves are not admissible as evidence in court proceedings.

Synopsis: Requiring each school board to certify to the State Ethics Commission, on or before October 1 each year, that the school board is in compliance with certain requirements of the Maryland Public Ethics Law.
Title: Maryland Public Ethics Law - School Boards - Compliance Certification

NarrowSubjects.Name: Counties -see also- Chartered Counties; Code Counties; etc.

bill_summary: Requires each local school board, including the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, to certify annually to the State Ethics Commission by October 1 that it complies with the Maryland Public Ethics Law regarding conflict of interest and financial disclosure provisions for board members and, if applicable, school system officials and employees.
responsible_party: State Ethics Commission
stakeholders: Local school board members, the Baltimore City Board of School Commissioners, and local school system officials and employees.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The State Ethics Commission and local school boards can handle the annual certification requirements with existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts the State Ethics Commission by requiring each local school board to annually submit a compliance certification regarding ethics and financial disclosure provisions to the Commission by October 1.

The Department of Education oversees the state's public education system and 24 local school systems whose governing school boards are subjected to the annual ethics compliance certification requirement.

Synopsis: Authorizing units in the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a certain process to include a notation of veteran status on an occupational license.
Title: Maryland Department of Labor - Licenses - Notation of Veteran Status and Eligibility for Benefits

NarrowSubjects.Name: Licenses -see also- AB Lic; Certifications; DrLic; Permits
Public Benefits -see also- FoodStmps; Housing; MedAsst
Records -see also- Land Records; Vital Records

bill_summary: Authorizes units within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process allowing applicants for occupational and professional licenses to request a veteran status notation on their license upon submitting proof of service, and to consent to having their contact information shared with Executive Branch agencies to determine eligibility for State and federal veterans' benefits.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Military veterans applying for or renewing occupational and professional licenses in Maryland, and relevant State Executive Branch agencies such as the Department of Veterans and Military Families.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures may increase minimally on a one-time basis by up to $12,000 as early as FY 2026 if units of MD Labor opt to establish the process and modify licensing systems. State revenues and local finances are not affected. Small business veteran licensees could experience minimal expenses if receiving a new license number necessitates updating vehicle markings and promotional materials.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes licensing units within the Maryland Department of Labor to establish a process to include veteran status notations on professional and occupational licenses and transmit applicant contact information to appropriate executive branch agencies.

The bill explicitly references certifications of veteran status issued by the Department of Veterans and Military Families and allows the department to receive contact information of consenting applicants to assist with determining eligibility for state and federal veterans' benefits.

Synopsis: Requiring the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty to stop the vessel as close as possible to the scene of the collision, accident, or casualty until the operator has rendered certain assistance and provided certain information; establishing certain criminal penalties for the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty who does not take certain actions in violation of the Act; etc.
Title: Boating Accidents - Duty to Stop at the Scene, Render Assistance, and Provide Information - Penalties

NarrowSubjects.Name: Crimes and Punishments -see also- Penalties and Sentnc; etc.
Death -see also- Homicide; Murder; Wrongful Death
Penalties and Sentences -see also- Death Penalty

bill_summary: Requires the operator of a vessel involved in a collision, accident, or other casualty resulting in bodily injury or death to immediately stop the vessel as close as possible to the scene to render assistance and provide identifying information, and establishes misdemeanor and felony penalties for failure to stop or render aid.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources
stakeholders: Vessel operators, boaters, and individuals involved in boating collisions or accidents on Maryland waters
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill is not expected to materially affect State or local finances or operations, although criminal fines and periods of incarceration are established for violations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Natural Resources Article under the State Boat Act, governing vessel accident response, reporting requirements to the Department of Natural Resources, and enforcement overseen by the Natural Resources Police.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes new misdemeanor and felony penalties carrying maximum prison sentences of up to 10 years, which could impact state correctional facilities and probation supervision.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates new criminal offenses with substantial terms of imprisonment, requiring legal representation by the Office of the Public Defender for indigent defendants charged under these provisions.
The bill establishes new criminal offenses and penalties that will be tried and adjudicated within the state court system.

Synopsis: Providing that the Governor appoint members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers with the advice and consent of the Senate.
Title: State Board of Stationary Engineers - Member Appointments - Advice and Consent of the Senate

NarrowSubjects.Name: General Assembly -see also- AELR Cmte; LegislativePolCmte
Public Officials -see also- Atty Gen; Compt; Coun Admin; etc

bill_summary: Requires that appointments made by the Governor to the State Board of Stationary Engineers be subject to the advice and consent of the Senate.
responsible_party: Governor, Maryland Senate, and Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Appointees and members of the State Board of Stationary Engineers, stationary engineers, and the boiler manufacturing and design industry.
fiscal_impact_summary: There is no state or local fiscal impact. The change is procedural in nature and does not directly affect governmental finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The State Board of Stationary Engineers is an occupational licensing board housed within the Maryland Department of Labor, and the Secretary of Labor advises on board appointments.
The bill alters the Governor's appointment procedure for the State Board of Stationary Engineers by requiring the advice and consent of the Senate.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting, processing, and submitting board appointments to the Senate for confirmation.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the statutory appointment and confirmation process for members of this state regulatory board.

Synopsis: Extending through fiscal year 2028 distributions by the Comptroller from funds gained from abandoned property in the State to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund; altering the staff and duties of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force; and extending through fiscal year 2028 an annual $14,000,000 appropriation by the Governor from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation.
Title: Access to Counsel in Evictions - Task Force and Special Fund

BroadSubjects.Name: State Government - Agencies, Offices, and Officials

NarrowSubjects.Name: Housing and Community Development, Department of
Salaries and Compensation -see also- Overtime; Reimb. Rates

bill_summary: This bill extends through fiscal year 2028 the requirements for the Comptroller to distribute $14 million annually from the Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund, and for the Governor to appropriate $14 million from the fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. It also transfers the staffing and appointment responsibilities for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development and authorizes compensation for certain tenant members of the task force.
responsible_party: Department of Housing and Community Development and Maryland Legal Services Corporation
stakeholders: Low-income tenants facing eviction proceedings, legal aid organizations, landlords, and members of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund revenues decrease by $14.0 million in FY 2028, offset by an identical $14.0 million increase in special fund revenues to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund. Special fund expenditures from the fund increase by $14.0 million in FY 2028 to provide funding to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation. The Department of Housing and Community Development can absorb task force administrative and compensation costs using existing budgeted resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the responsibility for staffing, designating the chair, and appointing members of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force from the Office of the Attorney General to the Department of Housing and Community Development, and authorizes the department to provide stipends or compensation to certain low-income tenant members.

The bill relieves the Office of the Attorney General of its statutory responsibilities to appoint members to and provide staff support for the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force, transferring those functions to the Department of Housing and Community Development.

The bill extends the requirement that the Comptroller distribute $14,000,000 annually from the State's Unclaimed Property Fund to the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund through fiscal 2028, and the Comptroller is responsible for accounting for the fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly modifies the composition, appointing authority, staffing, compensation provisions, and reporting requirements of the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force.

The bill extends the statutory mandate requiring the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $14,000,000 from the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund to the Maryland Legal Services Corporation in the State budget through fiscal 2028.

As the agency responsible for preparing the state budget and managing state revenues and expenditures, DBM is impacted by the continuation of the $14,000,000 mandated annual appropriation and the corresponding reduction in general fund revenues through fiscal 2028.
The State Treasurer is statutorily designated to hold the Access to Counsel in Evictions Special Fund separately and invest its moneys in the same manner as other State funds.
The Judiciary has designated seats on the Access to Counsel in Evictions Task Force and was consulted regarding the operational impacts of eviction legal representation.

Synopsis: Repealing the Department of Agriculture's authority over the identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.

bill_summary: This bill repeals the Maryland Department of Agriculture's statutory authority over the regulation, identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Agriculture
stakeholders: Maryland cantaloupe growers, wholesalers, retailers, and consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no effect on State or local finances or operations. The Maryland Department of Agriculture does not currently inspect or regulate cantaloupes, as regulation and oversight are conducted at the federal level by the USDA and FDA.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly repeals Title 10, Subtitle 9 of the Agriculture Article, removing the Maryland Department of Agriculture's statutory authority over the identification, inspection, and sale of cantaloupes.

Synopsis: Replacing references to mental hygiene with references to mental health in certain provisions of law governing public health; establishing that, by July 1, 2027, the Department of Health shall conduct a thorough review of Department regulations and adopt regulations to ensure consistency with the Act; and requiring the Department to update all public-facing electronic materials to be consistent with the Act as soon as practicable.

bill_summary: Replaces remaining statutory references to 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health' within the Health - General Article, renames the Mental Hygiene Community-Based Services Fund, and directs the Maryland Department of Health to update departmental regulations and public-facing electronic materials accordingly.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Maryland Department of Health, behavioral health service providers, and individuals seeking or receiving mental health services.
fiscal_impact_summary: State operational expenditures and regulatory updates can be absorbed within existing departmental resources. There is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends provisions of the Health - General Article administered by the Maryland Department of Health (MDH) and explicitly mandates that MDH review its regulations, adopt conforming regulatory amendments replacing 'mental hygiene' with 'mental health' by July 1, 2027, and update all public-facing electronic materials.

The bill amends Section 24-1105(b) of the Health - General Article, which directs the Comptroller to transfer proceeds and investment earnings into the newly renamed Mental Health Community-Based Services Fund.

Synopsis: Altering the membership of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust to include the Secretary of Disabilities or the Secretary's designee.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Disabilities and the Maryland Veterans Trust
stakeholders: Maryland veterans, their families, and members of the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees.
fiscal_impact_summary: Altering the composition of the Board of Trustees does not materially affect State or local government finances. The Secretary of Disabilities or their designee can serve on the Board with existing resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the composition of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust to add the Secretary of Disabilities (or their designee) as an ex officio member.

The Maryland Veterans Trust is staffed and supported by the Department of Veterans and Military Families, and the Secretary serves as the chair of the Board of Trustees whose membership is being altered.
The Secretary of Aging is an existing ex officio member of the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust, which is being expanded.
The Secretary of Health serves as an ex officio member on the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.
The Secretary of Human Services serves as an ex officio member on the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.
The Secretary of Labor serves as an ex officio member on the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.
The Adjutant General of the Military Department serves as an ex officio member on the Board of Trustees of the Maryland Veterans Trust.
The Governor maintains appointment authority over several members serving on the Maryland Veterans Trust Board of Trustees.

bill_summary: This bill alters the standards and procedures for medical and geriatric parole in Maryland. It requires the Maryland Parole Commission to consider an incarcerated individual's age when evaluating parole suitability, repeals the Governor's authority to disapprove medical parole decisions for individuals serving life sentences, and establishes eligibility criteria and hearing requirements for geriatric parole for individuals at least 65 years old who have served at least 20 years. Additionally, it mandates risk assessments for certain candidates, requires annual reporting on geriatric parole outcomes, and directs any realized correctional savings toward parole assessments, hearings, and reentry services.
responsible_party: Maryland Parole Commission and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Incarcerated individuals in Maryland correctional facilities (especially those aged 65 and older or those who are terminally ill or chronically incapacitated), crime victims, and correctional and parole staff.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $474,500 in FY 2026, rising to $575,600 in FY 2027 and $654,500 by FY 2030, reflecting the costs to hire four personnel (three psychologists and one administrative officer) to perform required risk assessments and complete reporting duties. The requirement for general fund expenditures may decrease if grant funds from the Performance Incentive Grant Fund are distributed to the Commission. Potential State incarceration cost savings are indeterminate and not quantified in the estimate. Local finances are not materially affected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS and its constituent entity, the Maryland Parole Commission (MPC), are the primary implementing agencies for the bill. DPSCS must submit names of qualifying incarcerated individuals, conduct risk assessments and parole hearings, provide reentry resources, adopt regulations, and report annual outcome metrics, resulting in an estimated general fund expenditure increase of over $474,000 in FY 2026.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Governor's Office of Crime Prevention and Policy
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: GOCPP houses the Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB) and administers the Performance Incentive Grant Fund. The bill authorizes JROB to recommend distributing savings from the fund to the Maryland Parole Commission to hire psychologists for risk assessments.

The bill directly amends executive authority by repealing the provision that allowed the Governor to disapprove a decision by the Maryland Parole Commission to grant medical parole to an incarcerated individual serving a life sentence.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Justice Reinvestment Oversight Board (JROB) is specifically tasked with receiving annual outcome reports from the Maryland Parole Commission on geriatric parole decisions and is authorized to recommend fund distributions to support risk assessments.

bill_summary: Senate Bill 215 revises state cannabis laws by repealing the authorization for the Maryland Cannabis Administration to issue up to 15 on-site consumption licenses in the second licensing round, and restricting on-site consumption license applications to social equity applicants under certain conditions. The bill authorizes on-site consumption licensees to process and repackage single-serving cannabis products and operate as food service facilities under local approval while prohibiting indoor smoking, off-premises removal, and outside cannabis. Additionally, it extends dispensary delivery of medical cannabis through July 1, 2026, clarifies dispensary zoning and 25% social equity supply rules, allows license transfers via employee stock ownership plans, and specifies that cannabinoid beverages are not exempt from the state sales and use tax as food.

stakeholders: Cannabis business licensees (dispensaries and prospective on-site consumption establishments), social equity applicants, medical cannabis patients and caregivers, adult-use cannabis consumers, and local political subdivisions.

The bill is not otherwise anticipated to materially affect State operations or finances, and the Maryland Cannabis Administration and Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission can handle implementation with existing resources. Local government operations and finances are not materially affected.

The bill authorizes on-site consumption establishments to operate as food service facilities governed under Health - General Article § 21-301, interacting with public health food safety regulations and the Cannabis Public Health Advisory Council.

bill_summary: This bill increases and adjusts several environmental fees, penalties, and funds administered by the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE). Specifically, it raises the maximum air quality permit fee cap and broadens the Maryland Clean Air Fund's uses; increases the per-barrel oil transfer fee from 5 to 9 cents through fiscal 2030; alters the basis of coal combustion by-product fees to include stored volumes; establishes new authority for septic and well construction permit fees if administered by MDE; and establishes the Private Dam Repair Fund alongside new annual dam registration fees, dam safety permit fees, and a loan program to assist private dam owners with repairs and removals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Owners of private and public dams, oil transfer licensees, industrial facilities with regulated air emissions, coal combustion by-product handlers and former generators, individuals seeking septic and well permits, and downstream communities.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by an estimated $5.0 million in FY 2026, rising to approximately $7.2 million in FY 2027 and $7.4 million annually by FY 2030 from increased and newly created fees. State special fund expenditures increase by $6.67 million in FY 2026 pursuant to contingent appropriations in the operating budget, with ongoing annual expenditures ranging between $6.38 million and $6.53 million for program administration and dam loans/repairs. Local government expenditures may increase minimally to pay applicable dam registration, dam safety permit, and air quality emissions fees.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency for the bill, which restructures multiple department fees, updates air quality and water pollution funds, implements a regulatory framework and registration system for dams, and administers the newly created Private Dam Repair Fund.

The State Treasurer is required to hold and invest the newly established Private Dam Repair Fund separately as a nonlapsing fund and credit its interest earnings under an exemption to State Finance and Procurement § 6-226.
The Comptroller is tasked with accounting for the newly created Private Dam Repair Fund and handling any pledged state funds withheld in connection with loan agreements.

The Attorney General is authorized to bring legal actions to recover loan defaults, late fees, interest, and penalties under the Private Dam Repair Fund loan program, and consults on annual enforcement reporting.
DNR owns dams in the state that will be subject to annual registration, potential dam safety permit fees, and regulatory oversight under MDE's updated dam safety provisions.
MDOT manages transportation infrastructure and stormwater embankments that may fall under the dam safety permitting requirements and fee schedules.
DBM is impacted as the bill enacts fee changes that trigger contingent special fund appropriations in the state budget and may require budgetary adjustments.
The Governor's Office receives annual reporting from MDE on the financial status, revenues, expenditures, and funded projects of the Private Dam Repair Fund.

DHS is a named partner utilized by the Program director to disseminate outreach materials and communications regarding available benefits to the expanded military population.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly amends the Education Article governing the Youth Suicide Prevention School Program administered by MSDE, requiring the department to update its regulations, program guidelines, and instructional objectives to incorporate awareness of the relationship between gambling and youth suicide.

MDH supports local school systems' suicide prevention programs through its School Suicide Prevention Toolkit and collaborates with the Maryland Center of Excellence on Problem Gambling to develop educational materials on gambling addiction.

bill_summary: Authorizes the State Highway Administration to place and operate up to eight speed monitoring systems on Interstate 695 and up to six on Interstate 83 in Baltimore County at high-risk crash locations, sets a maximum civil fine of $40 for violations, and dedicates fine revenue to program administrative cost recovery and roadway safety improvements on both highways.

stakeholders: Motorists traveling on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County
fiscal_impact_summary: Transportation Trust Fund (TTF) revenues increase, potentially significantly, from FY 2026 through FY 2030 from speed camera civil penalties; TTF expenditures increase correspondingly to cover administrative costs (estimated up to $600,000 annually) and roadway and safety improvements on I-695 and I-83. General fund expenditures increase by $12,208 in FY 2026 only for Judiciary District Court software reprogramming. Baltimore County finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly authorizes the State Highway Administration to place, operate, and maintain speed monitoring systems on Interstate 695 and Interstate 83 in Baltimore County, receive fine distributions for cost recovery and safety improvements, and submit a comprehensive report on the program by June 1, 2029.

As the parent department of the State Highway Administration and Motor Vehicle Administration, MDOT's Transportation Trust Fund will realize increases in revenues from collected fines and corresponding expenditures for system implementation and roadway safety improvements.

The District Court is responsible for prescribing uniform citations, adjudicating contested speed camera violations, collecting civil penalties, and remitting those funds to the Comptroller; the Judiciary also incurs fiscal costs for software reprogramming.

The bill explicitly mandates that civil penalty fines collected by the District Court for these specific speed monitoring systems must be remitted to the Comptroller for subsequent distribution to the State Highway Administration.

Under the Maryland Vehicle Law governing speed monitoring citations, the Motor Vehicle Administration provides registered owner information and is authorized to refuse or suspend vehicle registrations if penalties are not paid or contested.

The Maryland Stadium Authority owns and manages the Camden Yards Sports Complex, where the geofenced area and games authorizing these raffles are specifically located.

bill_summary: This bill defines 'visual representation' in Maryland's revenge porn statute to include computer-generated images, establishes a civil cause of action for defamation per se or invasion of privacy for victims of revenge porn with potential recovery of attorney's fees, and restricts public inspection of such visual representations within civil and criminal court records.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary
stakeholders: Victims of nonconsensual distribution of intimate visual representations (including computer-generated/deepfake images), defendants in revenge porn cases, civil litigants and attorneys, and state and local courts and law enforcement.
fiscal_impact_summary: State and local revenues and expenditures may increase minimally due to the expanded application of existing criminal misdemeanor penalties (fines up to $5,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years). The Judiciary can handle any additional civil actions using existing budgeted resources.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a civil cause of action for defamation per se or invasion of privacy, authorizes attorney's fees, and restricts public inspection of visual representations contained in court records for both civil and criminal cases under the statute. The Judiciary will handle these new civil filings and manage sealed court records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill broadens the definition of visual representation under the criminal revenge porn statute to include computer-generated imagery, which may result in additional misdemeanor criminal charges where indigent defendants require representation by the Office of the Public Defender.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: Expanding the scope of the criminal offense carries potential sentences of up to two years of incarceration and community supervision, which has a potential minimal fiscal impact on state correctional facilities and parole and probation services.

The statute explicitly authorizes the Attorney General or their designee to access and inspect protected visual representations in court records related to charges or actions under this section, and the office handles criminal appeals.
State law enforcement officers investigate criminal violations of revenge porn statutes and are explicitly authorized under the bill to inspect protected visual representations in court records.

fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can handle the reporting requirements to legislative committees and local Area Agencies on Aging using existing budgeted resources. There is no effect on state revenues, local finances, or small businesses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: SB 376 directly mandates the Maryland Department of Health and its Office of Health Care Quality (OHCQ) to submit quarterly reports to legislative committees on nursing home surveys and bi-annual reports to local area agencies on aging regarding surveyed nursing homes.

The bill requires reports on nursing home surveys to be provided directly to local Area Agencies on Aging (AAAs), which operate under the oversight and funding network administered by the Department of Aging to support older adults and long-term care advocacy.

stakeholders: Maryland law enforcement agencies, police officers, and the Independent Investigations Division of the Office of the Attorney General
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not significantly affected, as the Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission can review the report and issue recommendations using existing budgeted resources. State revenues are unaffected, and there is no local fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission (MPTSC) is an entity housed within the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services. The bill directly mandates MPTSC to annually review the Independent Investigations Division's report and issue recommendations based on that review.

The bill requires review of the annual report published by the Independent Investigations Division (IID), a specialized division within the Office of the Attorney General that investigates police-involved fatalities.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Maryland Police Training and Standards Commission is a permanent state commission assigned a new statutory duty to annually evaluate the IID report and submit recommendations.

bill_summary: Expands eligibility for public safety death benefits to include local 9-1-1 specialists and establishes a presumption that an eligible public safety officer who dies by suicide died in the performance of duties if they were diagnosed with duty-related post-traumatic stress disorder, acute stress disorder, or a trauma- and stress-related disorder.
responsible_party: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
stakeholders: Public safety officers (including law enforcement, correctional officers, firefighters, rescue squad members, state fire marshals, aviation employees, hazardous material response team employees, and 9-1-1 specialists) and their surviving family members or estates.
fiscal_impact_summary: State expenditures are not expected to see an immediate material impact, as the bill's provisions are expected to apply in a limited number of circumstances. Any potential increase in death benefit payments ($125,000 adjusted annually for CPI) can likely be absorbed within existing funding typically budgeted for line-of-duty death benefits ($850,000 in FY 2026). State revenues and local government operations and finances are unaffected.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS is the primary administering agency for the public safety death benefit under § 1-202 of the Public Safety Article. The Secretary and the Department are responsible for receiving death notices, notifying eligible beneficiaries, and adjudicating and paying claims, which this bill expands to include 9-1-1 specialists and certain deaths by suicide resulting from job-related PTSD.
MDEM oversees the Maryland 9-1-1 Board and coordinates state emergency management; the bill specifically extends public safety death benefits to 9-1-1 specialists.
Under § 1-202, death benefit payments are required to be funded through appropriations included by the Governor in the annual State budget.

bill_summary: Exempts specified areas within the Big Savage Mountain, Bear Pen, and Dan's Mountain Wildlands from wildland designations to permit the potential construction of an overhead electric transmission line by NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic, Inc., subject to obtaining a Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN) from the Public Service Commission. The bill establishes requirements for stakeholder engagement, Department of Natural Resources review, and wildland mitigation guarantees, including replacing lost wildland acreage at a 2-to-1 ratio.
responsible_party: Department of Natural Resources and the Public Service Commission
stakeholders: NextEra Energy Transmission MidAtlantic, electric utility customers, environmental and wildlife conservation groups, outdoor recreationists, and residents of Allegany and Garrett counties.
fiscal_impact_summary: State finances and operations are not anticipated to be materially affected, as the Department of Natural Resources and Public Service Commission can manage requirements with existing resources. If acreage lost from wildlands is not replaced within three years, federal fund revenues under the Pittman-Robertson Wildlife Restoration Act could be reduced in future years. Local governments in Allegany and Garrett counties may experience operational involvement in consultation and review without material fiscal impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DNR administers the State wildlands preservation system and is heavily involved in the implementation of the bill. It must consult on the design of the transmission line to minimize forest and habitat loss, receive public comments via a comment portal, conduct a 90-day deliberation period, provide the Secretary's recommendation before the wildland boundary adjustment is enacted, and work with the applicant to acquire replacement wildland acreage at a 2:1 ratio.

The Public Service Commission is the lead regulatory agency responsible for reviewing and approving applications for Certificates of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN). The bill amends CPCN requirements to mandate wildland impact mitigation guarantees for overhead transmission lines through designated wildland areas, and requires the Commission to notify the Department of Legislative Services upon meeting certain contingent milestones.

The Office of the People's Counsel represents the interests of residential utility consumers in proceedings before the Public Service Commission, including CPCN applications for major electric transmission line projects such as the Mid-Atlantic Resiliency Link.

MDE assists in evaluating environmental impacts, such as water and air quality, during the CPCN application and review process for electric transmission infrastructure, and served as an information source for the bill.

bill_summary: This bill alters the factors the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) considers when setting fees for generators of coal combustion by-products (CCBs) to include the volume of CCBs stored in landfills or storage units subject to monitoring. It removes the requirement that MDE lower fees if excess revenue is generated, requiring instead that excess funds be used to increase beneficial reuse and mitigate environmental and public health impacts at priority sites. The bill also creates the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee and directs MDE to adopt regulations implementing federal rules on legacy coal combustion residuals.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Generators and former generators of coal combustion by-products, owners and operators of coal ash landfills and storage sites, and communities near coal combustion residual sites.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $1,031,300 in FY 2027, growing to $1,102,600 by FY 2030 due to expanding the fee to stored CCBs; no revenue impact occurs in FY 2026 because of reporting and billing delays. Special fund expenditures increase by $200,000 in FY 2026 due to a contingent appropriation in the FY 2026 budget, growing to $216,500 by FY 2030. Because revenue collections are delayed until FY 2027, a General Fund deficiency appropriation may be necessary to cover the FY 2026 expenditure. Local finances are not directly affected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing agency under the bill. It is responsible for setting and collecting altered CCB generator fees, utilizing excess revenues for environmental mitigation and beneficial reuse, updating and adopting regulations to implement federal rules on coal combustion residuals, designating the chair, and co-staffing the Statewide CCB Coordinating Committee.

DNR's Power Plant Research Program (PPRP) is assigned specific statutory roles under the bill, including having a designated representative serve on the Statewide CCB Coordinating Committee and jointly providing staff support for the committee alongside MDE.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill creates a new state entity, the Statewide Coal Combustion By-Products Coordinating Committee, to meet semi-annually, share monitoring data, discuss remedial actions, and submit an annual findings report to designated committees of the General Assembly.
