bill_summary: The Registered Apprenticeship Investments for a Stronger Economy (RAISE) Act establishes the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development (MORAD), the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program, and the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program along with a dedicated nonlapsing special fund to incentivize employers to hire and retain apprentices. The bill also establishes the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board, mandates a 1:1 journeyworker-to-apprentice ratio with deviation procedures for nonhazardous occupations, alters annual apprenticeship reporting requirements, and repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Apprentices, employers, apprenticeship sponsors, labor organizations, qualified workforce intermediaries, and training providers across Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $1.5 million in FY 2026 to fund 14 staff positions and operating costs for MORAD, increasing to $1.73 million by FY 2030. General fund expenditures and special fund revenues/expenditures will increase by an indeterminate but potentially significant amount (up to $5.0 million annually) in FY 2027 through FY 2030 for Pay Per Apprentice program grants. General fund revenues increase minimally through FY 2028 from interest earnings on the special fund. Local impact is minimal to the extent local entities receive program grants.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MD Labor is the primary implementing agency. The bill establishes the Maryland Office of Registered Apprenticeship Development (MORAD), the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program, the Maryland Pay Per Apprentice Program, the associated special fund, and the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board within the department, along with adjusting apprenticeship ratios and reporting duties.

The bill explicitly requires the Director of the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program to consult with the Governor's Workforce Development Board in developing the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program.

The bill statutorily requires the Director of the Maryland Apprenticeship and Training Program to consult with the Department of Commerce in developing the Registered Apprenticeship Qualified Intermediary Program.

The bill mandates that the Governor include an appropriation in the annual budget bill to cover administrative costs for MORAD, authorizes appropriations for the special fund, and authorizes the Governor to appoint the chair and employer representatives to the new Advisory Board.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill establishes the Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board to advise and evaluate MORAD, while formally repealing the statutory Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee.
The bill creates the Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund as a special, nonlapsing fund and directs the State Treasurer to hold and invest the money of the fund.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the newly established Maryland Apprenticeship Incentive Pay Per Apprentice Program Fund.

DBM is impacted as the state's budget and personnel agency, as the bill establishes a mandated annual appropriation for MORAD administrative costs and involves funding for 14 new state personnel positions.
The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee on which the State Superintendent of Schools previously served.
The bill repeals the Youth Apprenticeship Advisory Committee on which the Secretary of Juvenile Services previously served.
The Office of Appointments assists the Governor in vetting and recruiting appointees for the newly established Registered Apprenticeship Development Advisory Board.

bill_summary: The Expungement Reform Act of 2025 alters statutory waiting periods for criminal record expungement to begin upon the 'completion of the sentence' rather than satisfactory completion, expands eligibility for expungement to include convictions for credit card theft and driving without a license, and adds criteria for court consideration (such as supervision success and payment or ability to pay restitution). Additionally, it shields from Maryland Judiciary Case Search any records of charges resulting in nolle prosequi with drug or alcohol treatment, charges marked stet at least three years prior, and pardoned cannabis possession convictions.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services (DPSCS)
stakeholders: Individuals with criminal records or convictions seeking expungement, particularly those with pardoned cannabis convictions, stet dispositions, credit card theft, or driving without a license charges, as well as victims and court personnel.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $23,824 in FY 2026 for one-time computer programming for the Judiciary, with potential minimal ongoing expenditure increases for the Judiciary and DPSCS if additional staff are needed to process an increased volume of expungement petitions. General fund revenues increase minimally from the $30 filing fee for expungement petitions. There is no material fiscal impact on local governments.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly impacts judicial operations by modifying expungement eligibility criteria, altering factors judges must consider during hearings, requiring $23,800 in IT programming for Maryland Judiciary Case Search to shield certain records, and potentially increasing the workload of court clerks processing expungement petitions.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The department houses the Criminal Justice Information System (CJIS) Central Repository, which receives and complies with court-issued expungement orders and maintains criminal history record information affected by the bill.
This is an Administration bill that aligns state record shielding on Maryland Judiciary Case Search with the Governor's executive order pardoning cannabis possession convictions.
As a primary law enforcement unit maintaining police records of arrests and criminal charges, the agency is required to comply with court orders to expunge qualifying police records.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Maryland Office of the Public Defender
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The office regularly assists indigent clients with post-disposition matters, including filing petitions for expungement, and is directly affected by expanded eligibility and altered waiting period timelines for criminal record expungements.

bill_summary: Reclassifies the crime of transporting a regulated firearm into Maryland for unlawful sale or trafficking from a misdemeanor to a felony and eliminates the three-year statute of limitations, allowing prosecution to be instituted at any time.
responsible_party: Maryland Judiciary and State's Attorneys
stakeholders: Individuals accused or convicted of unlawfully transporting or trafficking regulated firearms into Maryland, law enforcement agencies, and the judicial system.

bill_summary: Senate Bill 533 alters deadlines for completing investigations and filing administrative charges for alleged police officer misconduct. For public complaints, the investigating unit must complete its investigation and forward findings within 334 days, the administrative charging committee must make a determination within 30 days, and the entire process through disposition must be finished within 395 days after the appropriate official became aware of the incident. For misconduct investigations not reviewed by a committee, administrative charges must be filed within one year and one day from when the agency became aware of the incident. If the misconduct is subject to a criminal investigation, charges must be filed within one year and one day following the determination that the matter is not criminal, the final disposition of criminal charges, or notice that prosecutors declined to file charges.
responsible_party: Maryland state and local law enforcement agencies and administrative charging committees
stakeholders: Police officers, law enforcement agencies, administrative charging committees, and members of the public who file complaints alleging police officer misconduct
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, State and local government finances are not anticipated to be materially affected.

The MDTA operates a full-service, accredited police force that must comply with the bill's altered time limits for investigating officer misconduct complaints and filing administrative charges.
MDOT oversees modal administrations that employ sworn law enforcement officers (such as MTA Police and MDTA Police) that are directly impacted by the revised police disciplinary deadlines.
The MTA employs its own dedicated police force, and its internal misconduct investigations and administrative charging referrals are bound by the timelines specified in the bill.
DGS oversees the Maryland Capitol Police, whose sworn officers and internal investigatory procedures are governed by Maryland's statutory police accountability and disciplinary time limits.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: DPSCS conducts internal law enforcement investigations and employs sworn investigative personnel subject to the police accountability framework and time limits amended by the bill.

Morgan State University maintains its own independent police department whose internal misconduct investigations and charging procedures are subject to the bill's deadlines.
The Maryland Judiciary handles judicial appeals arising from police trial board decisions and statutory police discipline procedures governed by these timelines.
The Comptroller employs sworn enforcement agents, was surveyed for the bill's fiscal analysis, and must ensure any internal enforcement investigations comply with state police discipline standards.
The Department of Labor was consulted as an information source regarding the bill's fiscal and operational impact on state administrative and regulatory practices.

responsible_party: Maryland Department of Health
stakeholders: Service members, veterans, spouses, children, stepchildren of service members or veterans, and health care facilities in Maryland.
fiscal_impact_summary: The Maryland Department of Health can implement the bill using existing budgeted resources, with no effect on state revenues. There is no material impact on local government finances or operations.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill adds a new subtitle to the Health - General Article governing health care facilities—expressly including facilities operated by the Department of Health and the Behavioral Health Administration. It authorizes patient screening for service member community status, encourages compliance with Joint Commission health care equity standards, and requires the Department to submit an annual report on the needs and progress made toward health care equity for service member community members.

The bill directly amends State Government Article § 9-901, which establishes the core definitions (such as 'service member', 'veteran', 'reserve component', and 'uniformed services') governing the Department of Veterans and Military Families, aligning with its mission to support health care and services for veterans and their families.

As the head of the Maryland Military Department, the Adjutant General oversees the state's military forces, whose active and reserve personnel and families are directly categorized and impacted by the definitions and health equity initiatives established in this legislation.

Beginning in December 2026, the Governor receives an annual report from the Maryland Department of Health assessing the needs of service member community members, facility compliance, and progress toward health care equity.

The bill updates legislative committee references in procurement reporting provisions required of the Department of General Services.

fiscal_impact_summary: State and local government expenditures for workers' compensation are expected to decrease minimally due to administrative efficiencies and reduced subpoena costs. Operating as Chesapeake Employers' Insurance Company, the entity will realize administrative efficiencies and cost savings by avoiding subpoena fees when obtaining claimant medical and financial records for State and private workers' compensation claims.

fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State or local government finances or operations. The impact on small businesses is minimal.

bill_summary: The Maryland Tenant Mold Protection Act requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), in coordination with other state departments, to develop a centralized website and informational pamphlet regarding dampness and mold remediation. It mandates landlords to distribute this pamphlet to tenants and to conduct a mold assessment within 15 days of receiving written notice of mold, followed by remediation within 45 days (or a reasonable time if 45 days is not feasible) if mold is detected. Landlords must also ensure proper ventilation and low relative humidity. Additionally, MDE must adopt regulations by June 1, 2027, establishing uniform standards for mold assessment, remediation, and building codes.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Residential tenants, private and public landlords, local housing authorities, local code enforcement agencies, and mold assessment and remediation contractors.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $125,000 in FY 2026 only for MDE to hire a consultant to assist in drafting uniform regulations; other state agencies can handle duties with existing resources. State revenues are unaffected. Local government expenditures increase, potentially significantly starting in FY 2026, for local jurisdictions that own or manage residential properties to conduct assessments, remediation, and building retrofits (e.g., Prince George's County estimates capital retrofits of at least $10.3 million), as well as to enforce livability code standards.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary agency tasked with implementing the bill, including developing and updating a centralized website and informational pamphlet on mold remediation, as well as promulgating uniform regulations and standards for mold assessment and remediation by June 1, 2027.

MDH is statutorily required to coordinate with MDE on developing the centralized website and informational pamphlet, as well as consult on the adoption of uniform regulations for mold assessment and remediation.

DHCD is statutorily required to collaborate with MDE to develop the mold informational pamphlet and website, and to consult on the development of statewide mold assessment and remediation regulations.

DGS is mandated by statute to coordinate with MDE in developing the centralized website and informational pamphlet, and to consult with MDE on the regulations establishing standards for mold assessment and remediation.

MD Labor is required to coordinate with MDE and other agencies to develop the centralized website and informational pamphlet on mold remediation and dampness, and is the agency responsible for the state's Minimum Livability Code referenced in landlord maintenance requirements.

bill_summary: Transfers the Cyber Maryland Program, along with its associated fund and board, from the Maryland Technology Development Corporation (TEDCO) to the Maryland Department of Labor. The bill expands the program's required activities to include awarding competitive grants or contracts for cybersecurity workforce development, alters the membership of the Cyber Maryland Board, expands eligible grant recipients, and modifies annual reporting and funding provisions.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of Labor
stakeholders: Cybersecurity job seekers, students, employers, education and training institutions, registered apprenticeship sponsors, local workforce boards, and critical infrastructure operators.
fiscal_impact_summary: State net general fund expenditures and special fund revenues and expenditures increase by $3.0 million annually beginning in FY 2026, reflecting the repeal of a $99,000 annual mandated appropriation for TEDCO and a $3.1 million annual appropriation for the Maryland Department of Labor to administer the program and award grants. Local government entities may experience increased grant revenues.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill transfers the Cyber Maryland Program, the Cyber Maryland Fund, and the Cyber Maryland Board from TEDCO to the Department of Labor, making it the primary agency responsible for administering the program, awarding competitive workforce grants, and reporting on outcomes.

TEDCO currently houses and administers the Cyber Maryland Program and Fund; this bill transfers the program and associated funding out of TEDCO to MD Labor, while maintaining the TEDCO CEO on the Cyber Maryland Board.

The Secretary of Information Technology serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and the program's statutory purpose includes supporting DoIT's efforts to improve the State government's cybersecurity posture.

The Secretary of Commerce is designated as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and the board is required to coordinate with the Department of Commerce on cybersecurity workforce and industry initiatives.
The State Superintendent of Schools is added as a member of the Cyber Maryland Board, and elementary and secondary schools are eligible recipients of grants from the Cyber Maryland Fund.
The Secretary of Higher Education is added to the Cyber Maryland Board, and postsecondary educational institutions are eligible recipients of grants for cybersecurity programs.
The Adjutant General (or designee) is designated as an ex officio member of the Cyber Maryland Board.
The Secretary of Veterans and Military Families serves on the Cyber Maryland Board, and program initiatives specifically contemplate strategies supporting transitioning veterans.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the Cyber Maryland Fund.
The State Treasurer is statutorily required to hold and invest the monies of the Cyber Maryland Fund.

The Governor appoints private and educational representatives to the Cyber Maryland Board, receives annual progress reports, and is authorized to include program appropriations in the annual state budget.

Public higher education institutions are eligible grant recipients, Board membership includes representatives from public 4-year institutions, and the bill requires reporting on activities including UMBC's Center for Cybersecurity.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), in coordination with the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM), to establish cybersecurity standards, guidance, and reporting procedures for community water systems (CWS) and community sewerage systems (CSS). Systems serving more than 3,300 customers or using information/operational technology must adopt minimum cybersecurity standards, begin planning a zero-trust model, undergo biennial third-party maturity assessments, and report cyber incidents to DoIT. Additionally, the bill restricts public records inspection concerning operational technology and critical infrastructure security under Maryland's Public Information Act.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE), in coordination with the Department of Information Technology (DoIT) and the Maryland Department of Emergency Management (MDEM)
stakeholders: Public and private community water and sewerage system providers, local emergency managers, local governments owning or operating water/sewer utilities, cybersecurity service contractors, and Maryland water and sewer utility customers
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $271,700 in FY 2026, reflecting $171,700 for DoIT to hire one cybersecurity expert and $100,000 for MDEM for contractual support to develop guidance and conduct tabletop exercises, with total GF expenditures growing to $340,479 by FY 2030. State-owned and local government-owned water and sewerage systems face potentially significant cost increases starting in FY 2026 to achieve compliance, including an estimated $30,000 to $40,000 per third-party assessment and potential system restructuring costs. State and local revenues are unaffected.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill places primary regulatory and coordination responsibilities on MDE to establish cybersecurity standards, update regulations for community water and sewerage systems, integrate cybersecurity into operator certifications, and report biennially to the General Assembly.

DoIT is assigned key operational and oversight responsibilities under the bill, including hiring a dedicated operational technology cybersecurity professional, establishing an incident reporting structure, collecting biannual compliance certifications, and publishing annual reports.

MDEM and its Cyber Preparedness Unit are tasked with developing emergency risk communication guidance, coordinating with local emergency managers, and hosting annual tabletop exercises tailored to cybersecurity threats against the water and wastewater sector.

MES operates water and wastewater treatment facilities throughout Maryland on behalf of state, local, and private clients, directly subjecting its systems to the cybersecurity standards, planning requirements, and third-party assessments established by the bill.

Synopsis: Requiring the Governor to include $250,000 in the annual budget bill for fiscal years 2027 through 2030 to the Governor's Office for Children to provide grants to fund operating expenses for the Boys and Girls Clubs of Maryland.
Title: Governor's Office for Children - Boys and Girls Clubs of Maryland - Grant Funding
bill_summary: Requires the Governor to include an annual appropriation of $250,000 in the State budget for fiscal years 2027 through 2030 for the Governor's Office for Children to award grants supporting the operating expenses of the Boys and Girls Clubs of Maryland.
responsible_party: Governor's Office for Children
stakeholders: Boys and Girls Clubs of Maryland and the children, youth, and families served by them across the state.
fiscal_impact_summary: State general fund expenditures increase by $250,000 annually from FY 2027 through FY 2030 to fulfill the mandated grant appropriation. There is no fiscal impact in FY 2026, revenues are unaffected, and there is no local government impact.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Governor's Office for Children is the primary agency responsible for administering the mandated grant funding of $250,000 annually in fiscal years 2027 through 2030 to support the operating expenses of the Boys and Girls Clubs of Maryland.

The Department of Budget and Management is responsible for preparing and supervising the annual state budget and must implement the bill's statutory mandated appropriation for fiscal years 2027 through 2030.

The bill statutorily requires the Governor to include a specific appropriation in the annual executive budget submission for fiscal years 2027 through 2030 for the Governor's Office for Children, which sits within the Executive Department.

bill_summary: This bill modifies the administration and oversight of the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund (CRRF). It requires the Office of Social Equity (OSE), with assistance from the Comptroller, to oversee the CRRF, oversee the appropriation of funds, and train fund recipients. The bill also specifies authorized uses for community-based initiatives in low-income communities, caps local government administrative expenses from the fund at 15%, requires counties to develop a distribution plan in consultation with stakeholders prior to funding disbursement, and mandates annual reporting from counties to OSE.
responsible_party: Office of Social Equity
stakeholders: Communities disproportionately impacted by the historical enforcement of cannabis laws, low-income communities, community-based organizations, county and municipal governments, and the Office of Social Equity.
fiscal_impact_summary: OSE special fund expenditures increase by $65,986 in FY 2026 (reflecting a 0.5 FTE position and operating costs) and by $57,923 to $66,001 annually through FY 2030. To cover these administrative costs, revenues distributed to the Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund increase correspondingly, which reduces remaining sales and use tax revenues available for distribution: in FY 2026, General Fund revenues decrease by $32,993, CRRF revenues decrease by $23,095, other special funds decrease by $6,598, and aggregate county direct revenues decrease by $3,299 (with similar ongoing decreases). Counties may incur administrative costs to develop distribution plans and report data, but may retain up to 15% of their CRRF funds to defray these expenses.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The Office of Social Equity functions within the Maryland Cannabis Administration, and its operations and administrative costs under the bill are funded through the administration's Cannabis Regulation and Enforcement Fund.
The Comptroller assists the Office of Social Equity in overseeing the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund and remains statutorily responsible for accounting for the fund.
The State Treasurer is required by statute to hold the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund separately and invest its moneys.
The Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund is statutorily designated as subject to audit by the Office of Legislative Audits.
The Office of Social Equity consults with the Office of the Attorney General to determine the communities most impacted by disproportionate enforcement of cannabis prohibitions.
The Department of Commerce administers the Cannabis Business Assistance Fund, which experiences a minor fiscal impact via the redistribution of adult-use cannabis sales and use tax revenues.

The Department of Health administers the Cannabis Public Health Fund, which receives a statutory share of adult-use cannabis sales and use tax revenues slightly reduced by the allocation for administrative oversight expenses.
The Governor appoints the Executive Director of the Office of Social Equity, who administers and oversees the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund under the bill.

bill_summary: Establishes an extended producer responsibility framework requiring producers of packaging and paper products to join or establish producer responsibility organizations (PROs) or alternative collection programs, and submit producer responsibility plans to the Maryland Department of the Environment (MDE) for review and approval. Requires PROs to finance recycling infrastructure, reimburse local governments and service providers for eligible recycling and composting costs, and pay state administrative fees. The bill also establishes performance targets, mandates statewide recycling needs assessments every 10 years, and prohibits the sale of covered materials without an approved plan.
responsible_party: Maryland Department of the Environment
stakeholders: Producers, manufacturers, and brand owners of packaging and paper products, producer responsibility organizations (PROs), local governments, recycling and waste management service providers, and Maryland consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund revenues increase by $667,000 in FY 2026 from an assessment reimbursement fee paid by PROs, and subsequently match MDE administrative costs ($330,100 in FY 2027, rising to $572,300 in FY 2029). State special fund expenditures increase by $212,800 in FY 2026, growing to $572,300 by FY 2029 for personnel and operational oversight. Local government revenues will increase beginning around FY 2029 as local jurisdictions registered as service providers receive reimbursements from PROs for collecting and processing covered materials, alongside potential capital investments for local recycling infrastructure.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: MDE is the primary implementing and regulatory agency for the bill. Its Office of Recycling is tasked with reviewing and approving producer responsibility plans, conducting statewide recycling needs assessments, developing a statewide list of covered materials, registering service providers and producer responsibility organizations, collecting fees, adopting implementing regulations, and administering enforcement and the State Recycling Trust Fund.

agency_relevance.agency_name: Executive Commissions, Committees, Task Forces, and Advisory Boards
agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly alters the statutory purpose, membership, and responsibilities of the Producer Responsibility Advisory Council, requiring it to advise producers on drafting plans, review submitted plans and annual reports, and provide recommendations to MDE.

The OAG is responsible for enforcing civil and criminal violations of the Environment Article incorporated under the bill (§§ 9-334 through 9-344) and may be involved in advising on antitrust immunity provisions established for participating producers.
The Comptroller is statutorily designated to account for the State Recycling Trust Fund, which will receive new fee revenues and penalty collections from producer responsibility organizations.
The State Treasurer holds and invests the State Recycling Trust Fund, which is expanded to include dedicated fee revenues, fines, and penalties established by the bill.

MES provides solid waste management and recycling services to local jurisdictions and the State, coordinates with MDE on annual solid waste and recycling reporting, and operates facilities and services that may be impacted by producer responsibility reimbursements and infrastructure funding.

bill_summary: This bill requires the Maryland State Department of Education, in consultation with the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association, to establish and periodically update a list of similar boys' and girls' high school sports. It requires local county boards of education to ensure equal pay and assigning fees for high school sports officials who perform similar officiating roles in similar sports within the county, and to reject procurement bids or proposals that do not provide equal compensation.
responsible_party: Maryland State Department of Education and local county boards of education
stakeholders: High school sports officials (referees, umpires, and judges), officiating assignors and associations, local school systems, and high school athletic programs
fiscal_impact_summary: State revenues and expenditures are not affected, as the Maryland State Department of Education can handle requirements using existing resources. Local school system expenditures will increase in counties needing to equalize pay rates between officials for boys' and girls' sports; for example, Anne Arundel County estimates an annual increase of $20,700 and Frederick County estimates $5,013 beginning in fiscal 2026, while other jurisdictions already provide equal pay.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill directly mandates the Maryland State Department of Education (MSDE), in consultation with the Maryland Public Secondary Schools Athletic Association, to develop by September 1, 2025, and update every three years a list of similar boys' and girls' high school sports to govern pay parity for sports officials.

responsible_party: Maryland Insurance Administration
stakeholders: Health insurance carriers, insurance producers and brokers, and individuals aged 65 or older or those eligible to enroll or switch Medicare supplement policies.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not substantively change State activities or operations and has no local fiscal impact. Small business insurance brokers that sell Medicare supplement policies may see a potential meaningful benefit from increased commissions.

The Maryland Health Benefit Exchange oversees health coverage access and works closely with insurance producers and carriers in Maryland, and was consulted as an information source regarding health coverage and enrollment policies.

fiscal_impact_summary: State operations and finances are not materially affected. At the local level, there is a minimal expenditure decrease for the small number of municipalities (approximately six) that qualify for the audit exemption due to reduced auditing costs; municipal revenues are not affected.

bill_summary: This bill requires accommodations intermediaries (such as short-term rental platforms) meeting certain transaction thresholds to collect and remit local hotel rental taxes centrally to the Maryland Comptroller rather than directly to local jurisdictions. The Comptroller distributes the revenues back to the appropriate counties and municipalities, retaining up to 1.5% to cover administrative costs. The bill also alters interest rates on unpaid hotel rental taxes in Garrett County, shortens the grace period before penalties apply in Talbot County, and raises the maximum room rental tax Howard County is authorized to impose from 7% to 8%.
responsible_party: Comptroller of Maryland
stakeholders: Accommodations intermediaries (short-term rental platforms), accommodations providers/hoteliers, transient guests renting accommodations, and Maryland county and municipal governments.
fiscal_impact_summary: State special fund expenditures increase by approximately $1.3 million ($1,264,815) in FY 2028 for five new personnel and $800,000 in IT/programming costs, with ongoing annual personnel costs of $438,100 by FY 2030. State special fund revenues increase starting in FY 2028 from retaining up to 1.5% of collected local hotel rental taxes for administration. Local government revenues may increase through improved collection compliance; specifically, Howard County revenues could increase by approximately $828,600 annually beginning in FY 2028 if its hotel rental tax rate is increased to 8%.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill designates the Comptroller as the primary entity responsible for collecting and administering the local hotel rental tax from accommodations intermediaries, establishing remittance and distribution processes to counties and municipalities, conducting audits, and creating a unified tax return.

The bill provides for civil actions and tax enforcement concerning accommodations intermediaries, and the fiscal note specifically identifies the need for an Assistant Attorney General to handle legal advice, enforcement, and litigation arising from the new collection system.

The bill incorporates Title 13 procedural rights for accommodations intermediaries, including rights to appeal assessments and final determinations of the Comptroller, which are subject to administrative review by the Maryland Tax Court.

bill_summary: Extends the expiration date of a Class B-D-7 alcoholic beverages license issued for a premises on the 5700 block of Falls Road in Baltimore City until July 1, 2026, allowing for the completion of an ownership transfer and license renewal at the same location.
responsible_party: Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners
stakeholders: Class B-D-7 alcoholic beverages license holders and prospective transferees on the 5700 block of Falls Road, as well as patrons and businesses in the surrounding Baltimore City neighborhood.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill has no state fiscal effect and does not materially affect Baltimore City finances or operations. The small business impact is minimal.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill extends the expiration of a specific local alcoholic beverages license in Baltimore City. While local licensing and transfers are administered by the Baltimore City Board of License Commissioners with no state fiscal impact, the Comptroller maintains regulatory oversight of the alcohol industry in Maryland.

stakeholders: Officers and volunteers of Hatzalah of Baltimore, as well as residents and drivers in Baltimore City and Baltimore County.
fiscal_impact_summary: The bill does not materially affect State finances or operations. Local finances and operations in Baltimore City and Baltimore County are also not directly affected, as the bill is authorizing in nature.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Maryland Vehicle Law concerning vehicle lighting equipment authorized by the Motor Vehicle Administrator, permitting specific emergency lighting on privately owned vehicles of officers of a qualifying volunteer emergency medical service.

The bill amends the Transportation Article regarding vehicle equipment standards, and the Maryland Department of Transportation was consulted regarding the operational and statutory impact of the bill.

Synopsis: Increasing the percentage of beer not produced by the holder of a Class 5 brewery license that the license holder is permitted to sell for on-premises consumption if the holder also holds an applicable on-site consumption permit or a Class D license.

bill_summary: Increases from 25% to 35% the maximum percentage of beer not brewed on-site that a qualifying Class 5 brewery license holder is allowed to sell for on-premises consumption under an on-site consumption permit or Class D beer license.
responsible_party: Alcohol, Tobacco, and Cannabis Commission
stakeholders: Class 5 brewery license holders (specifically large-scale operations such as Open Gate Brewery in Baltimore County) and adult beer consumers.
fiscal_impact_summary: According to the Fiscal Note, the bill does not materially affect State or local government operations or finances.

agency_relevance.relevance_explanation: The bill amends the Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article to modify on-premises beer sales percentages for Class 5 breweries. According to the agency summary, the Comptroller of Maryland is responsible for regulating the alcohol industry and collecting state revenues.
